Find enclosed Safety Circular-01 (Rev-04) regarding Issue, Revision, Updation and Deletion of Delhi Metro SOP and SWO/DWO.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 01 (Rev-04)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR ISSUE, REVISION, UPDATION AND DELETION OF DELHI METRO SOP AND SWO/DWO
## 1. INTRODUCTION:

## 1. INTRODUCTION:

' Special Instruction' means instruction issued from time to time by the authorised officer in respect of particular cases or special circumstances.

## 1. INTRODUCTION:

This procedure order governs all the matters pertaining to the Introduction, Issuing, Revision, Updating and Deletion of Special Instructions in the form of JPOs for Delhi Metro such as Station Working  Order  (SWO),  Depot  Working  Order  (DWO)  and  SOPs  including  Safety  Circulars, Special Instructions, Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), Accident & Disaster Management Manual and Temporary Instructions pertaining to Main Line & Depot Operations on all lines.
This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the  Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 & Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules, 2022.
## 2. SCOPE:

## 2. SCOPE:

This  procedure applies for  issuing, revision  updating  and  deletion  of  various  JPOs  including Station Working Order (SWO) / Depot Working Order (DWO) and SOPs such as Safety Circular (SC), Special Instruction (SI), Temporary Instruction (TI), Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), Accident & Disaster Management Manual (A&DMM) on main line as well as in Depot where either due to nature of work or otherwise two or more than two departments are involved.
## 3. RESPONSIBILITIES:

## 3. RESPONSIBILITIES:

3.1. These Special Instruction are issued under the authority of Authorised Officer.
3.2. HOD  (Operation)  shall  be  responsible  for  issue,  control  and  updating  of  JPOs.  HOD (Operation) shall nominate at least one Dy HOD/Operation for this purpose.
3.3. All members of SSEC shall nominate atleast one Dy. HOD from their wing for preparation/ modifications/ review in SOP. Composition of SSEC is detailed hereafter.
3.4. Nominated  Dy.  HOD  of  concerned  department  shall  be  responsible  for  initiation,  review, modification,  implementation  and  withdrawal  of  SOPs.  However,  concerned  Dy  HOD  incharge of concerned department of concerned section/line shall be responsible for initiation, review, modification, implementation and withdrawal of SWO/DWO.
3.5. Nominated Dy. HOD of concerned department shall be responsible for review & revision of SOPs in case of changes in technology, modifications in the system, expansion of network or otherwise. However, concerned Dy HOD in-charge of concerned department of concerned section/ line shall be responsible for reviewing/ revising/ initiating of SWO/DWO due to these changes.
3.6. Nominated/Concerned Dy. HOD of the department initiating the draft JPO may call a meeting of  all  Nominated/Concerned  Dy.  HODs  for  describing  and  fast  approval  process  of procedures.
3.7. Intra departmental guidelines/instructions may be prepared and issued by Dy. HOD/HOD of the concerned department for the safe and smooth running of system for day to day working.
## 4. STANDING SAFETY EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE (SSEC):

## 4. STANDING SAFETY EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE (SSEC):

4.1. The  Standing  Safety  Executive  Committee  (SSEC)  shall  consist  of  HODs  of  various

## Introduction

departments for final reviewing of the above said JPOs as per procedure detailed hereafter. The members of Standing Safety Executive Committee(SSEC) are as follows: -
## 5. PROCEDURE FOR ISSUE/REVISION/WITHDRAWAL OF SOP:
## 5.1. SOPs/ SAFETY CIRCULARs/ ACCIDENT & DISASTER MANAGEMENT MANUAL:

## 5.1. SOPs/ SAFETY CIRCULARs/ ACCIDENT & DISASTER MANAGEMENT MANUAL:

Nominated Dy. HOD of the department initiating a SOP/SC/A&DMM shall prepare draft to be issued/revised/withdrawn and put up for review and concurrence of nominated Dy. HODs of concerned departments.
After review & concurrence of all nominated Dy HODs of concerned departments, Dy HOD  initiating  draft  SOP/SC/A&DMM  shall  put  up  concurred  draft  for  perusal  of members of SSEC & concerned HODs of other department(s) (if required).
The same may be reviewed and signed by Dy. HOD and HOD of project wing if required.
After review & concurrence of all members of SSEC and HODs of other department(s) (as the case may be), Dy HOD initiating the draft SOP/SC/A&DMM shall put up the concurred draft for perusal & approval of authorised officer.
After availing approval of SOP/SC/A&DMM from the authorised officer, Nominated Dy. HOD  of  the  department  initiating  the  draft  SOP/SC/A&DMM  shall  forward  the SOP/SC/A&DMM to nominated Dy. HOD of operations department for issue.
Nominated  Dy.  HOD/Operation  shall  issue  the  approved  SOP/SC/A&DMM  or  its corrigendum; as the case may be.
Note: Nominated Dy. HOD/Operation, if finds suitable, may merge the approved SOP/SC/A&DMM with any other corrigendum / SOP without technical change for issue.
## 5.2. SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONs :

## 5.2. SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONs :

Nominated Dy. HOD of the department initiating Special Instruction shall prepare draft of  the  Special  Instruction  to  be  issued/revised/withdrawn  and  put  up  for  review  and concurrence of nominated Dy. HODs.
After review & concurrence of all nominated Dy HODs, Dy HOD initiating the draft SI shall put up concurred draft for perusal of Concerned HODs.
After review & concurrence of all concerned HODs, Dy HOD initiating the draft SI shall put up the concurred draft for perusal & approval of authorised officer.
After availing approval of Special Instruction from the authorised officer, Nominated Dy.

## Introduction

HOD of the department initiating the draft SI shall forward the SI to nominated Dy. HOD of operations department for issue.

## Introduction

Note: Nominated  Dy.  HOD/Operation,  if  finds  suitable,  may  merge  the  approved  Special Instruction with any other corrigendum / SOP without technical change for issue.
## 5.3. TEMPORARY INSTRUCTION:

## 5.3. TEMPORARY INSTRUCTION:

Temporary Instruction is issued to meet an urgent need of instruction and/or for works which are temporary in nature. In case the instruction is required for a long period, it shall be included in the next issue/revision of appropriate JPO and shall be deleted after approval/circulation of that appropriate Instruction.
Temporary  Instruction  shall  be  prepared  by  nominated  Dy.  HOD  of  concerned department. If more than one department is involved in work, draft TI shall be reviewed and concurred by all concerned Dy. HODs.
After  scrutiny  by  concerned  Dy.  HODs,  this  shall  be  reviewed  and  approved  by concerned HOD(s). After approval of HODs, the Temporary instruction shall be issued by the nominated Dy. HOD/Ops.
Concerned  Dy.  HOD  of  concerned  department  initiating  temporary  instruction,  with concurrence of other concerned Dy HODs and approval of Concerned HOD(s), shall be responsible for deletion of instruction after completion of its need/ merger in appropriate instruction.
## 6. PROCEDURE FOR ISSUE/ WITHDRAWAL OF SWO/DWO:-

## 6. PROCEDURE FOR ISSUE/ WITHDRAWAL OF SWO/DWO:-

6.1. Nominated Dy. HOD of Operation department shall prepare draft of the Station Working Order/ Depot Working Order and put up for review and concurrence of all concerned Dy. HODs of O&M and Project wing as per requirements.
6.2. Nominated Dy. HOD/Operation shall put up draft SWO/DWO for review and concurrence of concerned Dy. HODs.
6.3. Nominated Dy. HOD/Operation shall put up reviewed and concurred draft SWO/DWO for perusal/concurrence of members of SSEC and Concerned HOD of other department(s) (if required).
6.4. After review & concurrence of all members of SSEC and HODs of other department(s) (as case may be), Nominated Dy. HOD/Operation shall put up the concurred draft for perusal & approval of authorised officer.
6.5. After approval of authorised officer, nominated Dy. HOD/ Operation shall issue SWO/DWO.
## 7. PROCEDURE FOR REVIEW AND REVISION PROCESS:
## 7 .1 Review and Revision For SOPs :-

## 7 .1 Review and Revision For SOPs :-

Any major changes/modification in system/technology or any other specific reasons shall invite immediate revision of SOPs including SC, SI, TI, SOPs and A&DMM.
## 7.2 Review and Revision For SWO/DWO:-

## 7.2 Review and Revision For SWO/DWO:-

Review of SWO/DWO shall be made,
Annually SWO/DWO shall be reviewed by concerned SM/CDC and Section in-charges of concerned departments. Same shall be reviewed by concerned Manager/Assistant

## Introduction

Manager and shall be forwarded to nominated Dy HOD/Ops by 15 of January every year  through  concerned  Dy  HOD/  in-charge  of  Line/Depot.  If  the  review  brings  out necessity  of  any  change  the  same  shall  be  issued  as  Correction  Slip  of  concerned SWO/DWO by nominated Dy. HOD/Operation following process detailed at Para 6.

## Introduction

AM/MGR/SWO Cell shall issue a note regarding completion of five years (from date of issue of SWO/DWO) and advising review of respective SWO/DWO for revision, well in advance. SWO/DWO shall be reviewed by concerned SM/CDC and Section in-charges of  concerned departments  for  revision  of  respective  SWO/DWO.  Same  shall  be reviewed  by  concerned  Manager/Assistant  Manager  and  shall  be  forwarded  to nominated  Dy  HOD/Ops  through  concerned  Dy  HOD/  in-charge  of  Line/Depot  for revision  of  respective  SWO/DWO.  Nominated  Dy/HOD/Ops  shall  decide  whether revision of SWO/DWO is required or another correction slip may issue.
ii) SWO/DWO shall be revised on major changes/modification in system/technology or any other specific reasons which invite immediate revision.
## 8. SPECIAL MEASURE:

## 8. SPECIAL MEASURE:

Whenever it is required to merge issued Corrigendum of any SC/ SI/ SOP / Correction Slip of SWO/ DWO without any technical change/modification, steps mentioned in Para-5 and 6 shall not be required. Such type of merging of issued corrigendum with concerned JPO shall be done by the nominated Dy. HOD/Operations and after approval of authorised officer only, next revision of the JPO shall be issued. Review by nominated/concerned Dy. HODs and SSEC shall not be required in such type of revision of JPOs.
## 9. CUSTODIAN OF SAFETY RULES AND PROCEDURES:

## 9. CUSTODIAN OF SAFETY RULES AND PROCEDURES:

The following officers/offices shall maintain an up-to-date copy of all concerned JPOs and shall ensure their employees are fully conversant with their contents.
All HODs of O&M wing in DMRC.
ii) Dean/DMRA, Shastri Park.
iii) Authorised person at Train Depots & Depots Control Centers.
iv) Authorised person at All Operation Control Centers.
Authorised person at All Stations.
vi) Authorised person at All Crew Controls
vii) Authorised person at All TSS/RSS

text:
## 3.  PROCEDURE

3.1. The time table trial runs shall be done before CMRS inspection with proposed time table for revenue service prepared and provided by  OCM/OCC.
3.2. Necessary hardware modifications for signaling and telecom gears will be done at required locations before commencing of time tabled train trials.
3.3. On receipt of ISA Certificates, required signaling and telecom softwares will be installed at the earliest at all required locations i.e. line side, OCC, etc. Signaling (Project) and Telecom (Project) to update  the same  prior to time tabled trials so that below  mentioned observations can be duly noted. The updated installed softwares will remain uploaded in the system.
3.4. Rolling Stock to update the softwares and hardwares as required prior to time table trials.
3.5. Passengers shall be deboarded at existing terminal station during time table train trials and TO of the train & nominated staff shall ensure that no passenger remains on board the train moving towards the new section.
3.6. Train movement in new section will not be in passenger service. Revenue services will only be started after CMRS sanction.
3.7. All trains shall traverse irrespective of Red/ Blank aspect of Buffer Signals at the end of the existing  terminal  station  during  the  trials.  TC/OCC  may  authorize  TO,  on  exchange  of Private Number to pass buffer signal.
3.8. Facts to be monitored during trial run are-
(i) MMI/VDU functioning
(ii) Actual time of reversal at terminal station
(iii) Actual run time in new section
(iv) Proper functioning of sequence of trains
(v) DIF indication
(vi) PIDS indication
(vii) Announcement in trains
(viii)  Announcement at stations

text:
## 3.  ATO MODE :

3.1. The entire metro network of Airport Line including sidings and main line entry/depot exit signals is equipped for ATP/ATO operation.
3.2. ATO could be available if:
(i) Train is in ATP (CM) mode.
(ii) Cab Signal is available.
(iii) Train ID is available on HMI.
3.3. ATO mode shall be enabled only:
(i) If train is at station platform
(a)  Train is stationary at normal stopping point.
(b)  Train is in ATP (CM) mode.
(c)  Cab Signal is available.
(d)  Train ID is available on HMI.
(e)  Emergency brake not applied.
(f) TBC is at 'Coasting' position.
(ii) If train is running
(a)  Train is in ATP (CM) mode.
(b)  Cab Signal is available.
(c)  Train ID is available on HMI.
(d)  Emergency brake not applied.
(e)  TBC is at 'coasting' position.
(f)  AVD is not bypassed in this case, TO shall press AVD after specified time interval till next stop.

## 4. Responsibility of Signaling department :

(i) Signaling Department shall ensure to provide ATO fitness of train to PPIO who will further endorse the 'ATO Fit' on train log book along with the train fitness certificate as per extant procedure.
(ii)  In case any train whose ATO fitness has been withdrawal/not fit for ATO, signaling staff may put  off  MCB  43F03  of  problematic  cab  only,  so  train  could  not  run  in  ATO  mode inadvertently or otherwise and inform to PPIO/RSC.

## 5.  Procedure :

5.1. To drive a parked train on main line, Select the 'Forward' direction; release the Parking brake and wait for the 'Proceed' indication on the HMI Panel. Display of target distance and target speed is considered as 'Proceed' indication.
5.2. To start a train in ATO, the traction brake controller must be placed in the 'Coasting' position. All car doors must be closed and the same must be confirmed through indication available at TCMS.

metadata.source: 8.3 SC-08C (Rev-01) PO for Operating Train in ATO in  AEL.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.3 SC-08C (Rev-01) PO for Operating Train in ATO in  AEL_p2_11

text:
## Introduction

The cab doors must be closed. The Train Departure indicator must be available on HMI.

metadata.source: 8.3 SC-08C (Rev-01) PO for Operating Train in ATO in  AEL.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.3 SC-08C (Rev-01) PO for Operating Train in ATO in  AEL_p1_0

text:
## Introduction

5.3. Pressing on the 'ATO START' buttons (2 no.) simultaneously will start the trains which will run automatically to the next station, observing all signal checks, speed restrictions, braking requirements and other operating restrictions including restart from a signal stop.
5.4. If a Train does not start in ATO mode even after pressing the 'ATO Start button, the train may be moved in ATP/CM mode duly informing the OCC.TO shall select the 'ATO' mode of driving at the next station after performing the platform duty.
5.5. In case train stops after or before designated NSP in ATO mode, then following procedure shall be followed:
(i) If  a  train  in  ATO mode of operation appears to be about to overrun the correct stopping mark, the TO should intervene by operating the TBC to the emergency braking position, or operating either of the 'Mushroom' emergency plungers in the cab.
(ii) If Train overruns the correct stopping point, then the TO must check the extent of overrun and shall follow the procedure order for stopping of train at platforms.
(iii) If a Train stops short of its normal stooping point even in automatic mode:
(a) TO shall drive the train in ATP mode up to Normal Stopping point.
(b) In  case  target  speed  is  not  available,  TO  shall  drive  the  train  up  to  the  designated NSP in degraded mode, as per extant procedure.
(c) After aligning the Train with the designated NSP only, the TO shall 'open' and 'close' the saloon/PSD doors and proceed further as per extant procedure.

## 6. Skip Stopping

(i) Whenever skip station command is initiated by TC, TC shall suitably inform TO & SC.
(ii)  If the train is in ATO mode, the skip stop will be accomplished automatically.
(iii) If there are passengers on board, an announcement (PA) must be made to inform them that the train will not stop at the named station including the reason for this abnormal service. SC of the concerned station shall also make announcement at the station.

text: ## 7. Train Should not be driven in ATO Mode :

metadata.source: 8.3 SC-08C (Rev-01) PO for Operating Train in ATO in  AEL.pdf

## 7. Train Should not be driven in ATO Mode :

(i) If any safety bypass switch is operated.
(ii)  Whenever it is required to move train with reduced traction power.
(iii) Whenever  it  is  required  to  move  train  with  caution  or/and  with  speed  limit  which  is  not imposed through the system.
(iv) During bad weather of frequent slip/slide conditions

text:
## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 13 (Rev.-05)

PROCEDURE ORDER TO ENSURE PROPER FUNCTIONING OF AUDIO FREQUENCY TRACK CIRCUITS (AFTCs) ON LINE SEGMENTS, CROSSOVERS, POINT ZONES & SIDINGS, WHERE TRAINS ARE NORMALLY NOT MOVING DURING REVENUE HOURS

metadata.source: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs_p1_1

text:
## 1.  INTRODUCTION

This procedure order is meant to ensure the movement of nominated non-revenue train/s on a daily basis over such line segments / crossovers / point zones / sidings, where in the normal course of operations, the movement of trains is either very rare or practically non-existent.

metadata.source: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs_p2_3

text:
## 2.  SCOPE

This  procedure  is  applicable  to  Line-1  to  6  and  AEL.  This  procedure  shall  be  read  in conjunction  Metro  Railways  General  Rules-2020,  Safety  Circulars  and  other  instructions  in vogue.

metadata.source: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs_p2_5

text: ## 3.  IDENTIFICATION OF RARELY USED LINES, CROSSOVERS, POINT ZONES & SIDINGS:

metadata.source: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs_p2_6

text:
3.1  The  line  segments,  crossovers,  point  zones  &  sidings  over  which  the  train  movements during normal course are very rare or practically non-existent, are likely to become rusty and  thereby  cause  the  AFTCs  equipped  thereon  to  behave  erratically  when  any  rare movement over them is contemplated.
3.2  Such line segments, crossovers, point zones & sidings shall be carefully identified by S&T Wing on which rusty movement during non revenue hours is required to be carried out and communicated to concern OCM so that it can be included in the time table of the line.
3.3  S&T wing shall examine the identified line segments, crossovers and point zones & sidings half yearly and any change or addition may be communicated the OCM, who will arrange to incorporate that in time table.
MOVEMENT  OF  NOMINATED  NON-REVENUE  TRAINS  OVER  RARELY  USED  LINE SEGMENTS, CROSSOVERS, POINT ZONES & SIDINGS DURING NON-REVENUE HOURS:
4.1  OCC  shall  ensure  that  while  preparing  the  train  time  table  of  any  line,  the  route  of nominated train/s along with the day shall be clearly specified in the time table. Also during timetable preparation it shall be ensured that at least once in a day or alternate day rusty movement is carried out over such lines/crossovers/points zone as given by S&T wing.

metadata.source: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs_p2_8

text: 4.2  During non-revenue hours the movement of nominated trains shall be carried out as per day wise route mentioned in the time table of the line to ensure proper shunting of the rails by the moving trains, thereby ensuring fault-free & safe functioning of AFTCs, equipped thereon.

metadata.source: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs_p2_9

text:
## Introduction

4.3  The  movement  of  nominated  Train/s  for  rusty  movement  shall  take  place  in  specified route/section as mentioned in the concerned line train time table. TC/OCC shall inform TO about the specified route/section in which rusty movement is to be performed and take an acknowledgement  before  starting  from  every  interlocking  station  up  to  next  interlocking station.

metadata.source: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 13 SC-13 (Rev-05)  PO for  Functioning of AFTCs_p1_0

text:
## Introduction

4.4  In case if there is any change in the plan as mentioned in the Time Table, TC /OCC shall inform TO under exchange of Private Numbers and TC/OCC shall maintain the record of such deviation along with the reasons.
4.5  The  train  shall  move  in  ATP  mode  under  cab  signaling.  TO  shall  follow  all  speed restrictions enforced in the section/s and follow cab/fixed signals. In case cab signal is not available train shall be driven in degraded mode as per the extant procedure.
4.6  The movement towards sidings shall be carried up to the Stopping Reverse Marker Board only.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p2_1

text:
## 1. INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order deals with the train operation in ATO mode in Line-2 and specifies the precautions and delineates role and responsibility of all the concerned Staff.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p1_3

text:
## 2. SCOPE

This  Procedure  Order  shall  be  applicable  for  Line-2  and  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro Railways General Rules-2020, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p2_5

text: ## 3. ATO MODE

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p2_6

text:
3.1. The  entire  metro  network  of  line-2  including  sidings  and  main  line  entry/depot  exit  signals  is equipped for ATP/ATO operation.
3.2. ATO could be available if:
(i) Front Cab ATC is localized and active.
(ii)  Train should be in ATP (MCS) mode displaying target speed.
3.3. Train Operator should select the 'ATO' mode only
(i) If train is at station Platform
(a) At  designated  Normal  Stopping  Point  (NSP)  and  saloon  doors  are  closed  after performing platform duty.
(b) TBC is at 'B-Max' position.
(ii)  If Train is in siding
(a)  Siding exit signal is Green/Violet with Route.
(b)  TBC is at 'B-Max' position.
3.4. DMS (in  RS1  trains)  and  Automatic  Door  opening  Switch  (in  RS2  trains)  shall  always  be  in 'AUTO' / 'Normal' position respectively with the facility of manual opening of saloon doors in ATO and non-ATO mode. In ATO mode of driving, door will open automatically and in non-ATO mode,  TO  shall  press  the  door  open  push  button  to  open  the  saloon  doors  as  per  extant procedure.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p2_8

text:
3.5. If  a  delocalized  train  (with  both  cab  delocalized)  reaches  to  any  siding  and  its  front  cab  gets localized  through  STIB  (after  cab  reversal)  or  a  train  coming  from  depot  to  main  line  entry signal  and  its  front  cab  get  localized  through  STIB,  the  train  will  automatically  move  in  ATO without the need of pressing 'START' button as soon as train Operator selects 'ATO' mode and the exit signal becomes permissive. Hence if following conditions are fulfilled then train will be move automatically in ATO,
(a)  Train is in siding or at depot exit signal
(b)  Train was delocalized initially and then get localize at STIB
(c)  Signal is permissive
(d)  Mode selector is put to ATO.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p2_9

text: ## 4.  RESPONSIBILITY OF THE SIGNALING DEPARTMENT:

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p3_0

text:
## 4.  RESPONSIBILITY OF THE SIGNALING DEPARTMENT:

(i) Signaling Department shall ensure to provide ATO & Auto Door Opening fitness certificate of train to PPIO who will further endorse the 'ATO Fit' on train log book along with the train fitness certificate as per extant procedure.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p1_1

text:
## 4.  RESPONSIBILITY OF THE SIGNALING DEPARTMENT:

(ii)  In  case  any  train  whose  ATO  fitness  has  been  withdrawn/not  fit  for  ATO,  Signaling Department shall inform to PPIO about the same and also ensure that ATO relevant card shall be removed from both the cabs of the train so that train could not run in ATO mode inadvertently or otherwise.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p3_2

text: ## 5.  PROCEDURE:

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p3_3

text:
5.1. To start the train in ATO mode, put MS to 'ATO' position and Start Button should be pressed till the Departure Order or the Dwell time countdown counter is timed out from the DMI screen.
5.2. If train does not start in ATO mode even after pressing the 'Start Button', the train may be moved in ATP mode duly informing the OCC. TO shall select the 'ATO' mode of driving at the next station after performing the platform duty.
5.3. In case any fault appears in the train at station platform and troubleshooting is to be carried out, mode selector shall be kept in a mode other than ATO.
5.4. In  case  train  stops  after  or  before  designated  NSP  in  ATO,  then  following  procedure  shall  be followed.
(i) If a train stops short of its normal stopping point, even in automatic mode
(a) TO shall blow 'Horn'& Drive the Train in ATP Mode up to Normal Stopping Point.
(b) In  case  Target  Speed  is  not  available,  TO  shall  drive  the  Train  up  to  the  designated Normal Stopping Point in Degraded Mode, as per extant Procedure.
(c) After  aligning  the  Train  with  the  designated  Normal  Stopping  Point  only,  the  TO  shall 'Open' and 'Close' the Saloon Doors and proceed further as per extant Procedure.
(ii) If a train stops beyond its normal stopping point but with the doors still on the platform, the TO shall 'Open' and 'Close' the Saloon Doors and proceed further as per extant Procedure.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p3_5

text:
(ii) If a train stops beyond its normal stopping point but with the doors still on the platform, the TO shall 'Open' and 'Close' the Saloon Doors and proceed further as per extant Procedure.
(iii)  If a train stops beyond the end of the platform
(a) TO  shall  inform  OCC.  After  taking  Authorization  from  OCC,  TO  shall  make  an announcement to the Passengers that due to some Technical Problem, the Train shall proceed  to  the  next  Station  without  opening  the  Saloon  Doors  &  the  Passengers  are requested  to  get  down  at  the  next  Station  and  board  the  Returning  Train  from  other Platform. TO shall apologize for the inconvenience caused.
(b) If  the  Train  is  the  last  Train  of  the  Day, OCC shall prevent the following Non- revenue Train (if any) from approaching the Platform.
(c) Only  after  ensuring  that  the  following  Train  has  been  brought  to  a  'Stop'  and  the  TO instructed not to move without OCC's Permission, the TC shall then authorize the Train at the  Platform  to  reverse  until  all  Doors  are  at  the  Platform  and  in  the  Alignment corresponding to designated NSP. TO shall, thereafter 'Open' & 'Close' the Doors and proceed further as per extant Procedure.
Note: The procedure order for stopping of train at platforms where steel barriers are installed shall be dealt as per the extant procedure.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p3_6

text:
## Introduction

5.5. Whenever a 'Station skip' command is given by TC, he shall inform TO & SC about the same. TO in turn shall switch over to ATP mode from ATO mode in running condition and control the train speed  through  TBC/MC  and  shall  reduce  speed  of  the  train  to  20  km/h  when  passing  through station platform & blow horn intermittently till cab passes the designated stopping point during the period of revenue operation. TO & SC shall also make related announcement in the train & station respectively.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p1_0

text:
## Introduction

5.6. Whenever a 'Keep door close' indication is displayed on DMI screen in ATO mode, door shall not open automatically and the Train Operator shall seek instruction from OCC. In case if it is required to perform platform duty at station, TO shall open the saloon doors in ATP mode as per the extant procedure.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p4_1

text: ## 6.  TRAIN SHOULD NOT BE DRIVEN IN ATO MODE IF:

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p4_2

text:
## 6.  TRAIN SHOULD NOT BE DRIVEN IN ATO MODE IF:

6.1. If any safety switch is operated to cutout.
6.2. If  Traction  block  condition  is  bypassed  from  Traction  Block  page  available  on  TCMS  (in  RS2 trains only) for the possible movement of train.
6.3. Whenever it is required to move the train with reduced traction power.
6.4. Whenever  it  is  required  to  move  the  train  with  caution  or/and  with  speed  limit  which  is  not imposed through the system.
6.5. Switch over to ATP mode from ATO, even in running condition if below mention fault appears:
(a) In RS1 train: 'CI fault PWM signal fault from PWM generator' and wheel slip/slide fault on TIMS.
(b) In  RS2  train:  ATP  Motor/Brake  train  line  fault  switch  to  Manual  mode,  ATP  PWM Reference fault switch to manual mode or wheel slip/slide fault appears on TCMS.
Note: Train Operator shall twist the DSD before bringing MS to ATP in RS2 trains to avoid the EB application due to DSD released.

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p4_3

text: ## 7.  EMERGENCY BRAKE APPLICATION IN ATO:

metadata.source: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.1 SC-08A (Rev-02)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-2_p4_4

text:
## 7.  EMERGENCY BRAKE APPLICATION IN ATO:

7.1. While  driving  in  ATO  mode,  if  emergency  brakes  applied  in  the  train  and  train  stops  in  mid section  then  Train  will  start  automatically  in  ATO  mode  as  soon  as  emergency  brake  gets released.
7.2. Whenever EB application triggered by Train Operator (putting TBC to EB position, using EBPB or by using DBV), TO shall not release the EB till train comes to a complete stop and then train will  move  further  in  Non-ATO  mode  till  next  station  NSP.  Thereafter  the  ATO  mode  can  be resumed.
7.3. If emergency brake applies in the train and EB gets stuck then Train Operator shall troubleshoots the fault as per extant procedure and drive the train in Non ATO mode up to next station.

text: ## 3. ATO MODE:

metadata.source: 8.6 SC-8F (Rev-01)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-8.pdf

text:
## 3. ATO MODE:

3.1. The entire mainline of metro network of line-8 is equipped for ATP/ATO operation from BCGN to JPW (including sidings).
3.2. ATO could be available if:
(a)  Route is set
(b)  Train is in ATP Mode
(c)  Target speed is available
(d)  Train ID is available (Note: ATO would also be available without Train ID but in this case every time 'ATO departure' command to be given by TC/SC (CATS/LATS/VDU)  until  Train  ID  is  not  available.  Therefore,  in  this  case  Train operation will be done in ATP mode, till the time train ID is available)
3.3. ATO mode shall be enabled only:
(a)  If train is at zero speed
(b)  TBC is at 'B-Max' position
(c)  Target speed is available in ATP mode.
(d)  Mode selector in AUTO position and ATO is selected from DMI
(e)  EB reset performed by TO from DMI after selection of ATO mode (if required).
NOTE :- From main line siding or Station platform, if the train is properly berthed, then 'ATO Dep' button on DMI can be pressed to depart. If the train is not properly berthed, then the train needs to be moved in ATP mode for some distance for proper berthing and then stop and select ATO mode, reset EB from DMI (if required) and press 'ATO Dep' Button to depart.

metadata.source: 8.6 SC-8F (Rev-01)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-8.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.6 SC-8F (Rev-01)  PO for Operating Train in ATO in L-8_p2_7

text:

## SAFETY CIRCULAR-18A (Rev.-02)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR AXLE COUNTER RESET IN LINE-7 & 9

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This  Procedure Order  deals with  axle  counter  soft  reset  from  ATS  MMI/VDU  provided  in SCR/OCC/BCC in Line-7 and SCR/OCC in Line-9.

## 2. SCOPE

This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the EBI screen UIC Operator manual (ATS Operating Manual), Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 & its amendment, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue on Line - 7 & 9.
This document is applicable to Traffic Controller (TC), Depot Controller (DCC), Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO), Station Controller (SC) and Signaling staff.
BCC (Backup Control Centre) and UTO (Unattended Train Operation) is not applicable for Line-09 as these facilities are not provided on Line-9.
## 3. REQUIREMENT OF AXLE COUNTER SOFT RESET

## 3. REQUIREMENT OF AXLE COUNTER SOFT RESET

If track section is flashing due to, power failure/ cold start of axle counter section/ miscount or any other error, soft reset operation is required.
When Axle Counter soft reset is issued, the Axle Counter system will reset count on the evaluator but the state of the section will remain occupied until a valid check-in/check-out has been completed. The valid check-in/check-out will require a train sweep through the fault section and can be done at speed with any train type (not necessarily a CBTC train). In a point section, sweeping in only one direction of point is  sufficient.
## 4. AFFECT OF AXLE COUNTER FAILURE

## 4. AFFECT OF AXLE COUNTER FAILURE

4.1.  Axle counters (AX) are part of secondary train detection system, failure in axle counter section does not cause a failure in primary train detection systems (CBTC radio) but both systems are not fully independent. Failure of axle counter sections that immediately follows a signal and that are adjacent to fixed block type axle counter section will not allow normal train movement. Under such cases CBTC trains have to move in RM/FWD as per extant procedures.
4.2.  As the Green aspect of the concerned route of failed axle counter section will not come, NonCBTC train has to proceed as per procedure.
## 5. ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITY OF TRAFFIC CONTROLLER AND STATION CONTROLLER

## 5. ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITY OF TRAFFIC CONTROLLER AND STATION CONTROLLER

Axle  Counter  Soft  Reset  command  will  be  given  by  Traffic  Controller/  Station  Controller (having the control of interlocking). In order to give Axle Counter Reset command, TC & SC shall take the following steps: -
5.1.  TC shall inform the failure to SGC. SGC shall troubleshoot the failure and keep updated to TC/OCC. SGC shall advise to TC/OCC to get the axle counter reset with details of axle counter to be reset.
5.2.  TC shall count the number of operating trains between the adjacent stations of the failed axle counter section by monitoring ATS MMI/ Video Wall and verify train ID of trains. TC/SC shall place  platform  hold  for  train  running  in  UTO/ATO/ATP  in  station  preceding  failure.  Train running in degraded mode shall be stopped as per extant procedure.
5.3.  TC/SC shall obtain current locations of all trains present in the affected section corresponding to the failed track section on train radio and ensure that no train is present in the section between adjacent stations of the affected section.

## Introduction

5.4.  If track section failure is ascertained positively and no train is present in the adjacent stations of the affected track section, verified through above Para-5.2 to 5.4, TC/SC shall give Axle Counter Soft reset command.

5.5.  In  case  of  any  ambiguity  regarding  vacancy  of  failed  track  section,  TC  shall  ask  Station Controller to verify it physically. After physical verification that no train is present on failed track section and complete section between the adjacent stations is clear, the TC/OCC will give Axle Counter soft reset command.
5.6.  After  giving  AX  soft  reset  command,  a  train  running  through  (sweep)  the  fault  section  is required in order to clear occupancy of the sections mentioned below.
For Line-7 (UTO Mode of Operation):
TC/OCC shall instruct nearest available RA/ETO to board the first train running through the fault section as per extant procedure and to take charge of train.
If signal aspect is red, Make the Train to sweep in RM mode through the fault section. TC shall instruct TO/ETO/RA of the train, required for sweeping the section, to change the mode in RM. TC shall ensure from ATS terminal that the mode of the train is changed to RM and then give the permission to TO/ETO/RA for running the train in RM. On completion of sweeping of fault section, Train will get ATP. TC shall confirm the clearance of fault section to TO/ETO/RA and shall instruct TO/ETO/RA to change the mode selector position. Thus train shall be moved in ATP/ATO for rest of section till next station.
If signal aspect is violet, then, TC/OCC shall instruct RA/ETO of first train running through the  fault  section,  under  exchange  of  private  No,  to  move  in  ATP  Mode  with  speed restriction of 25 kmph.

If signal aspect is violet, then, TC/OCC shall instruct RA/ETO of first train running through the  fault  section,  under  exchange  of  private  No,  to  move  in  ATP  Mode  with  speed restriction of 25 kmph.
RA/ETO of the train shall remain vigilant in the fault section. In case any ambiguity/ obstruction is observed, S/he shall immediately stop the train short of any obstruction and report to TC/OCC.
UTO mode shall be resumed from next platform.
## b) For Line-9:

## b) For Line-9:

If signal aspect is red, Make the Train to sweep in RM mode through the fault section. TC shall instruct TO of the train, required for sweeping the section, to change the mode in RM. TC shall ensure from ATS terminal that the mode of the train is changed to RM and then give  the permission to  TO for  running  the  train  in  RM.  On  completion  of sweeping of fault section, Train will get ATP. Thus train shall be moved in ATP/ATO for rest of section till next station.
Confirmation of clearance of fault section shall be confirmed by TC to TO and shall instruct TO to change the mode selector position.
If signal aspect is violet, then train may sweep through the fault section in ATP/ATO mode.
## Note: -

## Note: -

Any  vehicle  with  wheel  diameter  less  than  300  mm  will  not  be  detected  by  Axle Counter.
In case of Soft reset of Axle counter section is not possible due to any technical reason; SGC shall inform signaling maintenance staff to attend the fault/failure.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR   15 (Rev.-02)

## STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE ORDER FOR DEALING WITH TERRORIST ATTACK IN DELHI METRO AND BOMB THREATS OR PRESENCE OF OTHER EXPLOSIVE DEVICES IN METRO PREMISES, TRAINS, STATIONS AND RIGHT OF WAY FOR ALL LINES.

## 1.   INTRODUCTION

This procedure describes the standard operating procedure order for dealing with terrorist attack in Delhi metro and bomb threats or presence of other explosive devices in metro premises, trains, stations and right of way for all lines.

## 2.    SCOPE

This procedure is applicable for all Lines. This SOP applies to all Metro Employees working on the main line and Depot, Security Staff and Metro Police Personnel.
This  procedure  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  Metro  Railway  General  Rule-2020  and  its  amendment, Accident and Disaster Management Manual, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
For UTO Mode of Operation:Wherever, Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, is to be read as Train Operator (TO) / Roving Attendant (RA) / Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
## 3. Standard  Procedure  order  to  deal  with  BOMB  THREATS  or  presence  of  other  EXPLOSIVE DEVICES in Metro premises, Trains, Stations and Right of Way
## 3.1 Objective

## 3.1 Objective

The purpose of this SOP is to enable the concerned staff to handle such threats in an orderly manner:
(i) Seeking prompt assistance from Metro Police, Delhi Police, Bomb Squad, Fire Services and other agencies.
(ii)  Alerting  Passengers  without  spreading  panic,  advising  them  to  keep  away  from  unattended baggage and promptly report such matter to Metro employees.
(iii) Conducting search operations with least impact on current revenue operation.
## 3.2 Information

## 3.2 Information

Employees receiving a Call with a bomb threat should attempt to obtain as much Information as the Caller will divulge, including the following:
(i) Location of the bomb,
(ii)  Scheduled time of detonation,
(iii) Description of the bomb,
(iv) Type of bomb,
(v)  Source of information, callers ID, phone no. etc.
Employees shall immediately report any bomb threat call that they receive to Metro Police through OCC. The Metro Police will be responsible for the overall coordination of bomb related incidents and establish liaison  with  Police Control  Room,  Bomb Squad, Dog Squad, Fire Department and military personnel responding to the scene.
The DCP/ACP Metro Police or  their  nominated  Representative  is  responsible  for  determining  if  any premises/ facilities are to be cordoned off or evacuated.
## 3.3 KNOWN LOCATION OF THE BOMB

## Introduction

(i) When the Bomb is reported on an identified train, TC shall instruct the TO to proceed to the nearest station.

In case of UTO train without RA/ETO, TC shall apply train hold at next Station by suitable commands. TO/IC shall make announcement in trains for detrainment of passenger from train.
(ii) TO/TC  shall  secure  train  with  the  doors  open  for  inspection  by  police,  fire  or  other  authorized personnel. TO/RA/ETO if available in train shall stand at a safe distance and Platform should be blocked.
(iii) TC will instruct TO of approaching the Station on the adjacent track to stop outside the station and await further instruction.
In case of UTO train, TC shall apply EB/suitable train stop command in train approaching the station on the adjacent track to stop outside the station
(iv) When the bomb is reported in an identified station and directions are given by command personnel to  evacuate,  the  SM/SC/ACC  shall  make  prescribed  public  address  announcements  instructing passengers to leave the Station.
(v) Depending on the reported bomb location in the station, TC may order TO approaching the station to stop. In case of UTO train, TC shall apply EB/suitable train stop command in train approaching the station.
Train already at the station shall be permitted to continue their journey, out of the station in normal service.
(vi) When the bomb is reported on the right-of-way, TC/OCC will order TO on both tracks approaching the reported bomb location to stop their trains prior to reaching the affected area and to await further instructions.
In  case  of  UTO  train,  TC  shall  apply  EB/suitable  train  stop  command  on  trains  approaching  the reported bomb location to stop the trains prior to reaching the affected area.
Other trains shall be regulated on the Station platform.

In  case  of  UTO  train,  TC  shall  apply  EB/suitable  train  stop  command  on  trains  approaching  the reported bomb location to stop the trains prior to reaching the affected area.
Other trains shall be regulated on the Station platform.
(vii) Employees discovering suspicious objects or packages will not touch, move or otherwise disturb the items pending examination and clearance by appropriate police, fire or military personnel.
(viii) TO within or approaching a reported bomb location, and employees equipped with portable radios that  are  in  the  vicinity  of  discovered  suspicious  packages/objects,  will  discontinue  all  radio transmission.
(ix) If  it  becomes  necessary  to  transmit  by  portable  radio,  a  minimum  distance  of  150  feet  must  be maintained between (the suspicious item arid the radio transmitter).
## 3.4 LOCATION OF THE BOMB UNKNOWN

## 3.4 LOCATION OF THE BOMB UNKNOWN

When a bomb threat is received and the location and time are not given, OCC will issue the following instructions:
(i) Station Managers along with Metro Police personnel and security staff shall inspect stations for any unattended objects or packages.
(ii)  Designated  employees  shall  inspect  all  trains  arriving  at  terminals  for  unattended  objects  or packages.
(iii) Train Operators shall observe the right-of-way for unusual objects or packages.

## Introduction

(iv) In case of UTO train, TC shall arrange RA/ETO to take charge of some trains as per extant procedure to check right of way for unusual objects or packages. TC, IC and TPC shall be vigilant on the right of way of track and inside the train through available CCTV.

## Introduction

(v)  Employees discovering suspicious objects or packages shall secure the immediate area around the item and notify the Metro Police.
## 3.5 OCC ACTIONS & INSTRUCTIONS

## 3.5 OCC ACTIONS & INSTRUCTIONS

(i) OCC will inform all the concerned Departments & Disaster Management Team.
(ii) Inform HOD/O, Dy. HOD/O who in turn will brief DO, DE and MD about the incident keeping them apprised of the progress.
(iii) OCC will initiate operating procedures to ease train congestion.
(iv) When  a  prolonged  delay  in  service  is  anticipated,  OCC  may  turn  trains  at  both  ends  of  the suspected area and initiate terminal adjustments to ease train congestion.
(v) OCC and Station Managers will announce likely delays requesting passengers not to panic.
(vi) When the bomb is found & defused or the threat  is nullified  by  Authorized  personnel  and  it  is determined that it is safe to operate, OCC will announce resumption of normal operation and restore normal train services notifying all concerned departments.
(vii) OCC in charge/ Dy. HOD/O shall inform HOD/Corporate Communication department the details of the incident for briefing the media as considered necessary.
## 4.   PROCEDURE ORDER FOR DEALING WITH TERRORIST ATTACK ON DELHI METRO

## 4.   PROCEDURE ORDER FOR DEALING WITH TERRORIST ATTACK ON DELHI METRO

4.1 On receipt of information of any Terrorist Act on Metro Trains, stations or on The right-of-way in the form of:
Bomb explosion
Fire
Release of poisonous gases /chemicals
Or any other act likely to affect safety of passengers
4.2 OCC will take prompt action to get the entire metro network cleared of all passengers by asking:
(i) TO of stationary trains to discharge passengers requesting them to leave the station quickly. In case of UTO stationary train, IC shall make suitable announcement in train to leave the station quickly.
(ii)  TO of trains on run will be instructed to stop at the first Station and discharge all passengers. TO to take safe position 50 mtrs. away from the train. In case of UTO train running in section, TC shall apply hold in train at next station. IC shall make suitable announcement in train to leave the station quickly.
(iii) Station Managers/Controllers, Security and Metro Police personnel will ensure that passengers are evacuated from station premises without delay.
(iv) The sale of tickets shall be stopped temporarily.
4.3 The  entire  Metro  network  shall  remain  closed  till  rescue  and  search  operations  have  been completed.
4.4 OCC and Station Staff will make regular announcements about the current status of the Metro system to keep all concerned updated about the situation.
4.5 Revenue operations shall only be started after ensuring that the system is fully safe & secure.
## Applicable for all Lines.

## 3. General

3.1. S&T department shall ensure provision of Normal Stopping Point (NSP) boards at platforms for normal & reverse direction movement and Stopping Reverse Marker Boards (SRMB) in the sidings & in section where turn back facility is provided according to train configuration for guidance of Train Operator to stop the train correctly especially in case of degraded mode of operation.
3.2. OHE shall be made available up to the buffer stop towards dead end after track and Electric Engine Stop board (if required) shall be placed at the buffer stop. During train movement, Train Operator shall not cross the Electric Engine Stop Board, Buffer Stop Signal or buffer stop whichever comes earlier in any case.
3.3. In neutral section, NSDD (neutral section detection device) shall ensure VCB/ LCB opening/ closing accordingly. Also, the related boards of neutral section shall be placed at suitable locations to ensure safe train operation.

## 4.1. LINE-1&2: -

At platforms, 6/8-car train shall stop at 8-car NSP in normal direction of travel.
In reverse direction (say, single line working or in case of turn back from front crossover), 8-car train shall stop at 8-car NSP and 6-car train shall stop at 6-car NSP such that the rear of the train aligns with the rear end of the platform.
In sidings & in section where turn back facility is provided, 8-car train shall stop at 8-car SRMB and 6-car train shall stop at 6-car SRMB.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 27 'B' (Rev-03)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR MOVEMENT OF TRAIN OPERATOR BETWEEN PLATFORM & SIDING FOR MANNING/UNMANNING A STABLED TRAIN
## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This  Procedure  Order  details  the  Responsibilities  of  the  concerned  Metro  Staff  and  the Methodology to be followed for the Movement of Train Operator between Platform & Siding for Manning / Unmanning a Stabled Train.
## 2.0 SCOPE

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure is applicable for all lines. This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
For UTO mode of Train Operation: wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/ Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
## 3.0 GENERAL:

## 3.0 GENERAL:

3.1 OCC shall advise the Auxiliary System Controller for Tunnel Section or Station Controller for Elevated Section, who shall further arrange to switch 'ON/OFF' the Lights where available for the Safe Movement of Train Operator to/from the Siding.
3.2 Civil Department shall ensure that the Track Area / Siding Area are Safe for walking.
3.3 OCC shall ensure precautions are put in place during movement of Train Operator.
3.4 Train  Operator  shall  be  responsible  for  his/her  own  Safety  during  the  Movement  on  the 'Right-of-Way'.
3.5 Train  Operator  shall  look  in  each  direction  before  entering  on  and  standing  close  to  the Tracks.
3.6 Train  Operator  shall  not  walk,  stand,  step  or  sit  on  Running  Rails,  Guard  Rails,  Points  & Crossings, Cover Boards, Interlocking Apparatus and other Wayside Equipments.
3.7 Train Operator shall use the Walkways, wherever possible.
## 4.0 PROCEDURE FOR MANNING A STABLED TRAIN IN SIDING:

## 4.0 PROCEDURE FOR MANNING A STABLED TRAIN IN SIDING:

4.1 Train  Operator  shall report to the  Station  Controller,  when  detailed  by  the  Crew  Control to take the Charge of the Stabled Train.
4.2 Station  Controller  shall  confirm  from  OCC  for  the  designated  Platform,  from  which  the Movement is to be carried out.
4.3 Station  Controller  shall  carry  the  Track  Access  Gate  Key  &  Tetra  Set  and  accompany  the Train  Operator  who  shall  carry  with  him/her  the  Train  Logbook,  MASCON  Key,  PSL  Key (where applicable), Cab Door Key and the Tetra Hand Set, as applicable to the designated Platform. The Train Operator shall then inform OCC that he/she is ready to move for manning the Stabled Train in the Siding.
4.4 OCC shall hold trains as required and block concerned route as applicable so that no train can enter onto the track where movement of Train Operator from the Platform to Siding is to be carried out and regulate the following Trains in DN or UP Line accordingly to facilitate the Safe Movement of the Train Operator to the Siding.

## Introduction

4.5 OCC  shall  permit  Station  Controller  to  unlock  the  Track  Access  Gate  of  the  designated Platform and then authorize the Train Operator to move to the Siding for manning the Stabled Train.

## Introduction

4.6 After  getting  Permission  of  the  OCC,  Train  Operator  shall  move  to  the  Siding  from  the designated Platform via the Track/Walkway and Station Controller shall then lock the Track Access Gate.
4.7 OCC  shall  ensure  that  no  Point  Movement  takes  place  during  the  Movement  of  Train Operator from Platform to the Siding.
4.8 The Train Operator shall look after his/her own Safety and after reaching a Safe Zone, he/she shall confirm his/her arrival to OCC on Tetra.
4.9 OCC  shall  then  resume  Normal  Train  Service  by  unblocking  concerned  route/removing protections imposed as applicable.
## 5.0 PROCEDURE FOR UN-MANNING A STABLED TRAIN IN SIDING:

5.1 After stabling the Train in the Siding as per extant Procedure, the Train Operator shall collect MASCON Key, Square Key, , PSL Key (where applicable), Cab Door Key, Train Logbook and Tetra Handset and shall inform to OCC that he/she is ready to move to the Platform from the Siding.
5.2 OCC shall nominate the Platform for the Train Operator to move and confirm the same to the Train Operator & Station Controller.
5.3 OCC shall advise the Station Controller of the concerned Station to reach at the designated Platform.
5.4 Station Controller shall carry the Track Access Gate Key & Tetra Set and shall reach at the designated Platform.
5.5 OCC shall hold Trains as required and block concerned route as applicable so that no Train can enter onto the track where Movement of Train Operator from the Siding to Platform is to be carried out and regulate the following Trains in DN or UP Line accordingly to facilitate Safe Movement of Train Operator to the designated Platform.
5.6 OCC  shall  permit  the  Station  Controller  to  unlock  the  Track  Access  Gate  of  designated Platform and then authorize the Train Operator to move to the designated Platform from the Siding.
5.7 After getting Permission of the OCC, the Train Operator shall move to the Platform via Track / Walkway.
5.8 OCC  shall  ensure  that  no  Point  Movement  takes  place  during  the  Movement  of  Train Operator from Siding to the Platform.
5.9 The Train Operator shall  look  after  his/her  own  Safety  &  upon  reaching  to  the  designated Platform, he/she shall confirm his/her arrival to OCC on Tetra & SC shall then lock the Track Access Gate.

5.9 The Train Operator shall  look  after  his/her  own  Safety  &  upon  reaching  to  the  designated Platform, he/she shall confirm his/her arrival to OCC on Tetra & SC shall then lock the Track Access Gate.
5.10  OCC  shall  then  resume  Normal  Train  Service  by  unblocking  concerned  route/removing protections imposed as applicable.
## 6.0 ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINES

## 6.0 ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINES

6.1 In case of any failure where in train can't be inducted in UTO mode then TO/RA/ETO shall be sent to siding to take charge of the train.
## 6.2  PROCEDURE FOR MANNING A STABLED TRAIN IN SIDING.

## 6.2  PROCEDURE FOR MANNING A STABLED TRAIN IN SIDING.

(i) Traffic controller shall inform the TO/RA/ETO available on the station.

## Introduction

(ii) Traffic controller shall apply maintenance block (wherever applicable) and block all possible routes where train is stalled and stop train from available ATS commands, before permitting TO/RA/ETO to access the track for boarding the train. Simultaneously, TC/OCC shall inform SC to reach at platform for opening the Platform End Door (PED)/Manual Secondary Door (MSD) so that TO/RA/ETO can access the track.

## Introduction

(iii) Train  movement  of  both  lines  shall  be  stopped  before  movement  of  TO/RA/ETO  from platform to siding.
(iv) Platform  End  Door  (PED)/Manual  Secondary  Door  (MSD)  shall  be  opened  by  SC  for TO/RA/ETO to access the track after taking permission from TC/OCC.
(v) OCC shall ensure that no point movement takes place during the movement of TO/RA/ETO from platform to siding.
(vi) TO/RA/ETO after getting confirmation from SC, shall proceed towards the stabled train in siding  through  Platform  End  Door  (PED)  /Manual  Secondary  Door  (MSD).  After  that  SC shall close the Platform End Door (PED) /Manual Secondary Door (MSD) and ensure the status of ADCL on the PSL panel.
(vii) TO/RA/ETO shall open EAD (Emergency Access Device) of saloon door to board the train and TO/RA/ETO shall confirm TC/OCC regarding boarding in train.
(viii) TC/OCC shall then resume normal train service by unblocking concerned route/removing protection imposed as applicable.
(ix) TO/RA/ETO  shall  further  follow  instructions  of  OCC  and  if  required  shall  take  over  the charge of the train and troubleshoot as per extant procedure.
## 6.3  PROCEDURE FOR UN-MANNING A STABLED TRAIN IN SIDING.

(i) TO/RA/ETO  shall  confirm  from  TC/OCC  regarding  train  mode  and  position  of  the  mode selector  of  both  cab.  TO/RA/ETO  shall  collect  mascon  key,  square  key,  PSL  Key  (if applicable) tetra handset, other belongings and inform to TC/OCC that he is ready to move to platform from the siding.
(ii) TC/OCC shall nominate the platform for the TO/RA/ETO to move and confirm the same to the TO/RA/ETO & concerned SC.
(iii) TC/OCC shall ensure that whenever there is any movement of TO/RA/ETO for unmanning train in siding, all possible route from/to the siding where train is stabled, shall be blocked and  apply  maintenance  block  (wherever  applicable)  and  stop  train  from  available  ATS commands  before  authorising  any  such  movement  of  TO/RA/ETO    and  TC/OCC  shall confirm sleep/Aux off status of train from TO/RA/ETO .
(iv) Train movement of both lines shall be stopped before movement of TO/RA/ETO from siding to platform.
(v) TC/OCC  shall  ensure  that  no  point  movement  takes  place  during  the  movement  of TO/RA/ETO from Siding to the Platform.
(vi) After  getting  permission  of  the  OCC,  the  TO/RA/ETO  shall  operate the  EED  (Emergency egress device) of the saloon door to de-board the train and after closing the saloon  door he/she shall move to the platform.

(vii) TO/RA/ETO  shall  open  the  Platform  End  Door  (PED)  /Manual  Secondary  Door  (MSD)to enter platform and upon reaching to the designated Platform, TO/RAETO shall then close the  PED/MSD  and  ensure  The  status  of  ADCL  on  PSL  panel.  TO/RAETO  shall  confirm his/her arrival to TC/OCC on Tetra.
(viii) OCC  shall  then  resume  normal  train  service  by  unblocking  concerned  route/removing protections imposed from system (as applicable).

text:
## 3. During Stabling of Trains In The Depots

3.1. The Train Operator shall stable the Train at the Location intimated by the Depot Controller, as per the Procedure in vogue.
3.2. The Train Operator shall shut down the train as per instructions and properly fill up & sign the Log Book.
3.3. The Train Operator shall then leave the Train and submit the Log Book, Mascon key, Square Key, Swipe Card, as applicable and Tetra Set at the DCC and sign off.
3.4. It shall be the duty of the PPIO to collect the Log Books from the Depot Controller.
3.5. The PPIO shall look at the Log Books and get the bookings attended by the maintenance staff (RS and S&T) and get their signatures along with name and designation at the relevant place in the Log Books.

metadata.chunk_id: 35. SC 35 (Rev-01)  PO on Fitness of trains_p2_6

text:
## 4. During Induction of Trains from the Depots

4.1. After ensuring that the Maintenance staff as well as Housekeeping Staff have left the train and the doors of the train are closed, the Rolling Stock Supervisor in the PPIO shall endorse the fitness of the trains on the concerned Log Books, endorse the consist of the train (whether 6car  or  4-car  etc.)  at  the  prescribed  place  on  the  Log  Books  and  submit  them  to  the  Depot Controller.
4.2. The PPIO shall also submit a signed list of all the trains that have been given fitness along with their stabling locations to the DC at least 60 minutes prior to pilot train departure.
4.3. The Depot Controller shall confirm the validity of the fitness of the train from the Log Book and hand over the Log Book along with the Keys, Swipe Card and Tetra Set to the nominated Train Operator.
4.4. The Train Operator shall look at the fitness endorsed in the Log Book and if found valid, shall collect the Log Book and move for Train Preparation. In case the fitness is absent or invalid, the Train Operator shall not take charge of the train and inform the DC accordingly.
4.5. The  Train  Operator  shall  also  formally  acknowledge  that  he/she  has  been  told  about  the location of the stabling of the train by signing on the sign on register.
4.6. The Train Operator shall perform the pre-departure checks in depot as per procedure in vogue and if found fit, shall sign on the Log Book. If any problem is experienced, he/she shall report to DCC, who shall act as per extant instructions and practice.

This  Procedure Order covers the Action to be taken, if the Train undershoots or overshoots the Normal Stopping Point (NSP) at a Platform, where Steel Barriers are installed on Line-1, 2 3 & 4, the objective being to ensure the Safety & Convenience of the Passengers while Boarding & Deboarding the Train.

## 3.  GENERAL:

3.1. Steel Barriers have been installed at crowded platforms to avoid the occurrence of any incident of passengers falling on the track.
3.2. The barriers help in streamlining the de-boarding / boarding of Passengers from the Train.
3.3. Train Operators shall be attentive, while berthing the Train on the Platforms so as to stop the Train  in  perfect  Alignment  at  the  designated  Normal  Stopping  Point  (NSP),  so  that  all  the Saloon Doors of Train lie in between the consecutive Steel Barriers.

## 4.1.1. Case '1': Train Undershoots the NSP:

(i) TO shall blow 'Horn' & Drive the Train in ATP Mode up to Normal Stopping Point.
(ii) In  case Target Speed is not available, TO shall drive the Train up to the designated Normal Stopping Point in Degraded Mode, as per extant Procedure.
(iii)  After aligning the Train with the designated Normal Stopping Point only, the TO shall 'Open' and 'Close' the Saloon Doors and proceed further as per extant Procedure.

## 4.1.2.  Case 2: Train Overshoots the NSP and stops beyond the 8-Car NSP:

(i) The TO shall inform the OCC. After taking Authorization from OCC, TO shall make an announcement to the Passengers that due to some Technical Problem, the Train shall proceed to the next Station without opening the Saloon Doors & the Passengers are requested to get down at the next Station and board the Returning Train from other Platform. TO shall apologize for the inconvenience caused.
(ii) If the Train is the last Train of the Revenue Services, OCC shall prevent the following Non-revenue Train (if any) from approaching the Platform.
(iii)  Only after  ensuring  that  the  following  Train  (if  there  is  any)  has  been  brought  to  a 'Stop' and the TO instructed not to move without OCC's Permission, the TC shall then

## 4.2.1. Case '1': Train Undershoots the designated NSP:

(i) TO shall blow 'Horn' & Drive the Train in ATP Mode up to the designated NSP.
(ii) In  case Target Speed is not available, TO shall drive the Train up to the designated Normal Stopping Point in Degraded Mode, as per extant Procedure.
(iii)  After aligning the Train with the designated Normal Stopping Point only, the TO shall 'Open' and 'Close' the Saloon Doors and proceed further as per extant Procedure.

text: ## 4.2.2.  Case 2: 6 Car Train Overshoots the Designated 6 car NSP but stops before the 8Car NSP:

text:
## 4.2.2.  Case 2: 6 Car Train Overshoots the Designated 6 car NSP but stops before the 8Car NSP:

(i) TO  shall  open  the  Platform  Side  Cab  Door,  Step  Out  and  adjudge  whether  the Passengers can conveniently de-board & board, with the infringement, caused due to overshooting of the Train, beyond the designated NSP.
(ii) If  the  Visual  Verification  is  in  affirmative,  the  TO  shall  'Open'  and  'Close'  the  Saloon Doors and proceed further as per extant Procedure.
(iii)  If  the  Visual  Verification  of  the  TO  indicates  that  it  shall  not  be  convenient  for  the Passengers to de-board & board, he / she shall follow the following Guidelines:
(a)  TO shall blow 'Horn' & Drive the Train in ATP Mode or in Degraded Mode as per extant Procedure (if target speed is not available) up to 8-Car NSP.
(b)  Inform the OCC of the Action taken by him/her.
(c) After  aligning  the  Train  with  Next  8  Car  NSP,  the  TO  shall  'Open'  &  'Close'  the Saloon Doors and proceed further as per extant Procedure.
4.2.3.  Case 3: In case 6/8 car train overshoots the 8 car NSP, Para 4.1.2 shall be followed.

## 3. GENERAL

3.1.  Automatic turn back is used only on ATO fit train to  automatically drive the train from the arrival track to the departure track of a terminal station, via the turn back track from siding where the heading direction of the train is changed.

text: ## 4.  Pre-Conditions for Activating ATB mode : -

metadata.source: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back_p2_7

text:
## 4.  Pre-Conditions for Activating ATB mode : -

(i) The train is stationary at a platform NSP at the terminal station.
(ii) Train  is  in  Automatic  Mode  (ATO)  and  all  conditions  for  ATO  are fulfilled.
(iii) Concerned  'Reversal  Cycle'  is  set  by  TC/OCC  in  CATS  for  ATB.  If ATS  control is at local level, SC  shall set appropriate cycle in consultation with TC.

text: ## 5.  Normal operation in ATB mode :-

metadata.source: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back_p3_1

text: ## 5.1. At Arrival Platform :-

metadata.source: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back_p3_2

text:
(i)  When required  reversal  cycle  has  been  set  at  terminal  station  and train  stop  at  terminal  platform  NSP,  the  Automatic  Train  Control (ATC) initiates to  start  flashing  the  ATB  indication  on  the  DMI.  This indication will continue to flash endlessly (no time-out) till  TO acknowledges.
(ii)  Once the TO acknowledge the ATB indication flashing on DMI, ATC checks that the conditions for entering the ATB mode are fulfilled.
(iii)  If  the  conditions  for  ATB  operation  are  met,  a  message  will  get displayed  on  the  DMI  requesting  the  train  operator  to  "remove  cab key" (Mascon Key).
(iv)  The  train  operator  moves  the  Mode  Selector  to  "Off'  position  and removes  the  Mascon  Key  within  30  seconds  of  display  of  request message.
(v)  After this, the ATB mode is enabled and the ATB indication on  DMI becomes steady.
(vi)  After  activation  of  departure  button  (It  gets  lit),  train  operator  shall push the departure button (at Operating Panel-1).
(vii)  The departure button now starts flashing.

metadata.source: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back_p3_4

text:
(vi)  After  activation  of  departure  button  (It  gets  lit),  train  operator  shall push the departure button (at Operating Panel-1).
(vii)  The departure button now starts flashing.
(viii)  Normally, TO will remain inside the train. In this case TO must open and  close  the  cab  side  door  to initialize  Automatic  Turn  back Operation. The train will not start in ATB until and unless TO opens and then closes the cab side door. Subsequently when the train starts moving  in ATB,  S/he  will change  the  cab  after collecting his belongings.
(ix)  If Train Operator has been instructed to exit from the cab, S/he shall open the Cab Side door, and exit from the train after collecting all his belongings. Thereafter, TO shall close the Cab Side door and keep himself at a safe distance, following which the train departs automatically to the siding in ATB mode.
(x)  TO  will  activate  the  front  cab  after  reaching  at  departure  platform NSP  or  in  case  where  train  in  ATB  is  unmanned  relieving  TO  will activate the front cab.

metadata.source: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back_p3_5

text: ## 5.2. At Departure Platform :-

metadata.source: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back_p3_6

text:
## 5.2. At Departure Platform :-

(i)  A normal precision stop is performed by ATC at the departure track of the terminal station.
(ii)  At the terminal station ATB mode is terminated by information, "Stop and no ATB".
(iii)  When the train stops at the terminal station platform after completing the reversal,  ATC  remains  in  ATB  mode  and  supervise  the  target  in  stop until the TO inserts the Mascon key. When the TO inserts the Mascon key,  the  operation  mode  is  changed  according  to  signalling  condition and the target restriction is changed accordingly.

metadata.source: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 8.4 SC-8D (Rev-01)  PO for Automatic Turn Back_p3_7

(iv)  Departing  train  operator  shall  board  the  cab  and  activate  the  cab  and move the train as per extant procedure.

text:
Failure  Management  during  ATB  Interruption/Termination  : Beside    the schedule pattern of ATB, the ATB mode may terminate when
(i)  The TO takes control of train by means of the driver's controller, e.g. Emergency brake handle.
(ii)  The ATP interferes and stops the train by applying brake.
(iii)  The ATC is out of order.
(iv)  Automatic train Operation is not allowed.
6.1. When ATB mode is interrupted/ terminated, an irrevocable emergency brake will  be  applied  by  ATP  system.  Whenever  train  stops  at  any  location  in  turn back tracks, the train will have to be rescued by Train operator.
6.2. TC shall advise Train Operator to take over the control of train and carry out manual turnback.
6.3. If TO is not already present in the driving cab, TC shall inform crew control to  keep TO ready for rescue of train. TC shall cancel the  route.  He shall then wait till the cancelation of approach lock. After cancelation of route, TC shall block the route before authorizing TO, to go the stalled train in siding. If route cannot be cancelled, TC shall try to block the movement of stalled train by giving "Block TC" command on appropriate track circuit.
6.4. The train operator shall board the train and take control of the train by extant cab activation process.
6.5. Train  shall  be  moved  in  available  mode  of  train  operation  as  per  extant procedure.
Suspension  of  ATB:In  case  of  following  fault  sand/or  conditions,  ATB operation will be suspended.

text:
Suspension  of  ATB:In  case  of  following  fault  sand/or  conditions,  ATB operation will be suspended.
7.1. If  ATB  is  interrupted  in  two  consecutive  trains,  TC  shall  decide  to  stop reversal  in  ATB  mode  and  start  the  manual  turn  back.  TC  shall  inform Signaling  controller  for  rectification.  TC  shall  also  inform  concerned  Crew Controls and TOs about the stoppage of ATB mode. ATB will be resumed after  fault  rectification  and  same  will  be  conveyed  to  Crew  Control/Train Operators.
7.2. Trains  will  not  be  operated  in  ATB  during  bad  weather  as  conditions defined in Train Operator's instructions.
7.3. Whenever any excessive rush/unruly passengers' behavior at the departure    platform    is   noticed by SC or is reported to him by any other person, the Station Controller should verify it physically and subsequently inform TC who may suspend ATB operation.
7.4. While  approaching  the  departure  platform,  Train  Operator  (whenever available inleading cab) notices excessive rush/unruly passengers' behavior, the train shall be stopped immediately by application of EB and inform TC who may suspend ATB operation.
7.5. In case of any obstruction/person is reported in siding by Train Operator or by any other staff/person.
