## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 21A (Rev-00)
## PROCEDURE FOR OBSERVING RAIL FRACTURES & WELD FAILURES THROUGH RAIL CHECK SYSTEM ON LINE-7&8
## 1. INTRODUCTION: -

## 1. INTRODUCTION: -

1.1 This instruction details the steps for automatic Inspection of track structure to detect 'Broken rails', 'Running edge defects', 'surface detects' etc. through rail check system on Line-7&8 and actions thereto by the concerned officials.

## 1. INTRODUCTION: -

1.2 The Rail Check System (RCS) is fitted in Train Set #705 (on Line-07) and TS #801 (on Line08).
1.3 Separate Rail  Check  System (RCS) workstation for Line-7  and  8 is provided  at  06 th   floor OCC/Metro Bhawan/II.
1.4 RCS  workstation  is  manned  and  monitored  by  the  Civil  Controller  for  defects  /  alarms observation.
1.5 RCS monitoring data is saved for last three (03) days in hard disk provided in RCS system and same can be obtained from RS department as per extant procedure.
## 2. SCOPE: -

## 2. SCOPE: -

2.1 This Procedure order is applicable to Line-7 & 8.
2.2 This Procedure order shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules 2020 and its amendments and other relevant instructions in vogue.
## 3. PROCEDURE FOR RAIL CHECK SYSTEM (RCS) WORKING &OBSERVATION: -

## 3. PROCEDURE FOR RAIL CHECK SYSTEM (RCS) WORKING &OBSERVATION: -

3.1 Rail check system (RCS) performs automatic Inspection of track structure to detect 'Broken rails', 'Running edge defects', 'surface detects' etc.
3.2 The  track  is  monitored  by  the  onboard  system  for  the  following  defects  and  in  case  of detection of defects, alarms for the same are sent to RCS workstation at OCC on real time basis.

### 3. PROCEDURE FOR RAIL CHECK SYSTEM (RCS) WORKING &OBSERVATION: -

|   S.N. | Type of defects    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|      1 | Rail head anomaly  | Dark spots of a certain size or areas of dark spots along the rail head.                                                                                                                                              |
|      2 | Rail edge anomaly  | Dark spots of a certain size or areas of dark spots along the rail edge.                                                                                                                                              |
|      3 | Rail discontinuity | A dark strip across the rail head, perpendicular to the rail. Reason can be a joint or a rail break.                                                                                                                  |
|      4 | Wheel burn         | An imprint across the complete rail head which appears on both rails.                                                                                                                                                 |
|      5 | Corrugation        | A sequence of light cress and dark holes in driving direction.                                                                                                                                                        |
|      6 | Missing fastener   | There has to be a fastening element that covers a part of the rail foot at the place where a sleeper is below the rail. If nothing covers the rail foot in the area of a sleeper this is rated as a missing fastener. |

## Introduction

3.3 The surface of the track is recorded using digital line cameras installed onboard, the images taken  by  the  camera  form  an  endless  image  of  the  track.  This  stream  of  images  is  then continuously processed in real-time to detect defects in the track.

3.4 The  alarm  reported  at  RCS  workstation  at  OCC  shall  provide  the  attributes  for  each defect/alarm  vis-a-vis.  type  of  defect,  severity,  date  &  time,  route  name,  defect  width  & defect length etc.
3.5 When audio and visual alarm is generated at work station in OCC/MB/II, the Civil Controller shall take a note of it and inform immediately through Telephone and Email to line P- Way staff (JE/In-charge) for physical check.
3.6 Civil Controller should check the 'urgent' cases promptly and if the failure seems to be of genuine or emergency nature, suitable decision of imposition of TSR/single line working etc. shall be advised to Chief Controller till the P-way department confirm further action.
3.7 As per feedback received from Line staff, Civil Controller shall advise to Chief Controller in writing regarding change in Train Operation plan(e.g. TSR imposition, Single Line Working, Block  requirements  etc.)  ,  if  required.  Civil  Controller  shall  also  inform  to  all  concerned regarding failure and to take remedial action.
3.8 Chief Controller shall inform Assistant Chief Controller and Traffic Controller for implementing the advice of Civil Controller as per Para-3.6 or 3.7 of this SOP.
3.9 A  register  to  be  maintained  and  filled  on  daily  basis  by  the  Civil  Controller  regarding  all urgent cases detected by the system with date and time of detection which invoke TSR or other repercussions.

3.9 A  register  to  be  maintained  and  filled  on  daily  basis  by  the  Civil  Controller  regarding  all urgent cases detected by the system with date and time of detection which invoke TSR or other repercussions.
3.10 Concerned  PPIO  shall  try  to  induct  TS  #705  (on  Line-07)  and  TS  #801  (on  Line-08)  to maximum extent possible preferably in bigger loop of time table.
3.11 During  Train  set  TS  #705  (on  Line-07)  and  TS  #801  (on  Line-08)  under  maintenance beyond 72 hours, Civil controller in consultation with Chief Controller shall ensure manned pilot train movement as per Para-4.0 of SC-04.
## 4.  PROCEDURE FOR DOWLODING VIDEO FROM RAIL CHECK SYSTEM: -

## 4.  PROCEDURE FOR DOWLODING VIDEO FROM RAIL CHECK SYSTEM: -

4.1 Civil or any other official shall fill the 'Annexure-A' and submit to Civil Controller.
4.2 Civil Controller shall further submit it to Rolling Stock Controller.
4.3 Rolling  Stock  Controller  shall  arrange  the  data  files  through  PPIO  and  submit  to  Civil Controller.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 21 (Rev.-06)
## PROCEDURE FOR ATTENDING RAIL FRACTURES & WELD FAILURES DURING TRAFFIC HOURS

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order covers the Methodology of Attending & Repairing the Rail Fractures & Weld Failures during Traffic Hours.

## 2.0 SCOPE

2.1 This Procedure Order is applicable to all Lines.
2.2 This  procedure  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  Metro  Railway  General  Rule-2020,  Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
2.3 For UTO Mode of Operation: Wherever, Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, is to be read as Train Operator (TO) / Roving Attendant (RA) / Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
2.4 Wherever Traction Power controller (TPC) is mentioned, is to be read as Civil Controller at OCC/MB/II.
## 3.0 PROCEDURE

(i) On getting Information from the  Civil  Controller  at  OCC/MB/II /  Chief  Controller  /  any other controller in OCC or any other available means regarding the Rail Fracture / Weld Failure,  the  concerned  TC  shall  immediately  suspend  traffic  and  upraise  to  Civil Controller at OCC/MB/II.
(ii) Civil  Controller  at  OCC/MB/II  shall  report  the  Incident  to  SSE  /  SE  /ASE/  P.  Way, Mgr./AM/ P. Way, Dy HOD / P.Way  duly conveying the affected Line and the Location of the Fracture / Failure with reference to the nearest OHE Mast No.
(iii)  Concerned Chief Controller / Traffic Controller shall inform Signalling System Controller, Dy. HOD/O, Dy. HOD /TO of the affected line and HOD/O.
(iv)  Signalling Controller shall further inform Mgr./AM/S&T of affected line regarding the rail fracture/weld failure. Mgr./AM/S&T shall then take necessary action with regard to the failure.
3.2 TPC  shall  make  all  necessary  Arrangement  to  ensure  that  the  Fractured  Rails  are jumpered by the concerned Staff at the earliest possible.
3.3 The supervisor on Duty both in P.Way office and Signaling Offices shall proceed to the Site immediately along with their respective teams with equipments.

3.3 The supervisor on Duty both in P.Way office and Signaling Offices shall proceed to the Site immediately along with their respective teams with equipments.
3.4 The  emergency  equipments  shall  be  available  at  the  nearest  Station/P.Way  Line Store/Depot. Signaling and P.Way wings shall ensure availability of emergency equipments  including  jumper/tool  box.  At  Station  (where  provided),  the  box  containing Emergency equipments shall be kept in ASS Room. The key of the box shall be kept in Emergency  Key  Hive  of  SCR  and  shall  be  issued  to  P.Way  Staff  for  attending  Rail Fracture/Weld Failures.
3.5 List of Equipments available in the Emergency Rail Fracture Kit is given in the following Table:

### Introduction

|   S. No. | Item Description                                                                | Quantity (Nos.)   |
|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
|       1. | Double ended fish bolt spanner (39-41)mm                                        | 01                |
|       2. | Deep Socket size 16/17mm with T Handle & extension bar                          | 02                |
|       3. | Crow Bars/Tommy Bar                                                             | 01                |
|       4. | Joggle Fish Plates for weld fracture                                            | 02 (01 Pair)      |
|       5. | One meter/610 mmlong fish plate for rail fracture                               | 02 (01 Pair)      |
|       6. | C- Clamp ( for fracture in Ballasted section)                                   | 02 (01 Pair)      |
|       7. | Special Clamps (for fracture in Ballast Less Track)                             | 03                |
|       8. | Hand Flag Red                                                                   | 02                |
|       9. | Hand Flag Green                                                                 | 01                |
|      10. | Rail Closures ( size 12mm to 30mm)                                              | 05                |
|      11. | Keying Hammer ( Ballasted Track)                                                | 01                |
|      12. | Deep Socket 39-41mm with T- Handle and Extension Rod (for Ballast less section) | 01                |
|      13. | Rail Jumper (2m Long)                                                           | 02                |
|      14. | Insulated Hand Gloves                                                           | 02 set, (04 Nos)  |

## Introduction

3.6 The  P.  Way  and  Signaling  Team  shall  proceed  to  the  Station,  nearest  to Rail Fracture/Weld  Failure  Location  either  by  Emergency  Vehicle  or  by  any  other  quickest mode of transport. PTW shall be taken by EPIC of concerned department as per extant procedure.

3.7 During  journey  to  the  Station,  the  Supervisor  shall  inform  TPC/OCC  about  the  Station from which the Track Access is required by P. Way and Signaling Supervisors. TPC shall inform  CHC/OCC  who  will  coordinate  with  station  to  provide  PTW  as  per  extant procedure to avoid any delay in granting PTW.
3.8 Mgr/AM/SSE P.Way shall also proceed to the site and keep in touch with TPC/OCC & Supervisor /P.Way/Office for details and chalked out Action Plan.
3.9 On reaching the Site of Fracture/Failure Location, the Supervisor/P.Way/office shall carry out Emergency Repairs as per the Procedure indicated below:
(i) The end of fractured rails shall not be touched by naked hands and the staff carrying out repairs shall wear insulated Hand Gloves. The Fractured Rails shall be jumpered by the Rail Jumper 2 m long to ensure continuity of the Return Current.
(ii) The Fractured Rails/weld shall then be joined by using Meter / 610 mm long Fish Plates or  Joggle  Fish  Plates  with  the  help  of  Bolted  Clamps/Special  Clamps/  C-  Clamps (depending  upon  the  location  of  the  Fracture  Rail/  Weld  and  Ballasted/Ballast  Less Track). If the gap at Fracture does not exceed 30mm, insertion of any closure Rail Piece shall not be necessary.

(iii)  As  soon  as  the  Emergency Work  is  completed,  the  Supervisor  shall  communicate  to OCC that the Track is fit for Traffic at speed of 15 Kmph for the first Train & 25 Kmph for subsequent  Trains  by  exchanging  Private  Number  and  confirming  the  affected  OHE

## Introduction

Mast Nos. till ATP/ATO fitness is not received. TPC/OCC shall give in writing to CHC in the format meant for imposition of TSR.

## Introduction

(iv)  After  resuming  Traffic,  TPC  shall  inform  HOD/Civil,  DGM/P.Way,  AM/Mgr./P.Way  & SSE/P.Way. Chief Controller/Traffic Controller & Signalling Controller  shall  inform  Dy. HOD/O, Dy. HOD/TO of the affected Line and HOD/O.
(v) After  Temporary  Repairs  of  the  Rail  Fracture/  Weld  Failure,  the  SSE/P.Way  shall arrange for the requisite Traffic Block & make necessary arrangements to carry out the Permanent repairs, preferably in the same night.
3.10 Traffic on the Line/Section or part thereof, (as the case may be): -
(i) Shall remain suspended till the receipt of Track Fit Message in the OCC.
(ii) Shall  be  permitted  in  RM/degraded  mode  as  per  feasibility  if  track  fitness  and  PTW cancellation is submitted by Civil wing until ATP/ATO/UTO fitness is not submitted by Signaling wing.
(iii)  Single line working and movement on adjacent track shall be as per Rule-63, 64, 65 and 70 of MRGR.
(iv)  Shall  resume  normal  service  after  receipt  of  track  fitness  and  ATP/ATO/UTO  fitness both by Civil and Signaling wing.
## 4.0 STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINES:

## 4.0 STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINES:

4.1 TC/OCC  shall  stop  the  trains  approaching  to  affected  section  and  discontinue  UTO mode of operation in the affected section on both lines.
4.2 Concerned Crew control shall ensure availability of RA/ETO for movement of trains in affected section as per requirement.
4.3 In  case  RA/ETO  is  not  onboard,  TC/OCC  shall  instruct  nearest  available  RA/ETO  to board the trains in affected section as per procedure.
4.4 TC/OCC shall instruct RA/ETO to take the charge of train, further movement shall be done as per Para 3.
4.5 UTO mode shall remain suspended till receipt of track fitness and fitness of Signalling equipments both by Civil and Signaling wing.

## 4.  Procedure To Obtain A 'Hot Work' Permit:

4.1. A 'Hot Work' Contractor determines a need for the 'Hot Work'.
4.2. The  'Hot  Work'  Contractor  ensures  that  the  area  around  'Hot  Work'  Activities  is  in compliance with the Safety Requirements of the 'Hot Work' Permit.
4.3. The  'Hot  Work'  Contractor  contacts  a  'Permit  Authorizing  Individual  (PAI)'  of  Work Allotting Agency.
4.4. The PAI inspects the 'Hot Work' Site and completes the 'Hot Work' Permit Form.
4.5. The PAI posts a 'Fire Watch', if the situation requires one.
4.6. Once all 'Permit' Safety Guidelines are satisfied, the PAI signs and posts the 'Permit'.
4.7. The 'Hot Work' Operator can then begin 'Hot Work'.

Shall be responsible for the Safe Operation of 'Hot Work' Activities.
Shall  determine  Flammable  Materials,  Hazardous  Processes,  or  other  potential Fire Hazards in the .Work Area'.
Shall ensure that Combustibles in the near vicinity of Hot Work are moved out to a Safe  Distance  /  covered  tightly  with  fire-retardant  or  non-combustible  material  / swept clean or kept wet. Near vicinity in U/G Stations & Tunnels shall be within a radius of 35 feet.
Shall  not  permit  the  'Hot Work',  if  the  Combustibles  cannot  be  moved  to  a  Safe Distance or cannot be shielded against Ignition.
Shall  determine  that  Fire  Protection  &  Extinguishing  Equipments  are  accessibly located at the Work Site.
Shall ensure that a Fire Watch is posted at the site, if needed.
Shall direct the 'Fire Watch' to check the Site 30 Minutes after the Completion of Work, for any Smoldering Fires.
Shall paste the Permit at the Work Site, if deploying of a 'Fire Watch' is not considered necessary.

## 6.1. Fire Watch' shall:

Be trained to understand the inherent Hazards of the Hot Work Site and of the Work Project, as a whole.
Ensure that Safe Conditions are maintained during the 'Hot Work' Operations.
Shall be authorized to stop the work, if unsafe conditions develop.
Have the Fire Extinguishing Equipment readily available in the proximity of the Work Site and be trained in its use.
Be familiar with the Facilities and Procedures for sounding an Alarm in the event of breaking out of Fire.
Watch for Fires in all exposed areas.
Try  to  extinguish  Fire  within  the  capabilities  of  Fire  Extinguishing  Equipment available.
Sound  the  Fire  Alarm  immediately,  if  the  Fire  is  beyond  the  capabilities  of  the Extinguishing Equipment available.
Perform  other  Duties,  but  none  that  shall  distract  him  /  her  from  Fire  Watch Responsibilities.
OCC and SC/SM of the respective Station shall not allow any 'Hot Work', if the 'Hot Work' Permit is not pasted on the Work Site.

## Permit Check List

√ The Equipments and its Components in use for Hot Work are as per IS Specifications.
√ Flammable & Combustible Materials in the vicinity of Hot Work Area have been removed or covered with Fire Retardant Guards or Metal Shields.
√ All Floors and Surfaces in the vicinity of Hot Work Area have been swept free of Combustible Dust or Debris.
√ Any Openings or Cracks in the Walls, Floors, or Ducts that are potential travel passages for Sparks, Heat and Flames have been covered.
√ An Operable Fire Extinguisher is nearby and accessible.
√ Sprinkler Heads that could be activated by Hot Work have been covered with a Wet Rag.
√ Smoke Detectors in the Area of Hot Work have been covered to prevent false Alarms.
√ A Fire Watch has been posted, if it is required, during Hot Work Operations and for 30 minutes after the Work has been completed.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR- 22 (Rev.-05)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR TAMPING OF BALLASTED TRACK OF MAIN LINE AND DEPOT WITH TAMPING MACHINE AND MOVEMENT OF RGM

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order covers the Methodology for Tamping of Ballast Track of Main Line and Depot with Track Tamping Machine (TTM) and movement of RGM.

## 2. SCOPE

This procedure shall be read in conjunction Metro Railway General Rule-2020, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
## 3. PROCEDURE FOR WORKING OF TTM:

3.1 Tamping Work shall be carried out under Engineer's Possession, in Traffic Block only. While the work on Main Line shall be undertaken during Non-revenue Hours, that in the Depot can be done in Revenue Hours.
3.2 Standard Procedure for Granting & Cancellation of Power Block, Traffic Block and Permit to Work shall be followed.
3.3 SSE/SE/ASE from P. Way, Signalling and OHE Wings shall prepare a Joint Inspection Program for Identification and Marking of S-Bonds, Track-side ATP Equipments, Earthing Cables / Strips and other Equipments related to their Systems and shall make a Scheme detailing the restricted Locations,  where  necessary  Precautions  shall  be  required  to  be  taken  during  the  Tamping Process. The Scheme, so prepared shall be verified and approved by the Mgr./AM/P. Way, Mgr./AM/Sig and Mgr./AM/OHE.
3.4 Supervisors from P. Way & Staff not below the rank of Maintainer from Signaling and OHE shall be present in the section during tamping operations in this case the EPIC shall be minimum JE from P.Way who will ensure that no signaling and OHE field equipment gets damaged during actual working of the TTM.
3.5 P. Way Supervisor shall ensure that the Super Elevation on the Curve shall not be more than the Standard Design Value and lifting of the Track in Straight shall not be more than 20 mm at any one time.
3.6 During Tamping work, any abnormality shall be immediately reported to concerned controller/staff in OCC/DCC by all the staff involved in the process.

3.6 During Tamping work, any abnormality shall be immediately reported to concerned controller/staff in OCC/DCC by all the staff involved in the process.
3.7 After the cancellation of Block Supervisor of P.Way and Staff not below the rank of Maintainer from Signaling & OHE shall board the pilot train in the affected section to check their respective Systems.  If  any  abnormality  is  noticed,  the  same  shall  be  reported  to  DCC  or  concerned controller in OCC immediately. The concerned Controllers/Staff in OCC/DCC shall coordinate with  concerned  controllers  in  OCC  or  staff  in  DCC  to  get  the  abnormality  cleared.  In  case rectification is pending on the affected portion of the Track, the Section shall be blocked for the Movement of following Trains. The OCC/DCC Shall permit Movement on the affected Section

## Introduction

only after getting written Confirmation of Clearance/Fitness of the Section from the concerned Controller/Staff in the OCC/DCC.

## Introduction

3.8 In case of a Failure of the Tamping Machine when it is working on the Main Line, the Operation Wing shall arrange for a Diesel Locomotive in coordination with Rolling Stock Wing for necessary Recovery System for the removal of Tamping Machine from the Section.
3.9 All the related Safety Precautions detailed in Metro railway General Rules 2020, Station Working Rules and other Safety Circulars issued from time to time shall be followed in true spirit. All Personnel present in the Work Section shall use their Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE).
3.10 Display of suitable Warning Boards / Banner Flags at the Starting & End Locations as also on the approach of Non-tamping Area, shall be arranged by the P. Way Supervisor in advance of the commencement of Tamping Operation.
3.11 RGM/TTM will be piloted by EPIC and the responsibility of movement shall be with EPIC.
3.12 Tamping Machine/RGM, being a 'Non-ATP' Vehicle, its Speed in any case shall not be allowed to exceed 25 Kmph.
Note: For working under Live OHE height of RGM/TTM shall not exceed 4028 mm in any case.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 39 B (Rev-03)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR STOPPING OF TRAINS AT PLATFORMS WHERE PSDs ARE INSTALLED ON LINE -2, 7 & 8

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

This  procedure  order  covers  the  action  to  be  taken  whenever  any  train  running  in  ATO/ ATP/UTO mode undershoots/overshoots the Normal Stopping Point (NSP) or stopping window at a platform where Platform Screen Doors/Gates (PSD/PSG) are installed on Line-2, 7 & 8, the objective  being  to  ensure  the  safety  &  convenience  of  the  passengers  while  boarding  &  deboarding the train.

## 2.  SCOPE

This  procedure is  applicable for  Line-2,  7  &  8.  Platform  Screen  Doors have  been  installed at each Platform of Line-7 & 8 and Kashmiri Gate to Central Secretariat (except Patel Chowk) of Line-2 to avoid the occurrence of any incident of falling of passenger and objects on the track and control unauthorized access to track.
Train  Operators  (TO)/Roving  Attendants  (RA)/  Emergency  Train  Operators  (ETO)  shall  be specifically attentive while stopping the train on the platforms so as to stop the train in perfect alignment at the designated Normal Stopping Point (NSP) so that all the saloon doors of train are aligned to corresponding PSDs.
This  document  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro  Railways  General  Rules,  2020  &  its amendment, SWO, Safety Circulars and other relevant instructions in vogue.
## 3.  HANDLING OF UNUSUAL SCENARIO (UNDERSHOOT/OVERSHOOT) ON LINE-7&8

If  train  stops  before/beyond  the  NSP  i.e.  beyond  stopping  window  width  of  total  1700  mm (-700mm & +1000 mm to NSP), following steps shall be followed
3.1 Undershoot Scenario : - If train undershoots and stops before the NSP (beyond -700mm) in Automatic Train Operation/Automatic train Protection
(i) Train Operators (TO)/Roving Attendants (RA)/ Emergency Train Operators (ETO) shall move the train ahead in ATP mode in such a manner to stop the train at NSP and open the doors.
(ii) If  ATP  proceed  code  is  not  available,  the  Train  Operators  (TO)/Roving  Attendants (RA)/ Emergency Train Operators (ETO) shall move the train in degraded mode as per the extant procedure up to NSP and open the doors.
3.2 Overshoot  Scenario:If  train  overshoots  and  stops  after  NSP  (beyond  +1000mm)  in ATP/ATO Mode:-

3.2 Overshoot  Scenario:If  train  overshoots  and  stops  after  NSP  (beyond  +1000mm)  in ATP/ATO Mode:-
(i) Train  Operator  (TO)/Roving  Attendant  (RA)/  Emergency  Train  Operator  (ETO)  shall inform TC/OCC about the overshooting and seek instructions. The TC shall ensure that all PSDs are detected as closed and following train has been ensured as stopped. After ensuring these aspects, TC shall advise the Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO) to try moving the train in reverse (RS-10 trains in Line7&8 have a feature that train can be moved in reverse up to 10 meter in ATP without SCS cutout)  in  ATP  mode  and  stop  the  train  at  NSP/within  stopping  window.  After  having

## Introduction

stopped  the  train  at  NSP/stopping  window,  the  Train  Operator  (TO)/Roving  Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO) shall open the doors.

(a) Train  Operator (TO)/  Roving  Attendant (RA)/  Emergency Train  Operator (ETO) shall seek instructions from TC.
(b) The  TC  shall  ensure  vacancy  of  platform  track  section,  all  PSDs  are  detected  as closed and following train if any has been ensured as stopped. After ensuring these aspects, TC  shall authorize the Train Operator (TO)/ Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency  Train  Operator  (ETO)  to  reverse  the  train  in  cut  out  mode  up  to NSP/stopping window under exchange of private numbers.
(c) After  getting  authorization  from  OCC,  Train  Operator  (TO)/Roving  Attendant(RA)/ Emergency  Train  Operator(ETO)  shall  Blow  'Horn'  &  Drive  the  Train  in  reverse direction in cut out mode up to Normal Stopping Point/stopping window at speed not exceeding 5 kmph.
(d) After  stopping  the  train  at  Normal  Stopping  Point/stopping  window,  Train  Operator (TO)/ Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO) shall open the doors and perform platform service.
(e) Subsequently,  the  Train  Operator  (TO)/  Roving  Attendant  (RA)/  Emergency  Train Operator (ETO) shall revert to normal driving mode.
Note :-If the train can't be reversed in Cut out mode, then passengers may be allowed to disembark from the train by emergency escape door
## 3.3 FOR UTO MODE OF TRAIN OPERATION ON LINE-7&8

## 3.3 FOR UTO MODE OF TRAIN OPERATION ON LINE-7&8

(i)
For  Line-7If  train  undershoots/overshoots  within  -/+10meter  from  the  NSP  in  UTO mode,  train  shall  automatically  perform  jog  forward/jog  back  after  6  seconds  of complete stand still and align itself to NSP.
For  Line-8 -  If  train  undershoots/overshoots  within  -/+10meter  from  the  NSP  in  UTO mode, train shall automatically perform jog forward/jog back and align itself.
(ii) If train undershoots and stops before the NSP (beyond -10m) in UTO Mode of operation or  does  not  jog  forward  and  align  itself  to  NSP  (automatically) , TC/OCC  shall  give departure  command,  Train  shall  move  upto  NSP  in  UTO  Mode  and  perform  normal platform service in UTO Mode.

## Introduction

(iii) If train overshoots and stops after NSP in UTO Mode of operation and does not perform jog back or could not align itself to NSP (automatically) :

TC/OCC  shall  advise  IC  to  make  announcements  for  passenger  information  that service  at  this  station  is  not  possible  due  to  technical  reasons  and  passengers desirous to alight at this station are requested to de-board at next station. The IC shall also express regrets for the inconvenience caused to the passengers.
After making announcement, TC/OCC shall give departure command for next station platform.
If the train happens to be the last revenue train of the day, TC shall instruct the nearest available TO/RA/ETO to board the train as per extant procedure if not already onboard and instruct TO/RA/ETO to take charge.
Further train movement shall be as per Para 3.2 (i) &/or 3.2 (iii).
HANDLING OF UNUSUAL SCENARIO (UNDERSHOOT / OVERSHOOT) FOR ONLY THOSE STATIONS OF LINE-2 WHERE PSDs ARE INSTALLED
If the train doors are within +/- 500 mm of normal stopping point, normal procedure for opening of train doors & PSD may be followed If train stops before/beyond the NSP i.e. beyond stopping window width of total 1000 mm (-500mm & +500 mm to NSP), following steps shall be followed
4.1  Undershoot  Scenario :-  If  train  undershoots  and  stops  before  the  NSP  (beyond  -500mm)  in Automatic Train Operation/Automatic train Protection
(i) Train Operators (TO) shall move the train ahead in ATP mode in such a manner to stop the train at NSP and open the doors.

(ii) If ATP proceed code is not available, the Train Operators (TO) shall move the train in degraded mode as per the extant procedure up to NSP and open the doors.
4.2  Overshoot Scenario:If train overshoots and stops after NSP (beyond +500mm) in ATP/ATO Mode, then the TO must check the extent of overrun:
(i) If  the  train  doors  are  within  PSD  window  (i.e.  upto  +500mm  from  NSP):normal procedure  for  opening  of  train  doors  and  PSD  shall  be  followed.  The  stopping  window location is indicated by a stopping window marker in orange colour on the side of platform towards TO seating side.
(ii) If train stops beyond PSD stopping window (i.e. beyond +500mm from NSP):-
Train Operator (TO) shall inform TC/OCC and seek for instructions.
Preferably ,  TC/OCC shall  advise  the  Train  Operator  to  move  the  train  up  to  next station  after  making  announcements  for  passenger  information  that  service  at  this station is not possible due to technical reasons and passengers desirous to alight at this station are requested to de-board at next station. The Train Operator shall also express regrets for the inconvenience caused to the passengers.
However,  if  OCC  decides  to  reverse  the  train  depending  upon  the  existing conditions or if train is the last revenue train of the day, the following steps shall be taken by Train Operator & TC;

After  getting  authorization  from  OCC,  Train  Operator  (TO)  shall  Blow  'Horn'  & Drive  the  Train  in  reverse  direction  in  SCS/ATP  cutout  mode  up  to  Normal Stopping Point/stopping window at speed not exceeding 5 kmph.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR-08E (Rev.-02)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR OPERATING TRAIN IN ATO MODE IN LINE-7&9

## 1. INTRODUCTION:

This  Procedure  Order  applies  for  Train  Operation  in  ATO  Mode  in  Line-7&9  and  specifies  the precautions and delineates role and responsibility of all the concerned Staff.

## 2. SCOPE

:
2.1  This Procedure Order shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules-2020 and Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules-2022 & Special Instructions in vogue.
2.2 In  case  of  Line-09, wherever  'Train/Saloon  doors  and  PSD''  is  mentioned  to  be  read  as 'Train/Saloon Doors' only as PSD is not installed on Line-09.

## 3. ATO MODE:

3.1  The entire mainline of metro network of Line-7&9 is equipped for ATP/ATO operation.
3.2  ATO could be available if:
(i) Route is set
(ii) Train is in ATP Mode
(iii)  Target speed is available
3.3  ATO mode shall be enabled only:
(i) If train is at zero speed
(ii)  TBC is at 'B-Max' position
(iii) Target speed is available in ATP mode.
(iv) Mode selector in AUTO position and ATO is selected from DMI
(v)  EB reset performed by TO from DMI after selection of ATO mode.
NOTE : - From main line siding or Station platform, if the train is properly berthed, then ATO start button can be pressed to depart. If the train is not properly berthed, then the train needs to be moved in ATP mode for some distance for proper berthing and then stop and select ATO mode, reset EB from DMI and press ATO Start Button to depart.

## 5. PROCEDURE:

5.1. If using ATO without ATB
(i)  Put  mode  selector  in  AUTO  in  moving  direction  CAB  and  rear  cab  mode  selector  in  OFF position,
(ii)  ATO icon (Right Side of DMI Screen) needs to be selected from DMI,
(iii) After  ATO  selection  Train  operator  has  to  verify  symbol  'A'  is  displayed  on  DMI  at  current mode position.
(iv) EB to be released from DMI.
(v)  'START' button will glow continuously. Train operator has to press (2-6 sec) departure button unless train starts moving.

## Introduction

5.2. In  ATO  mode,  Train  Operator  has  to  ensure  that  SCS  switch  is  in  NORMAL  position  in  both CABs.  The  platform  side  doors  will  be  enabled,  when  the  train  has  stopped  within  stopping window. Saloon doors and PSD will be opened automatically. The train and PSD doors shall be closed by the TO at the end of dwell time.

5.3. If  train  does  not  start  in  ATO  mode  even  after  pressing  the  'START'  button,  the  train  may  be moved in ATP mode if target is available otherwise use RM mode duly informing the OCC giving information  about  status  of  icon  'Train  Located',  'CBTC'  and  next  available  mode'  Blinking Yellow border' (Right Side of Screen) on DMI. TO shall select the 'ATO' mode of driving after confirmation from OCC either at next station or in between station after stopping the train as per procedure [SC-8E - 5.1 or 5.2)].
5.4. In  case  train  stops  after  or  before  designated  NSP  in  ATO,  then  following  procedure  shall  be followed.
In  Case  of  Line  -  07:  In case train stops after or before designated NSP in ATO, then following procedure shall be followed.
(i) If a Train stops short of its normal Stopping point in ATO mode.
(a)  TO shall drive the train in ATP mode up to the Normal Stopping Point (NSP) and change mode to ATO, train door and PSD will be opened automatically and follow further as per the extant procedure.
(b)  In case Target speed is not available, TO shall drive the train up to the designated Normal Stopping Point in degraded mode, as per extant procedure.

(b)  In case Target speed is not available, TO shall drive the train up to the designated Normal Stopping Point in degraded mode, as per extant procedure.
(c) After aligning the train with the designated Normal Stopping Point only, the TO shall 'Open'  and  'Close'  the  train  doors  &  PSD  and  proceed  further  as  per  extant procedure.
(ii) If a Train stops beyond its Normal Stopping Point and overshoot distance is less than 10m (verify on DMI), then
(a)  TO  shall  inform  OCC  and  put  mode  selector  in  REV  position  after  verifying REVERSE is enabled on DMI ('REV' in Green),
(b)  Blow 'Horn' & reverse the train to align with designated NSP
(c)  Verify on DMI train Berth symbol is positive
(d)  Change mode to ATO, train doors will be opened automatically and follow further the extant procedure.
(iii)  If a Train stops beyond its Normal Stopping Point and overshoot distance is more than 10m (verify on DMI) OR Reverse is not enable ('REV' in Red), then
(a)  TO should inform to OCC, If TO is instructed to move further to next station by OCC, TO  shall  make  announcement  to  the  passengers  that  due  to  some  Technical problem, the train shall proceed to the next station without opening the saloon doors &  the  passengers  are  requested  to  get  down  at  the  next  station  and  board  the returning  train  from  the  other  platform.  TO  shall  apologize  for  the  inconvenience caused.

(b)  If the train is the last Train of the day, OCC shall prevent the following Non-Revenue Train (if any) from approaching the platform.
(c)  Only after ensuring that following train/Vehicle has been brought to a STOP and the Train Operator instructed not to move without permission from OCC. The TC shall then authorize the train at the platform to reverse in cut out mode until all doors are at the platform and in the alignment corresponding to designated NSP. Then
Open & close the train doors and PSD as per procedure established for SCS mode operation.

## Introduction

After closing train door and PSD, TO shall put SCS in Normal position and wait for 2 minute until both VATC boot-up and move in RM mode to initialize train.

After confirmation from OCC, TO shall change operating Mode to ATO from RM, when train will be communicating (Green CBTC icon on DMI) and in moving block section.
In  Case  of  Line-09:  In  case  train  stops  after  or  before  designated  NSP  in  ATO,  then following procedure shall be followed.
(i) If a Train stops short of its normal Stopping point in ATO mode
(a)  TO shall blow 'Horn'& Drive the train in ATP mode up to the normal stopping point.
(b)  In case Target speed is not available, TO shall drive the train up to the designated Normal stopping point in degraded mode as per extant procedure.
(c) After aligning the train with the designated normal stopping point only, the TO shall 'Open' and 'Close' the saloon doors and proceed further as per extant procedure.
(ii) If  a  Train  stops  beyond  its  Normal  Stopping  Point  but  with  the  Doors  still  on  the Platform, the TO shall Open & close saloon doors and proceed further as per extant procedure.
(iii) If a train stops beyond the end of the platform
(a)  TO  shall  inform  OCC.  After  taking  authorization  from  OCC,  TO  shall  make announcement to the passengers that due to some Technical problem, The Train shall proceed  to  the  next  station without  opening  the  saloon  doors  &  the passengers are requested to get down at the next station and board the returning train from the other platform. TO shall apologize for the inconvenience caused.

(b)  If train is the last train of the day, OCC shall prevent the following Non - revenue Trains (if any) from approaching the platform.
(c) Only after ensuring that the following trains has been brought to a Stop and the TO instructed not to move without OCC's permission, the TC shall then authorize the train at the platform in the alignment corresponding to designated NSP. TO shall, thereafter open & close the doors and proceed further as per extant procedure.
5.5. Whenever a 'Station skip' command is given by TC, he shall inform TO & SC about the same. TO  in  turn  shall  continue  to  move  in  ATO  mode  when  entering  or  passing  through  station platform TO shall blow horn intermittently till cab passes the designated stopping point during the  period  of  revenue  operation.  TO  (If  auto  announcement  is  not  working)  &  SC  shall  also make related announcement in the train & station respectively.
5.6. Whenever a 'Keep door close' indication is displayed on DMI screen in ATO mode, door shall not open automatically and the Train Operator shall seek instruction from OCC. In case if it is required to perform platform duty at station, TO shall open the saloon doors in ATO mode as per the extant procedure.

5.7. Whenever TO is instructed from OCC to inhibit automatic opening of train doors for a particular platform/station in ATO mode, TO shall inhibit instructed side doors using DMI by using 'Inhibit Left Doors' or 'Inhibit Right Doors' or 'Inhibit Both Doors' before entry at platform. In case if it is required to perform platform duty at station, TO shall open the saloon doors in ATP mode as per the extant procedure. Door inhibition will be reset, as train will come outside station.
NOTE:  In  case  of  door  inhibition  from  DMI,  Train  doors  &  PSD  will  not  open.  Platform duty/doors cycle is required to move train in ATO.

## 6. TRAIN SHOULD NOT BE DRIVEN IN ATO MODE IF:

6.1. If any safety switch is operated to cutout.

## 6. TRAIN SHOULD NOT BE DRIVEN IN ATO MODE IF:

6.2. Whenever it is required to move the train with reduced traction power.
6.3. Whenever it is required to move the train with caution or/and with speed limit which is not imposed through the system.
6.4. Whenever slip/slide fault is activated in train.

## 7. EMERGENCY BRAKE APPLICATION IN ATO Mode:

If  emergency brake is applied in the train due to any reason, check alarm available on DMI for the reason  of  EB  application,  also  verify  status  of  'Train  Located',  'CBTC',  Train  integrity  status  and 'Next available Mode' and convey it to OCC. After releasing emergency brake from DMI if target is available in ATO Mode train will start automatically without any intervention. If  target  speed  is  not  available  in  ATO  mode  after  releasing  EB,  check  target  in  ATP  mode  if  not available then move train in RM as per the extant procedure. If EB gets stuck, then
Train Operator shall check ADCL status if train is in between station or platform.
If  train  is  at  platform  check  all fire  detectors  are  in  normal  condition from TCMS VDU and no PAD is active from MOP.
If  none  of  above  situation,  then  move  in  RM (if EB is  recoverable)/SCS Cut-Out  as per  instruction from OCC to drive the train up to next  station  as per extant  procedure and ask for Signaling  staff intervention.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 39 A (Rev-02)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR STOPPING OF TRAINS AT PLATFORM WHERE PSD ARE PROVIDED

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

This  procedure  order  covers  the  action  to  be  taken,  if  the  train  under/over  shoots  the  Normal Stopping  Point  (NSP)  or  stopping  window  at  a  platform  where  PSD  are  installed,  the  objective being  to  ensure  the  safety  &  convenience  of  the  passengers  while  boarding  &  de-boarding  the train.

## 2.  SCOPE

This  document to  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro  Railways  General  Rules  -  2020,  (Chap-IV Rule-32 (11)) and Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules, 2022, station working orders in vogue and other Special Instructions issued, from time to time for working of trains.

## 3.  GENERAL

3.1. Platform  Screen  Doors  have  been  installed  at  each  Platform  of  Airport  Line  to  avoid  the occurrence of any incident of passengers falling on the track.
3.2. Train Operators shall be specifically attentive, while berthing the train on the platforms so as to stop the train in perfect alignment at the designated Normal Stopping Point (NSP), so that all the saloon doors of train are aligned to corresponding PSD.

## 4. Handling of Unusual Scenario:

4.1. Undershoot the NSP/stopping window in Automatic Train Operation:
If a train in ATO mode of operation appears to be about to overrun the correct stopping mark, the TO should intervene by operating the TBC to the emergency braking position, or operating either of the 'Mushroom' emergency plungers in the cab.
If the train stops short of the stopping point the TO must move the train in manual control to the correct point as per the extant procedure.
4.2. Train overruns the correct stopping point, then the TO must check the extent of overrun:
Within +/- 500 mm stopping window. The stopping window location is indicated by a stopping window marker in orange colour on the side of platform towards TO seating side.
Beyond stopping window but saloon doors within PSD / EED zone.
Beyond Stopping window, such a distance that the one saloon door is beyond MSD.
Beyond platform by such a distance that at least two saloon doors are beyond MSD.
If train stops beyond the end of the platform.
If the train doors are within +/- 500 mm of stopping point, normal procedure for opening of train doors & PSD may be followed.
TO must inform TC about the train overrun beyond normal stopping window of +/- 500 mm, beyond which door opening authorization shall not be available from ATC.

## Introduction

In case of 4.2(b) above, the train doors may be opened and passengers de-boarded through EED or else train may be reversed to bring it within the stopping window by selecting the cut out mode and reverser after seeking permission from TC with exchange of private numbers.

In case of 4.2 (c) above, the train may be reversed to bring it within the stopping window by selecting the cut out mode and reverser after seeking permission from TC with exchange of private numbers.
In  case  of  4.2(d)  above,  train  shall  either  be  driven  to  next  station  or  be  reversed  to  the stopping point of same station. TO must seek instructions from TC before driving the train to next station or for reversing his train using cut out mode with exchange of private numbers. TC/TO must make an announcement to passenger in the train, informing them that it will not be possible for  them to alight and give the reason, extending apologies for the inconvenience. TO must then request them to remain on the train to the next station and take a train back.

In  case  of  4.2(e)  above  the  train  operator  shall  seek  instructions  from  TC,  and  if  TC  can prevent the following train from approaching the platform by using signaling controls and if reversing  will  not  affect  the  operation  of  other  trains,  then  TC  may  authorized  TO  under exchange of Pvt. number to reverse train until all doors are at platform and train is  correctly positioned at  stopping  point  or  otherwise  an  announcement  shall  be  made  to  the passengers and train may proceed to next station without opening the doors. But if the train is last train of the day then it may be reversed on instructions of TC under exchange of Pvt. Number  and  stopped  at  normal  stopping  point.  If  the  train  cannot  be  reversed  then  the passengers may be allowed to disembark from the train by emergency escape door.
After reversal and passenger de-boarding at platform, TO shall revert to normal driving mode before starting to the next station.
The train must then continue to the next station driven in normal mode as the case may be till next station.
4.3. If the train overruns or attempts to overrun more than one station in a trip under ATO mode, then ATP mode must be selected and the train shall be driven manually in CM mode until it can be changed over with another train from depot.
4.4. In Manual mode, TO must endeavor to not overrun the normal stopping window to avoid need for any reversal.
## 5.0 Failure of Platform Screen Door/ Platform Edge Door/ Emergency Escape Door:

## 5.0 Failure of Platform Screen Door/ Platform Edge Door/ Emergency Escape Door:

In case any PSD/PED/EED remains open and its closing is not possible, ADCL (All Door Close Loop) signal shall not be available and the train shall not be able to enter into/leave from platform in  ATP/ATO  Mode.  If  any  PSD  become  faulty  and  PSD  open/close  operation  is  not  possible, same can be bypassed using LCKS (Local Control Key Switch) having two positions i.e. Auto and Bypass/Manual.
PSD/PED bypass preferably should be done in closed condition. Few cases for abnormal working of PSD, and action to be taken; are detailed as under:
In case, Train door is faulty, corresponding PSD  shall open/close normally. Traffic Controller/OCC shall instruct, Train operator (TO)/RS staff to paste sticker on faulty train door and  to  Station  controller  (SC)  for  announcement  on  the  station  about  unavailability  of particular train door/PSD for passenger service, Rolling Stock Controller shall arrange to get Faulty Train Door rectified at the earliest.

## Introduction

In case, Communication of PSD with Signalling is failed, TO shall open/close PSD using PSD Local Control Panel (PSL). Maintenance staff shall be informed for fault rectification.

## Introduction

In  case, All  or individual PSD is not opening/closing with the train doors and by the use of PSL, TO/SC shall assist the passengers to board/deboard the train using Emergency Manual Release Handle and concerned PSD shall be bypassed in closed condition, as detailed in Para 5.1. Maintenance staff shall be informed for fault rectification.
In case, Complete power failure of PSD system, automatic operation of PSD with signalling/ Manual  operation  from  PSL/ECB/LCKS  shall  not  work.  In  this  case,  all  trains  shall  be required to move in degraded mode in affected station platform area. TO/SC shall assist the passengers to board/deboard the train using Emergency Manual Release Handle, SC shall open the PSD manually from platform side by using square key and follow precautions as per para  5.2.  Maintenance  staff  shall  be  informed  for  fault  rectification  and  PSD  operation normalcy.
In case of obstruction detection while PSD closing, PSD shall make three attempts to close automatically.  If  obstacle  is  still  present,  the  PSD  shall  stop  in  unlocked  position.  In  such case,  Station  controller  shall  verify  the  removal  of  the  obstruction.  After  removal  of  the obstruction, door close command shall be sent by TO from the train. In case door closing not possible,  PSL  shall  be  operated  by  SC  to  close  the  door.  In  case  door  still  doesn't  close, concerned PSD shall be barricaded as per Para 5.2.
## 5.1 PSD Bypass in closed condition: -

## 5.1 PSD Bypass in closed condition: -

If  any PSD become faulty and PSD open/close operation is not possible. Station Controller shall apprise the fault to Traffic Controller (TC) immediately and further TC  shall communicate the same to Signalling System Controller (SGC).
In  case  PSD becomes faulty in closed condition, TC shall permit to bypass the concerned PSD in consultation with SGC.
In case, PSD becomes faulty in open condition, TC shall permit to SC to manually close the concerned PSD in consultation with SGC, SC shall close the open PSD manually by pushing it. TC shall permit to bypass the faulty PSD in closed condition. In case, PSD closing is not possible even by manual pushing Para 5.2 shall be followed.
After  getting  permission  from  TC,  SC  shall  bypass  the  concerned  PSD  via  LCKS  (Local Control Key Switch) located in the header box, and paste advisory on bypassed door that door is not in use.
SGC shall instruct the nearest available staff to attend the failure.
TC shall give message to all train operator about bypassed PSD. At such platform TO shall ensure ample time is provided for passenger service.
Note: In New Delhi to Dwarka Sec-21, PSD/PED bypass is not possible in open position.
## 5.2 If closing of PSD/PED is not possible and need arises to bypass in open condition: -

## 5.2 If closing of PSD/PED is not possible and need arises to bypass in open condition: -

SC shall apprise the fault to TC immediately and further TC shall communicate the same to Signalling System Controller (SGC).
TC shall permit to bypass the concerned PSD in open condition in consultation with SGC.
After getting permission from TC, SC shall bypass the concerned PSD in open condition via LCKS (Local Control Key Switch) located in the header box, and depute a look-out person at the Platform.  Look-out  person shall keep watch for any unauthorized access on the tracks from bypassed PSD/PED.

## Introduction

SGC shall  instruct  the  nearest  available  staff  to  attend  the  failure.  In  case  rectification  is taking considerable time, maintenance staff shall try to close the concerned PSD and bypass it.

## Introduction

TC  shall  impose  Temporary  Speed  Restriction  (TSR)  of  20  KMPH  in  the  station  platform area.
TC shall give a message to all the TOs to follow 20 KMPH speed restriction in the affected platform area and to blow horn while entering the station platform.
In case TSR cannot be incorporated in the CATC system or any train is moving in Degraded Mode, TC shall instruct the SC of previous station to issue the caution order regarding speed restriction  of  20  KMPH due  to PSD failure.  In  case Train  shifts  to  degraded  mode  in midsection  while  approaching  the  affected  station,  TC  shall  instruct  the  Train  Operator  under exchange of private number regarding speed restriction of 20 KMPH in the station area of the affected station.
## 5.3 Failure of EED

SC shall try to close the faulty EED. If closing of EED is not possible, SC shall apprise the fault to TC immediately and further TC shall communicate the same to Signalling System Controller (SGC).
SC shall depute a look-out person at the Platform. Look-out person shall keep watch for any unauthorized access on the tracks from faulty EED.
In New Delhi to Dwarka Sec-21 section , SGC shall instruct the nearest available staff to attend the failure.
Note:  In  New  Delhi  to  Dwarka  Sec-21  section,  EED  shall  be  bypassed  by  maintenance staff.
At I.I.C.C.- Dwarka Sector 25 station : -
TC shall permit to bypass the EED in open condition in consultation with SGC.
After getting permission from TC, SC shall bypass the EED in open condition via LCKS (Local Control Key Switch) located at associated PSD, and barricade the bypassed EED.
SGC shall instruct the nearest available staff to attend the failure.
TC shall impose TSR of 20 KMPH in the station platform area.
TC shall give a message to all the TOs to follow 20 KMPH speed restriction in the affected platform area and to blow horn while entering the station platform.

TC shall impose TSR of 20 KMPH in the station platform area.
TC shall give a message to all the TOs to follow 20 KMPH speed restriction in the affected platform area and to blow horn while entering the station platform.
In  case  TSR  cannot  be  incorporated  in  the  CATC  system  or  any  train  is  moving  in Degraded  Mode,  TC  shall  instruct  the  SC  of  previous  station  to  issue  the  caution  order regarding speed restriction of 20 KMPH due to PSD failure. In case Train shifts to degraded mode  in  mid-section  while  approaching  the  affected  station,  TC  shall  instruct  the  Train Operator under exchange of private number regarding speed restriction of 20 KMPH in the station area of the affected station.
Note: 1) In New Delhi to Dwarka Sec-21 SCRs, PSD MMI or any other panel is not available to view status of PSD/PED/EED,  in  the  said  section  signalling  staff shall be  responsible  for observation of normal working of PSD and reporting/ rectification of failure of PSD/PED/EED. ECB is also not available at New Delhi to Dwarka Sec-21 SCRs.
At I.I.C.C.- Dwarka Sector 25 station, the status of each door is displayed at PSC, MMI in SCR and door/close status is also displayed at the PSL.
At I.I.C.C.- Dwarka Sector 25 station, in case of Emergency, PSDs can be opened/closed by selecting emergency mode at ECB (Emergency Control Box) provided in SCR, after taking all necessary precautions for passenger safety.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 26 (Rev.-09)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR REMOVAL OF KITES & THREADS FROM OHE DURING TRAFFIC HOURS IN RAIL CORRIDOR

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This  Procedure  Order  details  the  Responsibilities  of  the  concerned  Metro  Staff  and  the Methodology  to  be  followed  for  the  Work  of  removal  of  Kites  &  Threads  from  the  OHE, spotting hot points & other emergency requirements during day light hours to be carried out to avoid damage to the OHE.

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure is applicable for all lines. This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro  Railways  General  Rules,  2020  and  its  amendment,  Safety  Circulars  and  other instructions in vogue.
For UTO mode of Train Operation: wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/ Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO).

3.1. These  Works  shall  require  the  Access  on  the  'Right-of-Way'  on  open  viaduct  during Traffic Hours and as such, the Staff undertaking these Works shall continually be vigilant and extra cautious to ensure their own Safety. They shall look in each direction before entering upon and standing close to the Tracks.
3.2. Staff shall not walk, stand, step or sit on the running Rails, Points & Crossings, Guard Rails, Cover Boards, PVC Conduit, Interlocking Apparatus or other Wayside Equipments.
3.3. Staff  shall  use  the  Safety Walkway,  whenever  possible. While  walking  in  DN  Direction they shall use UP Track Walkway and in UP Direction, the DN Track Walkway.
3.4. Under no circumstances, the Staff shall go in front of any moving vehicle.
3.5. Staff shall not cross the track from DN side to UP side and Vice-Versa.
3.6. The  EPIC  &  the  Gang,  while  working  during  Track  Access,  shall  be  extra  cautious  in removing  of  the  Foreign  Objects  like  Kites  &  Threads  from  the  OHE,  as  the  Work infringes the Schedule of Moving Dimensions.
4.0 DMRC Traction staff, not below the Rank of Sr. Maintainer having competency, shall be the EPIC.
5.0 All Accesses to the Track shall be within an EP. In a longer Section, the number of Accesses may be simultaneously permitted.

4.0 DMRC Traction staff, not below the Rank of Sr. Maintainer having competency, shall be the EPIC.
5.0 All Accesses to the Track shall be within an EP. In a longer Section, the number of Accesses may be simultaneously permitted.
6.0 There is restricted clearance between Tracks and fencing wall in the section SHD to SLAP DN line  (L-1),  AEL  and  middle  walkway  between  DSG  to  NBAA  (L-1),  BAPB-BVHM  (L-6) section. Therefore, track access shall not be demanded and given in this section during traffic hours.
7.0 The gang shall consist of a minimum two authorized electrical DMRC staff but not more than three, of which one should be the EPIC & one to function as the 'Look- out Man', to caution the Gang about all approaching Trains in the area of both directions.

## Introduction

8.0 EPIC  along  with  Gang  Members  shall  inform  the  TPC  and  directly  contact  the  Station Controller of the concerned Station for taking the Possession of the Section. He shall fill the requisite Performa for getting the 'Permit-to-Work', duly mentioning therein the Nos. of Gang Members  (DMRC),  Entry  &  Exit  Stations,  Nature  of  the  Work,  Location  and  the  expected Duration. All the Gang Members shall enter & exit the Section from a single Station. SC shall confirm from OCC/TC about the PTW under exchange of private numbers.

9.0 The Entry / Exit of the Gang shall be recorded in the Possession Register maintained in SCR.
10.0 The  EPIC  shall  ensure  that  all  the  Gang  Members  including  him  are  protected  with  PPE Gears  (Hi-Vi  Vest,  Helmet,  Safety  Shoes  etc).  The  EPIC  must  have  Tetra  Set  &  Mobile Phone with him and hand signal flags (both red and green for use of walkway in day light).
11.0 OCC/TC shall apprise about the Track Access to the Chief Controller & OCM.
12.0 The OCM shall take permission of HOD/O or Dy.HOD/O for giving Access to Track to the EPIC and his Gang. However, before granting of the Track Access, the CHC/OCM:
12.1. Shall  check  that  the  Location  does  not  fall  within  the  List  of  Locations  /  Sections mentioned in Para '6' above.
12.2. Shall communicate the details of Track Access under section, on Train Radio of the concerned Line.
13.0 A written Caution Order, giving complete details of the Work being carried out, shall be issued by the Station Controller of the adjacent Stations of the 'Track Possessed Section', to each TO entering into the said Section on any of the UP / DN Lines.
14.0 All TOs shall observe Caution and blow horn continuously in the entire stretch of the 'Caution Driving Area' i.e. the Area under the Track Access.
15.0 Any abnormality, requiring extension of Track Access shall have to be immediately informed by the EPIC to OCC/TC & the Station Controller for further action.

15.0 Any abnormality, requiring extension of Track Access shall have to be immediately informed by the EPIC to OCC/TC & the Station Controller for further action.
16.0 After completion of the work, the EPIC shall clear the Section of Men, Materials, Equipments and Infringements and cancel the Track Access by submitting the Performa for Cancellation of 'Permit-to-Work' to the SC of the exit Stations and EPIC will also inform TPC. The SC, after acknowledging the Cancellation Request, shall inform the OCC/TC regarding the Cancellation of Track Access.
This  shall  be  treated  as  the  Cancellation  of  the  said  Track  Access,  only  after  which  the Normal Working in the Section can be restored.
17.0 In inclement weather like rainy/foggy weather and poor light conditions such 'Permit to Work' may not be granted.
## 18.0  PRECAUTIONS

## 18.0  PRECAUTIONS

18.1. Only the kite threads which are very essential to be removed for safety of OHE shall be removed during day time with the help of operating rod by OHE staff.
18.2. During this activity one staff shall be essentially kept as look out man. The Lookout man shall have whistles to caution the other staff about incoming trains.
18.3. In case operating rod is stuck with the structure due to any reason, EPIC shall stop movement of trains  by  delivering  message  to  the  TC/OCC&TO  on  Tetra  set  in  the operation mode frequency.

## Introduction

18.4. If  train  doesn't  stop  due  to  any  reason, OHE staff shall leave the operating rod and bring himself at safe distance from the train.

## Introduction

18.5. The kite threads at any location which require excessive effort shall not be attended during day time; these shall be removed in non traffic hours.
## 19.0  ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINES

## 19.0  ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINES

TC/OCC shall apprise about the Track Access to the Chief Controller. Chief Controller shall coordinate  with  the  OCM  and  relevant  Crew  Control,  which  in  turn  ensure  availability  of RA/ETO for movement of trains in affected section. Before PTW to OHE EPIC is granted by Station Controller, TC/OCC shall discontinue UTO mode of operation in the affected section and instruct nearest available RA/ETO to board the train (if RA/ETO is not already onboard) as  per  extant  procedure  &  to  take  charge  of  trains  at  preceding  platform  of  the  affected section and trains will be moved cautiously under ATP signalling mode till the track portion is occupied by OHE EPIC.
