## SAFETY CIRCULAR   32 (Rev.-04)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF TRAIN OPERATION DURING FLASHING / DAMAGE OF PANTOGRAPH

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

The Purpose of this Procedure Order is to enable all concerned Staff to handle cases of flashing in pantograph or/and Damage of pantograph of train in main line in orderly manner.

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

This procedure should be read in conjunction with Metro Railway General Rules, 2020 and Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules, 2022 and other Safety Circulars, Special Instructions in vogue.

## 2.  SCOPE

This Procedure Order is applicable to all the Train Operators, Station Controllers, Traffic Controllers, Traction  Power  Controllers  and  Rolling  Stock  Controllers  or  any  other  staff,  who  are  actively  or otherwise associated with the movement of Trains both during Revenue and Non-revenue Hours on the Main Line.
## 3.1 If Flashing / Flashing Sound with OHE tripping is observed in a train by its Train Operator or by others, and reported to OCC

## 3.1.1

If Train is standstill at platform NSP, Train Operator of that Train shall visually verify the condition of OHE and all pantographs carefully and report to TC with details of damage (if any).
## In case of UTO mode of operation :

## In case of UTO mode of operation :

TC/OCC shall apply PF HOLD on receiving of any such information.
RSC & TPC shall inspect OHE & all Pantograph using pantograph facing camera and analyse fault.
TC/OCC shall instruct SC to visually verify the condition of OHE and all pantographs carefully.
RSC/TPC/SC shall report abnormality with details of damage (if any) to TC/OCC.
RSC /TPC shall confirm TC/OCC for further movement of train.
If train is moving, Train Operator of that train shall inform TC and continue moving up to next station platform NSP. After stopping the train at Station NSP, TO shall visually verify the condition of OHE and all pantographs carefully and report to TC with details of damage (if any).

## In case of UTO mode of operation :

TC/OCC shall apply PF HOLD on receiving of any such information.
RSC & TPC shall inspect OHE & all Pantograph using pantograph facing camera and analyse fault.
TC/OCC shall instruct SC of the immediate next station to visually verify the condition of OHE and all pantographs carefully.
RSC/TPC/SC shall report abnormality with details of damage (if any) to TC/OCC.
RSC /TPC shall confirm TC/OCC for further movement of train.

## Introduction

If  train  is  moving and Train Operator feels/notices heavy vibration or OHE damage or sag in OHE or any infringement in OHE, TO shall stop the train immediately, inform TC and Come out at walk way of the parapet/tunnel or at grade level at the side of ballasted track, watch the OHE and all pantographs carefully and report TC with details of damage (if any).
## In case of UTO mode of operation:

## In case of UTO mode of operation:

If entanglement/damage of any pantograph of the train occur, the Auto drop-down function of the train shall drop down all the pantographs of the train and stop the train immediately by application of Emergency brakes (EB) automatically. Alarm of the Auto Drop-Device (ADD) activation shall appear to TC/RSC.
In such case, TC shall instruct the nearest available RA/ETO to board the train as per extant procedure and take charge of the train.
RSC & TPC shall inspect OHE & all Pantograph using pantograph facing camera and analyse fault.
RSC/TPC/SC shall report abnormality with details of damage (if any) to TC/OCC.
RSC /TPC shall confirm TC/OCC for further movement of train.
3.1.2 Traffic Controller shall stop following trains in the same line to avoid entry in that section till the OHE is verified and regulate other trains as per requirement.

## 3.1.3

If  no  apparent  problem  is  observed  by  TO/RA/ETO/SC/TPC/RSC  (as  the  case  may  be)  in pantograph(s) of the Train and OHE after flashing then the train shall be moved as per steps mentioned in Case I (Para 3.2) .
If there is visible problem reported by TO/RA/ETO/SC/TPC/RSC (as the case may be) in OHE, then the train shall be moved as per steps mentioned in Case II (Para 3.3) .
If  there  is  visible  problem reported  by  by TO/RA/ETO/SC/TPC/RSC (as the case may be) in pantograph(s), then the train shall be moved as per steps mentioned in Case III (Para 3.4) .
## 3.2 Case I :- No apparent problem is observed by Train Operator after flashing
## 3.2.1 For Non-UTO Mode of Operation

## 3.2.1 For Non-UTO Mode of Operation

If no apparent problem is observed by Train Operator in pantograph(s) of the train and OHE after flashing then, the TO shall report TC the mast number in front of him and the train shall be moved further. However, RSC shall arrange the train to be checked by RS staff at the earliest even if there is no apparent problem observed by the Train Operator. TPC shall arrange to check OHE at the location where flashing is reported.
Traffic Controller shall instruct TO of the adjacent line (wherever applicable) to observe the OHE of other line by driving at speed not more than 25 kmph for two stations at least, from the suspected location so as to enable TO to look for any abnormality in OHE. TO will report the status of OHE accordingly.
If  adjacent  line  TO  reports  normal  status  of  OHE,  the  first  train  in  the  same  line  to  be instructed to move at a speed not exceeding 40 kmph with front Pantograph lowered in the said section.
If it is not possible to get the OHE checked by adjacent line train, e.g. in tunnel, the following two trains in the same line should be instructed to move at a speed not exceeding 25 kmph with front Pantograph lowered in the said section to observe any abnormality so that train can be stopped short of any abnormality, if there is any, and report the same to OCC.

## Introduction

If no apparent problem in OHE is observed by Train Operators in (ii) or (iii) above, normal services may be resumed.

## Introduction

If any visible problem is observed in OHE by Train Operators in (ii)  or (iii) above, action detailed in Case II shall be adopted.
## 3.2.2 In case of UTO Mode of Operation

## 3.2.2 In case of UTO Mode of Operation

If no apparent problem is observed by ETO/SC/TPC/RSC in pantograph(s) of the train and OHE then, the train shall be moved further. However, RSC shall arrange the train to be checked by RS staff at the earliest. TPC shall arrange to check OHE at the location where flashing is reported.
TC shall instruct nearest available RA/ETO to board (If already not on board) the following first train in the same line as per procedure and instruct to take charge & to move at a speed not exceeding 10 kmph with front Pantograph lowered in the said section to observe any abnormality so that train can be stopped short of any abnormality, if there is any, and report the same to OCC.
RSC & TPC shall also inspect OHE through CCTV camera of the following first train in the same line for any abnormality in the section, on observation of any abnormality, RSC/TPC immediately report the same to TC/OCC who in turn shall instruct RA/ETO to stop the Train.
If  no  apparent  problem  in  OHE  is  observed  by ETO/RA /TPC/RSC /  field  staff  of  RS / traction in (i) to (iii) above, normal services may be resumed.
If any visible problem is observed in OHE by ETO/RA/TPC/RSC/ field staff of RS / traction in (i) to (iii) above, action detailed in Case II shall be adopted.
## 3.3 Case II :- Problem in OHE is observed
## 3.3.1 For Non UTO Mode of Operation

## 3.3.1 For Non UTO Mode of Operation

(i) If any problem is reported/ observed in OHE as in 3.1.3(b) or 3.2.1(v) or 3.4.1(v) or otherwise, the train shall be moved as advised by RSC and TPC. Where ever Emergency power block is not required for OHE rectification and trains can be moved with Pantograph management or at reduced speed as per RSC/TPC advice, same shall be done.
(ii) If the problem is observed in OHE, TPC shall arrange for the rectification by OHE staff and if needed, emergency Power Block may be taken by the OHE staff. Only after fitness certificate by authorized OHE staff, that the said section of OHE is fit for movement of train, any train movement shall be undertaken. Any speed restriction, if required to be imposed in the affected section even after restoration, it shall be specifically mentioned in the fitness certificate given to OCC. If the movement of stalled Train is not possible due to OHE damage then traffic shall be regulated  using  single  line/short  loop  as  required.  The  passenger  of  stalled  train  between stations may be rescued as per rule no. 50 of MRGR-2020 .
## 3.3.2  In case of UTO Mode of Operation

## 3.3.2  In case of UTO Mode of Operation

(i) If any problem is reported/ observed in OHE as in 3.1.3(b) or 3.2.2 (v) or 3.4.2 (iv) or otherwise RSC and TPC shall decide whether Emergency power block is required for fault rectification or Train can be moved in UTO Mode with some speed restrictions.
(ii) In case RSC & TPC decides that emergency power block is required for OHE rectification TPC shall arrange emergency Power Block to be taken by the OHE staff.
(iii)  In case RSC & TPC decides that Train can be moved in UTO Mode with some speed restrictions TSR shall be imposed as per extant procedure.
(iv)  Only  after  fitness  certificate  by  authorized  OHE  staff,  that  the  said  section  of  OHE  is  fit  for movement of train movement (with or without speed restriction), any train movement shall be

## Introduction

undertaken. Any speed restriction, if required to be imposed in the affected section even after restoration, it shall be specifically mentioned in the fitness certificate given to TC/OCC.
## 3.4 Case III: Damage to Pantograph(s) is observed
## 3.4.1 For Non-UTO Mode of Operation:-

(i)
If  the  damage to pantograph is reported as in 3.1.3 (c) above or otherwise, at the station platform, the damaged pantograph(s) shall be lowered by Train Operator and shall be secured by RS/OHE staff ( Damaged Pantograph means the Pantograph which is neither in raised position nor in sitting position as illustrated in Figures attached at the Annexure A ) . The further train movement will be done only as per advice of RS/OHE staff. Special care should be taken before permitting any movement towards underground ROCS section due to considering its limited height.
If  the  movement  of  train  having  damaged  pantograph  is  not  possible  or  the  damaged pantograph cannot be lowered (pantograph entanglement) then that train shall not be moved till  authorized  by  RS  staff  for  movement.  TO  shall  operate the  isolating cock  of  damaged pantograph. Meanwhile traffic shall be regulated using single line/short loop as required. The passenger of stalled defective train between stations may be rescued as per rule no. 50 of MRGR-2020 .
(ii) Traffic Controller shall instruct TO of the adjacent line (wherever applicable) to observe the OHE of  other  line  by  driving  at  speed  not  more  than  25  kmph  for  two  stations  at  least,  from  the suspected location so as to enable TO to look for any abnormality in OHE. TO will report the status of OHE accordingly.
If  adjacent line TO reports normal status of OHE, the first two trains in the same line to be instructed to move at a speed not exceeding 10 kmph with front Pantograph lowered in the said section.

If  adjacent line TO reports normal status of OHE, the first two trains in the same line to be instructed to move at a speed not exceeding 10 kmph with front Pantograph lowered in the said section.
(iii) If it is not possible to get the OHE checked by adjacent line train, e.g. in tunnel, the following two trains entering in the same line should be instructed to move at speed not exceeding 10 kmph with front pantograph lowered in the said section to observe for any abnormality so that train can be stopped short of any abnormality, if there is any, and report the same to OCC.
(iv) If no problem is observed by Train Operators in (ii) or (iii) above, then following trains shall be moved at the speed of max 40 kmph till the fitness certificate for the reported section is given by OHE department.
(v) If  the  problem is observed in OHE by any of the Train Operators in (ii)  or  (iii) above, action detailed in Case II shall be adopted.
(vi) In case of damage in pantograph(s) is confirmed, TC shall immediately ask TO of previous 02 trains to have passed through the affected section, to check pantographs of their train at next platform for any abnormality. Subsequently, pantographs of previous two trains to have passed through the affected section shall also be checked by RS staff.
## 3.4.2 In case of UTO Mode of Operation

## 3.4.2 In case of UTO Mode of Operation

(i)
If  the  damage to pantograph is reported as in 3.1.3 (c) above or otherwise, at the station platform, the damaged pantograph(s) shall be lowered by RSC in line- 8/ by TC in Line-7 and shall be secured by RS/OHE staff ( Damaged Pantograph means the Pantograph which is neither  in  raised  position  nor  in  sitting  position  as  illustrated  in  Figures  attached  at  the Annexure A).
TC shall instruct nearest available RA/ETO to board (If already not on board) the train as per procedure and instruct to take charge. The further train movement will be done only as per

## Introduction

advice of RSC/TPC. Special care should be taken before permitting any movement towards underground ROCS section due to considering its limited height.

If  the  movement  of  train  having  damaged  pantograph  is  not  possible  or  the  damaged pantograph cannot be lowered (pantograph entanglement) then that train shall not be moved till authorized by RS staff for movement. RS Staff shall operate the isolating cock of damaged pantograph.  Meanwhile  traffic  shall  be  regulated,  as  required.  The  passenger  of  stalled defective train between stations shall be rescued as per rule no. 50 of MRGR-2020.
(ii) TC shall instruct nearest available RA/ETO to board (If already not on board) the following first train in the same line as per procedure and instruct to take charge & to move at a speed not exceeding 10 kmph with front Pantograph lowered in the said section to observe any abnormality so that train can be stopped short of any abnormality, if there is any, and report the same to OCC.
(iii) RSC & TPC shall also inspect OHE through CCTV camera of the following first train in the same line for any abnormality in the section, on observation of any abnormality, RSC/TPC immediately report the same to TC/OCC who in turn shall instruct RA/ETO to stop the Train.
(iv) If the problem is observed in OHE by any of the RSC/TPC/RA/ETO in (ii) or (iii) above, action detailed in Case II shall be adopted.

(iv) If the problem is observed in OHE by any of the RSC/TPC/RA/ETO in (ii) or (iii) above, action detailed in Case II shall be adopted.
(v) In  case  of  damage  in  pantograph(s)  is  confirmed,  TC  shall  immediately  arrange,  to  check pantographs of previous 02 trains which have passed through the affected section through the SC of next approaching station for any abnormality. Subsequently, pantographs of previous two trains to have passed through the affected section shall also be checked by RS staff.
## 4. Actions of RS & OHE staff to deal with the entangled pantograph(s)

All the action mentioned to be undertaken at the incident site shall be undertaken by RS/OHE staff only when train is discharged with passenger under provisions of power block.
4.1 The RSC, on getting the information about Pantograph entanglement shall inform PPIO, inspection in  charge  and  officers'  in  charge  of  the  concerned  depot  immediately  about  the  incident  duly mentioning site location including nearest OHE mast no., pantograph location and time. Similarly, TPC shall instruct OHE Team of concerned depot and/or nearby depot to reach at the site with necessary break down recovery material.
4.2 After getting information, inspection in-charge along with his team will arrange to rush to the site by road with all his tools and HV jackets as soon as possible. In case the incident location is closer to other sister depot, he will immediately arrange to place the request though PPIO of his depot to PPIO of nearest sister depot to immediately mobilize rescue/restoration team to incident site.
4.3 The senior most supervisor of the RS/OHE department on reaching the incident site shall first make a very careful note of all the relevant details pertaining to the incident (pantograph as well as OHE) and shall take photographs pertaining to the incident and shall arrange to make a sketch indicating the details.
If  both RS and OHE maintenance team reach the site, the supervisor of OHE team shall be the EPIC and he shall control the rescue work.
4.4 The power block granting and cancellation shall be done by EPIC as per extant procedure.
4.5 The securing of pantograph/restoration work shall be started only after getting the permission from the EPIC, about the power block.

4.4 The power block granting and cancellation shall be done by EPIC as per extant procedure.
4.5 The securing of pantograph/restoration work shall be started only after getting the permission from the EPIC, about the power block.
4.6 The EPIC after confirming that OHE is dead and earthed shall allow OHE and RS staff to climb on the roof of the train to secure the damaged pantograph.
4.7 EPIC  will  also  arrange  for  preservation  of  such  evidences  as  may  be  useful  subsequently  for investigating the cause of breakdown.
4.8 It will be ensured by RS maintenance team to operate the isolating cock of damaged pantograph after the train is withdrawn from revenue service.

## Introduction

4.9 RS/OHE maintenance team will secure the broken pantograph with manila/wire rope from the base frame of the pantograph in such a manner that it does not come in contact with OHE during the run.

4.10 RS maintenance staff will also collect all broken pieces of pantograph.
4.11 After completion of securing work, the EPIC will inform the OCC about the same.
4.12 OHE will be charged by TPC only after getting clearance from site as per power block as per extant procedure.
4.13 In case of damage to only one pantograph of the train, the movement of train may be permitted with other healthy pantograph with restricted speed and train may be stabled to the nearest siding or if possible in the depot.
4.14 After completion of restoration work and resumption of train services foot plating of complete section shall be done by OHE staff for ensuring healthiness of the OHE.
4.15 On completion of Rescue procedure of the train involved in the incident, the inspection in-change will submit a detailed report to PPIO/depot in-charge along with all the damage details/observations at incident site, photographs and problems encountered during the securing of pantograph/rescue of train.
4.16 After getting defective trains stabled in the depot, maintenance staff will plan the replacement of the pantograph as per pantograph replacement procedure.
4.17 After replacement of defective pantograph, the train will be stabled on IBL and after taking power block of that IBL, the contact pressure of replaced pantograph with OHE will be measured by the maintenance staff. After that the train will be tested on the test track as per the extant procedure for testing train on test track.
4.18 Joint inspection of train roof as well as OHE shall be organized duly recording all the evidences.

4.18 Joint inspection of train roof as well as OHE shall be organized duly recording all the evidences.
4.19 Roof  of  all  those  trains  which  have  passed  in  succession  prior  to  affected  trains  shall  also  be checked at the earliest in depot.
Safety  Precautions  to  be  undertaken  by  maintenance  staff  when  handling  damaged pantograph on main line
5.1 Before moving to the incident site, staff must take the Permit for "Access to Track" as per extant procedure.
5.2 While moving on the track staff must wear visibility jackets.
5.3 Before climbing on the train  roof,  it  must  be  ensured  that  power  block  has  been enforced  and discharge rods have been placed. The limits of power block shall be carefully noted.
5.4 The securing of the ladder to be used for climbing on the train roof must be ensured.
5.5 While climbing on the roof for securing broken pantograph, maintenance staff must be very careful as there may not be any support available to the safety belts.
5.6 While securing broken pantograph on roof of-the train, any tools, ladder must not infringe with other line and must be kept at a safe distance of 2 metre from the other charged line.

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This  Procedure  Order  describes  the  Rules  and  Regulations  to  be  followed  by  Staff  for emergency  evacuation  of  passengers  through  track  side  emergency  exit  door  in  via-duct section.

metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p1_3

text:
## 2.0 SCOPE

2.1 This Procedure Order contains the Procedures for Train-to-Track detrainment arising out of:-
(i) Traction Current Failures.
(ii) Failure of Rolling Stock and consequent Stalling of a Train in the Tunnel/viaduct or at a Station.
(iii)   Fire or Fusing in a Train stalled in the Tunnel/viaduct or at a Station.
(iv)  Any other Incident causing immobilization of the Train.
2.2 This Procedure Order is applicable to AEL.
2.3 This  procedure  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  the  Metro  Railways  General  Rules-2020, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.

## 3.0 GENERAL:-

3.1 In case of any untoward incident in underground section, priority should be given to evacuate passengers to the nearest station/ platform and evacuation of passengers through track side emergency exit should be carried out only if evacuation to station platform is found infeasible as last resort due to any reasons such as:
(i) Broken ROCS/FOCS
(ii) Earthquake
(iii)  Train Derailment
(iv)  Fire/Smoke at station
(v) Terrorist attack at station
(vi)  Structure collapse
(vii) Flooding etc.

3.3 Doors of these track side emergency exits are integrated with Fire Alarm System and BMS SCADA through electromagnetic locking arrangement (provided by E&M department) to meet security and safety concern.

## Introduction

3.4 The Track side emergency exit doors can be operated, controlled and monitored from BMS Workstation of concerned SCR (provided by E&M department) and Workstation of ASC/OCC (as a standby). Monitoring of above mentioned doors is also provided with Fire Alarm System of Concerned SCR.
3.5 Exit Doors of track side emergency exit are at Ground Level. The Door connects Staircase leading to track side emergency exit. Near track side emergency exit access door, emergency telephone  (to  contact  OCC),  ETS  and  fire  hydrants  are  provided.  Inside  the  track  side emergency  exit  Tetra  coverage,  CCTV  coverage  and  intercom  (at  mid-level  of  track  side emergency exit) are provided.
3.6 Appropriate luminous, reflective bilingual signages are provided by Revenue Cell/ Operation in each track side emergency exit shaft for guidance of passengers during evacuation. Caution boards and UP/DN line indication boards are also provided at track level doors. The inner ring of track side emergency exit is painted by Civil Department for easy identification of entrances from track side.
3.7 SM  of  all  adjacent  stations  of  track  side  emergency  exit  shall  ensure  that  all  Station Controllers and other selected Staff working at stations have visited the track side emergency exit  and  acquainted  themselves  with  the  surroundings  and  also  the  Pathway  from  the Staircase and the assurance regarding same has been taken.

text: ## 4.0 PROCEDURE FOR OPERATIONS OF ELECTROMAGNETIC DOOR LOCK:

metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p3_2

text: ## 4.1 To open the Trackside emergency exit door through SCR BMS Workstation:

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p3_3

text:
## 4.1 To open the Trackside emergency exit door through SCR BMS Workstation:

Door open command and door close command are provided for each trackside emergency exit door.  These  commands  are  available  in  Access  Control  System  (ACS)  graphics  of  BMS SCADA workstation.
When required, station staff shall select the door open command to demagnetize the door lock. The  door  will  get  open,  door  open  status  will  reflect  at  ACS  graphic  of  BMS  SCADA  work station and the hooter will blow in station control room, the same can be silenced from Fire PC or  FACP.  The  station  staff  shall  acknowledge  the  alarms  at  Fire  PC  and  SMS  SCADA workstation. After demagnetization of EM lock, door can be opened physically.
4.2 To open the Trackside emergency exit door (from inside) locally from concerned door: When required, the doors can be opened from door level also. To open the door from door level, press/break the glass of 'Emergency Door Release Unit' equipment installed near the door to release the electromagnetic lock. The door will get open, door open status will reflect at ACS graphic of SMS work station and the hooter will blow in station control room, the same can be silenced from Fire PC or FACP. The station staff shall acknowledge the alarms at Fire PC and SMS SCADA workstation. After demagnetization of EM lock, door can be opened physically.

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p3_4

text: ## 4.3 To  close  the  Trackside  emergency  exit  door  through  SCR  BMS  Workstation  (in  case opened through SCR):

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p3_5

text:
## 4.3 To  close  the  Trackside  emergency  exit  door  through  SCR  BMS  Workstation  (in  case opened through SCR):

After ensuring physical closing of door, click the particular door close command from BMS Workstation  to magnetize the door  lock. Reset Fire  PC/FACP  to  ensure the door locking. The energization of magnetic lock can be ensured, if door close status will reflect at ACS graphic of SMS SCADA workstation and no fire hooter blows after fire alarm system is reset.

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p3_6

text: ## 4.4 Closure of door if power supply fails:

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p4_0

text:
## 4.4 Closure of door if power supply fails:

In the case of power supply failure to the Electromagnetic lock, door lock will demagnetize automatically. Door open status will reflect at ACS graphic of SMS SCADA work station and the hooter will blow in station control room. The station staff shall acknowledge the alarms at Fire  PC  and  SMS  SCADA workstation. Power supply is to be resumed by station staff to magnetize the door.

text: ## 5.0 PROCEDURE FOR EVACUATION

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p4_3

text:
In any Emergency Situation, when the Train is stalled on UP or Down Line in via-duct area and  Detrainment  of  Passengers  becomes  inevitable,  this  can  be  planned  from  Train  to  a point-of-  safety  using  Trackside  Emergency  exit  door.  The  decision  to  use  Trackside Emergency exit door for emergency evacuation shall be taken by TC only after approval as per  extant  Standard  Operating  Procedures  in  vogue  regarding  Passenger  Detrainment  in viaduct, Deciding Evacuation route, TVS (if required) & Lighting (if required).
5.1 The  TC  will  stop  the  following  train  at  the  station  in  rear  immediately  and  will  stop  train movement on adjacent line prior to permit passenger evacuation on foot. The TC will regulate other  trains  in  the  unaffected  area to  provide  optimum train  service  by  introducing  short  loop operation.  The  TC  will  block/lock  the  en-route  points  in  the  path  of  passenger  evacuation  for ensuring that points in the route of detrainment are not altered while detrainment is in progress.
5.2 TC shall inform ASC at concerned OCC, to switch on Tunnel Lights and TVS (if required) of both tunnels  (UP  &  Down)  between  concerned  stations,  through  central  or  station  level  BMS  to ensure proper lighting and ventilation.
5.3 During evacuation from train, Passengers are to be clearly informed by Train Operator about the Evacuation Route using track side emergency exit door.

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p4_5

text:
5.3 During evacuation from train, Passengers are to be clearly informed by Train Operator about the Evacuation Route using track side emergency exit door.
5.4 TC/OCC shall instruct SM/SC or other nominated Staff of concerned station to position himself at relevant track side emergency exit door.  OCC/MB-1, OCC/MB-2 & OCC/SHPK shall liaison with  each  other,  while  instructing  SM/SC  to  ensure  firmed-up  Communication  and  proper Coordination.
5.5 Upon  getting  Instructions  from  TC/OCC,  SM/SC  or  other  nominated  staff  shall  give  the command  for  opening  of  electromagnetic  door  lock  and  immediately  rush  to  the  track  side emergency exit door , along with 'On Duty' E&M Staff deployed at Station and other Staff for assistance. SM/SC or the nominated Staff will carry Key (if required), Tetra Set, First Aid Box, Torch (during night) and Loud Hailer and move towards the track side emergency door by road or through tunnel/viaduct as situation permit.
5.6 Evacuation  from  Train  towards  track  side  emergency  door  shall  be  commenced  by  TO  in consultation  with  TC  and  TO  shall  direct  Passengers  towards  track  side  emergency  door Location.
5.7 If required more assistance, TC shall instruct SM/SC of other involved/adjacent stations to reach at track side emergency door.
5.8 TC/OCC shall also arrange attendant for Emergency Services at relevant track side emergency door at Ground Level (if required).

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p4_6

text:
5.7 If required more assistance, TC shall instruct SM/SC of other involved/adjacent stations to reach at track side emergency door.
5.8 TC/OCC shall also arrange attendant for Emergency Services at relevant track side emergency door at Ground Level (if required).
5.9 SM/SC  or  other  nominated  Staff  at  track  side  emergency  door  shall  receive  /  guide  the Passengers, render First Aid (if required), coordinate with Emergency Services and keep OCC informed. SM/SC or other nominated Staff shall count the number of evacuated Passengers and relay it to OCC either through Emergency Telephone placed at track side emergency door or by other available means of Communication.

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p4_7

text:
## Introduction

5.10  TC/OCC shall tally the number of Passengers relayed by SM/SC or other nominated Staff with the number relayed by the TO of the affected train.

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p1_0

text:
## Introduction

5.11  TC/OCC will inform emergency services such as CATS, Fire services for rendering help in evacuation of sick, aged, infirm and person with disabilities.
5.12  After all Passengers have been evacuated, SM/SC or other nominated Staff shall inspect the affected area to ensure that all Passengers have been evacuated and confirm the same to TC/OCC.
5.13  Special  Arrangements  shall  be  made  for  evacuation  of  sick,  aged,  infirm,  and  person  with disabilities.
5.14  On resumption of services, Train  Operators  of  first train  in  UP  &  Down  directions  between affected stations shall operate trains cautiously with restricted Speed of 15 KMPH looking out for any Passenger's/ma t erial (if any).
5.15  The  area  of  track  side  emergency  exit  door  at  CH-13692  falls  in  Army  area  near  Mehram Nagar.  The  SM/SCs  of  Delhi  Aero  city  Station  will  move  to  this  gate  by  road  as  situation permit. The Army official will permit entry after certification.
5.16  A feeder bus (if available) will be provided (from LMC - Last Mile Connectivity) to carry the evacuated passengers to the nearest station/location.
5.17  The area of track side emergency exit door at CH-6470 falls near Budha Garden and easily accessible by road for evacuation of passengers.
5.18  Evacuation shall be also monitored from CCTV by Station/ OCC.

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p5_1

text: ## 6.0 JOINT INSPECTION OF TRACK SIDE EMERGENCY EXIT:-

metadata.source: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 19.1 SC-19A (Rev 00) Evacuation from Track side emergency exit_p5_2

text:
## 6.0 JOINT INSPECTION OF TRACK SIDE EMERGENCY EXIT:-

(i) Joint  inspection  of  all  track  side  emergency  exit  shall  be  done  yearly  b y AM/Mgr.  level (Operation,  Telecom,  E&M,  and  Civil  department)  for  their  condition  and  fitness  for  safe evacuation.  AM/Mgr  (Operations)  of  concerned  line  shall  coordinate  for  the  joint  check  of track side emergency exit, a joint inspection report of the same may be forwarded to all Dy. HODs concerned.
(ii)  Joint  inspection  of  all  track  side  emergency  exit  shall  be  done  on  Quarterly  basis  by Supervisor  level  staff  (operations,  Telecom,  E&M  and  civil  department)  for  their  condition and fitness for safe evacuation. Station Manager of adjacent station shall coordinate for the joint  check of track side emergency exit. A joint inspection report shall be forwarded to all AM/Mgr. concerned.
(iii) In  addition  to  above,  concerned  wings  may  conduct  inspections  at  higher  frequency/  at regular intervals to keep their system ready to use.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 40 (Rev. - 03)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR RESETTING OF PAB/ PECU/ PAEH/ PAD/PIC IN RS-1, RS-2, RS-3, RS-10, RS-13 AND CAF TRAINS

## 1. INTRODUCTION:

This procedure deals with the resetting and overriding the activated Passenger Alarm Button (PAB)/Passenger  Emergency  Communication  Unit  (PECU)/Passenger  Alarm  Emergency Handle  (PAEH)/Passenger  Alarm  Device (PAD)/Passenger  Intercom  Communication (PIC) from active cab through TIMS/PIS Panel/MOU which has been provided in RS1/ RS2/ RS3/ RS10/RS13 & CAF trains.

## 2. SCOPE:

2.1 This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railway General Rules 2020 and its  amendment,  Safety  Circulars,  Station  Working  Orders,  Operating  &  Troubleshooting Manual of concerned RS and other Instructions issued, from time to time for the working  of trains.
2.2 This procedure shall be applicable to all Lines and staff associated with resetting/overriding of  PAB/  PECU/  PAEH/  PAD/PIC  in  RS1,  RS2,  RS3,  RS10,  RS13  and  CAF  trains respectively running on main line.
## 3. GENERAL INFORMATION:
## 3.1  RS1/RS13 Trains:

## 3.1  RS1/RS13 Trains:

If PEA of any car operated, train shall not move after stopping and EB gets applied each time when motoring command initiated.
If train is stopped in mid-section and EB is getting applied when motoring command is given then PEA can be overridden through TIMS as per extant procedure.
Train movement shall not be affected if another PEA/s operates in the same car  whose one  or more PAB is already in override state.
If PEA of any other car operated, train shall not move after stopping and EB gets applied each time when motoring command initiated. In this case PEA can again be override through TIMS if train stop in mid-section.
PEA overridden through TIMS shall not be operational till the physical resetting.
No audio alarm is generated in the cab if any other PEA of same car is operated when one PEA of the car is already in override position.
## 3.2  RS2 Trains:

## 3.2  RS2 Trains:

In  case  of  PECU  operation,  train  movement  shall  not  affect  till  the  opening  of  train doors (saloon/cab door) and traction block shall apply after opening of train  doors.
Resetting  of  PECU  can  be  done  from  PIS  panel  available  in  driving  cab.  After  that Traction Block shall release and train can move normally.
Affected PECU shall be operational after resetting it from Cab as PAB of RS2 train is of self-releasing type that does not demand physical resetting.
## 3.3  RS3 Trains:

## 3.3  RS3 Trains:

If  PAEH  of any car is operated, train shall not move after stopping and ATP EB gets applied each time when motoring command initiated.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR- 08G (Rev.-01)

## 1. INTRODUCTION

The entire mainline of metro network of line-7 is equipped for ATP/ ATO/ UTO operation from MKPR to SVVR (including sidings) and Depot (MKPD and VND). This Procedure Order covers the process of UTO operation on Line - 7.

## 2. SCOPE:

This Procedure Order applies for Train Operation in UTO Mode in Line-7.
This Procedure Order shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 & Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules, 2022, relevant Safety Circulars& Special Instructions in vogue.
## 3. UTO MODE:

## 3. UTO MODE:

3.1. The entire mainline of metro network of line-7 is equipped for ATP/ ATO/ UTO operation from MKPR to SVVR (including sidings) and Depot (MKPD and VND).
## 3.2. UTO could be available if:

## 3.2. UTO could be available if:

Route is set
Train is initialized in ATP
Target speed is available in ATP Mode.
Train ID is available (Note: UTO would also be available without Train ID but in this case every  time  Route  has  to  be  set  by  TC/DC/SC  (CATS/LATS/VDU)  until  Train  ID  is  not available).
## 3.3. UTO mode shall be enabled only:

## 3.3. UTO mode shall be enabled only:

All safety Switches are in normal position
If train is at zero speed
TBC is at 'B-Max' position
Target speed is available in ATP mode.
Mode selector is in AUTO position of both cabs and UTO is selected from ATS/ DMI of active cab.
EB reset (if required) to be performed remotely by TC/DC or by TO/RA/ETO from DMI after selection of UTO mode

## 4. RESPONSIBILITY OF THE SIGNALING DEPARTMENT:

Signaling Department shall ensure to provide UTO fitness of train to PPIO who will further endorse the 'UTO Fit' on train log book along with the train fitness certificate as per extant procedure.
## 5.1. Procedure for Selection of UTO mode

## 5.1. Procedure for Selection of UTO mode

TO/RA/ETO Shall Put mode selector in AUTO in both CABs.
UTO icon (right  side  of  DMI  screen)  needs  to  be  selected  from  DMI  by  TO/RA/ETO  after confirmation by TC/DC/SC or remotely from ATS after confirmation of 'Train Located' icon on DMI by TC/DC/SC in consultation with TO/RA/ETO.
After UTO selection TO/RA/ETO has to verify symbol 'UTO' is displayed on DMI at current mode position.

## Introduction

TO/ RA/ ETO needs to release EB from DMI or remotely by TC/SC/DC (if required).

If the train is properly berthed, then train will automatically depart after finish of DWELL Time and closing of doors. If the train is not properly berthed even after Automatic Jog back/ forward, then the train needs to be moved in ATP/ REV mode upto NSP for proper berthing and then stop  and  select  UTO  mode,  reset  EB  remotely  or  from  DMI  (if  required)  and  shall  inform TC/SC/DC.
5.2. When the train has stopped within stopping window, platform side doors will be enabled and saloon doors & PSD will be opened automatically. The saloon and PSD doors will be closed automatically at the end of dwell time and the train will depart automatically.
5.3. If train doesn't start in UTO mode even after finish of dwell time, then OCC shall give start train command  manually.  If  train  doesn't  take  start  command  then  the  train  may  be  moved  in ATP/ATO/RM mode (whichever available) as per extant procedure. After stopping train at next station, TO/RA/ETO shall select UTO mode after confirmation from OCC as per procedure (refer para 5.1 above).
5.4. In  case train stops after or before designated NSP in UTO, then following procedure shall be followed.
Train itself perform 'jog back/jog forward' operation after 6 seconds of complete stand still, if it stops +10 m overshoot and -10 m undershoot from NSP to align itself with the NSP. If after 'jog back/jog forward' operation, train is not able to align itself with NSP following procedures are to be followed.

If a Train stops short of its normal Stopping point in UTO mode.
TO/RA/ETO shall drive the train in ATP mode up to the Normal Stopping Point (NSP) and open train doors and PSD. Close door after platform service. Change mode to UTO as per procedure (refer para 5.1 above).
In case Target speed is not available, TO/RA/ETO shall drive the train up to the designated Normal Stopping Point in degraded mode, as per extant procedure.
After aligning the train with the designated Normal Stopping Point only, the TO/RA/ETO shall  'Open'  and  'Close'  the  train  doors  &  PSD  and  proceed  further  as  per  extant procedure.
If train stops beyond its Normal Stopping Point, then-
TO/RA/ETO shall inform TC/OCC and seek for instructions.
Preferably, TC/OCC shall advise the Train Operator to move the train up to next station after making announcements for passenger information that service at this station is not possible due to technical reasons and passengers desirous to alight at this station are requested to de-board at next station. The Train Operator shall also express regrets for the inconvenience caused to the passengers.
However, if TC/OCC, on permission from CC/OCM, decides to reverse the train depending upon the existing conditions or if train is the last revenue train of the day, the following steps shall be taken by Train Operator & TC;
TO/RA/ETO shall verify if REVERSE is enabled on DMI and seek instructions from TC.

TO/RA/ETO shall verify if REVERSE is enabled on DMI and seek instructions from TC.
The TC shall  ensure  vacancy  of  platform  track  section,  all  PSDs  are  detected  as closed and following train if any has been ensured as stopped. After ensuring these aspects, TC shall authorize the TO/RA/ETO to reverse the train in REV/SCS-cutout (as applicable) mode up to NSP/Stopping window under exchange of private numbers.

## Introduction

After getting authorization from TC/OCC, TO/RA/ETO shall Blow 'Horn' & Drive the Train  in  reverse  direction  in  REV/SCS-cutout  mode  (as  applicable)  up  to  Normal Stopping Point/stopping window.

## Introduction

After stopping the train at Normal Stopping Point/stopping window, TO/RA/ETO shall open the doors as per extent procedure and perform platform service. After closing of train doors and PSD, TO/RA/ETO shall put SCS in normal position (if operated) and wait for 2 min until both VATC boot-up and inform TC and seek further instructions from OCC for train movement in RM/ATP/ATO/UTO mode as per availability.
If the train can't be reversed, then passengers may be allowed to disembark from the train by emergency escape door.
NOTE:- On main line ONLY DDSC siding is equipped with the facility of conducting UST (UTO Self Test) including Sleep/Wake Up process hence only DDSC Siding can be used as stabling location for UTO mode trains.
## 6. TRAIN SHOULD NOT BE DRIVEN IN UTO MODE IF:

## 6. TRAIN SHOULD NOT BE DRIVEN IN UTO MODE IF:

6.1. If any safety switch is operated to cutout.
6.2. Whenever it is required to move the train with reduced traction power.
6.3. Whenever it is required to move the train with caution or/ and with speed limit which is not imposed through the system.
6.4. Whenever slip/slide fault is activated in train.
6.5. ETS/BLS is operated
6.6. Rail facture is reported.
6.7. Total interlocking failure
6.8. Kite thread is reported.
6.9. PTW issued.
6.10. Earthquake
6.11. High wind

## 4.2 Train moving on up gradient with less power (Single / double / triple unit operation or train coupled with other train:

## 5.  ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF STAFF
## 5.1 Train Operator

## 5.1 Train Operator

(i) When train is stationary. TO shall keep the Master Controller at braking position.

## 5.1 Train Operator

(ii) On up gradient, TO shall be more careful. TO shall avoid coasting and keep TBC at maximum powering to avoid any possibility of roll back.
(iii) On up gradient, if it is required to bring the train at standstill due to signal or any other reason, TO shall drive the train from standstill using Pmax (maximum powering). If train is to start on gradient and with failure of tractive Power effort of one unit, 'high tractive effort to be initiated.
(iv) TO shall release 'high tractive effort' once gradient is negotiated.
## 5.2 Traffic Controller

## 5.2 Traffic Controller

(i) TC to ensure that if the train is running with reduced power/brakes or coupled train, the route from main line to depot is set & locked up to the stabling location or the route is set &locked and clear up to next platform on mainline. Only then, TC shall instruct TO for train movement to negotiate the rising gradients.
(ii) TC to ensure that if the train is running with reduced power/brakes or coupled train, there is sufficient gap between this train and train following it.
(iii) TC shall ensure that in case of movement of combined consist or divided train, preceding trains are protected by creating sufficient gap by diverting the route of concerned train by movement of points as far as practical. It is to be noted that divided train shall not roll back.
## 5.3 Depot Controller

## 5.3 Depot Controller

(i) DC to ensure that if the train is running with reduced power/brakes or coupled train, the route from main line to depot is set & locked up to the stabling location. Only then DC instruct TO for train movement to negotiate the rising gradients.
(ii) DC to ensure that if the train is running with reduced power/brakes or coupled train, there is sufficient gap between this train and train following it.
## 5.4 Station Controller

## 5.4 Station Controller

(i) If interlocking control of said section is local, Station Controller shall perform the role of TC.

## Introduction

(ii) SC  shall  make  regular  announcement  at  P/F  if  a  train  with  reduced  braking  power  is passing and ensure the safety of passenger by advising to stay behind the yellow line on platform, if PSD not available. However, if PSDs are available at the stations, same shall remain closed.
## 6.  ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINE: -

## 6.  ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINE: -

6.1.  In case of failure as detailed under Para 4.4 (Sr No 2),
In case bogie isolation is required, RSC shall give suitable command to isolate required BIC.
After bogie isolation, TCMS shall apply speed restriction of 50 kmph, subsequently Signalling system shall apply speed restriction of 50 KMPH TC/OCC shall instruct nearest available TO/RA/ETO to board the train at next platform.
6.2.  In case of failure as detailed under Para 4.4 (Sr No 3 &4)
TC/OCC shall immediately apply suitable/relevant commands to bring the train to stop.
In case RA is not on board, TC shall instruct the nearest available TO/RA/ETO to board the train as per extant procedure and take charge of the train.
6.3.  TC/CHC-OCC  shall  instruct  IC  for  announcements  inside  the  trains  to  keep  passengers informed
6.4.  RSC/OCC shall also instruct nearest Line RS staff to reach the faulty train.
6.5.  Further movement shall done as per extant procedure detailed under Para 4.4
## 7.  STEPS IN CASE OF ROLLBACK DETECTION IN UTO MODE: -

When Train is in UTO mode, VATC system (Signalling System) applies EB on detection of roll back as detailed in Para-3.0.
The following steps shall be followed in case of rollback detection in UTO Mode of operation: -
7.1. TC/OCC shall release the EB from ATS using suitable commands.
7.2. If the EB gets released, then the train shall depart normally.
7.3. If the EB does not gets released from OCC, then TC/OCC shall instruct TO/Roving Attendant to take charge of the train.
In case RA is not on board, TC shall instruct the nearest available TO/RA/ETO to board the train as per extant procedure and take charge of the train.
7.4. TO/Roving Attendant shall put mode selector in ATP mode and check if the EB release option is available. If yes, TO/Roving Attendant shall acknowledge the EB and move the train in ATP mode as per procedure in vogue.
7.5. If  the  EB  still  does  not  get  released,  TO/Roving  Attendant  shall  move the  mode  selector position to FORWARD and check the status of EB.
7.6. If the EB gets released, TO/Roving Attendant shall drive the train in RM Mode as per extant procedure.
7.7. If the EB is still applied, TO/Roving Attendant shall move the mode selector to STANDBY position, operate SCS switch to cut-out position and put it back in normal position as per extant procedure.
7.8. If EB  gets released,  TO/Roving Attendant shall drive train in available mode  ie UTO/ATO/ATP/ROS/RM as per extant procedure

7.8. If EB  gets released,  TO/Roving Attendant shall drive train in available mode  ie UTO/ATO/ATP/ROS/RM as per extant procedure
7.9. If the EB does not get released and the train is in mid-section, TO/Roving Attendant shall move  the  train  up  to  NSP  of  next  station  in  SCS  cut-out  mode  with  mode  selector  in FORWARD position as per extant procedure.
7.10. If  the  EB  gets  released  at  the  NSP,  then  the  train  shall  depart  in  available  mode  ie UTO/ATO/ATP/ROS/RM as per extant procedure.
7.11. If the EB is still applied after following above steps, TO/Roving Attendant shall inform the OCC and further ATP staff shall attend the train as per the guidance of SGC/OCC.
7.12. The Train shall be withdrawn from revenue services.

## 1. Introduction

The purpose of the procedure order is to delineate roles and responsibility of Train Operators, OCC staff,  Station  staff  and  other  metro  staff  for  carrying  out  prompt  and  safe  passenger evacuation from an immobile train in order to minimize hardship to the passengers.

## 2.  Scope

This Procedure Order is shall be applicable when a metro train becomes disable/immobile in the block section and it cannot be moved on its own power or cannot be even rescued with another assisting train either due to failure of Rolling stock or Rigid Over Head Catenary/ OHE system  or  obstruction  on  Permanent  way  system  due  to  its  own  failure  or  for  any  other technical reasons. Detrainment of passengers from such immobile/disable train shall be  train to walkway, carried out as per the procedure order detailed in the subsequent paras.

## 5. Authority for detrainment

The  Train  Operator  must  make  all  out  efforts  to  run  the  train  to  the  next  station  to  avoid detrainment between stations wherever feasible. However, if it is not possible, the detrainment shall  take  place  with  the  authority  of  Chief  controller/Traffic  Controller  in  consultation  with HOD/O or Dy HOD/O. In the case of extreme emergency, when the safety of passengers is at risk and Communication with the Operation Control Centre (OCC) has failed, the TO shall try to  contact  OCC  by  any  viable  means  of  communication  including  DMO  mode  of  Radio, Emergency  Telephone,  or  mobile  phone  of  any  passenger.  If  communication  can  not  be established  with  OCC,  the  TO  shall  initiate  passengers  evacuation  on  foot  towards  station ahead so that the stalled train acts as a protection. TO shall initiate passenger's evacuation on foot. In case a train is in tunnel for more than 10 minutes and TO is not communicating/responding, then a team of two persons from rear station should be sent to train to assist/rescue, along with appropriate means of communication, Square Key and swipe card and TC in this case shall stop train movement on both tracks i.e. including adjacent track also

## PART-II: DETRAINMENT OF PASSENGERS DUE TO EXPLOSION &/OR FIRE

This procedure order deals with detrainment of passengers from a train due to EXPLOSION & FIRE in all standard gauge sections/lines of Line-5 and Line-6 . The system is not designed for bomb explosion. The threat of Bomb etc is to be dealt with security measures. This is a contingency plan,  proposed with intent, that what best can be done  under the circumstances. This  procedure  order  should  be  read  in  conjunctions  with  General  Rules  and other relevant existing safety circulars.

## 1. Introduction

The purpose of the procedure order is to delineate roles and responsibility of Train Operators, OCC staff,  Station  staff  and  other  metro  staff  for  carrying  out  prompt  and  safe  passenger evacuation from an immobile/disable train in order to minimize hardship to the passengers.

## 2.  Scope

This Procedure Order shall be applicable when a train becomes immobile/disable due to EXPLOSION & FIRE in the train which and it cannot be moved further or rescued by assisting train. Detrainment of passengers from such immobile/disable train to walkway shall be carried out in event of the following:
2.1. Bomb blast causing fire and smoke and train gets stalled in either elevated or underground tunnel section between two stations in of BG line.
2.2. Fire & Fusing- train stalled in section between two stations in BG line including underground tunnel sections.

The  point  of  relative  safety  in  case  of  fire/EXPLOSION  causing  fire  and/or  smoke  is outside of the  train  as  compared  to  the  inside  of  train.  Therefore,  TC  may  immediately initiate  the  process  of  de-boarding  whenever  an  emergency  situation  involving  fire  and EXPLOSION is reported by TO of affected train. The smoke, being light in weight, has tendency  to  move  to  higher  gradient.  The  passengers  shall  be  guided  to  keep  a handkerchief or other cloth, preferably wet, to cover their noses and advance by bending towards  the  nearest  cross passage or  the  station  on  either  side  in  the  event  of  smoke coming in their passage. The passengers can be guided to use cross passages to get in to another non affected tunnel during such evacuations.
The trains in SG lines (RS-3 trains) are equipped with 02 emergency side doors on both sides  a  car  and  are  marked  by  yellow  and  black  stripes.  The  passengers  can  be evacuated  through  the  designated  emergency  side  door/doors  on  to  the  side  walkway which can support passengers' evacuation.
Configuration in which TVS is to be operated will be critical and shall be decided by CHC and ASC under guidance of senior most person in charge of control office present over there.
Tunnel lights of the affected section will be switched on immediately.
Station staff shall be  sent  immediately  from  the  station  to assist  in  passenger's evacuation.

## PART-II: DETRAINMENT OF PASSENGERS DUE TO EXPLOSION & FIRE

This procedure order deals with detrainment of passengers from a train due to EXPLOSION &/OR FIRE in DMRC-Airport Line. The system is not designed for bomb explosion. The threat of Bomb etc is to be dealt with security measures. This is a contingency plan, proposed with intent, that what best can be done under the circumstances. This procedure order should be read in conjunctions with MRGR 2020 and other relevant existing safety circulars.

## 1. Introduction :

The purpose of the procedure order is to delineate roles and responsibility of Train Operators, OCC  staff,  Station  staff  and  other  metro  staff  for  carrying  out  prompt  and  safe  passenger evacuation from an immobile/disable train in order to minimize hardship to the passengers.

## 2.  Scope

This  Procedure  Order  shall  be  applicable  when  a  train  becomes  immobile/disable  due  to EXPLOSION & FIRE in the train which and it cannot be moved further or rescued by assisting train. Detrainment of passengers from such immobile/disable train to track shall be carried out in event of the following:
2.1. Bomb blast causing fire and smoke and train gets stalled in either elevated or underground tunnel section between two stations in of DMRC -Airport line.
2.2. Fire & Fusing - train stalled in section between two stations in DMRC-Airport line including underground tunnel sections.

The station  controller  shall  clear  the  concerned  platform  from  waiting  passengers  and,  if necessary, stop incoming passengers, he shall position himself along with security staff on the platform to receive the arriving passengers, count them as they arrive and render first aid if required or provide necessary help.

text:
## Introduction

The  physically  challenged  and  sick  passengers  will  be  assisted  to  evacuate  to  the designated station by Station staff or by volunteering other able bodied co passengers.

metadata.chunk_id: 41.3 SC 41C (Rev-01) Detrainment & evacuation of passenger in AEL_p1_0

text:
## Introduction

The TO, station staff or other metro staff available in the train will make all out efforts to count the number of passengers exiting from the emergency door/doors and the final count  will  be  tallied  with  the  count  by  the  SC  of  receiving  station.  If  both  the  counts match, the evacuation is complete.
In case the number of passengers could not be counted or the combined count of TO, station staff or other metro staff do not tally with the count of the SC after the completion of passengers evacuation, the first train, to move in this section on both directions, shall be allowed to run at restricted speed not exceeding 15 KMPH, TO shall be on look out for  people  on  track  and  be  prepared  to  stop  short  if someone  is  there  and report  the same to OCC.
The SM/SCs of other stations will take all adequate measures for crowd control. The SCs of other stations and TOs of other trains will regularly make announcements at their stations  and  in  their  trains  regarding  delay,  arrival  departure  of  trains  and  change  in traffic plan if any.

text:
## 7.3. Traction Power Supply

Traction power supply may not be switched off normally during traffic hours, except in following conditions;
For prevention of arcing.
Serious damage to the OHE system.
Detrainment works need to be carried out within 02 meters of OHE system.
Detrainment involves movement of personnel within 02 meters of OHE system.

metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p2_2

text:
## 1.  SCOPE

This procedure is applicable for the movement of trains from main line to depot or vice versa or within the depot. It defines the roles and responsibilities of staff and actions to be taken by them during  the  train  movement.  This  Procedure  Order  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro Railway General Rules 2020 and Special Instructions in vogue.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p1_3

metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p2_4

text:
## 2.  OBJECTIVE

2.1. Ensuring safe movement of trains from main line to depot or vice versa or within the depot.
2.2. Ensuring un-ambiguous communication during authorization.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p2_5

text: ## 3.  PROCEDURE FOR ENTRY FROM MAIN LINE TO DEPOT

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p2_6

text:
3.1. The  PPIO  shall  provide  the  plan  to  Depot  Controller  (DC)  in  advance  for  stabling  of particular train set on a particular track/berth according to their maintenance schedule.
3.2. Traffic Controller (TC)/Station Controller (SC) shall inform Depot Controller (DC) about train no. & train set no. whenever a train is to be sent to depot from main line with exchange of private no.
However if trains to be sent to depot are scheduled trains as per time table in vogue, single private no shall be exchanged for all scheduled trains before sending first train to depot.
3.3. TO shall stop the train at mainline exit signal and inform TC/SC about train ID, Train Set, & it's  location.  TC/SC  shall  inform  Train  Operator (TO) that  route  for the train  is  set  and  on getting proceed indications at main line exit signal, TO shall move the train up to depot entry signal.
3.4. If traffic plan changes due to any emergency for depot bound train & destination of the train has been changed, TC/SC shall give the message to the Train Operator under exchange of private no.
3.5. Territory/jurisdiction  of  OCC  is  up  to  depot  entry  signal  whereas  that  of  DCC  starts  from depot entry signal. In case of any fault appears in train at transfer track after departure of train from main line exit signal till the depot entry signal, OCC shall be the guiding authority.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p2_8

text: 3.6. TO  shall  stop  the  train  at  depot  entry  signal  and  select  depot  group  mode  on  train radio/tetra. He shall then inform the train no., train set no., driving cab no., depot entry signal no. & aspect to DC and seek authorization.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p2_9

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p2_10

text:
## 3.7.

DC shall set route for the train from depot entry signal up to stabling location as far as possible for the arrival of the train to depot.
If it is not feasible to set the complete route from depot entry signal to stabling location, he may set partial route upto or between intermediate shunt signals. However, in that case fresh authorization shall be required before moving the train further.
3.8. DC, while giving authorization to TO for movement shall clearly mention the train no., signal no. & aspect and destination up to which it is authorized and shall offer his private number.
3.9.
TO shall acknowledge the message by repeating, DCs private no., his train no., train set no.,  signal  number  &  aspect  and  destination  up  to  which  it  is  authorized.  He  shall  then provide his private number to DC and make the entry in the private number book.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p2_11

text:
## Introduction

TO must not exchange the private number with DC if the signal is at ON/blank aspect. If DC intends to allow the train to pass the signal at danger/blank, the TO must ensure that the DC  has  explicitly given authorization to pass  the concerned  depot  signal  at danger/blank.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p1_0

metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p3_1

text:
## 3.10.

After exchanging the private no. with DC at depot entry signal, TO shall select depot entry mode (ATP/ROS/Depot RM) and proceed further upto the authorized intermediate shunt signal or stabling location.
In  case authorization is given by DC upto intermediate shunt signal, TO shall invariably stop the train short of the signal and seek authorization from the DC under exchange of a fresh set of private numbers.
In case if any other enroute depot signal is at danger/blank, TO shall invariably stop the train short of the signal, inform DC and seek authorization under exchange of a fresh set of private numbers.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p3_2

metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p3_3

text:
## 3.11.

TO shall proceed into depot cautiously as directed under the control of depot signals with a  speed  not  exceeding  25kmph  and  observing all  speed  restriction  placed  from  time  to time.
While  entering  depot,  the  TO  shall  observe  the  speed  restriction,  obey  depot  signals, various  instructions  boards  and  verbal  instruction  of  the  DC  given  on  radio  or  other communication system and respect all other operational procedures.
3.12. After stopping of train at stabling location, Train Operator shall stable the train as per extant procedure.

text: ## 4.  PROCEDURE FOR EXIT FROM DEPOT TO MAIN LINE

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p3_5

text:
## 4.  PROCEDURE FOR EXIT FROM DEPOT TO MAIN LINE

4.1. Rolling Stock Staff in the PPIO shall ensure that whole train length is lying in the Electrified zone  and  shall  then  endorse  the  fitness  of  the  train  on  the  concerned  log  book  as  per Procedure.
4.2. PPIO, in consultation with DC shall plan, as far as possible, the operational ID No. to trains fit  for  revenue service  in such  a  way  that no two trains are planed back to back at short interval  from  same  location  or  adjacent  locations  that  have  same  points  en  route  unless there is an exigency.
4.3. DC  shall  inform  TC/SC,  the  Train  sets  along  with  its  scheduled  operational  ID  to  be despatched for main line in advance with exchange of private no. However, if trains  to be sent for main line  are  schedule train as per time table in  vogue, single private no shall be exchanged between DCC and TC/SC before sending first train to main line.
4.4. Before proceeding to the main line, TO shall perform various pre-departure checks as per procedure in vogue.
4.5. On  completion  of  pre  departure  checks,  TO  shall  inform  DCC  that  train  is  ready  for departure along with train no., train set no., driving cab no. & stabling location and seeks authorization from DC.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf

text:
## 4.6.

Depot  Controller  shall  set  the  route  for  the  train  from  stabling  location  to  depot  exit signal/main line entry signal as far as possible.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p3_8

## Introduction

If  it  is  not  feasible  to  set  the  complete  route  from  stabling  location  to  depot  exit signal/main  line  entry  signal,  he  may  set  partial  route  upto  or  between  intermediate shunt signals. However, in that case fresh authorization shall be required before moving the train further.

text:
## Introduction

4.7. DC, while giving authorization to TO for movement shall clearly mention the train no., signal no. & aspect and destination up to which it is authorized and shall offer his private number.
4.8.
TO shall acknowledge the message by repeating, DC private no., his train no., train set no., signal number & aspect and destination up to which it is authorized. He shall then provide his private number to DC and make the entry in the private number book.
TO must not exchange the private number with DC if the signal is at ON/blank aspect. If DC intends to allow the train to pass the signal at danger/blank, the TO must ensure that the DC has explicitly given authorization to pass the concerned depot shunt signal at danger/blank.

metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p4_2

text:
## 4.9.

After  exchanging  the  private  no.  with  DC  from  stabling  location,  TO  shall  select ATP/ROS/Depot RM mode and proceed further upto the authorized intermediate shunt signal or depot exit/main line entry signal.
In case authorization is given by DC upto intermediate shunt signal, TO shall invariably stop the train short of the signal and seek authorization from the DC under exchange of a fresh set of private numbers.
In case if any other enroute depot signal is at danger/blank, TO shall invariably stop the train short of the signal, inform DC and seek authorization under exchange of a fresh set of private numbers.
4.10. Territory/jurisdiction of DC is up to main line entry signal whereas that of OCC starts from main line entry signal. In case fault appears in train before the main line entry signal, DC shall be the guiding authority.
4.11. TO shall proceed cautiously as directed under the control of depot signals up to depot exit signal with a speed not exceeding 25 kmph.
4.12. TO shall stop the train at depot exit signal/main line entry signal and change the mode of train radio/tetra to main line, inform TC/SC about train ID, train set and its location.
4.13. TC/SC shall set route for the train for main line and authorize train operator to enter main line on exchange of private number.

text: ## 5.  TRAIN MOVEMENT IN DEPOT

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p4_4

text:
## 5.  TRAIN MOVEMENT IN DEPOT

5.1. Train  Operator  should  be  vigilant  and  cautious during  train  movement  in  depot  and  s/he should be able to 'STOP' the train short of any obstruction or 'ELECTRIC ENGINE STOP BOARD'.
5.2. RS Department shall ensure that SBL/IBL indication & numbering boards (bi-directional), speed boards in washing line, retro reflective cross marks on the entry gates of workshop lines, pit wheel lathe, blow down plant, any other building are placed where ever required.
5.3. RS Department shall ensure that no work activity in train from inside or outside takes place till the complete stabling of the train.
5.4. Civil Department shall ensure the availability of boarding/de-boarding platforms in stabling lines  and  provision  of  retro  reflective  tapes  on  buffers,  point  no.  plates  for  all  noninterlocked points at suitable height perpendicular to the track and fouling mark board.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p4_5

text:
## Introduction

5.5. Signalling department shall ensure provision of point no. plates for all interlocked points at suitable height perpendicular to the track, signal no. plates for all shunt signals at suitable height perpendicular to the track, arrow mark on the shunt signals to indicate concerned line, ATC begins/ends board, stopping reverse marker boards, stopping boards.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p1_0

text:
## Introduction

5.6. Electrical  department  should  ensure  sufficient  lighting  in  SBL/IBL  &  on  the  pathway  and Electric engine stop boards.
5.7. Telecom department shall provide master clocks in SBL/IBL and communication system.

text: ## 6.  PRECAUTIONS TO BE TAKEN IN CASE OF POWER BLOCK/SHADOW POWER BLOCK DURING DEPOT ENTRY/EXIT OF A TRAIN TO/FROM MAIN LINE

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p5_2

text:
6.1 DURING POWER BLOCK IN DEPOT WHICH INVOLVES TRANSFER TRACK :-
(i) All the blocks in depot during revenue/non revenue hours involving transfer tracks, will be granted by DC duly informing TC under exchange of private number.
(ii) In  case  of  requirement  of  power  block  in  depot  involving  transfer  track,  it  shall  be responsibility  of  TPC  to  inform  TC  in  writing  (in  OHE  Charge/Discharge  Register) regarding  the  requirement  before  granting  of  power  block  and  the  same  shall  be acknowledged by TC.
(iii)     After granting the power block TPC shall inform TC in writing (in OHE Charge/Discharge Register)  and  DC  under  exchange  of  private  number  (through  tetra  /  intercom) regarding granting of power block and the same shall be acknowledged by TC& DC.
(iv)    TC shall inform concerned SC (having the control of interlocking of depot entry/exit line) under exchange of private number regarding Power Block in depot entry/exit including the affected route/routes explicitly.
(v)        TPC  shall  clearly  indicate  the  section  of  OHE  w.r.t.  mast  number  and  affected  route which is in power block condition and affected lines/transfer track (whichever applicable) wherein train movement is not feasible & restricted due to the power block.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p5_4

text:
(vi)    Concerned EPIC shall employ appropriate measures to protect/isolate the section under power  block/EP  as  per  extant  procedure.  TC/SC  &  DC  shall  also  isolate  such route/routes  by  using  signaling  system  and  in  case  of  failure  of  signaling  system TC/SC/DC  shall  execute  the  isolation  as  per  extant  procedure  of  manual,  so  as  to prevent/isolate any train movement in the section under power block.
(vii) Before cancellation of power  block, TPC  shall inform TC  in writing  (in  OHE Charge/Discharge  Register)  and  DC  under  exchange  of  private  number  (through tetra/intercom)  regarding  cancellation  request  of  power  block  and  the  same  shall  be acknowledged by TC and DC.
(viii) After canceling the power block TPC  shall inform to TC  in writing (in  OHE Charge/Discharge Register) and DC under exchange of private number (through tetra / intercom) regarding cancellation of power block and the same shall be acknowledged by TC & DC.
(ix)   TC/SC before setting the route of the train from third platform/main line up to the depot entry signal (under its jurisdiction) shall ensure that no power block is in effect in the planned route of the train.

metadata.source: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 35.1 SC-35A (Rev-02) PO for movement of the train in Depot Entry-Exit_p5_5
