## EMERGENCY EVACUATION FROM STAIRCASE AT MID TUNNEL SHAFT IN VARIOUS LINES

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION

This  Procedure  Order  describes  the  Rules  and  Regulations  to  be  followed  by  Staff  for emergency  evacuation  of  passengers  by  climbing  up  evacuation  shaft/mid  tunnel  shaft  in underground section.

## 2.0  SCOPE

2.1 This  Procedure  Order  contains  the  Procedures  for  Train-to-Walkway/Train-to-Track detrainment arising out of: -
Traction Current Failures.
ii) Failure of Rolling Stock and consequent Stalling of a Train in the Tunnel or at a Station.
iii)   Fire or Fusing in a Train stalled in the Tunnel or at a Station.
iv)  Any other Incident causing immobilization of the Train.
2.2 This Procedure Order is applicable to Line-2, 6, 7 and AEL.
2.3 This procedure shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 & Metro Railways General (Amendment)  Rules, 2022, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
2.4 For UTO Mode of Operation:- Wherever, Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, is to be read as Train Operator (TO) / Roving Attendant (RA) / Emergency Train Operator (ETO).

## 3.0  GENERAL:-

3.1 In  case  of  any  untoward  incident  in  underground  section,  priority  should  be  given  to evacuate  passengers  to  the  nearest  station/  platform  and  evacuation  of  passengers through mid-tunnel shaft should be carried out only if evacuation to station platform is found infeasible as last resort due to any reasons such as:-
Broken ROCS
ii) Earthquake
iii)  Train Derailment
iv)  Fire/Smoke at station
Terrorist attack at station
vi)  Structure collapse
vii) Flooding etc.
3.2 The Mid Tunnel Shaft / Evacuation shaft is provided at Cross Passage of UP & Down lines in the section where intra station distance is comparatively more for evacuation by climbing up the evacuation shaft in tunnels. Different locations and their specifications are mentioned in Annexure-A.
3.3 The tunnel ventilation system equipments installed at mid-shaft as defined in Annexure A can  be  operated,  controlled  and  monitored  from  OCC.  The  Station  Level  Control, comprising Work Station & Ventilation Control Panel, is located in SCR.
3.4 Exit Doors of Mid-shaft open at Ground Level. The Door connects Staircase leading to Cross Passage. In tunnel, near cross passage access door, emergency telephone (to contact OCC), ETS and fire hydrants are provided. Inside the mid tunnel shaft Tetra coverage, CCTV coverage and intercom (at mid-level of mid tunnel shaft) are provided.

## Introduction

3.5 Access door of Mid Tunnel Shaft are secured by Electromagnetic Lock, at Ground and Track level as defined in Annexure-A provided by E&M Department.

## Introduction

3.6 Appropriate  luminous,  reflective  bilingual  signage  along  with  Step  Count  indications starting from ground level are provided by Revenue Cell/Operation in each mid tunnel shaft for guidance of passengers during evacuation. Caution boards and UP/DN line indication boards are also provided at track level doors. The inner ring of tunnel is painted by Civil Department for easy identification of Mid Tunnel Shafts Entrances from track side.
3.7 SM of all adjacent stations of mid shaft shall ensure that all Station Controllers and other selected  Staff  working  at  stations  have  visited  the  Mid  Tunnel  Shaft  location  and acquainted themselves with the surroundings and also the Pathway from the Staircase up to the Cross Passage in the Tunnel and the assurance regarding same has been taken.
## 4.0  PROCEDURE

## 4.0  PROCEDURE

In any Emergency Situation, when the Train is stalled on UP or Down Line in Tunnel and Detrainment of Passengers becomes inevitable, this can be planned from Train to a pointof-safety using Walkways/Track as applicable up to Cross Passage and then to the Ground Level through the Mid Tunnel Shaft. The decision to use mid tunnel shaft for emergency evacuation  shall  be  taken  by  TC  only  after  approval  as  per  extant  Standard  Operating Procedures in  vogue  regarding  Passenger  Detrainment  in Tunnel,  Deciding  Evacuation route, Ventilation & Lighting, Stopping Train Movement and Operation of TVS (if available) shall be followed, besides the Procedure to use Mid Shaft, described below:-

The TC will stop the following train at the station in rear immediately and will stop train movement  on  adjacent  line  (in  the  affected  section)  prior  to  permit  passenger evacuation  on  foot.  TC  will  regulate  other  trains  in  the  unaffected  area  to  provide optimum train services as far as possible by implementing different traffic regulation measures.  The  TC  or  concerned  SC  (if  signaling  control  is  available  at  local)  will block/lock  the  enroute  points  in  the  path  of  passenger  evacuation  for  ensuring  that points in the route of detrainment are not altered while detrainment is in progress.
ii) Whenever passenger evacuation through mid tunnel shaft is required or opening of mid tunnel  shaft  door  is  required,  UTO  mode  of  Train  Operation  shall  be  suspended  in affected section by TC/OCC till normalization of situation.
4.2 TC shall inform ASC at concerned OCC, to switch on Tunnel Lights and TVS of mid tunnel  shaft  (as  defined  in  Annexure  A)  and  of  both  tunnels  (UP  &  Down)  between concerned stations, through central or station level BMS and ensure proper lighting and ventilation in Tunnel and Mid tunnel shaft.
4.3 During evacuation from train, Passengers are to be clearly informed by Train Operator about the Evacuation Route through Mid Tunnel Shaft.

4.3 During evacuation from train, Passengers are to be clearly informed by Train Operator about the Evacuation Route through Mid Tunnel Shaft.
4.4 TC/OCC shall instruct SM/SC or other nominated Staff of concerned station to position himself at Mid Tunnel Shaft. OCC/MB-1, OCC/MB-2 & OCC/SHPK shall liaison with each other,  while  instructing  SM/SC  to  ensure  firmed-up  Communication  and  proper Coordination.
4.5 Upon getting Instructions from TC/OCC, SM/SC or other nominated staff shall give the command for opening of electromagnetic door lock and immediately rush to the Mid Tunnel Shaft Location, along with 'On Duty' E&M Staff deployed at Station and other

## Introduction

Staff for assistance. SM/SC or the nominated Staff (who is in possession of concerned Mid Shaft key) shall carry Keys of the Mid Shaft, Tetra Set, First Aid Box, Torch (during night) and Loud Hailer and move towards the mid shaft by road or through tunnel as situation permit.

## Introduction

4.6 Evacuation from Train towards Mid Shaft shall be commenced by TO in consultation with TC and TO shall direct Passengers towards Mid Shaft Location.
4.7 In case further assistance is required, TC shall instruct SM/SC of other involved/adjacent stations to reach at mid tunnel shaft.
4.8 TC/OCC shall also arrange attendant for Emergency Services at Mid Shaft Location at Ground Level (if required).
4.9 SM/SC  or  other  nominated  Staff  at  Mid  Tunnel  Shaft  shall  receive  /  guide  the Passengers, render First Aid (if required), coordinate with Emergency Services and keep OCC informed. SM/SC or other nominated Staff shall count the number of evacuated Passengers and relay it to OCC either through Emergency Telephone placed at Cross Passage or by other available means of Communication.
4.10 TC/OCC shall tally the number of Passengers relayed by SM/SC or other nominated Staff with the number relayed by the TO of the affected Train.
4.11 TC/OCC will inform emergency services such as CATS, Fire services for rendering help in evacuation of sick, aged, infirm and person with disabilities.
4.12 After all Passengers have been evacuated, SM/SC or other nominated Staff shall inspect the  Stair  case  leading  to  Cross  Passage  to  ensure  that  all  Passengers  have  been evacuated and confirm the same to TC/OCC.
4.13 Special Arrangements shall be made for evacuation of sick, aged, infirm, and person with disabilities.
4.14 On resumption of services, Train Operators of first train in UP & Down directions between affected stations shall operate trains cautiously with restricted Speed of 15 KMPH looking out for any Passenger's/material (if any).
## Note:-

## Note:-

(i) Joint  inspection  of  all  mid  shafts  shall  be  done  yearly  by  AM/Mgr.  level  (Operation, Telecom,  Safety,  E&M,  and  Civil  department)  for  their  condition  and  fitness  for  safe evacuation. AM/Mgr (Operations) of concerned line shall coordinate for the joint check of mid  shaft,  a  joint  inspection  report  of  the  same  may  be  forwarded  to  all  Dy.  HOD concerned.
(ii) Joint inspection of all mid tunnel shafts shall be done on Quarterly basis by Supervisor level staff (operations, Telecom, Safety, E&M and civil department) for their condition and fitness for safe evacuation. Station Manager of adjacent station shall coordinate for the joint  check  of  mid  shaft.  A  joint  inspection  report  shall  be  forwarded  to  all  AM/Mgr. concerned.
(iii)  In addition to above, concerned wings may conduct inspections at higher frequency/ at regular intervals to keep their system ready to use.
Guidelines for operation of electromagnetic lock provided at emergency exit doors of mid tunnel shaft are placed at 'Annexure-B.'

'Annexure - B'
## OPERATION OF ELECTROMAGNETIC LOCKS PROVIDED AT EMERGENCY EXIT DOORS OF MID TUNNEL SHAFTS OF LINE-06, 07 & AIRPORT LINE.
## 1.0 General:

## 1.0 General:

1.1 There are emergency exits which have been provided in mid-shafts of Line-06, 07 & Airport Line in order to provide safe exit for the commuters in case of any emergency.
1.2 Electromagnetic locks integrated with fire alarm system are provided at doors of these emergency exits for access control from inside/outside of mid-shaft through Fire Alarm Control Panel (FACP) or by local provision at respective door. The details of doors where electromagnetic locks are provided are given in Annexure-A.
1.3 Electromagnetic door should normally be in locked condition i.e. in close condition.
## 2.0 Procedure for opening of doors.

## 2.0 Procedure for opening of doors.

2.1 To open the emergency exit access door through FACP: One push button for each door is provided at concerned FACP. When required, staff shall press the push button to demagnetize the door lock. The hooter will blow indicating door open alarm and the same can be acknowledged from concerned Fire PC or FACP. Now the door can be opened physically.
2.2 To  open  the  emergency  exit  access  door  (from  inside)  locally  from  concerned door: When required, the doors can be opened at door level. To open the door at door level, break the glass of 'Emergency break glass unit' which is installed near the door to release the electromagnetic lock. The hooter will blow indicating door open alarm and the same can be acknowledged from concerned Fire PC or FACP. Now, the door can be opened physically.
## 3.0 Procedure for closing of doors

## 3.0 Procedure for closing of doors

3.1 To close the emergency exit access door through FACP (in case opened through FACP): Press  the  respective  door's  pushbutton  in  FACP  to  close  the  door  and  give system reset from concerned Fire PC or FACP . The energization of magnetic lock of respective door can be ensured if no hooter blows after system resetting.
3.2 To close the emergency exit access door after power supply failure: In the case of power  supply  failure  to  the  Electromagnetic  lock,  door  lock  will  get  demagnetize automatically.  The hooter  will  blow  indicating  door  open  alarm  and  the  same  can  be acknowledged from concerned Fire PC or FACP. Power supply is to be resumed by concerned staff to magnetize the door again.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 25 (Rev.05)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR MOVEMENT OF TRAINS IN MAIN LINE DURING FAILURE OF INTERLOCKING SYSTEM

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order covers the Responsibilities for Safe and efficient Movement of Revenue Trains on a Line or a part of it, in the event of Total Failure of Interlocking System.

## 2.0 SCOPE

2.1 This Procedure Order is applicable to all lines and the DMRC Staff working on the Main Line and  actively  participating  in  the  Running  of  Trains  including  the  Signalling  Maintenance  Staff responsible for the proper Up-keep of the Interlocking System.
2.2 This Document should be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and its  amendment,  Station  Working  Orders  in  vogue  and  other  Special  Instructions  issued,  from time to time in this connection.
2.3 For  UTO Mode of Train Operation: Wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it  is to  be read as Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
## 3.0 GENERAL

## 3.0 GENERAL

3.1. A Failure of Interlocking may have one or more of the following scenario:
(i) Failure of Line Side Signals - may become blank or display 'Red' / 'On' aspect.
(ii) Failure of Interlocking as a whole.
(iii) For all Lines Except AEL: Total failure of ATS Work stations and VDU/CCIP at Station Control Rooms and OCC.
(iv) For AEL Only: Total Failure of ATS Work stations at Station Control Rooms and OCC with non-availability of ARC.
3.2 Authorisation for Train Movement in Non-ATP Mode shall be given by OCC/TC as per extant procedure. As in such a situation the ATS view will not be available to SC at station.
3.3 OCC / CHC shall inform Security Controller and DMRP/ State Police for mobilizing Security Staff for Crowd Management.
3.4 OCC  /  CHC  shall  take  different  traffic  regulation  measures  for  Train  Regulation,  subject  to availability of suitable Crossovers and favorable Traffic conditions.
3.5 OCC /  CHC  shall  ensure  that  Central  Announcement  is  made  at  all  Stations  in  the  affected Section  informing  Passengers  about  the  likely  delay  in  Train  Services.  Station  Controllers  at Stations in the affected Section shall monitor such Announcements being made at their Stations and  additionally  make  such  Announcements  regularly  at  their  Stations  for  the  guidance  of Passengers.
## 4.0 RESPONSIBILITIES: -
## 4.1 OCC / Traffic Controller (TC):

## 4.1 OCC / Traffic Controller (TC):

(i) OCC/TC shall inform all the TOs, in affected Section, regarding the failure of Interlocking System and not to move their Trains from Platforms unless Authorised.

## Introduction

(ii) OCC/TC shall inform the Chief Controller to take Charge of the Incident Management and Coordination.

(iii) OCC/TC shall obtain the current location of all the Trains in the affected Section or may nominate a Staff to obtain the same.
(iv) A  miniature  Control  Chart  shall  be  used  by  TC  to  record  the  position  of  Trains  in  the affected Section, i.e. at Stations, between Stations and in Terminal Sidings. This chart shall form the basis of further Train regulation by the TC.
(v) OCC/TC shall suspend Reversal of Trains at Intermediate Terminals, if any in the affected Section.
(vi) OCC/TC shall obtain an Assessment of the likely Fault Rectification Time from Signalling System  Controller  and  shall  advise  Stations  and  Train  Operators  about  likely  delay  in restoration of Normal Services.
(vii) OCC/TC will inform Station Controllers of the Interlocked Stations in the affected Section to clamp and padlock all Points on the Main Line in the desired Position. Station Controllers of the Terminal Stations shall be asked to set up Manual Terminal Operation as per instruction of TC/OCC.
(viii) On  receiving  the  confirmation  from  the  concerned  Station  controllers  that  all  the  Points have been clamped and padlocked and a Manual Terminal System (where required) has been set up at the Terminal, OCC/TC shall authorize the TOs to move their Trains selecting ROS mode / RM Mode of Operation and observing a maximum Speed of 25 Kmph, with the readiness  to  stop  short  of  any  obstruction.  A  Train  shall  be  allowed  to  move  only  if  the Section including the Platform of the next Station is 'Clear'.

(ix) TC or any other Staff, nominated by the Chief Controller shall make the announcements in affected  Stations  from  OCC  or  the  OCC/TC  shall  instruct  the  concerned  SCs  to  make proper  Announcements. These Announcements shall be for the guidance of Passengers with regard to System Status, likely delays and to update them the likely time of Restoration of Normal Services.
(x) The  Signalling  System  Controller  in  OCC  shall  advise  the  concerned  Supervisors  and Officers  for  Fault  Rectification.  Traffic  Controller  shall  inform  the  OCM,  Dy.  HOD/O  and HOD/O about the Incident and the action so far taken by him. OCM, on getting information shall arrive in the OCC and take over the Charge of Incident Management.
(xi) OCC/TC shall advise Security Controller to mobilize DMRP/State Police /CISF & Security Staff to assist Station Staff in the Crowd Control, where required.
(xii) OCC shall,  at  regular  intervals,  update  all  concerned  of  the  likely  Time  of  restoration  of Normal  Running.  For  this  Chief  Controller  can  take  help  of  TC  or  any  other  designated Staff.

(xiii) During  manual  point  operation,  no  train/vehicle  movement  shall  be  allowed  /  authorized over  a  point  which  is  being  operated  manually  either  through  individual  operation  from workstation  /panel  or  mechanically  at  site  unless  the  staff  carrying  out  manual  point operation  has  assumed and  communicated relative  position  of  safety  and  has  confirmed secured status of point."
## 4.2 Train Operator:

## 4.2 Train Operator:

(i) When the TO, working under Cab Signalling Mode, does not get the Proceed Command within  sixty  second,  TO  shall  immediately  report  the  matter  to  OCC  /  TC,  indicating complete details like the Train ID and its exact Location, Signal Aspect, Failure in Train (if any) and ask for further Instructions.

## 4.2 Train Operator:

(ii) When advised by OCC/TC of the Fault Condition & possibility of likely delays in the Service, TO shall inform the Train Passengers the fact of the occurrence of Technical Failure and likely delays to be encountered in the Service. TO shall also update the Passengers with the current Status, as received from TC or SC.
(iii)  On receipt of Authorization from OCC/TC or SC (as the case may be), the TO shall work the Train, following the prescribed Rules & Procedures for the Incident Situation.
(iv)  Train Operators shall report their Arrival / Departure Timings at each Station of the affected section to the OCC/TC for recording on the Manual Control Chart and for effecting Train Regulations, as may be necessary in the Incident Situation.
## 4.3 Station Managers / Station Controllers:

## 4.3 Station Managers / Station Controllers:

(i) Becoming aware of the Interlocking  Failure  due to  any  one  of  the  reasons  mentioned  in Para '3.0', or when informed by the OCC about it, the SM/SC shall alert Security at their Station and DMRP/ State Police about the likely delays and the Need for Crowd Control at the Station, particularly so at the Platform Level.
(ii) SM/SC at Stations, where the Interlocking has failed shall clamp and pad lock the Points as instructed  by  OCC/TC and confirm the position of  Points  by  individual  point  No.  and the Position thereof, under the exchange of Private Numbers.
(iii)  SM/SC will give Authority to Proceed to TOs in written or by exchanging private number with TO, as per existing Procedures in vogue and as instructed by OCC/TC.
(iv)  SM/SC will keep OCC informed of the effects of Train delays, including the overcrowding at the Station and Platform and take necessary action as per OCC/TC's Instructions regarding Crowd  Control,  which  may  include  Stopping  the  Sale  of  Tickets,  Stopping  Entry  to  the Station and Granting of Refund etc.
(v) In  the  event  of  failure  of  Communication,  duties  of  OCC  shall  devolve  upon  SCs  of  the Interlocked Stations.
## 5.0 TRAIN REGULATION: -

## 5.0 TRAIN REGULATION: -

5.1 In cases where the Failure is localized over a part of the Network, there is bound to be a mismatch between the two portions of the Line - the portion of Line capable of allowing Normal Speed Operation of the Trains and the affected portion, where a Speed Limit of 25 Kmph has been imposed.
5.2 This  Situation  shall  call  for  appropriate  Train  Regulation  to  avoid  Congestion  on  the affected  portion.  Such  a  Regulation  may  become  all  the  more  necessary,  if  there  is  an intervening Interchange Station with the other Line operating under Normal Conditions.
5.3 In  the  prevailing  Situation,  sizeable  Traffic  may  develop  on  the  Partially  Disabled  Line causing heavy overcrowding at certain Stations. Situation can be partly answered by taking recourse  to  Turn  Back  /  Short  Loop  Operation,  subject  to  the  availability  of  suitable

## Introduction

Crossover Connections and favourable Traffic Conditions. Decision in this regard shall be judiciously taken in the OCC in consultation with OCM and advised to all concerned.
## 6.0 CROWD MANAGEMENT:

## 6.0 CROWD MANAGEMENT:

6.1 If  the  Failure  causes  or  likely  to  cause  the  build  up  of  Crowd  on  a  Platform,  the  Station Controllers  in  consultation  with  OCC  shall  take  following  actions  to  reduce  the  Flow  of Passengers to the Platforms by:
(i) Making an Announcement, appealing to the Passengers to remain in the Concourse, till further Advice.
(ii) Stopping some or all of the Inwards Escalators / Lifts.
(iii)  Changing some or all of AFC Gate Modes in 'Incident Mode'.
(iv)  Instructing  Token  Vending  Operators  to  either  vend  Tokens  slowly  or  cease  selling  of Tokens.
(v) Restrict entry into the Station.
6.2 If despite all these measures taken, the Crowd build up is likely to become unmanageable and the Failure is likely to get prolonged then, in consultation with OCC, Passengers may be advised to leave the Station and Station Entrances may be closed. If station is closed for Passengers, it should be adequately displayed on PIDS and announced regularly using PA System.
6.3 When the Train Services are restored,  the restrictive  measures may  be  progressively  or completely  removed  as  instructed  by  OCC,  depending  upon  the  Level  of  Train  Services available.
## 7.0 INTRODUCTION OF 'SHORT LOOP' OPERATION ON THE UN-AFFECTED PORTION:

## 7.0 INTRODUCTION OF 'SHORT LOOP' OPERATION ON THE UN-AFFECTED PORTION:

'Short Loop' Operation shall enable running of Trains at Time Table intervals. Precautions to be taken before introducing such 'Short Loop' Operation should include the following:
## 7.1 Advance notice:

## 7.1 Advance notice:

Advance  Notice,  through  PIDS  /  PAS,  shall  be  given  to  the  Passengers  that  due  to  some Technical Failure, the Trains shall get reversed from an Intermediate Point. The Notice about the change in Pattern of Train Services and ensuing Turn back / Short Loop Operation shall thereafter  be  regularly  announced  for  the  benefit  of  Passengers,  till  resumption  of  Normal Services.
7.2 Short Loop Operation shall be started only with the approval of HOD/O, Dy. HOD/O, OCM.
7.3 It shall be ensured that the Tokens are issued / sold up to the Revised Destination only.
7.4 SM/SC  shall  ensure  that  the  Announcement  with  respect  to  Change  in  Pattern  of  Train Services,  and  the  Change  of  Platform  at  Terminal,  is  made  for  the  Passengers  waiting  in Concourse and at other places at the Stations including concerned Platforms.
7.5 SM/SC shall also put the Visible Barriers in the path of Platforms not in use, as the case may be.
## 8.0 REFUND OF FARE / REVALIDATION OF TICKETS: -

## 8.0 REFUND OF FARE / REVALIDATION OF TICKETS: -

Adequate arrangements shall be made for Refund of Fare / Revalidation of Tickets in case of Service Suspension / Short Loop Operation / Train delays in accordance with the Business Rule in vogue.
## 9.0 MANUAL TERMINAL OPERATION: -

9.1 Manual Terminal Operation is a method of controlling  a  Terminal  Interlocking,  whereby  the predetermined position of Points is clamped & padlocked and the Position of one point called the  Manual  Control  point  (MCP)  is  manned,  clamped  and  pad  locked  for  each  Train Movement.
9.2 The Manual Control Point at the Terminal Station is required to be manned by the SC on duty equipped  with  Portable  Radio,  Hand  Signal  Flag  /  Tri-colour  Torch,  Crank  handle/point operation rod, duplicate point keys, Private No. & Authority to Proceed Books. The Duties of SC shall be:
To inform the OCC/TC under the exchange of Private Numbers that all other Points except the Manual Control Point have been clamped & padlocked, as required for Manual Terminal Operation and as per Instructions of OCC / TC.
SC will display a Red Hand Signal during the day and Red Light during the Night to the Incoming Train.
SC  will  set,  clamp  and  pad  lock  the  Manual  Control  Point  in  desired  Position  for  the admission of a Train and shall inform the same to OCC / TC under the Exchange of Private Numbers and authorize TO to proceed as per extant procedure. On being authorized, Train Operator shall move cautiously and shall stop the Train short of the Points to verify that the Points are set in the intended Direction of Movement for which he has been authorized.
Each time before the Train Movement, SC shall keep himself at a Safe Distance.

Each time before the Train Movement, SC shall keep himself at a Safe Distance.
After the Terminating Train has cleared the Points, SC will set the Manual Control Point in the desired direction, clamp and pad lock for the Dispatch of the Train, and shall inform the same to OCC / TC under the Exchange of Private Numbers and authorise TO to proceed as  per  extant  procedure.  On  being  authorized  Train  Operator  shall  move  cautiously  and shall  stop  the  Train  short  of  the  Points  to  verify  that  the  Points  are  set  in  the  intended Direction of Movement for which he has been authorized.
Figures, illustrating the Position of Points during Manual Terminal Operation at a Terminal Interlocking for Turn Back Operation are placed as Annexure - 'A'.
9.3 Since the Station Yard during this period is treated as Non-interlocked, Station Controller of Terminal Station shall ensure that there is only one Train Movement at a time.
In  case  of  a  Terminal  Station  where  Rear  Crossovers  are  used  for  Manual  Terminal Operation, the following Train shall leave the Platform for reversal only after the previous Train has cleared the Siding and is berthed on the Platform for Departure.
In  case  of  a  Terminal  Station  where  Front  Crossovers  are  used  for  Manual  Terminal Operation,  the  following  Train  shall  leave  preceding  Station  Platform  only  when  the previous Train has departed from the Terminal Station and is continuing its journey.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 33 (REV.-08)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR RESCUE OF A REVENUE IMMOBILISED TRAIN

## 1. INTRODUCTION:

This  Procedure  Order  details  with  the  Responsibilities  of  the  concerned  Metro  Staff  and  the Methodology and Precautions to be followed by them in rescuing a Defective Train, which has been immobilized in the Section.

## 2. SCOPE:

2.1 This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 & Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules, 2022, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
2.2 Speed limits prescribed in this JPO are applicable for Train to Train rescue.
DEFECTIVE TRAIN: Defective Train is a Train which is immobile i.e.
3.1 The one having no Traction Power due to Defective Pantographs or VCB not Closed and / or no means available for generating further compressed air.
3.2 The one having Emergency Brakes / Service Brakes applied on all Cars and these are not getting released.
3.3 Unbraked Train:A train in which no brake is working including pneumatic brake either due to any fault or due to isolation of BIC (where Electro Pneumatic Isolation Cock (EPIC) isolation is not possible).
## The Defective Train does not include a Derailed Train (in-capable of being moved).

## The Defective Train does not include a Derailed Train (in-capable of being moved).

If a Train stalls between Stations due to the loss of Overhead Traction Power, the actions of the Train Operator (TO), OCC & other Staff shall be governed by MRGR 50 (2).
If a Train stalls between Stations due to a Failure in the Track, the TC / OCC shall seek confirmation from the P. Way Official In-charge of the Section and if the Track cannot be given 'Fit' within 15 minutes, the Procedure detailed in MRGR 50 (3) shall be adopted.
If the Train is immobile and the Fault cannot be rectified within 15 minutes, the TC/CHC/OCC shall take decision for Rescue Operation in consultation with HOD or Dy.HOD/Operations. However, if concerned department declares the train as disabled before 15 minutes then process for rescue of immobile train shall be initiated immediately. In addition, TC/CHC/OCC shall initiate steps to decongest the affected Line adopting relevant Train Regulation Strategy.
Rescue Operation of defective train, with Passengers On-board or without Passengers shall be decided by the TC/OCC based on the following guidelines:
## 7.1 Defective Train:

## 7.1 Defective Train:

(i) If the Defective Train is at a Platform, the Passengers shall be de-boarded at the Platform. If the defective train is stalled in section between stations then Train to Train Rescue shall be done.
(ii) In case of poor/no Ventilation or insufficient Lighting in the Defective Train or rescue of the passenger from defective train is not feasible by an assisting train then, all the passengers shall be de- boarded from train towards the nearest Station as per extant procedure, after ensuring that there is no Train Movement on the adjacent Track.
(iii) If Electro-Pneumatic Isolation Cock (EPIC) is not able to be isolated due to limited access on any Section/Line, then the rescue process will be carried out by RS department and decision to evacuate passengers from the train will be taken by RSC based upon the extent of braking available in the defective train.
## 7.2 Assisting Train:

## 7.2 Assisting Train:

(i) If the Assisting Train is located between the Defective Train and the Station, the Rescue Operation can be conducted with the Passengers in the assisting train.

(ii) If the Assisting Train is at or approaching the Platform, the Passengers shall be de- trained from the assisting train and then the Rescue Operation shall be conducted.
In case, it is decided to rescue the Train with Passengers, necessary Announcement shall be done by the Train Operator (TO) to the Passengers to hold tight in the event of any jerk to the Train. After successful Coupling Operation, on arrival at next Station the Passengers shall be de-trained from both Defective and Assisting Trains.
In case of a Train stuck in Underground Section for more than 02 minutes, TC/OCC shall advise ASC to run TVS in Congestion Mode or any appropriate Mode.
In  case  of  De-trainment  of  the  Passengers  from  the  Train  to  Track  or  Train  to  Walkway  in underground Sections, the TC/OCC shall advise the ASC to switch-on all Tunnel Lights in the affected Section and plan the operation of TVF according to movement of evacuation.
In case of De-trainment of the Passengers from the Train to Track or Train to Walkway (as per Rolling Stock), extant procedure pertaining to the same shall be followed.
Assisting Train shall be decided by the CHC/OCC, depending upon the Location of the Defective Train  shall,  thereafter,  plan  for  Push/Pull  operation  as  per  feasibility/availability  of  appropriate location shall also be decided by CHC/OCC.
Additional assisting train may be planned by the CHC/OCC for boarding of passengers of defective train when it is not possible for de-boarded passenger to walk.

Additional assisting train may be planned by the CHC/OCC for boarding of passengers of defective train when it is not possible for de-boarded passenger to walk.
In case of rescue operation of immobile train, concerned Chief Controller /OCC shall decide the talk group for communication during rescue operation as per extant procedure (SC-31). OCC shall designate an OCS (Officer in Charge Site) to establish a positive single point control at the scene. The OCS shall be the Operations supervisor at the scene. If no supervisor is present then the assisting train operator shall be appointed OCS. If desirable, SC of nearest station shall provide PPE for the TO of defective train.
The Defective Train shall be coupled with the Assisting Train, as per the extant Procedure and moved to the nearest Siding or Depot appropriately under authorization of TC/OCC .
## 16. STEPS FOR RESCUE OF DEFECTIVE UNBRAKE TRAIN:-

## 16. STEPS FOR RESCUE OF DEFECTIVE UNBRAKE TRAIN:-

After consulting OCC, De-board all the passengers from Defective train through emergency doors towards decided station as per extant procedure.
Unbraked defective train will be moved under Engineers Possession where a person not less than JE/RS shall be EPIC, who will remain in the defective train cab and position himself at such location from where couplers of defective/assisting train could be observed (so that he can ensure normalization of BIC in case of any abnormality).
Appropriate  number  of  Rolling  Stock  Staff  with  tetra  set  shall  board  inside  the  unbrake defective train and position themselves at different places so that they can isolate BIC after coupling and normalize the BIC whenever EPIC instructs them due to any abnormality.
Combined consist shall be moved to next station platform/suitable location (as feasible, where it is possible to operate EPIC) at restricted speed of max 5 kmph. (In this case, braking is to be done by DBV only).
Assisting Train TO shall give continuous tractive effort to avoid speed variation & to keep full attention and additional precautions if section have gradient or rainy/wheel slip slide condition.
The Combined Consist (Defective Train coupled with the Assisting Train) shall move in cut out mode as per MRGR (50). The Maximum Permissible Speed for the Movement of the Combined Consist on Main Line / Depot is as appended below:

## Introduction

Before Stabling the Defective Train in any Siding, the Siding Length shall be confirmed by OCC to the Train Operator (TO) of Defective as well as Assisting Train. The length of the sidings available on each line is attached at Annexure-A for ready reference.

After securing the points en-route, TC/OCC shall advise the SC of the concerned Station to reach at the Exit Signal of the Siding. The SC shall stand on the Walkway near the foot of the Exit Signal of the Siding, along with Red/Green Flag or Tricolor Torch and shall ensure that while pushing the Defective Train in the Siding, Cab Door of the Active Cab of the Assisting Train does not cross the Exit Signal of the Siding. This is to ensure that the defective train does not occupy the track circuit ahead of the exit signal of the siding which may infringe the main line movement and the noncoupling end of defective train remains at a safe distance from the buffer.
After stopping the combined consist, TO of assisting Train shall uncouple assisting train as per laid  procedure  on  authorization  of  TC/OCC  and  change  cab  for  turning  back  the  train  as  per guidelines of TC/OCC.
In case of train rescue under para 7.1 (iii) and Para 16 of this SOP, once train is stabled, EngineerPossession-In charge shall normalize isolated BIC & EPIC before uncoupling of train, he shall also secure the stabled train.
SMs / SCs shall keep the OCC informed of the effects of Train Delays, including the Station and Platform Overcrowding and take necessary action as per OCC's Instructions regarding Crowd Control, which may include Stoppage of the Sale of Tickets, Stopping Entry to the Station and Granting of Refund etc. In any case, the Overcrowding at the Platform Level shall not be allowed to take place.

First train in the affected section shall move cautiously not exceeding 25kmph in both directions only after section clearance by EPIC/OCS. After clearing the section clear message to be relayed by TO to OCC in group mode. In case of any abnormality reported by Train Operator, same should be conveyed by TC/CC to concerned department for quick rectification.
After  clearing  the  Main  Line  or  stabling  the  defective  train  at  siding/suitable  location,  normal Operation shall be restored.
## 25. ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINE:

## 25. ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINE:

25.1 TC/OCC shall instruct the TO/RA/ETO to take the charge of defective, assisting and other trains (if required) as per extant procedures.
25.2 All  necessary  announcements  in  train/s  shall  be  done  by  Information  Controller.  If Announcement is not feasible, same shall be done by TO/RA/ETO.
25.3 The combined consist (defective train coupled with the assisting train) shall move in Cut Out Mode.  The  maximum  permissible  speed  for  the  movement  of  combined  consist  on mainline/depot shall be as per speed mentioned in para-17.
25.4 The Information Controller shall do necessary Announcement to the Passengers.

## 5.0 GENERAL:

5.1 Train shall be moved in degraded mode under the following circumstances after authorization from TC is obtained on exchange of private number as per Para '8'.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR-07 A (Rev-07)
## PROCEDURE FOR TRAIN MOVEMENT IN DEGRADED MODE IN LINE 1 & 2

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

It  deals  with  the  action  to  be  taken  by  Traffic  Controller,  Train  Operator  &  Station  Controller during train movement in degraded mode.

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure is applicable for the Train Movement in Degraded Modes of Train Operation in Line  1  &  2  and  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro  Railways  General  Rules  2020  and  its Amendment, Safety Circulars & Other Instructions in vogue.
## 3.0 DEFINITIONS:

## 3.0 DEFINITIONS:

3.1 Degraded Mode: Degraded  Mode  of  Train  Operation,  hereafter  referred  as  Degraded  Mode includes train movement in ROS, RM & Cut-Out Mode. The train is moved by TO on his line of sight exercising utmost vigilance so as to stop short of any obstruction ensuring that train speed does not exceed 25 kmph or less if applicable.
3.2 Route  Set :  A  route  is  considered  as  set  if  its  valid  indication  on  the  LVS/CATS/LATS  is displaying the track in white colour and on CCIP / VDU in yellow colour.
3.3 Point Set & Locked :
(i) On Line-1 (i-ATS) :A point is indicated as set & locked if and only if a valid indication for set & locked along with a cyan colour rectangle box on the point, is displayed on the LVS (Large Video Screen)/CATS/LATS. However, on CCIP a white dot on the fouling side of the point is displayed for set & locked indication.
(ii) On Line-2 (ALSTOM ATS) :A  point  is  indicated  as  set  &  locked  if  and  only  if  a  valid indication  for  set  &  locked  along  with  a  white  dot  on  the  fouling  side  of  the  point,  is displayed on the LVS/CATS/LATS/CCIP/VDU.
3.4 Danger Signal : A Danger Signal means that a Fixed Signal is displaying:-
(i) Red aspect; or
(ii) Flickering of aspects; or
(iii) Multiple aspects; or
(iv) No aspect (Blank).

## Introduction

5.2 Movement in degraded mode shall be authorized from one point to other as per below given guidelines, provided the route is clear of any obstruction from the origin to the destination & all points enroute are set & locked and if there are any signal enroute, passing the same shall be explicitly included in the authorization clearly stating the aspect.

(i) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  from  one  station  platform  to  next  station platform.
(ii) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized to the train stopped in the mid-section/siding from the point of stopping to the next station platform.
(iii) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  from  a  station  platform  to  an  intervening fixed signal before the next station platform, provided section is clear upto the intervening fixed signal, explicitly informing TO if next station is occupied, duly instructing TO to stop at foot of such fixed signal.
(iv) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  from  a  station  platform  to  an  intervening fixed signal or up to the next station platform, having a train in section, provided the TO of the preceding train in section has reported receipt of ATP/Proceed Code, without waiting for  the  train  to  clear  the  section,  explicitly  informing  TO  to  move  cautiously  observing utmost caution so as to stop short of any obstruction.
(v) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized to a revenue train by TC on permission of Chief Controller from one fixed signal to next fixed signal, covering more than one stations, only  after  ensuring  that  the  track  up  to  the  destination  signal  is  indicated  clear  on CATS/LVS,  explicitly  informing  TO  if  station  platform  next  to  the  destination  signal  is occupied.

(vi) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  to  a  non-revenue  train  (a  train  without passengers) by TC on permission of Chief Controller from one fixed signal to next fixed signal, covering more than one station, provided train does not stop at intermediate stations &  ensuring  that  the  track  up  to  the  destination  signal  is  indicated  clear  on  CATS/LVS, ensuring  that  the  station  platform  immediately  next  to  the  destination  signal  is  clear  of trains.
(vii) During reversal/stabling in siding, authorization shall be given up to SRMB/stabling point.
## Note:- TC shall not authorize any train working in degraded mode to move upto a virtual signal.

## Note:- TC shall not authorize any train working in degraded mode to move upto a virtual signal.

5.3 After  entering  into  a  station  platform  if  a  train  stops  before  the  NSP  and  movement  up  to  the NSP is to be done in degraded mode, train operator shall move in  degraded mode up to the NSP  only  after  ensuring  that  the  track  on  the  line  of  sight  up  to  the  NSP  is  clear  of  any obstructions. TO shall inform OCC about the same and if further movement in degraded mode is required beyond the NSP, TO, before any such movement, shall obtain authorization from TC as per Para '8'.
5.4 In case of intermediate terminal stations (stations other than terminal station where reversal of trains  takes  place  or  train  being  introduced  from/sent  to  depot),  before  authorizing  train movement in degraded mode from adjacent stations on either side towards intermediate terminal stations, TC in addition to Para '8' shall also ensure that, there is no train under reversal at the platform at intermediate terminal station and/or no train is being introduced from/sent to depot and the track up to the end of next platform is clear.
5.5 TC shall inform Chief Controller as and when train operation in degraded mode is authorized detailing train number, location and destination up to which it has been permitted. All cases of

## Introduction

ROS/RM/Cutout  authorization  should  be  documented  in  a  register  for  scrutiny  by  OCM/Chief Controller.

## Introduction

5.6 In  case  CATS  is  not  functioning  at  OCC,  TC  shall  advice  SC  of  the  concerned  interlocking station to take control on LATS and responsibility of granting authorization to the TO shall now devolve upon the SC who will follow the detailed procedure for Traffic Controller described in this circular. SC will ensure track clearance and route/points set & locked indications from the LATS & CCIP / VDU.
6.0 As per rule -23 of Metro Railway General Rule, 2020, In case train is running in degraded mode and train operator observes that a fixed signal is not displaying any aspect, he shall report the condition  to  the  traffic  controller  by  radio.  TC  shall  follow  the  procedure  as  per para  '9' as applicable.
## 7.0 ROLES & RESPONSIBLITIES OF STAFF DURING MOVEMENT IN DEGRADED MODE:
## 7.1 Train Operator:

(i) Whenever proceed code is not available to train, TO shall inform TC/SC as per Para '8.2' and shall seek instructions for movement in degraded mode.
(ii) Train operator shall never pass a signal at danger when Train is driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out Mode without authorization from TC as per Para '8.2' .
(iii) On  receiving authorization  from  TC  under  exchange  of  private  number  TO  shall acknowledge the same as per Para '8.2 '.
(iv) While  moving  in  degraded  mode, TO  is  responsible for  the  safe  movement  of  train.  He shall take following precautions while working the train.
(a) TO shall never operate train in degraded mode without authorization from TC as per Para 8.2 only exception being the provision in Para '5.3'
(b) While working the train in degraded mode from one station platform to next station platform, TO shall be watchful of the signal enroute, if any. If aspect of such signal is more restrictive than the aspect for which authorization is provided by TC, TO shall stop his train at the foot of such signal and shall seek fresh instruction from TC for movement in degraded mode.
(c) While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode,  TO  shall  not  allow  his  train  under  any circumstances  to  pass  the  next  station/signal/location  for  which  authorization  is provided by TC, unless authorized by TC, afresh, as per Para '8.2' of this circular.

(d) While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode  TO  shall  work  the  train  duly  observing speed  restriction  of  25  kmph  or  the  lower  speed  where  ever  prescribed  as  per TSR/PSR.TO shall keep the Train Speed such that it can be brought to stop with in half the distance of visibility estimated by him and he should be able to stop his train short of any obstruction.
(e) When authorized to pass a signal at danger by TC/SC under the exchange of private number/written authority, TO shall move cautiously, look out for points (if available) that  they  are  set  for  intended  direction  of  movement,  proceed  cautiously  over  the points  exercising  utmost  vigilance  and  be  prepared to  stop  short  of  points  in  case they are lying in wrong direction or are not set properly. TO must be alert to locate any train ahead of his/her train & be prepared to stop short of the train.
(v) After  resumption  of  ATP  /  Coded  manual  mode  from  degraded  mode,  TO  must  inform OCC/TC about the same.

## Introduction

(vi) TO shall inform passengers through train PA system of likely delay/slow speed of train.
## 7.2 Traffic Controller:

## 7.2 Traffic Controller:

(i) Authorization to pass signal at danger and/or to move in degraded mode shall be given by TC when having control as per the provisions given in this circular.
(ii) In case of failure of CATS, TC shall transfer control to the SC of the concerned interlocking zone on the LATS, on whom the responsibility of providing authorization for movement in degraded mode shall now devolve.TC shall inform TOs about the same. After restoration of CATS in OCC, control shall be transferred back to TC duly informing TOs.
(iii) TC shall  regulate  the  traffic  in  the  network  &  shall  arrange  to  inform  passengers  of  the likely delay, as required, by guiding Train Operators/Station Controllers for doing so.
## 7.3 Station Controller:

## 7.3 Station Controller:

(i) In case CATS is not functioning at OCC and operation is being controlled locally by SC through LATS/CCIP / VDU at station level, responsibility of granting authorization to the TO shall devolve upon the SC who will follow the detailed procedure for Traffic Controller described  in  this  circular.  SC  shall  ensure  track  clearance  and  route  set,  points  set  & locked indications from the LATS & CCIP / VDU.
(ii) Whenever  consistency  of  information  about,  signal  no  &  its  aspect,  route  setting  &  its clearance  up  to  desired  location,  points  set  &  lock  indication  is  sought  by  TC,  SC  shall provide the same by comparing the indications available on LATS & CCIP / VDU.
(iii) In  case  points  not  detected  set  and  locked,  when  instructed  by  TC,  SC  shall  physically examine the points, manually operate & secure (clamp & padlock) the points detected set & lock in  the  intended  direction  of  movement  and  shall  communicate  the  same  to OCC under the exchange of private number.
(iv) If required, SC shall inform passengers through PA system about the likely delay.
## 8.0 GRANTING AUTHORIZATION:

8.1. CONFIRMATION BY TC: Whenever authorization for movement in degraded mode is sought by train operator, TC shall satisfy himself from CATS/LVS about the following.
(i) TC  shall  compare  the  indication  of  CATS  &  LVS  and  shall  also  confirm  that  the  life indicators  of  CATS  are  working  properly  satisfying  himself  that  the  valid  indications  are available  on  CATS/LVS.  If  required,  TC  may  confirm  the  consistency  of  the  information from the SC, who shall confirm the same by comparing the indications on LATS & CCIP / VDU .
(ii) TC shall satisfy himself that there is no ambiguity about the information received from TO and  shall  ensure  that  the  information  is  consistent  with  the  indications  available  on CATS/LVS.
(iii) TC shall  look  for  the  availability  of  signal  &  points  enroute  to  the  next  station  and  shall ensure that the route is set up to the destination being authorized and points enroute, if any,  are  detected  set  &  locked  on  CATS/LVS  and  no  conflicting  route  is  set.  While providing authorization with Danger Signal & Points enroute, TC shall additionally confirm the  status  of  such  point  as  set  &  locked  from  the  SC,  who  shall  confirm  the  same  by comparing on LATS & CCIP / VDU .
(iv) TC shall  ensure that  the  track  ahead  is  clear  up  to  the  destination  being  authorized  on CATS & LVS. If Track circuit is showing occupied, he will ask TO to reconfirm the status of

## Introduction

track ahead on his line of sight. If TO's information is not sufficient, TC may also ask SC of next station to physically check the track occupancy from the station platforms. If required, TC, through radio communication, may try to establish the location of preceding train as per time table and shall ensure that track is clear up to the destination being authorized.

## Introduction

8.2. COMMUNICATION DURING DEGRADED MODE: Following guidelines for communication in degraded mode should be followed to ensure safety.
(i) Any instruction to the TO for authorizing him to move in degraded mode shall be given on Radio  on  exchange  of  private  number  between  TO  and  TC.  In  case  of  communication failure,  control  shall  be  transferred  to  the  SC  of  concerned  interlocking  zone  and authorization for movement in degraded mode shall be given to the TO by the concerned SC on exchange of private number or in writing if communication fails between them also.
(ii) Whenever a signal is Danger and proceed code is not available to train, TO shall inform TC giving his Train Number, exact location, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), status of track on his line of sight, localization status of train & direction of travel and shall seek authorization from TC before moving the train in degraded mode.
(iii) TC, while giving authorization to TO for movement in degraded mode shall clearly mention the train no, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), line (UP/DN) & destination up to which it is authorized, the degraded mode in which movement is authorized and shall offer his private number.
(iv) TO shall acknowledge the message by repeating, TC private no, his train no, status of line of sight, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), line & destination upto which it is applicable and the degraded mode in which movement is authorized. He shall then provide his private number to TC and make the entry in the private number book.

## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR IMPOSITION & CANCELLATION OF TEMPORARY SPEED RESTRICTIONS AND ISSUE OF CAUTION ORDERS ON LINE - 8

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This  Procedure  Order  covers  the  Methodology  of  Imposing  and  Cancellation  of  Temporary Speed Restrictions on Line - 8 equipped with Signalling & Train Control System of NIPPON.

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and its amendments, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue for Working of Trains on Line 8.
For UTO mode of Train Operation: wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/ Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
## 3.0 PROCEDURE:

3.1 All  the  requests  for  imposition/cancellation  of  TSR  on  main  line  should  be  made  to  Chief Controller/OCC and the CHC/OCC  shall instruct Traffic Controller for the Imposition/ Cancellation of Temporary Speed Restrictions & Issue of Caution Orders to Train Operators, as required on the Main Line Sections.
3.2 In cases of any of the TSR Commands, not directly being under Control of TC, Compliance of the same shall be ensured by TC through the Station Controllers on the Exchange of Private Numbers.
3.3 All  Requests  for  the  Imposition/Cancellation  of  Temporary  Speed  Restrictions  &  Issue  of Caution  Orders  to  the  Train  Operators  in  case  of  non-UTO  operation,  as  required  within  the Depot, shall be submitted to the Depot Controller, who is responsible for Coordination of all such Requests. Depot Controller shall also inform the TSR details to the PPIO, under Exchange of Private Numbers, to enable him to advise the Shunting Supervisors accordingly.
3.4 All Requests of the TSRs shall be submitted by the Authorized Personnel of Rank, not less than Junior Engineer as per prescribed format in Annexure-' C ' .

3.4 All Requests of the TSRs shall be submitted by the Authorized Personnel of Rank, not less than Junior Engineer as per prescribed format in Annexure-' C ' .
3.5 On receipt of Request for Imposition/ Cancellation of Temporary Speed Restriction (TSR) on a Section / in the Depot, the Traffic Controller / Depot Controller shall verify the Track Segment Number(s) corresponding to the OHE Mast Nos. from SGC & TPC and shall take further action for Imposition / Cancellation of the Temporary Speed Restriction by referring conversion table at Annexure- B for L-8. Virtual Block means imaginary blocks of smaller length which are parts of any track section to facilitate imposition of TSR on a limited area and thus not affect the entire length of track section.
3.6 The Requests, arising out of Emergency or Failure, shall be taken up promptly duly advising the Official, who has made the Request..
3.7 The Requests for the TSRs for a Planned Work shall normally be submitted before 1700 Hrs. of the previous day.
3.8 Traffic Controller / Depot Controller shall keep a record of accepted TSR Requests.
3.9 TSRs can be implemented through central/local ATS for main line and DATS for Depots in terms of affected Track Sections/Virtual Blocks and, therefore, the Traffic Controller / Depot Controller

Further, CHC/ACC/TC can impose Global TSR on  main  line,  whenever  necessary.  However,  Global  TSR  shall  be  cancelled  by  TC/SC  only. 3.12 The Traffic Controller shall advise the Crew Control & Concerned Station Controllers (adjacent to TSR section) regarding all TSRs to be enforced during next day on the entire Mainline on daily basis and shall maintain a Record of the same. TC/OCC shall advise to the said RA/ETO passing through the  affected  Section  to  move  in  ATP  Mode  along  with  details  of  TSR  imposed,  under  the Exchange of Private number. Traffic Controller shall confirm from the said RA/ETO with regard to the  imposition  of  TSR  who  in turn  shall  intimate  the  Target  Speed  displayed  on  DMI  over  the affected  area  to  the  Traffic  Controller,  CHC/ACC/OCC  shall  also  verify  it  from  the  speed  field (Train Information) of the Signaling view of the first train passing the affected Section.

After restoration, Chief controller shall verify that all TSRs which are prevailing have been applied in the system.

3.16 Since Trains can run in non-ATP Mode at Speeds lower than 25 Kmph, the System as such can not enforce the TSRs of Values less than 25 Kmph in non-ATP Mode of Working..
In  case  value  of  TSR  imposed  is  less  than  25  kmph  and  need  arises  for  train  movement  in degraded mode, TC/OCC shall instruct  nearest available  RA/ETO  to  board  (If  already  not  on board) the train as per procedure. RA/ETO shall take the charge of the train. Value of TSR shall be advised to the Train Operator in writing in the form of caution order by the station controller of the  preceding  station  or  by  Traffic  Controller  under  exchange  of  private  number  (if  train  has already left preceding station). Such an advise shall be in addition to the TSR imposed by the System.
3.17 In  case  of  non-UTO  operation,  all  TSRs  in  the  Depot  shall  be  advised  in  writing  to  the  Train Operators.
3.18 The  Depot  Controller  shall  advise  the  TSRs  in  writing  or  on  phone,  under  the  Exchange  of Private  Numbers,  to  the  Maintenance  Rail  Vehicles,  whenever  the  Traffic  Block  is  granted  to them.
3.19 The Drivers of Maintenance Rail Vehicles shall respect and follow the Caution Orders advised to them, while moving on Main Line / Depot line.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 38 (REV-03)
## JOINT PROCEDURE ORDER FOR OPERATING THE TRAIN DURING FLOOD CONDITION (MAIN LINE AND DEPOT)
## 1.0 Objective & Scope

## 1.0 Objective & Scope

The purpose of this Procedure Order is to establish the responsibilities and guidelines for safe operation of trains during flood conditions. These guidelines are to be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 & its amendment, Accident & Disaster Management Manual. These guidelines shall be applicable to both Ballasted and Ballast less Tracks.

## 1.0 Objective & Scope

For UTO Mode of Train Operation: Wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
## 2.0 Procedure

2.1 Any  Train  Operator/Station  Controller or any  other staff,  who  observes  the  water accumulation/water logging on the track, shall report to Traffic Controller (TC) or nearest Station Controller in case of main line flood and to Depot Controller (DC) in case of flood in Depot. Reporting person shall observe Flood Gauge wherever available or visual inspection at  any  other  places,  giving  as  much  details  as  possible  including  approximate  length  of affected track and approximate level of water. If possible, he shall also report whether water is stagnant or flowing, raining status in that area or any other relevant information.
2.2 In  case  Train  Operator (TO)  himself  notices  the flood  on  track  then  simultaneously  after reporting to TC/DC, he shall take utmost care while driving through the flood affected areas to judge the water level even if flood gauge is not available. While driving through the flood affected track, TO/Shunter shall follow the guidelines mentioned in sub para 2.5.1, 2.5.2 & 2.5.3. In case of any doubt TO/Shunter shall seek instruction from TC/DC as the case maybe.

2.3 On receipt of message of flooding on track in Station/Depot, Station Controller (SC)/Depot Controller  (DC)  shall  immediately  inform  Traffic  Controller  to  regulate  entry  of  trains  to Station/Depot. TC shall also inform to the Chief Controller (CHC) to coordinate and CHC shall  inform  about  the  same  to  other  controllers  i.e.,  Civil  Controller,  TPC,  RSC,  ASC, Telecom  System  Controller  and  Signaling  System  Controller  who  shall  inform  their respective In-charge/Dy. HOD and mobilize field staff to take necessary precautions.
2.4 Traffic  Controller  and  Depot  Controller  shall  share  above  mentioned  information  (water level/flood  etc.)  among  each  other.  During  rainy  season,  Traffic  Controller  and  Depot Controller shall also try  to  know  water/flood  position  on  the  track  from  the  Train Operators/Station Controllers/PPIO. If, PPIO is being informed or is aware about the water level/flooding on track then PPIO must immediately inform the same to the respective Depot Controller with as much details as may be available with him.

2.5 After receiving the above said details about water level etc. Depot Controller for Depot and Traffic Controller for Main Line shall decide in consultation with respective controllers (Civil Controller,  Signalling  System  Controller,  Telecom  System  Controller,  RSC,  TPC,  ASC) whether  train  operation  is  safe  within  flood  affected  area  and  can  be  continued  or  train movement has to be stopped forthwith. OCC/DCC Controllers shall regulate the trains in the following manner:
## 2.5.1 In case of Ballast less Track: -

## 2.5.1 In case of Ballast less Track: -

2.5.1.1 If the level of the accumulated water is at the level of the rail fastenings, the train may be allowed to run at a reduced speed of 25 KMPH in RM Mode and simultaneously, information should be relayed to JE/P-Way to immediately  proceed to the site to monitor the situation.

## Introduction

2.5.1.2 If the level of the accumulated water has risen above the level of the track fastenings but the rail top is visible to the TO, the train may be allowed to run at a reduced speed of 25 KMPH in RM Mode.

## Introduction

2.5.1.3 If the level of accumulated water has risen further and the rail top has submerged, the TO should look out for Flood Gauge, if any, installed at the location by the side of the track and make assessment of the depth of water on the rail top. Features of the Flood Gauge and method of its reading has been mentioned in the para 2.5.3.
If the depth of water over rail top is less than 75 mm, the train should be allowed to move at a restricted speed of 10 KMPH in RM Mode.
If  the  water  has reached 75 mm over rail top, further train movement should be suspended.
If  the  Flood  Gauge  is  not  available  at  the  location  and  TO  is  unable  to  make judgment  about  depth  of  water  over  the  rail  top,  train  movement  should  be suspended and TO shall seek further instruction from OCC/DCC.
2.5.1.4 In the event of water accumulation above the rail top, JE/P-Way should move to site without any delay and make assessment of depth of water over rail top. If the depth of  water over rail top is less than 75 mm, he should allow the trains to pass at a restricted speed of 10 KMPH in RM Mode. In case the depth of water over rail top is more than 75 mm, train movement should continue to remain suspended. The JE/PWay should take adequate measures towards reduction of water level and trains should be allowed to pass only in case water recedes to a level lesser than 75 mm above rail top.
## 2.5.2 In case of Ballasted Track: -

## 2.5.2 In case of Ballasted Track: -

2.5.2.1 If the accumulated water has resulted in submergence of majority of the ballast in the track, the train movement should be immediately suspended, and information should be relayed to JE/P-Way to immediately proceed to the site. The JE/P- Way should check the affected track and only if the track has not been disturbed, should allow the train over the track at dead slow speed, in RM Mode.
2.5.2.2 In case of rising of water over the rail top, JE/ P-Way should continuously monitor the situation and measure the depth of water over rail top. If the depth of water over rail top is less than 75 mm, train should be allowed to pass the location in accordance with the procedure outlined in para- 2.5.2.1 above. If the water has risen more than 75 mm over rail top, train movement should be immediately suspended. The JE/ PWay should take adequate measures towards reduction of water level. JE/ P-Way should allow the trains to pass the location only when the water recedes to level lesser than 75 mm above rail top and after ensuring that the track is safe and the ballast below the sleepers is intact.
## 2.5.3 Detail of Flood Gauge

## 2.5.3 Detail of Flood Gauge

2.5.3.1 Bottom level of the MS Plate should coincide with the top level of the lower rail of the track.

## 2.5.3 Detail of Flood Gauge

2.5.3.2 Flood Gauge should be installed on left side of the track (in respect of the direction  of movement of train) and it should not infringe the SOD as applicable.
2.5.3.3 Separate gauges should be fixed for Up line and Down line track.
2.5.3.4 The mounting of MS plate on the MS angle should be adjustable type so that height of the gauge can be adjusted. The MS angle should be firmly fixed to the viaduct at the bottom with suitable arrangement.
2.5.3.5 The white paint on the MS plate should be of retro reflective type.
2.5.3.6 Water level touching the vertex of the inverted white painted triangle is to mean that water is  at  the  level  of  the  rail  top.  Similarly,  submergence  of  the  gauge  altogether  i.e., disappearance of white inverted triangle, is to mean that water level has exceeded beyond 75 mm over the rail top.
2.5.3.7 In cases of tunnels wherein due to SOD restrictions or site conditions, it is not possible to fix  the above flood gauge then the above flood gauge shall be painted on the circular tunnel wall with a yellow background. (Picture - 01)

## Introduction

2.6 Signaling Controller shall continuously monitor S&T gears and take necessary action duly informing  CHC  (for  main  line)/DCC  (for  Depot  line)  of  repercussions,  if  any.  Signaling controller shall take continuous feedback and confirm AM/Manager or Dy HOD of Section so that instructions can be obtained.

## Introduction

2.7 RSC shall continuously monitor the flood level and inform the CHC whenever train movement is required to be stopped.
2.8 ASC shall switch on the tunnel light if underground section is affected.
2.9 In case water level rising/ accumulation beyond safer limits as judged by P-Way staff, Traffic Controller/ Depot Controller in consultation with TPC, RSC, Signalling System Controller, Telecom System Controller& other Controller, shall make necessary arrangement to stable the trains at safer locations at Main Line/Depots as the case maybe.
2.10 After flood is subsided, all departments shall check their equipment including track/structure, OHE, S&T etc. of affected zone and shall submit the fitness certificate to respective controller (Civil Controller, TPC, ASC, Signalling System Controller, Telecom system Controller RSC etc.)  of  OCC.  After  receipt  of  such  fitness  certificates,  all  other  Controller  (TPC,  ASC, Signalling System Controller, Telecom System Controller, RSC etc.) shall also communicate the same to Chief Controller/OCC.
2.11 Location of Flood gauges with respective mast number is attached as ' Annexure-A '.
## 2.12  FOR UTO MODE OF TRAIN OPERATION: -

## 2.12  FOR UTO MODE OF TRAIN OPERATION: -

2.12.1 Civil Controller shall observe all flood prone area from OCC in consultation with TC and RSC. Train front camera shall also be used for monitoring from OCC to get information about water accumulation on the track.
2.12.2 Civil Controller/Civil Official shall guide field staff or depute staff in flood prone area as per requirements for observation of flood in metro premises; if situation arises.
2.12.3 Whenever water logging/water accumulation is observed on track by RA/ETO or any other staff or by any other means, UTO mode shall be suspended if water level is at the level of rail fastening or above rail fastening.
2.12.4 If UTO train is stopped before water accumulation section and it is not safe to move forward  due  to  water  level,  TC  shall  reverse  that  train  in  UTO  mode  upto  previous platform.
2.12.5 In case RA is not onboard, TC shall instruct the nearest available ETO to board the train as per extant procedure.
2.12.6 TC shall instruct IC for suitable announcements inside the trains to keep passengers informed. ACC/OCC shall do relevant announcements at station.
2.12.7 Further train movement and speed restriction shall be as per extant procedure.

## 5.0 GENERAL:

5.1 Train  shall  be  moved  in  degraded  mode  under  the  following  circumstances  only  after authorization from TC is obtained on exchange of private number as per Para '8' .
(i) In case of loss of proceed code.
(ii) For passing a signal at danger when driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out mode.
(iii) Violet  Signals  shall  be  considered  as  Danger  Signal  when driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out mode.
