## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 07 C (Rev.-05)
## PROCEDURE FOR TRAIN MOVEMENT IN DEGRADED MODE IN LINE - 5 & 6

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure is applicable for the Train Movement in Degraded Modes of Train Operation in Line - 5 & 6 and shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and its Amendment, Safety Circulars & Other Instructions in vogue.

## 3.0 DEFINITIONS:

3.1 Degraded Mode: Degraded  Mode  of  Train  Operation,  hereafter  referred  as  Degraded  Mode includes train movement in ROS, RM & Cut-Out Mode. The train is moved by TO on his line of sight exercising utmost vigilance so as to stop short of any obstruction ensuring that train speed does not exceed 25 kmph or less if applicable.
3.2 Route  Set :  A  route  is  considered  as  set  if  its  valid  indication  on  the  MPD/  CENTRAL MMI/LOCAL MMI/VDU is displaying the track in white colour.
3.3 Point Set & Locked : A point shall be considered as set & locked if and only if valid indication of MPD/ CENTRAL MMI/LOCAL MMI/VDU displays the corresponding route as set & the point under reference set &not flashing and a valid indication for set & locked.
3.4 Danger Signal : A Danger Signal means that a Fixed Signal is displaying:-
(i) Red aspect; or
(ii) Flickering of aspects; or
(iii) Multiple aspects; or
(iv) No aspect (Blank).

## Introduction

(i) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from one station platform to next station platform.

(ii) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  to  the  train  stopped  in  the  midsection/siding from the point of stopping to the next station platform.
(iii) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from a station platform to an intervening fixed  signal  before  the  next  station  platform,  provided  section  is  clear  upto  the intervening  fixed  signal,  explicitly  informing  TO  if  next  station  is  occupied,  duly instructing TO to stop at foot of such fixed signal.
(iv) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from a station platform to an intervening fixed signal or up to the next station platform, having a train in section, provided the TO of  the  preceding  train  in  section  has  reported  receipt  of  ATP/Proceed  Code,  without waiting  for  the  train  to  clear  the  section,  explicitly  informing  TO  to  move  cautiously observing utmost caution so as to stop short of any obstruction.
(v) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized to a revenue train by TC on permission of  Chief Controller from one fixed signal to next fixed signal covering more than one stations only after ensuring that the track up to the destination signal is indicated clear on MMI/MPD, explicitly informing TO if station platform next to the destination signal is occupied.

(vi) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized to a non-revenue train (a train without passengers) by TC on permission of Chief Controller from one fixed signal to next fixed signal covering more than one station, provided train does not stop at the intermediate stations  &  ensuring  that  the  track  up  to  the  destination  signal  is  indicated  clear  on MMI/MPD, ensuring that the station platform immediately next to the destination signal is clear of trains.
(vii)  During  reversal/stabling  in  siding,  authorization  shall  be  given  up  to  SRMB/stabling point.

5.3 After entering into a station platform if a train stops before the NSP and movement up to the NSP is to be done in degraded mode, train operator shall move in degraded mode up to the NSP  only  after  ensuring  that  the  track  on  the  line  of  sight  up  to  the  NSP  is  clear  of  any obstructions. TO shall inform OCC about the same and if further movement in degraded mode is required beyond the NSP, TO, before any such movement, shall obtain authorization from TC as per Para '8'.
5.4 In case of intermediate terminal stations (stations other then terminal station where reversal of trains  takes  place  or  train  being  introduced  from/sent  to  depot),  before  authorizing  train movement  in  degraded  mode  from  adjacent  stations  on  either  side  towards  intermediate terminal  stations,  TC  in  addition  to Para  '8' shall  also  ensure  that,  there  is  no  train  under reversal  at  the  platform  at  intermediate  terminal  station  and/or  no  train  is  being  introduced from/sent to depot and the track up to the end of next platform is clear.
5.5 TC shall inform Chief Controller as and when train operation in degraded mode is authorized detailing train number, location and destination up to which it has been permitted. All cases of RM/Cutout  authorization  should  be  documented  in  a  register  for  scrutiny  by  OCM/Chief Controller.
5.6 In case MMI is not functioning at OCC, TC shall advice SC of the concerned interlocking station to  take control on Local MMI and responsibility of granting authorization to the TO shall now

## Introduction

devolve upon the SC who will follow the detailed procedure for Traffic Controller described in this circular. SC will ensure track clearance and route/points set & locked indications from the Local MMI&VDU.

## Introduction

6.0 As per rule no. 23 Metro Railways General Rules, 2020, In case train is running in degraded mode and train operator observes that a fixed signal is not displaying any aspect, he shall stop his train and seek instructions from the traffic controller by radio. TC shall follow the procedure as per Para '9' as applicable.
## 7.0 ROLES &RESPONSIBILITIES OF STAFF DURING MOVEMENT IN DEGRADED MODE:

(i)  Whenever proceed code is not available to train, TO  shall  inform TC/SC  as  per Para '8.2' and shall seek instructions for movement in degraded mode.
(ii)  Train operator shall never pass a signal at danger when Train is driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out mode without authorization from TC as per Para '8.2' .
(iii)  On  receiving  authorization  from  TC  under  exchange  of  private  number  TO  shall acknowledge the same as per Para '8.2' .
(iv)  While moving in degraded mode, TO is responsible for the safe movement of train. He shall take following precautions while working the train.
(a)  TO shall never operate train in degraded mode without authorization from TC as per Para '8.2' only exception being the provision in Para '5.3' .
(b)  While  working  the  train  in  degraded mode from one station platform to next station platform, TO shall be watchful of the signal enroute, if any. If aspect of such signal is more restrictive than the aspect for which authorization is provided by TC, TO shall stop his train at the foot of such signal and shall seek fresh instruction from TC for movement in degraded mode.
(c)  While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode,  TO  shall  not  allow  his  train  under  any circumstances  to  pass  the  next  station/signal/location  for  which  authorization  is provided by TC, unless authorized by TC, afresh, as per Para '8.2' of this circular.

(d)  While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode  TO  shall  work  the  train  duly  observing speed  restriction  of  25  kmph  or  the  lower  speed  where  ever  prescribed  as  per TSR/PSR.TO shall keep the Train Speed such that it can be brought to stop with in half the distance of visibility estimated by him and he should be able to stop his train short of any obstruction.
(e)  When authorized to pass a signal at danger by TC/SC under the exchange of private number/written authority, TO shall move cautiously, look out for points (if available) that  they  are  set  for  intended  direction  of  movement,  proceed  cautiously  over  the points exercising utmost vigilance and be prepared to stop short of points in case they are lying in wrong direction or are not set properly. TO must be alert to locate any train ahead of his/her train & be prepared to stop short of the train.
(v) After  resumption  of  ATP  /  Coded  manual  mode  from  degraded  mode,  TO  must  inform OCC/TC about the same.
(vi) TO shall inform passengers through train PA system of likely delay/slow speed of train.

## 7.2 Traffic Controller:

(i) Authorization to pass signal at danger and/or to move in degraded mode shall be given by

## Introduction

TC when having control as per the provisions given in this circular.

## Introduction

(ii) In  case  of  failure  of  MMI  in  OCC,  TC  shall  transfer  control  to  the  SC  of  the  concerned interlocking  zone  on  the  Local  MMI/VDU,  on  whom  the  responsibility  of  providing authorization for movement in degraded mode shall now devolve.TC shall inform TOs about the  same.  After  restoration  of  MMI  in  OCC,  control  shall  be  transferred  back  to  TC  duly informing TOs.
(iii) TC shall regulate the traffic in the network & shall arrange to inform passengers of the likely delay, as required, by guiding Train Operators/Station Controllers for doing so.

## 7.3 Station Controller:

(i)  In  case  MMI  is  not  functioning  at  OCC  and  operation  is  being  controlled  locally  by  SC through  MMI/VDU at station  level,  responsibility  of  granting  authorization  to  the  TO  shall devolve upon the SC who will follow the detailed procedure for Traffic Controller described in  this  circular.  SC  shall  ensure  track  clearance  and  route  set,  points  set  &  locked indications from the Local MMI&VDU.
(ii)  Whenever  consistency  of  information  about,  signal  no  &  its  aspect,  route  setting  &  its clearance  up  to  desired  location,  points  set  &  lock  indication  is  sought  by  TC,  SC  shall provide the same by comparing the indications available on  MMI&VDU.
(iii)  Incase  points  not  detected  set  and  locked,  when  instructed  by  TC,  SC  shall  physically examine the points, manually operate & secure (clamp & padlock) the points not detected set & lock in the intended direction of movement and shall communicate the same to OCC under the exchange of private number.
(iv)  If required, SC shall inform passengers through PA system about the likely delay.

8.1 CONFIRMATION BY TC: Whenever authorization for movement in degraded mode is sought by train operator, TC shall satisfy himself from MMI/MPD about the following.
(i)  TC shall compare the indication of MMI& MPD and shall also confirm that the life indicators of  MMI  are  working  properly  satisfying  himself  that  the  valid  indications  are  available  on MMI/MPD. If required, TC may confirm the consistency of the information from the SC, who shall confirm the same by comparing the indications on MMI&VDU.
(ii)  TC shall satisfy himself that there is no ambiguity about the information received from TO and  shall  ensure  that  the  information  is  consistent  with  the  indications  available  on MMI/MPD.
(iii)  TC  shall  look  for  the  availability  of  signal&  points  enroute  to  the  next  station  and  shall ensure that the route is set up to the destination being authorized and points enroute, if any, are  detected  set  &  locked  on  MMI/MPD  and  no  conflicting  route  is  set.  While  providing authorization with Danger Signal & Points enroute, TC shall additionally confirm the status of such point as set & locked from the SC, who shall confirm the same by comparing on Local MMI & VDU.

(iv)  TC  shall  ensure  that  the  track  ahead  is  clear  up  to  the  destination  being  authorized  on MMI& MPD. If Track circuit is showing occupied, he will ask TO to reconfirm the status of track ahead on his line of sight. If TO's information is not sufficient, TC may also ask SC of next station to physically check the track occupancy from the station platforms. If required, TC, through radio communication, may try to establish the location of preceding train as per time table and shall ensure that track is clear up to the destination being authorized.

## Introduction

8.2 COMMUNICATION DURING DEGRADED MODE: Following guidelines for  communication  in degraded mode should be followed to ensure safety.

## Introduction

(i)  Any instruction to the TO for authorizing him to move in degraded mode shall be given on Radio  on  exchange  of  private  number  between  TO  and  TC.  In  case  of  communication failure,  control  shall  be  transferred  to  the  SC  of  concerned  interlocking  zone  and authorization for movement in degraded mode shall be given to the TO by the concerned SC on exchange of private number or in writing if communication fails between them also.
(ii)  Whenever a signal is Danger and proceed code is not available to train, TO shall inform TC giving  his  Train  Number,  exact  location,  signal  number  &  aspect  (if  signal  is  available), status  of  track  on  his  line  of  sight,  status  of  train  &direction  of  travel  and  shall  seek authorization from TC before moving the train in degraded mode.
(iii)  TC, while giving authorization to TO for movement in degraded mode shall clearly mention the train no, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), line (UP/DN) & destination upto which it is authorized, the degraded mode in which movement is authorized and shall offer his private number.
(iv)  TO shall acknowledge the message by repeating, TC private no, his train no, status of line of sight, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), line & destination upto which it is applicable and the degraded mode in which movement is authorized. He shall then provide his private number to TC and make the entry in the private number book.

## 5.0 GENERAL:

5.1 Train  shall  be  moved  in  degraded  mode  under  the  following  circumstances  only  after authorization from TC is obtained on exchange of private number as per Para '8' .
(i)  In case of loss of proceed code.
(ii)  For passing a signal at danger when driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out Mode.
(iii)  Violet signals shall be considered as Danger Signal when driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out mode.
(iv)  If ATP/Coded Manual mode cannot be selected due to any reason.

## PROCEDURE FOR TRAIN MOVEMENT IN DEGRADED MODE IN LINE 3 & 4

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure is applicable for the Train Movement in Degraded Modes of Train Operation in Line  3  &  4  and  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro  Railways  General  Rules  2020  and  its Amendment, Safety Circulars & Other Instructions in vogue.

## 3.0 DEFINITIONS:

3.1 Degraded Mode: Degraded  Mode  of  Train  Operation,  hereafter  referred  as  Degraded  Mode includes train movement in ROS, RM & Cut Out Mode. The train is moved by TO on his line of sight exercising utmost vigilance so as to stop short of any obstruction ensuring that train speed does not exceed 25 kmph or less if applicable.
3.2 Route Set :  A route is considered as set if its valid indication on the MPD/ATS MMI/CENTRAL VDU/LOCAL VDU is displaying the track in white colour.
3.3 Point Set & Locked : A point is indicated as set & locked if and only if a valid indication for set & locked  along  with  point  no.&  its  box  is  displayed  in  white  colour  on  the  ATS  MMI/CENTRAL VDU/LOCAL VDU& a white dot on the fouling side of the point, is displayed on the MPD.
3.4 Danger Signal : A Danger Signal means that a Fixed Signal is displaying:-
(i) Red aspect; or
(ii) Flickering of aspects; or
(iii) Multiple aspects; or
(iv) No aspect (Blank).

## Introduction

(i)  Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  from  one  station  platform  to  next  station platform.
(ii)  Degraded Mode movement can be authorized to the train stopped in the mid-section/siding from the point of stopping to the next station platform.
(iii)  Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from a station platform to an intervening fixed signal before the next station platform, provided section is clear upto the intervening fixed signal, explicitly informing TO if next station is occupied, duly instructing TO to stop at foot of such fixed signal.
(iv)  Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from a station platform to an intervening fixed signal or up to the next station platform, having a train in section, provided the TO of the preceding train in section has reported receipt of ATP/Proceed Code, without waiting for the train  to  clear  the  section,  explicitly  informing  TO  to  move  cautiously  observing  utmost caution so as to stop short of any obstruction.
(v) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized to a revenue train by TC on permission of Chief Controller from one fixed signal to next fixed signal covering more than one stations only after ensuring that the track up to the destination signal is indicated clear on CENTRAL VDU/ATS MMI/MPD, explicitly informing TO if station platform next to the destination signal is occupied.

(vi)  Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  to  a  non-revenue  train  (a  train  without passengers)  by  TC  on  permission  of  Chief  Controller  from  one  fixed  signal  to  next  fixed signal covering more than one station, provided train does not stop at intermediate stations &  ensuring  that  the  track  up  to  the  destination  signal  is  indicated  clear  on  CENTRAL VDU/ATS MMI/MPD, ensuring that the station platform immediately next to the destination signal is clear of trains.
(vii)  During reversal/stabling in siding, authorization shall be given up to SRMB/stabling point.

## Note:- TC shall not authorize any train working in degraded mode to move upto a virtual signal.

5.3 After  entering  into  a  station  platform  if  a  train  stops  before  the  NSP  and  movement  up  to  the NSP is to be done in degraded mode, train operator shall move in degraded mode up to the NSP  only  after  ensuring  that  the  track  on  the  line  of  sight  up  to  the  NSP  is  clear  of  any obstructions. TO shall inform OCC about the same and if further movement in degraded mode is required beyond the NSP, TO, before any such movement, shall obtain authorization from TC as per Para '8'.
5.4 In case of intermediate terminal stations (stations other then terminal station where reversal of trains  takes  place  or  train  being  introduced  from/sent  to  depot),  before  authorizing  train movement in degraded mode from adjacent stations on either side towards intermediate terminal stations, TC in addition to Para '8' shall also ensure that, there is no train under reversal at the platform at intermediate terminal station and/or no train is being introduced from/sent to depot and the track up to the end of next platform is clear.
5.5 TC shall inform Chief Controller as and when train operation in degraded mode is authorized detailing train number, location and destination up to which it has been permitted. All cases of ROS/RM/Cutout  authorization  should  be  documented  in  a  register  for  scrutiny  by  OCM/Chief Controller.

## 7.1. Train Operator:

(i) Whenever proceed code is not available to train, TO shall inform TC/SC as per Para '8.2' and shall seek instructions for movement in degraded mode.
(ii) Train operator shall never pass a signal at danger when Train is driven in RM or ROS or Cut-Out mode without authorization from TC as per Para '8.2' .
(iii) On  receiving authorization from TC  under exchange of private number  TO  shall acknowledge the same as per Para '8.2' .
(iv) While moving in degraded mode, TO is responsible for the safe movement of train. He shall take following precautions while working the train.
(a)  TO  shall  never  operate  train  in  degraded  mode  without  authorization  from  TC  as  per Para '8.2' only exception being the provision in Para '5.3' .
(b)  While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode  from  one  station  platform  to  next  station platform, TO shall be watchful of the signal enroute, if any. If aspect of such signal is more restrictive than the aspect for which authorization is provided by TC, TO shall stop his train at the foot of such signal and shall seek fresh instruction from TC for movement in degraded mode.
(c)  While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode,  TO  shall  not  allow  his  train  under  any circumstances to pass the next station/signal/location for which authorization is provided by TC, unless authorized by TC, afresh, as per Para '8.2' of this circular.

(d)  While working the train in degraded mode TO shall work the train duly observing speed restriction of 25 kmph or the lower speed where ever prescribed as per TSR/PSR.TO shall keep the Train Speed such that it can be brought to stop with in half the distance of visibility  estimated  by  him  and  he  should  be  able  to  stop  his  train  short  of  any obstruction.
(e)  When authorized to pass a signal at danger by TC/SC under the exchange of private number/written authority, TO shall move cautiously, look out for points (if available) that they  are  set  for  intended  direction  of  movement,  proceed  cautiously  over  the  points exercising utmost vigilance and be prepared to stop short of points in case they are lying in wrong direction or are not set properly. TO must be alert to locate any train ahead of his/her train & be prepared to stop short of the train.
(v) After  resumption  of  ATP/  coded  manual  mode  from  degraded  mode,  TO must  inform TC about the same.
## 7.2. Traffic Controller:

## 7.2. Traffic Controller:

(i) Authorization to pass signal at danger and/or to move in degraded mode shall be given by TC when having control as per the provisions given in this circular.
(ii) In  case  of  failure  of  CENTRAL  VDU/ATS  MMI,TC  shall  transfer  control  to  the  SC  of  the concerned interlocking zone on the LOCAL VDU & ATS MMI, on whom the responsibility of providing authorization for movement in degraded mode shall now devolve.TC shall inform TOs about the same. After restoration of CENTRAL VDU/ATS MMI in OCC, control shall be transferred back to TC duly informing TOs.
(iii) TC shall regulate the traffic in the network & shall arrange to inform passengers of the likely delay, as required, by guiding Train Operators/Station Controllers for doing so.
## 7.3. Station Controller:

## 7.3. Station Controller:

(i) In  case  CENTRAL  VDU/ATS  MMI  is  not  functioning  at  OCC  and  operation  is  being controlled  locally  by  SC  through  LOCAL  VDU/ATS  MMI  at  station  level,  responsibility  of granting  authorization  to  the  TO  shall  devolve  upon  the  SC  who  will  follow  the  detailed procedure for Traffic Controller described in this circular. SC shall ensure track clearance and route set, points set & locked indications from the LOCAL VDU & ATS MMI.
(ii) Whenever  consistency  of  information  about,  signal  no  &  its  aspect,  route  setting  &  its clearance  up  to  desired  location,  points  set  &  lock  indication  is  sought  by  TC,  SC  shall provide the same by comparing the indications available on  LOCAL VDU & ATS MMI.
(iii) Incase  points  not  detected  set  and  locked,  when  instructed  by  TC,  SC  shall  physically examine the points, manually operate & secure (clamp & padlock) the points not detected set & lock in the intended direction of movement and shall communicate the same to OCC under the exchange of private number.
(iv) If required, SC shall inform passengers through PA system about the likely delay.

## 8.0 GRANTING AUTHORIZATION:

8.1. CONFIRMATION BY TC: Whenever authorization for movement in degraded mode is sought by train operator, TC shall satisfy himself from CENTRAL VDU/ATS MMI/MPD about the following.
(i) TC shall compare the indication of CENTRAL VDU/ATS MMI& MPD and shall also confirm that the life indicators of CENTRAL VDU/ATS MMI are working properly satisfying himself that  the  valid  indications  are  available  on  CENTRAL VDU/ATS MMI/MPD. If required, TC may confirm the consistency of the information from the SC, who shall confirm the same by comparing the indications on LOCAL VDU & ATS MMI.
(ii) TC shall satisfy himself that there is no ambiguity about the information received from TO and  shall  ensure  that  the  information  is  consistent  with  the  indications  available  on CENTRAL VDU/ATS MMI/MPD.
(iii) TC  shall  look  for  the  availability  of  signal  &  points  enroute  to  the  next  station  and  shall ensure that the route is set up to the destination being authorized and points enroute, if any, are detected set & locked on CENTRAL VDU/ATS MMI/MPD and no conflicting route is set. While  providing  authorization  with  Danger  Signal  &  Points  enroute,  TC  shall  additionally

## SAFETY CIRCULAR- 09 (Rev.-02)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR INSTALLATION / TESTING / REPAIR / MAINTENANCE OF SOLAR PANELS ON ROOF TOP OF ELEVATED STATIONS
## 1.0  INTRODUCTION:

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION:

Solar  panels  have  been  installed  on  curved  /  inclined/  RCC  roof  of  station  buildings  /  Depot sheds & buildings at various Lines of DMRC. List of DMRC sections where roof-top solar plants on curved/ inclined roofs are installed are attached as Annexure-A.

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION:

Considering  DMRC's  focus  on  Solar  Energy,  procedure  for  Installation/  Repair/  Testing  and Maintenance of solar panels during Revenue and non-revenue hours is formulated.
For UTO Mode of Operation: Wherever, Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO) / Roving Attendant (RA) / Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
## 2.0 SCOPE:

2.1  This Procedure Order describes the procedure for installation (on elevated stations) of solar panels on curved/ inclined roof tops during revenue hours as well as non-revenue hours.
2.2  This Procedure Order also describes the procedure for Repair/ Testing and Maintenance of already installed solar curved rooftop panels during revenue hours and non-revenue hours
2.3  This procedure order is applicable to all existing / future roof top solar plants on curved/inclined roofs of all Lines. This Document shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules-2020 and Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules-2022, Safety Circulars, Station Working Orders and other Instructions in vogue.
3.0     PROCEDURE: The following procedure shall be followed ensuring due precautions.
3.1 Precautions  to  be  Taken  Before  Starting  the  work  of Installation/  Repair/  Testing  and Maintenance of solar panels :
Before start of any new installation work at a station, a joint survey/ inspection of roof sheet and other technical requirements, will be conducted at the proposed station, by a team comprising of representatives from:
(a)  Solar/Project and
(b)  O&M wings of Civil, E&M, Traction, Operations and Safety.
This  team  shall  inspect  the  rooftop  conditions  and  look  for  any  deterioration  on  roof structures from platform level or other accessible location. Only after ensuring that roof sheeting is fit for  such  nature  of  work,  the  installation  may  be  planned  after  signing  of joint  report  by  staff  of  minimum  Supervisor  level  of  these  departments  at  the  time  of inspection.

Solar Panel installation work shall be carried out only after adopting approved method statement, to be ensured by EPIC.
ii) Before start of any installation work : The area of skylights & the open spaces on either side of the roof / nearby Overhead Protection Cable (OPC) wire shall be barricaded and insulated. This work of barricading and insulation of the open spaces of the roof shall be done during non-revenue hours. Only after completion of the barricading/insulation work, the installation work shall be taken up during Revenue Hours. Any unsafe area on the roof sheets, shall be clearly demarcated.

## Introduction

iii) Solar wing shall ensure that the structural drawings of proposed modifications/additions on  roof  structure  along  with  the  method  statement  of  carrying  out  such  work  at  each metro station shall be approved by DMRC Design wing.

iv) Copies of such approved method statement and goods for construction drawings/design shall be shared with Civil/O&M wing and E&M/O&M wing well before taking up the work.
A copy of  program /schedule  of  work  proposed  to  be carried  out  of  the  roof  of  metro stations shall be informed to Civil (O&M) wing and Safety (O&M) Wing well in advance by Solar Project Wing (for installation work only).
vi) Nature of work:
(a) Installation of Panels: Installation work of solar structure and solar panels is to be carried out during revenue as well as non-revenue hours. The estimated installation schedule shall be conveyed by Dy.HOD of Project wing along with method statement (approved by HOD/Project) to OCC through concerned Dy. HOD of O&M wing.
(b) Repair/Testing/Maintenance of Solar panels: is to be carried out during revenue hours, under the approved programme by Dy. HOD of E&M of O&M wing. This work is  to  be  preferably  carried  out  during  10:00Hrs  to  16:00  Hrs,  when  solar  panel generate electricity  and  voltage/current  can  be  measured  with  the  help  of  relevant instrument.

vii) For  Installation/Repair/Testing  and  Maintenance  of  solar  panels  during  non-revenue hours, concerned team shall inform the planned schedule through concerned O&M wing to Operation Control Centre (OCC) every Friday, so that it would be suitably incorporated (as  per  feasibility)  in  weekly  Block  paper  (as  per  SC-02).  If  the  work  carried  out  in revenue  hours,  then  Installation/Repair/Testing  and  Maintenance  of  solar  panels  team shall inform through concerned O&M department to Operation Control Centre (OCC) and concerned station managers in advance (two days prior of start of solar Installation/Repair/Testing and Maintenance of solar panels work) with details mentioning day of such work and portion of roof which shall be used for such work.
viii) Caution order shall be issued to the Train Operators accordingly.
ix) Traffic Controller (TC) shall grant Permit To Work (PTW) as per SC-02 and SC-09.
If  the  said  work is to be carried out in two-meter (2m) vicinity zone of Live OHE, then work to be carried out in only non-revenue hours under shadow power block. Permit to work (PTW) with shadow power block is required as per SC-02.and other related safety circulars.
xi) During solar panel Installation/Repair/Testing and Maintenance of solar panels work, all safety aspects shall be ensured by the Engineer's Possession in Charge (EPIC) i.e. use of PPEs such as proper safety shoes, safety jacket, safety belt (harness), helmet etc. It shall be ensured that the length of rope connecting life line shall not exceed 3 meters.

xii) The rooftop  access  at  each  location  is  provided  by  broad  step  ladder  with  hand  rails, which makes it safe for persons in accessing & reaching to the roof. In case the same is not  available,  roof  shall  be  accessed  using  sky  lift  of  suitable  height  or  by  erecting scaffolding where ladder for going over roof is not available/ feasible.
xiii) Checklist  for  installation  of  solar  roof  curved  is  attached  as  Annexure-D  and  for maintenance of Solar roof curved/ inclined is attached as Annexure-E. This check list is to be filled by Engineer's Possession in Charge (EPIC). Check list shall be submitted to on duty Station Controller before start of work along with Permit To Work (PTW).
## 3.2 Precautions to be ensured while executing the Installation / Repair/ Testing/ Cleaning/ Maintenance of solar panels on curved roof tops:

## 3.2 Precautions to be ensured while executing the Installation / Repair/ Testing/ Cleaning/ Maintenance of solar panels on curved roof tops:

The  Engineer's  possession  in  charge  (EPIC)  (Competent  DMRC  staff  of  minimum  JE rank of solar project wing for installation and Competent staff of E&M (O&M) wing with EPIC competency for repairing/ testing and maintenance) along with installation/ repair/ testing and maintenance team of solar panels shall report to the concerned station. The Engineer's  possession  in  Charge  (EPIC)  shall  apply  for  Permit  to  Work  (PTW)  in  the

requisite Performa duly endorsing the fact about his being aware of 'Live OHE status' and 'train movement on status'. Station controller of the concerned station must ensure the endorsement in the Permit to work (PTW) requisition.

ii) Permit  To  Work  (PTW)  requisition  given  by  Engineer's  Possession  in  Charge  (EPIC) shall include the number of persons and equipment details and no unauthorized person shall be allowed to access the roof top during solar panel Installation/Repair/Testing and Maintenance of solar panels work.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR-06 (REV-05)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR TRAIN MOVEMENT ON ELEVATED/AT GRADE SECTION OF ALL LINES DURING HIGH WIND SPEED DUE TOTHUNDER STORM / CYCLONE

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION:

This procedure order deals with train movement on elevated/at grade sections during high surface wind speed caused by Thunderstorm/Cyclone or any other weather disturbance. Wind speed above 70 kmph is considered as ' High Wind Speed' .

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION:

This  Procedure  order  and  speed  restriction  stipulated  herein  shall  be  applicable  to  all elevated/at grade platforms of all lines (SG/BG sections). However, regulation of traffic shall be  required  in  underground  section  also  of  a  line  in  sync  with  operating  condition  on elevated/at grade portion of that line.

## 2.0  SCOPE:

This procedure is applicable to all lines. This procedure order should be read in conjunctions with Metro Railways General Rules-2020 and Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules2022,  Accidents  &  Disaster  Management  Manual  and  other  relevant  existing  procedure orders.
For UTO mode of Train Operation: Wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
## 3.0  OBJECTIVE:

## 3.0  OBJECTIVE:

The purpose of the procedure order is to ensure utmost safety for trains and passengers during  high  speed  wind  and  also  delineate  roles  and  responsibility  of  OCC  staff,  Train Operators, Station staff and other metro staff in such scenario.
## 4.0  WIND SENSOR:

## 4.0  WIND SENSOR:

Details of wind monitoring system and their jurisdictions are placed at Annexure 'A' & in case of  failure  of  any  wind  sensor,  details  of  secondary/tertiary  wind  sensors  are  placed  at 'Annexure-B '.
## 5.0  ACTIONS TO BE TAKEN BY OCC, STATION, TRAIN OPERATION & OTHER STAFF:
## 5.1 General Guidelines:

## 5.1 General Guidelines:

(i) ASC/OCC/MB-2,  on  becoming  aware  of  the  high  speed  wind  through  wind  sensor monitor installed at his work desk shall watch it for further increase in wind speed. When wind speed increases and exceeds 60 km/h, 70 km/h and 90 km/h, ASC/OCC/MB-2 shall immediately inform (verbally) to CHC/OCC/MB-2 for implementing train movement restriction on respective lines through Traffic Controllers as specified in para-5.2 of this JPO. After communicating verbally, ASC/OCC/MB-2 shall then also confirm in writing to CHC/OCC/MB-2. The  above  verbal  communications  made  to  CHC/OCC/MB-2  shall clearly mention the time and details of detection of event by wind sensor monitor.
(ii) CHC/OCC/MB-2  shall  immediately  inform  CHC/OCC/MB-3  and  CHC/OCC/MB-1;  to accordingly implement train movement restriction on respective lines.
(iii) CHC/OCC/MB-1, CHC/OCC/MB-2 & CHC/OCC/MB-3 shall advise respective TCs and all other controllers in the OCC regarding high wind situation and to follow the PO for train movement in such situation.
(iv) CHC/OCC/MB-1, CHC/OCC/MB-2 and CHC/OCC/MB-3 shall also advise Dy. HOD/Operations (Station Operation) concerned, officers/officials concerned of

## Introduction

Operations/ Electrical/ Track/Civil/S&T department of respective line accordingly about the high wind speed as monitored.

(v) All TC shall implement/instruct train movement restrictions as stipulated in this PO on concerned lines by suitable commands and/or by giving instructions as blanket message to  all  Train  Operators  in  group  mode  (for  immediate  ATO  suspension  and  speed restriction enforcement) and keep on repeating it regularly till the speedy wind conditions improve and settle down to normal level.
* Cases involving UTO mode of train operation shall be dealt with as per Para 9.0.
(vi) On receipt of such instruction from TC, Train Operators shall acknowledge the message and comply accordingly by strictly adhering to speed restriction. TOs of the trains running in UTO/ATO mode shall change over to CM/ATP mode immediately to achieve manual control on speed of train.
(vii) Traffic Controller shall also advise Station Controllers about the wind condition, traffic plan etc. and ask them to take necessary action accordingly.
(viii) Station  Controllers  shall  ensure  announcement  at  their  respective  stations,  inform Station  Manager  and  take  other  appropriate  actions  as  required  or  as  instructed  by TC/OCC. Station Manager/Station Controller shall inspect platform level to check for any abnormality  and  must  see  that  no  self-moveable  item/equipment  is  left  at  platform without securing it properly.
(ix) It  shall  be  the  responsibility  of  the  concerned  staff  that  after  completion  of  work/ maintenance, any equipment/material that may hinder passenger movement is removed or properly secured at some suitable place.

(ix) It  shall  be  the  responsibility  of  the  concerned  staff  that  after  completion  of  work/ maintenance, any equipment/material that may hinder passenger movement is removed or properly secured at some suitable place.
(x) However, if any material found unremoved by maintenance (E&M, Lift, Escalator etc.) department;  it  shall  be  removed  by  station  staff  after  consultation  with  concerned department and take other appropriate actions as required or as instructed by TC/OCC.
(xi) Train Operators shall make announcements in respective trains to keep passengers informed inside train.
(xii) Surprise mock drill shall be conducted on regular interval for preparedness in case of high wind speeds due to Thunderstorm/ Cyclone.

## 5.0 GENERAL:

5.1 Train  shall  be  moved  in  degraded  mode  under  the  following  circumstances  only  after authorization from TC is obtained on exchange of private number as per Para '8' .
(i) In case of loss of proceed code.
(ii) For passing a signal at danger when driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out mode.
(iii) White signals shall also be considered as Danger Signal when driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out mode.
(iv) If ATP mode cannot be selected due to any reason.
5.2 Movement in degraded mode shall be authorized from one point to Station platform or Fixed Signal  whichever  is  earlier  as  per  below  given  guidelines,  provided  the  route  is  clear  of  any obstruction from the origin to the destination.
## PROCEDURE FOR TRAIN MOVEMENT IN DEGRADED MODE IN AIRPORT EXPRESS LINE

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION:

It  deals  with  the  action  to  be  taken  by  Traffic  Controller,  Train  Operator  &  Station  Controller during train movement in degraded mode. This procedure is applicable for the Train Movement in Degraded Modes of Train Operation in Airport Express Line.

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure is applicable for Airport Express Line and shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways  General  Rules  2020  and  its  amendments,  Safety  Circulars  &  Other  Instructions  in vogue.

## 3.0 DEFINITIONS:

3.1 Degraded Mode: Degraded  Mode  of  Train  Operation,  hereafter  referred  as  Degraded  Mode includes train movement in ROS, RM & Cut-Out Mode. The train is moved by TO on his line of sight exercising utmost vigilance so as to stop short of any obstruction ensuring that train speed does not exceed 25kmph and 40kmph in case of High speed cutout mode or less if applicable.
3.2 Route  Set :  A  route  is  considered  as  set  if  its  valid  indication  on  the  OCC  ATS  MMI/RPS Display/Station ATS MMI is displaying the track in green colour.
3.3 Point Set & Locked : A point is indicated as set & locked if and only if a valid indication for set & locked  along  with  point  no.  &  its  box  is  displayed  in  white  colour  on  the  ATS  MMI/RPS Display/Station MMI.
3.4 Danger Signal : A Danger Signal means that a Fixed Signal is displaying:-
(i) Red aspect; or
(ii) Flickering of aspects; or
(iii) Multiple aspects; or
(iv) No aspect (Blank).

## Introduction

(i) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  from  one  station  platform  to  next  station platform or fixed signal whichever is earlier.

(ii) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized to the train stopped in the mid-section/siding from the point of stopping to the next station platform or fixed signal whichever is earlier.
(iii) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  from  a  station  platform  to  an  intervening fixed signal before the next station platform, provided section is clear upto the intervening fixed signal, explicitly informing TO if next station is occupied, duly instructing TO to stop at foot of such fixed signal.
When driving in degraded mode (i.e. RM/Cut out mode), TO shall always bring his/her train to  a  complete  stop  irrespective  of  the  aspect  of  line  side  signal-either  short  of  the  fixed signal at Red/ White or at the stopping point of station platform (whichever is earlier) and shall seek authorization from TC.
(iv) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  from  a  station  platform  to  an  intervening fixed signal or up to the next station platform, having a train in section, provided the TO of the preceding train in section has reported receipt of ATP/Proceed Code, without waiting for  the  train  to  clear  the  section,  explicitly  informing  TO  to  move  cautiously  observing utmost caution so as to stop short of any obstruction.

(v) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  to  a  non-revenue  train  (a  train  without passengers) by TC on permission of Chief Controller from one fixed signal to next fixed signal covering more than one station, provided train does not stop at intermediate stations & ensuring that the track up to the destination signal is indicated clear on RPS display/ATS MMI/MPD, ensuring that the station platform immediately next to the destination signal is clear of trains.
(vi) During reversal/stabling in siding, authorization shall be given up to SRMB/stabling point

5.3 After  entering  into  a  station  platform  if  a  train  stops  before  the  NSP  and  movement  up  to  the NSP is to be done in degraded mode, train operator shall move in degraded mode up to the NSP  only  after  ensuring  that  the  track  on  the  line  of  sight  up  to  the  NSP  is  clear  of  any obstructions. TO shall inform OCC about the same and if further movement in degraded mode is required beyond the NSP, TO, before any such movement, shall obtain authorization from TC as per Para '8'.
5.4 TC shall inform Chief Controller as and when train operation in degraded mode is authorized detailing train number, location and destination up to which it has been permitted. All cases of ROS/RM/Cutout  authorization  should  be  documented  in  a  register  for  scrutiny  by  OCM/Chief Controller.
5.5 In case RPS display/ATS MMI is not functioning at OCC, TC shall advice SC of the concerned interlocking station to  take control on Local ATS MMI and responsibility of granting authorization to  the  TO  shall  now  devolve  upon  the  SC  who  will  follow  the  detailed  procedure  for  Traffic Controller described in this circular. SC will ensure track clearance and route/points set & locked indications from the LOCAL ATS MMI.

6.0 As per rule - 23 of Metro Railway General Rule, 2020, In case train is running in degraded mode and train operator observes that a fixed signal is not displaying any aspect, he/she shall stop  his/her  train  and  seek  instructions  from  the  traffic  controller  by  radio.  TC  shall  follow  the procedure as per Para '9' as applicable.
## 7.0 ROLES& RESPONSIBLITIES OF STAFF DURING MOVEMENT IN DEGRADED MODE:

## 7.1 Train Operator:

(i)  Whenever proceed code is not available to train, TO shall inform TC/SC as per Para '8.2' and shall seek instructions for movement in degraded mode.

(ii)  Train operator shall never pass a signal at danger when Train is driven in RM or ROS or Cut-Out mode without authorization from TC as per Para '8.2' .
(iii)  On  receiving authorization from  TC  under  exchange of private number, TO  shall acknowledge the same as per Para '8.2' .
(iv)  While moving in degraded mode, TO is responsible for the safe movement of train. TO shall take following precautions while working the train.
(a)  TO shall never operate train in degraded mode without authorization from TC as per Para '8.2' only exception being the provision in Para '5.3' .
(b) While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode  from  one  station  platform  to  next  station platform  (in  case  of  non-revenue train),  TO shall  be  watchful  of  the  signal  enroute,  if any. If aspect of such signal is more restrictive than the aspect for which authorization is provided by TC, TO shall stop his train at the foot of such signal and shall seek fresh instruction from TC for movement in degraded mode.
(c) While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode,  TO  shall  not  allow  his  train  under  any circumstances  to  pass  the  next  station/signal/location for which  authorization is provided by TC, unless authorized by TC, afresh, as per Para '8.2' of this circular.

(d)  While working the train in degraded mode TO shall work the train duly observing speed restriction of 25 kmph or the lower speed where ever prescribed as per TSR/PSR.TO shall keep the Train Speed such that it can be brought to stop with in half the distance of  visibility  estimated  by  him  and  TO  should  be  able  to  stop  his  train  short  of  any obstruction.
(e)  When authorized to pass a signal at danger by TC/SC under the exchange of private number/written authority, TO shall move cautiously, look out for points (if available) that they  are  set  for  intended  direction  of  movement,  proceed  cautiously  over  the  points exercising  utmost  vigilance  and  be  prepared  to  stop  short  of  points  in  case  they  are lying  in  wrong  direction  or  are  not  set  properly.  TO  must  be  alert  to  locate  any  train ahead of his/her train & be prepared to stop short of the train.
(v)  After resumption of ATP mode from degraded mode, TO must inform TC about the same.
(vi)  Under degraded movements, if visibility is so low that the driver/Train operator is not be able to see the aspect of signal or the setting of point or is not able to recognize the terrestrial features  of  the  line/station,  the  driver/Train  Operator,  either  must  not  proceed  until  the visibility  is  at  an  acceptable  level.  The  driver/TO  must  take  a  decision  based  on  the condition at site under intimation to OCC.

(vii)  TO must note that  in  Cut  out  mode,  the  train  may  acquire  a  speed  above  this  safe  limit speed due to down gradients and must take action to positively ensure that the train speed is limited to the speed limit of 25 kmph, as applicable. TO is fully responsible for driving the train  safely  below  25  kmph  in  cut  out  mode,  on  line  of  sight  observing  line  side  signals, proper  setting  of  points  for  the  route  and  train/obstruction  ahead  taking  due  note  of  the location up to which TO has been authorised to go by TC.
(viii)  TO shall inform passengers through train PA system of likely delay/slow speed of train.

## 7.2 Traffic Controller:

(i)  Authorization to pass signal at danger and/or to move in degraded mode shall be given by TC when having control as per the provisions given in this circular.

## 7.2 Traffic Controller:

(ii)  In  case  of  failure  of  RPS  Display/ATS  MMI,  TC  shall  transfer  control  to  the  SC  of  the concerned  interlocking  zone  on  the  LOCAL  ATS  MMI,  on  whom  the  responsibility  of providing authorization for movement in degraded mode shall now devolve. TC shall inform TOs about the same. After restoration of RPS display/ATS MMI in OCC, control shall be transferred back to TC duly informing TOs.
(iii)  TC shall regulate the traffic in the network & shall arrange to inform passengers of the likely delay, as required, by guiding Train Operators/Station Controllers for doing so.

## 7.3 Station Controller:

(i)  In case RPS/ATS MMI is not functioning at OCC and operation is being controlled locally by SC through LOCAL ATS MMI at station level, responsibility of granting authorization to the TO shall devolve upon the SC who will follow the detailed procedure for Traffic Controller described in this circular. SC shall ensure track clearance and route set, points set & locked indications from the ATS MMI.
(ii)  Whenever  consistency  of  information  about,  signal  no  &  its  aspect,  route  setting  &  its clearance  up  to  desired  location,  points  set  &  lock  indication  is  sought  by  TC,  SC  shall provide the same by comparing the indications available on  ATS MMI.
(iii)  In  case  points  not  detected  set  and  locked,  when  instructed  by  TC,  SC  shall  physically examine the points, manually operate & secure (clamp & padlock) the points not detected set & lock in the intended direction of movement and shall communicate the same to OCC under the exchange of private number.
(iv)  If required, SC shall inform passengers through PA system about the likely delay.

8.1 Confirmation By TC: Whenever authorization for movement in degraded mode is sought by train operator, TC shall satisfy himself from RPS display/ATS MMI/MPD about the following.
(i)  TC  shall  compare  the  indication  of  RPS/ATS  MMI  and  shall  also  confirm  that  the  life indicators of ATS MMI are working properly satisfying himself that the valid indications are available  on  RPS  display/ATS  MMI.  If  required,  TC  may  confirm  the  consistency  of  the information  from  the  SC,  who  shall  confirm  the  same  by  comparing  the  indications  on LOCAL ATS MMI.
(ii)  TC shall satisfy himself that there is no ambiguity about the information received from TO and  shall  ensure  that  the  information  is  consistent  with  the  indications  available  on RPS/ATS MMI/MPD.
(iii)  TC shall  look  for  the  availability  of  signal  &  points  enroute  to  the  next  station  and  shall ensure that the route is set up to the destination being authorized and points enroute, if any,  are  detected  set  &  locked  on  RPS/ATS  MMI/MPD  and  no  conflicting  route  is  set. While providing authorization with Danger Signal & Points enroute, TC shall additionally confirm the status of such point as set & locked from the SC, who shall confirm the same by comparing on LOCAL ATS MMI.

(iv)  TC shall  ensure that  the  track  ahead  is  clear  up  to  the  destination  being  authorized  on RPS  display/ATS  MMI  &  MPD.  If  Track  circuit  is  showing  occupied,  he  will  ask  TO  to

## Introduction

reconfirm the status of track ahead on his line of sight. If TO's information is not sufficient, TC  may  also  ask  SC  of  next  station  to  physically  check  the  track  occupancy  from  the station platforms. If required, TC, through radio communication, may try to establish the location of preceding train as per time table and shall ensure that track is clear up to the end of next platform.

## Introduction

(v)  While  authorizing  the  limit  of  movement  in  RM  mode  or  low  speed  cut  out  mode  (at  a maximum speed of 25 kmph), TC shall ensure that the  train  ahead  has  left  the  station ahead and is continuing its journey except in exceptional cases of rescue train or other similar emergency to be decided by Chief Controller, wherein the train being driven under line of sight may be permitted to go near the disabled train ahead or any track obstruction at lower speed such that TO is able to safely stop his train short of obstruction or disabled train ahead.
(vi)  In case of a train running in high speed cut out mode (at a maximum speed of 40 kmph), the  TC  shall  take  specific  permission  from  Chief  Controller  for  such  movement  and  if permitted,  shall  ensure  that  the  train  ahead  is  at  least  two  block  sections  away  and  is continuing its journey.
## NOTE:  Driving  of  trains  in  high  speed  cut  out  mode  is  prohibited  until  further instructions.

(vii)  In RM, Low speed cut out mode and high speed cut out mode, the TC shall also ensure that  no  two  trains  are  in  the  same  ventilation  section  unless  permitted  by  the  chief controller due to exigencies of service.
(viii)  This  minimum  inter  train  safety  distance  as  mentioned  above  can  be  reduced  if  the permitted train speed is lower than above maximum permissible speeds in these modes. Such lower maximum permitted speed shall be specifically advised by the TC to the TO while authorizing him to proceed. Such reduction in train separation should be permitted very carefully considering the various factors governing the braking distance including any brake malfunction/isolation and downgrades etc. and after having confirmed from the train operator under exchange of private numbers that the train speed shall be kept below the agreed limit.
8.2 COMMUNICATION DURING DEGRADED MODE: Following guidelines for communication in degraded mode should be followed to ensure safety.
(i)  Any instruction to the TO for authorizing him to move in degraded mode shall be given on Radio  on  exchange  of  private  number  between  TO  and  TC.  In  case  of  communication failure,  control  shall  be  transferred  to  the  SC  of  concerned  interlocking  zone  and authorization for movement in degraded mode shall be given to the TO by the concerned SC on exchange of private number or in writing if communication fails between them also.

(ii)  Whenever a signal is Danger and proceed code is not available to train, TO shall inform TC giving his Train Number, exact location, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), status  of  track  on  his  line  of  sight,  status  of  train  &  direction  of  travel  and  shall  seek authorization from TC before moving the train in degraded mode.
(iii)  TC, while giving authorization to TO for movement in degraded mode shall clearly mention the train no, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), line (UP/DN) & destination up to which it is authorized, the degraded mode in which movement is authorized and shall offer his private number.

## Introduction

He/she  shall then provide his private number to TC and make the entry in the private number book.

10.0  While authorizing reception of trains, moving in degraded mode, at terminal stations, in addition  to  normal  precautions  as  detailed  in  previous  Para,  TC  shall  take  following additional precautions :

10.1  If  no  trains  are  stabled  on  stabling/overlap  tracks  or  are  stabled  on  the  line  other  than  the reception line  then:
(i) At both DSTO & NDRU, normal precautions for degraded movements are required to be taken.
10.2  If trains  are stabled on the stabling/overlap track of receiving platform, then:
(i) At DSTO, the overlap should be set towards the other line (rear crossover reversed)
(ii) At NDRU, train should be received on the other platform (if possible)
10.3   If trains are stabled on both the stabling overlap tracks then:
(i) At DSTO, TO shall be intimated of the obstruction ahead and asked to proceed with extra caution towards the platform under exchange of Private number.
10.4  If stabled trains are not indicated as occupied on the overview panel:
(i) TC shall immediately intimate Signaling Fault Controller of the fault.
(ii) At DSTO, TC shall block the Track circuit using ATS MMI.
(iii) At NDRU,TC shall block the Track circuit and in case train is received on the same line then,  points  in  the  route  shall  be  electrically  locked  and  also  advise  the  TO  to  be  extra cautious while moving the train towards the platform.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR-41A (Rev-01)

P ROCEDURE ORDER FOR DETRAINMENT OF PASSENGERS FROM IMMOBILE/ DISABLE TRAIN  DUE  TO  TECHNICAL  FAILURES  AND  EXPLOSION  &  FIRE  IN  STANDARD  AND BROAD G AUGE SECTIONS/LINES -1,2,3,4, 7, 8, 9 OF METRO SYSTEM

## SAFETY CIRCULAR-41A (Rev-01)

This  procedure  order  has  two  parts  namely  Part-I  &  Part-II  where  Part-I  deals  with detrainment of passengers due to technical failures and Part-II deals with detrainment of passengers due to EXPLOSION & Fire. This PO shall be read in conjunction with MRGR 2020 and  safety  circulars,  SC-12,  SC-12A,  SC-15,  SC-16,  SC-33  and  SC-34  and  supersedes provisions made in the earlier safety circulars in case of any conflict.

## 1. Introduction

This  procedure  order  deals  with  detrainment  of  passengers  from  an  immobile  train  due  to technical failures in all broad gauge sections/lines- 1, 2, 3 & 4 and standard gauge lines Line-, 7, 8 & 9.
The purpose of the procedure order is to delineate roles and responsibility of Train Operators (TO), OCC staff, Station staff and other metro staff for carrying out prompt and safe passenger evacuation from an immobile train in order to minimize hardship to the passengers.

## 2. Scope

This  procedure  order  should  be  read  in  conjunction  with  MRGR  2020,  Accident  &  Disaster Manual and other relevant existing safety circulars.
For UTO mode of train operation : Wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
This Procedure Order shall be applicable when a metro train becomes disable/immobile in the block section and it cannot be moved on its own power or cannot be even rescued with another assisting train either due to failure of Rolling stock or Rigid Over Head Catenary/ OHE system or  obstruction  on  Permanent  way  system  due  to  its  own  failure  or  for  any  other  technical reasons. Detrainment of passengers from such immobile/disable train shall be train to track, carried out as per the procedure order detailed in the subsequent paras.

## 4. General Instructions for all metro lines

4.1. Planned detrainment will only start after confirming that movement of trains on both tracks has been suspended.
4.2. Metro  staff  shall  be  deployed  to  assist  the  Train  Operators  (TO)  &  the  detraining passengers, in their safe evacuation.
4.3. Train unable to move due to derailment or mechanical failure:

## Introduction

If  a  train  cannot  be  moved  as  a  result  of  derailment  or  axle  lock  leading  to  possible infringement, the train shall switch-on the flasher light and sends alarm to Operations Control Centre on Line-7 and 8, on other lines information shall be conveyed to OCC by any means of communication. Traffic controller to stop all the trains to affected area. Operations Control Centre shall take necessary action to restore train movement.

## Introduction

Movement of trains on adjacent tracks is prohibited and shutdown of traction on same or adjacent line shall be as per advice of TPC. Further, Traffic Controller shall follow all provisions of MRGR 50 (3).
4.4. For tunnels: In case of smoke or fire in the tunnel and/or train, traffic controller & Auxiliary system controller shall follow sub rule (5) of MRGR 52 for supply of fresh air and extraction of smoke, using information from cameras and information received otherwise,
4.5. During Broken OHE/ROCS, The passenger should not be evacuated towards broken OHE side unless discharge rod is provided.
4.6. First train in the section from both directions after rescue of the failed train post evacuation must run in RM mode at the speed of 15kmph.

## 5. Authority for detrainment

The Train Operators (TO) must make all out efforts to run the train to the next station to avoid detrainment between stations wherever feasible. However, if it is not possible, the detrainment shall  take  place  with  the  authority  of  Chief  controller/Traffic  Controller  in  consultation  with HOD/Ops or Dy.HOD/Ops. In the case of extreme emergency, when the safety of passengers is  at risk and Communication with the Operation Control Centre (OCC) has failed, the Train Operators (TO) shall try to contact OCC by any viable means of communication including DMO mode of Radio, Emergency Telephone, or mobile phone of any passenger. If communication cannot be established with OCC, the Train Operators (TO) shall initiate passengers evacuation on foot towards station ahead so that the stalled train acts as a protection. In case a train is in tunnel for more than 10 minutes and Train Operators (TO) is not communicating/responding, then a team of two persons from rear station should be sent to train to assist/rescue, along with appropriate means of communication, Square Key and swipe card for RS-2 trains and TC in this case shall stop train movement on both tracks i.e. including adjacent track also.

## 6. Plan-A : Actions & precautions to be taken for detrainment in elevated/at grade sections/lines

The following actions and precautions will be taken in case of an immobile/disable train, stalled between stations.
6.1. In case of P. way, OHE, Traction power supply failure or mechanical RS failure that causes train to become disable/immobile and it is not possible to carry out rescue with assisting train for  more  than  15  minutes,  CHC/OCC  in  consultation  with  HOD/Ops  or  Dy.HOD/Ops  shall decide  to  detrain  passengers  from  the  train  to  track  on  foot  for  evacuating  them  to  the designated station.
6.2. The Traffic  Controller,  in  consultation  with  the  Train  Operators  (TO),  shall  decide  to  which Station passengers shall be evacuated, which shall normally be the nearest station. However, it  can be an alternative station, if the situation so warrants, depending upon the location of trains  and  damage to track,  train  or  structures.  The  TC  will  inform  Security  Controller  and DMRP/Police  depending  upon  the  requirement  for  effective  crowd  control.  Lights  on  open viaduct to be switched on in case of detrainment during night if available.
6.3. The  TC  will  stop  the  following  train  at  the  station  in  rear  immediately  and  will  stop  train movement  on  adjacent  line  prior  to  permit  passenger  evacuation  on  foot.  The  TC  will

## Introduction

regulate other trains in the unaffected area to provide optimum train service by introducing short  loop  operation.  The  TC  will  block/lock  the  en-route  points  in  the  path  of  passenger evacuation for ensuring that points in the route of detrainment are not altered while detrainment is in progress.

6.4. The  traffic  controller  shall  inform  the  Train  Operators  (TO)  of  the  affected  train  about  the evacuation plan as to which station the passengers will be sent and whether the evacuation shall  be  done  through  emergency  door  towards  the  designated  station  or  both  emergency doors, depending upon train location, number of passengers in the train and other prevailing conditions.
6.5. Train Operators (TO) / Information Controller (IC) (in case of UTO mode of operation) of the train  will  make  necessary  announcements  in  the  train  to  inform  passengers  about  the evacuation plan and will also make following pre-recorded/manual announcements regularly to avoid panic reactions.
Request passengers to remain calm,
Listen patiently and follow the directions being given.
Exit from the train only when directed.
Request volunteer co-passengers/metro staff present in the train to assist physically challenged, senior citizens, women, children and sick passengers in their safe evacuation.
Request any metro staff travelling in the train to assist during the imminent evacuation.
6.6. Prior to opening of emergency door towards the designated station, announcement advising passengers about the tripping hazards on track, status of live overhead wires, where to walk, not to lift any object such as an umbrella or walking stick above their head level to prevent electrocution and what to expect at the station shall be made.
6.7. The Train Operators (TO) will put the Mode Selector to 'OFF' position and will take the Mascon key out to deactivate the cab. For UTO mode of Operation, please refer para 6.14.

6.7. The Train Operators (TO) will put the Mode Selector to 'OFF' position and will take the Mascon key out to deactivate the cab. For UTO mode of Operation, please refer para 6.14.
6.8. The  Train  Operators  (TO)  will  open  emergency  door  towards  the  designated  station himself/herself and advise travelling staff or passengers to open another emergency door, if instructed to do so by the OCC. The Train Operators (TO) will advise passengers detraining from other emergency door to go to the designated station only, after exiting
6.9. The traffic controller shall inform the station Controller at the station designated to receive the passengers and  to  immediately  arrange  to  send  station  staff,  equipped  with  a  specially provided Tetra set and loud hailer, to the site to assist in passenger evacuation. 7.3. The  TC  will  stop  the  following  train  at  the  station  in  rear  immediately  and  will  stop  train movement on adjacent line prior to permit passenger evacuation on foot. The TC will block/lock the enroute points in the path of passenger evacuation for

## PART-II: DETRAINMENT OF PASSENGERS DUE TO EXPLOSION & FIRE

This procedure order deals with detrainment of passengers from a train due to EXPLOSION &/OR FIRE in all broad gauge sections/lines- 1, 2, 3 & 4 and standard gauge lines Line-, 7, 8 & 9. The system is not designed for bomb explosion. The threat of Bomb etc is to be dealt with security measures. This is a contingency plan, proposed with intent, that what best can be done under the circumstances. This procedure order should be read in conjunction with MRGR 2020 and other relevant existing safety circulars.

## 1. Introduction:

The purpose of the procedure order is to delineate roles and responsibility of Train Operators (TO)s, OCC staff, Station staff and other metro staff for carrying out prompt and safe passenger evacuation from an immobile/disable train in order to minimize hardship to the passengers.

## 2. Scope

This Procedure Order shall be applicable when a train becomes immobile/disable due to EXPLOSION & FIRE in the train and it cannot be moved further or rescued by assisting train. Detrainment of passengers from such immobile/disable train to track shall be carried out in event of the following:
2.1. Bomb blast causing fire and smoke and train gets stalled in either elevated or underground tunnel section between two stations.
2.2. Fire  &  Fusing  -  train  stalled  in  section  between  two  stations  including  underground  tunnel sections.

## 4. Authority for detrainment

The Train Operators (TO) must make out all efforts to run the train to the next station to avoid detrainment between stations wherever feasible. However, if it is not possible, the detrainment shall  take  place  with  the  authority  of  Chief  controller/Traffic  Controller  in  consultation  with HOD/Ops or Dy.HOD/Ops. In the case of extreme emergency, when the safety of passengers is  at risk and Communication with the Operation Control Centre (OCC) has failed, the Train Operators (TO) shall try to contact OCC by any viable means of communication including DMO mode of Radio, Emergency Telephone, or mobile phone of any passenger. If communication cannot be established with OCC, the Train Operators (TO) shall initiate passengers evacuation on foot towards station ahead so that the stalled train acts as a protection. In case a train is in tunnel for more than 10 minutes and Train Operators (TO). is not communicating/responding, then a team of two persons from rear station should be sent to train to assist/rescue, along with appropriate means of communication, Square Key and swipe card for RS-2 trains and TC in this case shall stop train movement on both tracks i.e. including adjacent track also.

The smoke, being light in weight, has tendency to move to higher gradient. The passengers shall be guided to keep a handkerchief or other cloth, preferably wet, to cover their noses and advance by crawling/walking on knees/bending towards the nearest cross passage or the station on either side in the event of smoke coming in their passage. The passengers can be guided  to  use  cross  passages  to  get  in  to  another  non  affected  tunnel  during  such evacuations.

## 5. NIGHT STABLING OF CMV/ CTMC IN MAINLINE .

To increase effective maintenance time during block it is desirable to stable CMV/CTMC in the mainline during night.
5.1. Request for night stabling of CMV will be included in the requisition for Weekly General Order submitted by TPC to Chief Controller.
5.2. Night stabling of CMV/CTMC will be planned at siding nearest to EP section granted to CMV/CTMC.
5.3. CMV/CTMC will be stabled at designated siding on mainline only a day prior to its approved work as per Weekly General Order.
5.4. To vacate sidings for night stabling of CMV/CTMC if required then night stabling trains will be sent to depot, if feasible.
5.5. After  stabling  of  CMV  at  siding,  CMV/CTMC  in-charge  will  ensure  that  all  mechanical/ parking brakes are fully applied. He will secure the CMV/CTMC by putting scotch blocks at both sides of wheels at all four end wheels and chain must be tied around scotch blocks on wheels and must be tied with fixed object at track side. A red colored retro reflective tape not less than (10 cm X 10 cm) - 2 nos shall be pasted at both side of CMV/CTMC and Red

text: ## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 07 E (REV-03)

## Applicable to Line - 7 & 9 only.

Subject:- Procedure for Train Movement in Degraded Mode in Line - 7 & 9.
Find enclosed Safety Circular-07E (Rev-03) regarding 'Procedure for Train Movement in Degraded Mode in Line - 7 & 9'.
All concerned are to ensure that staff working under them have read and understood the procedure and assurance regarding the same is taken.
This is issued with the approval of the competent authority.
(Rajesh Kumar Raghav) Sr. DGM/Ops/Cord.
Copy to: All EDs/HODs (O&M) and DG (DMRC Academy), All Dy. HODs (O&M), Mgr/AM (Concerned Line, Station and OCC),
All Stations, All Crew Controls, All DCC and DMRC Academy
## PROCEDURE FOR TRAIN MOVEMENT IN DEGRADED MODE IN LINE - 7 & 9

## 2.0 SCOPE

2.1 This procedure is applicable for the Train Movement in Degraded Modes of Train Operation in Line-7.
2.2 Since the Signaling system for Line-9 has same Bombardier signaling which is used on Line-7. Therefore, this procedure is applicable for Line-9 also except for following.
(i) Wherever "CATS/Video wall" or "CATS & Video wall' is mentioned in SC-07E to be read as 'CATS" only in case of Line-9.
(ii) Para '7.1 (vii & viii)' is not applicable for Line-09, as PSD is not provided onLine-09.
2.3 This procedure Order shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railway General Rules, 2020 and its Amendment, Safety   Circulars & other Instructions in vogue.
2.4 For UTO mode of Train Operation: Wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/Emergency Train Operator (ETO).

## 3.0 DEFINITIONS

3.1 Degraded Mode: Degraded  Mode  of  Train  Operation,  hereafter  referred  as  Degraded  Mode include strain movement in RM, ROS & Cut-Out Mode. The train is moved by TO on his line of sight exercising utmost vigilance so as to stop short of any obstruction ensuring that train speed does not exceed 25 kmph or less if applicable.
3.2 Route Set : A route is considered as set if its valid indication on the VIDEO WALL/CATS/LATS/VDU is displaying the track in white colour.
3.3 Point Set & Locked : A point is indicated as set & locked if and only if a valid indication on the VIDEO WALL/CATS/LATS/VDU displays the corresponding route as set and the point  under reference  set  &  locked  (i.e.  displaying  cyan  square  box  on  Point  as  given  below)  and  not flashing.
3.4 Danger Signal : A Danger Signal means that a Fixed Signal is displaying:-
(i) Red aspect; or
(ii) Flickering of aspects; or
(iii) Multiple aspects; or
(iv) No aspect (Blank).
## 4.0 OBJECTIVE

## 4.0 OBJECTIVE

4.1 Ensuring total safety of trains running in degraded mode.

## 4.0 OBJECTIVE

4.2 Ensuring unambiguous communication for authorization in Degraded Mode.
4.3 Ensuring efficient movement of trains in degraded mode.
## 5.0 GENERAL

5.1 Train shall be moved in degraded mode under the following circumstances after authorization from TC is obtained on exchange of private number as per Para'8' .
(i) In case of loss of communication between train and wayside radio system.
(ii) In case of loss of proceed code.
(iii) For passing a signal at danger when driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out mode.
(iv) Violet Signal shall be considered as danger Signal when driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out mode.
(v) If ATP/Coded manual mode cannot be selected due to any reason.
5.2 Movement in degraded mode shall be authorized from one point to other as per below given guidelines, provided the route is clear of any obstruction from the origin to the destination & all points enroute are set & locked and if there are any signal enroute, passing the same shall be explicitly included in the authorization clearly stating the aspect.
(i) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from one station platform to next station platform.
(ii) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  to  the  train  stopped in the midsection/siding from the point of stopping to the next station platform.
(iii) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from a station platform to an intervening fixed signal before the next station platform, provided section is clear upto the intervening fixed signal, explicitly informing TO if next station is occupied, duly instructing TO to stop at foot of such fixed signal.

(iii) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from a station platform to an intervening fixed signal before the next station platform, provided section is clear upto the intervening fixed signal, explicitly informing TO if next station is occupied, duly instructing TO to stop at foot of such fixed signal.
(iv) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from a station platform to an intervening fixed signal or up to the next station platform, having a train in section, provided the TO of the preceding train in section has reported receipt of ATP/Proceed Code, without waiting for  the  train  to  clear  the  section,  explicitly  informing  TO  to  move  cautiously  observing utmost caution so as to stop short of any obstruction.
(v) In case TC gets positive indication on ATS of any train, running in degraded mode, has receiving  ATP/Proceed  Code,  TC  shall  advise  TO  to  stop  his  train  and  select  ATP  for further movement.
(vi) During reversal/stabling in siding, authorization shall be given up to SRMB/stabling point.

## Note:- TC shall not authorize any train working in degraded mode to move upto a virtual signal.

## 10.0 CBTC Communication Failure Management

## 10.0 CBTC Communication Failure Management

In case of the CBTC Communication Failure where the Train/Trains are required to move in Degraded Mode, Location of Train/Train's will not be available only lost train indication on its last location with Rake ID will be available on ATS MMI/ VDU/Video Wall. In this case, there is possibility  of  more  than  one  (CBTC  or  Non  CBTC)  Train  present  in  the  same  axle  counter (Track Section). The following steps shall be adopted:-
(i) TC shall positively identify leading Train by comparing view on ATSMMI/VDU.
(ii) After  ensuring  identification  of  leading  Train,  TC  shall  authorize  leading  Train  as  per extant  procedure  described  in  this  procedure  order.  TC  shall  also  advice  TO  of succeeding Train/Train's present in the segment to wait for further instruction.
(iii)    After the leading Train, so authorized to move in Degraded Mode, clears the authorized destination PF/Signal, TC shall authorize TO of succeeding Train to move in Degraded Mode as per extant procedure.
(iv) If  location  of Train/Train's is not available through presence of Train ID or Rake ID on ATS MMI or VDU (Video Wall), TC shall confirm locations along with train ID from Train Operators  in  the  failed  Track  Segment.  Leading  Train  will  be  identified  using  this information, line of sight clearance and verification from timetable.
(v) In  case  of  control  is  at  local,  the  responsibility  of  TC  will  delve  upon  the  concerned Station Controller.

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order governs the Movement of the first Train in any Section as a Pilot Train. Running of Pilot Train assumes added importance on Sections, wherein certain Maintenance / Repair  /  Other  Work  including  certain  Installation  Work  had  been  carried  out  by  taking  the Engineer's Possession of the Section or part thereof.

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

The Procedure specifies the Precautions and Care to be taken by all the concerned Staff.

## 2.0 SCOPE

This Procedure Order is applicable for all Lines and shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 & Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules, 2022 & Special Instructions in vogue.
For UTO mode of Train Operation: Wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/Emergency Train Operator (ETO).

## 3.0 PROCEDURE

3.1 Before the  movement of Pilot  Train,  OCC must ensure  that  all  the  EPICs  /  Sub-EPICs  have submitted PTW Cancellation Forms as per extant procedure in vogue.
