(b) Hot Weather : -

During extreme hot weather condition, P. Way wing will request for hot weather patrolling in  ballasted  section  of  Line-01  (between  SHD  and  KG)  and  Line-03  (between  IDPT  ASDM & LN) to concerned TC/OCC well in advance with relevant details such as time of piloting, who will further inform to concerned Train Operator. Authorised P. Way staff will accompany Train Operator at requested time for track inspection in concerned section as per existing procedure to ensure safety against buckling of track. The speed of the train shall be as per proceed code or as advised by P. Way staff.
3.3 OCC shall coordinate with DCC and outstation stabled train TOs for the Movement of the Pilot Train. The Movement of the Pilot Train(s) (i.e. the first Train in any Section or part thereof) shall take place, as per the timings given in the concerned Line Train Time Table.
3.4 The  Train  shall  move  in  ATP  Mode  under  Cab  Signalling.  TO  shall  follow  all  the  Speed Restrictions enforced in the Section(s) and follow Cab and Fixed Signals. In case Cab Signalling is not available, the Train shall be driven in the Degraded Mode, as per Procedure in vogue.
3.5 The Pilot Train (s) will move from the Depot as per Time Table. It will also perform Revenue or Non-Revenue Service according to the Time Table.

3.5 The Pilot Train (s) will move from the Depot as per Time Table. It will also perform Revenue or Non-Revenue Service according to the Time Table.
3.6 Though in Revenue Service, the Train will continue to act as a Pilot Train as mentioned in the Time Table with a Maximum Restricted Speed as mentioned in Para 3.2. While stopping Train at every station TO shall also ensure proper opening/closing of saloon doors and PSDs (where provided) of correct side, and if any abnormality noticed in opening/closing of doors inform to OCC.
3.7 Piloting by Testing/Night Trial Train:
(i) However, a testing train or night trial train in its way to depot or stabling location shall also work as pilot train in addition to scheduled pilot train. Testing train or night trial train shall follow all speed restrictions as per Para 3.2 & mode of operation as per Para 3.4.
(ii) If  the  section  of  the  Piloting  needs  to  be  different  as  mentioned  in  above  at  S.no.  (i), TC/OCC shall apprise CHC/OCC and advise TO under exchange of Private Numbers, duly specifying the Section, the reason & the speed restriction to be followed therein.
(iii) During said movement Station Skip shall be avoided.
3.8 If no abnormality is noticed during pilot train run, the same shall be reported by TO to TC/OCC after end of piloting section.  Normal services as per train time table shall be allowed thereafter.
3.9 If any abnormality is noticed during the Pilot Train Run by the TO: -

3.9 If any abnormality is noticed during the Pilot Train Run by the TO: -
(i) Which is not likely to  affect  the  Safe  Running  of  Trains,  the  same  shall  be  reported  to OCC and TO will drive the Train cautiously.
(ii)  Which is likely to  affect/ infringe the Safe Running of Trains, he/she shall stop the Train short  of  the  Obstruction  and  report  the  same  to  OCC  immediately.  The  TC/OCC  shall coordinate  with  concerned  Controllers  in  OCC  to  get  the  abnormality  /  infringement cleared. For Pending rectification on the affected portion of the Track, the Section shall be blocked for the Movement of following Revenue Trains. OCC will arrange Movement of Revenue Trains with Temporary Single Line Working / Short Loop Operation or any other expedient,  as  deemed  fit.  The  OCC  will  permit  Movement  on  the  affected  Section  only after getting written Confirmation of Clearance / Fitness of the Section from the concerned Controller (s) in the OCC.

Sidings, Third Platform and  inside the Depot  (including transfer track); fitness of equipments/ track/OHE etc. & SOD clearance in the said section shall be ensured by concerned department. ## 4.3 For Line-7 :-

## 4.3 For Line-7 :-

(i) Pilot train movement shall be performed by non-revenue train in ATP Mode. After getting confirmation  of  UTO  Self-Testing  (UST)  from  TC/OCC,  RA  shall  board  the  train(s)  (if already not on-board) which are scheduled for piloting on mainline from the designated location. After reaching inside the train, RA shall uncover the operating desk (if covered) and shall change Mode Selector position from 'Auto' to 'ATP' under exchange of private number with TC.
(ii) The movement of pilot train(s) shall take place in ATP mode (as per extant procedure). RA shall keep sharp lookout and stop the train if any abnormality is noticed, and inform the TC/OCC.
(iii) Staff from other department i.e. Civil, Traction, RS, Signalling, Tele, E&M etc. may board for piloting as per requirement.
(iv) After completion of mainline piloting, in case no abnormality is observed, RA shall switch over the train to UTO mode as per extant procedure.
## 4.4 For Line-8 :-

(i) Pilot train movement shall be performed by non-revenue train in UTO mode (with RA onboard)  at  speed  provided  by  CATC  with  maximum  speed  40  kmph  in  UTO  system.  In case, CATC provides speed profile greater than 40 kmph, piloting shall be done in ATP mode with speed limit of 40 Kmph. TC/OCC shall instruct on board RA to take charge of train, under exchange of Private Number, duly specifying the Section, driving mode & the speed restriction to be followed therein for piloting.
(ii) RA shall board the trains which are scheduled for piloting from the designated location. RA shall open panel number-2 before start of pilot train movement and inform to TC/OCC over tetra. S/he shall remain alert to press EBPB-2 in case any abnormality is observed and inform to TC/OCC over tetra.
(iii) Before  start  of  the  pilot  train  movement,  TC/OCC  shall  ensure  application  of  'Out  of Service'  feature  at  the  platforms/section  on  which  non-revenue  pilot  train  movement  is defined in time table and also in train.

(iv) Staff from other department i.e. Civil, Traction, RS, Signalling, Tele, E&M etc. may board the  piloting  train  preferably  from  depot/stabling  location  till  the  last  station  of  schedule piloting for schedule inspection work to avoid interruption /train delay/ manual intervention. However, in emergency staff may board/de-board from/at other stations also. Maintenance Staff shall inform TC/OCC well in advance and after getting confirmation/permission  of  TC/OCC,  Staff  shall  reach  near  first  door  of  train  in  DOT  of designated platform. The steps for on boarding/de-boarding of maintenance staff in UTO piloting train is detailed below:

## Introduction

(a)  TC shall apply platform hold at designated platform and inform RSC duly advising him to isolate all doors except 1st platform side door of train in DOT (Direction of Travel).

(b) RSC shall isolate all doors except 1st platform side door of train in DOT.
(c) TC shall give door open command.
(d)  Maintenance staff shall board/de-board in/from train from first saloon door and confirm to TC/OCC.
(e)  After  Staff  confirmation,  TC  shall  give  door  close  command  and  advise  RSC  to normalize the isolated doors.
(f) RSC shall normalize the isolation of all doors and ensure that all doors are closed and inform to TC.
(g)  After RSC confirmation, TC shall release platform hold and depart the train.
Note :-  If  train  is  in  ATP  mode, RA shall board/de-board the maintenance staff from first saloon door of the train by giving suitable command.
4.5 Duties of Other Controllers in OCC ( For Line - 7 & 8 ):-
(a) Civil Controller: Continuous monitoring and analysis of the Rail Check System shall be ensured by Civil Controller on its workstation. Images of track through rolling stock front and rear track cameras shall be analysed by the Civil Controller on daily basis for the pilot trains on Civil Controller workstation and corrective action shall be initiated immediately on noticing  any  abnormality  and  appraise  the  matter  to  concerned  Sr.  Officers  and  Chief Controller. If required, Civil Controller shall use RSC workstation to analyse the past feeds of  track  camera,  after taking  consent from RSC. In case, Civil Controller requires video footage of any  section for fault  analysis,  S/he  may  demand  the  recorded  video  of front camera of piloting train & data of RCS from RSC as per procedure in vogue.

(b) Traction  Power  Controller  (TPC): Images of OHE through rolling stock front  and rear catenary  cameras  and  Panto-OHE  cameras  shall  be  analysed  by  the  Traction  Power Controller on daily basis for the pilot trains on TPC workstation and corrective action shall be initiated immediately on noticing any abnormality and appraise the matter to concerned Sr. Officers and Chief Controller. If required, TPC shall use RSC workstation to analyse the past feeds of cameras, after taking consent from RSC. In case, TPC requires video footage of any section for fault  analysis,  S/he  may  demand the  recorded  video  of front camera of piloting train & data of RCS from RSC as per procedure in vogue.
(c) Signalling System Controller (SGC): SGC shall analyse data received from signalling system on daily basis for the pilot train for any possible fault on Signalling equipments/System. In case, of finding of any abnormality, SGC shall immediately take the necessary steps for rectification of abnormality and upraise the matter to concerned Sr. Officers, OCM and Chief Controller.
(d) Chief Controller: on the basis of feedback of concerned controller, Chief Controller shall decide the required operation strategy.
4.6 RA shall close the panel number-2 (Line-8) / operating desk (Line-7) after completion of pilot train run and confirm the same to TC/OCC under exchange of private number.
4.7 RA shall seek permission and inform to TC/OCC before de-boarding the train.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 16 (Rev.-02)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR DETRAINMENT OF PASSENGERS IN AN UNDERGROUND TUNNEL SECTION

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

In most Crisis Situations, the prompt Detrainment of Passengers and their Safe Evacuation from the Incident  Train  immensely  helps  in  mitigating  their  Hardship  and  Distress.  This  Procedure  Order describes  the  Rules and  Regulations  to  be followed  by  Staff for  detraining  the Passengers from a Train, stalled in an Underground Section.

## 2.  SCOPE

This  procedure  is  applicable  for  all  Lines.  Procedure  Order  contains  the  Procedures  for  Train-toTrack, Train-to-Walkway and Train-to-Train Detrainments, arising out of:
(i) Traction Current Failures.
(ii) Failure of Rolling Stock and consequent Stalling of a Train in the Tunnel or at a Station
(iii) Fire or Fusing in a Train stalled in the Tunnel or at a Station.
(iv) Any other Incident causing immobilization of the Train, including Arson / Terrorist Activity.
The Document has been divided in '6' Parts. Part-I provides the Basic Guiding Principles in facilitating Detrainment. Part-II lists out the Roles & Responsibilities of Metro Staff in affecting Detrainment. PartIII & IV deal with Train-to-Train and Train-to-Track / Train-to-Walkway Detrainment. Part-V & VI cater for  the  specific  situations  like  Traction  Current  Failure  or  Fire  /  Fusing  in  the  Train  leading  to  the Detrainment of Passengers from it. Instructions relating to Fire / Fusing in the Train should be read in conjunction with the Instructions contained in Safety Circulars - '12' & '12A' SC-41A & SC-41B & SC41C
This procedure shall be read in conjunction Metro Railway General Rule-2020, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
## PART I
## 3.  BASIC GUIDING PRINCIPLES IN FACILITATING DETRAINMENT

## 3.  BASIC GUIDING PRINCIPLES IN FACILITATING DETRAINMENT

3.1 While deciding whether 'Detrainment' is necessary, due consideration shall be given to:
(i) The Cause of the Incident.
(ii) Environmental Condition in the Train Cars.
(iii)  When the Train could resume working.
(iv)  Any other relevant factors e.g. Passengers Panic and unrest etc.
3.2 In  case  of  any  Eventuality  or  Distress  Situation  on  a  stalled  Train,  normally  the  Passengers  are detrained  to  the  Track/  walkway,  the  Process  known  as  'Train-to-Track/  walkway'  Detrainment. However, if the circumstances are like to  make  the 'Train-to-Track/ walkway' Detrainment inappropriate, the Passengers from the stalled Train may be detrained to an Assisting Train either on the same track or on adjacent track in what is called 'Train-to-Train' Mode of Detrainment.
3.3 Detrainment must only take place with the Authority of the Traffic Controller (TC), except in the cases of extreme Emergencies like Failure of Communication with OCC, and Deterioration of Environmental Conditions due to little prolonged failures of Rolling Stock / OHE and / or break out of Fire / Fumes and likely hood of its quick spreading in the surrounding, causing or likely to cause great Risk to the Safety  of  Passengers.  In  all  such  cases,  TO  shall  assume  the  functions  of  OCS  and  take  such

## Introduction

immediate Action so as to render all possible help to the distressed Passengers in the Stalled Train, including their emergency Evacuation from it.

3.4 The TO must make all out Efforts to run the Train to the next Station to avoid Detrainment between the Stations.
3.5 To enable a Train to reach the nearby Station it may be necessary, depending upon the Situation, to arrange:
(i)  A Wrong Direction Movement.
(ii)  Provide Assistance by sending another Train to the Incident Site.
3.6 If  Detrained  on  the  Track/  walkway,  the  Passengers  must  be  directed  to  the  next  Station  in  the Normal Direction of Running except when the Distance between the Train and the Station ahead is more and it is an Emergency of the kind that it is not feasible to make the Passengers to move in the Normal Direction of the Running of Train on that Line.
3.7 Before authorizing passengers' detrainment from train to track / walkway, the Traffic Controller shall stop the following train at the preceding station, wherever possible, on the same line and shall also arrange for Traffic to be suspended on the adjacent Track for the duration of the Evacuation. This Restriction shall apply until the Detrainment has been completed, confirmed by the TO and the Track declared Clear of the Passengers.
3.8 Detrainment, wherever possible, should be carried out with the assistance of Station Staff.
3.9 Once it has been decided to de-train the Passengers either between the Stations or at the Station:
(i) Information must be regularly given to the Passengers by Public Announcement, informing them about  the  Arrangements  being  made  and  the  Procedure  to  be  followed  for  detrainment. Passengers shall also be explicitly warned on Tripping Hazards, where to walk and what to expect at the Station.

(ii) The OCC should inform the Security Control for Assistance from Metro Police/Local Police for Crowd Control at Stations.
3.10 To  prevent  the  Passengers  from  diverging  from  the  decided  Detrainment  Route  and      falling  on Obstructions,  Passenger  must  be  clearly  informed  of  the  Route  &  Direction  of  Detrainment  and repeatedly  warned  to  avoid  Points  and  Crossings,  Cross-passages,  and  other  Pockets  of  such Hazards. In addition, TC must issue directions to Station Controller that the Points in the Route of Detrainment are not altered, while the Detrainment is in progress. In fact, all the Points in the Route of Evacuation shall be blocked by suitable Blocking Commands and the Fleet Mode, if Set, shall be immediately Cancelled.
3.11  Staff assisting in the Detrainment should be, as far as applicable, equipped with:
(i) Hand Lamps / Torches.
(ii) Loudhailers.
(iii) Hand Portable Radios.
(iv) Mobile Phones (if available).
3.12  Tunnel  Lights  shall  be  Switched-on  before  any  Staff  or  Passenger  is  likely  to  embark  on  to  the Track.
3.13  Detrainment and Evacuation Route should be properly and effectively ventilated.
3.14  Traction Supply may not be Switched-off, except:

(i) For preventing Arcing,

(ii) In the case, the Overhead Line is defective, is displaced or likely to get damaged.
(iii) Fire Hydrant System is to be used, in the portion affecting OHE.
(iv) Detrainment/Rescue Operation Needs require the work to be carried out within 2 Meters of OHE System.

7.0 Emergency  Evacuation  from  Staircase  at  Mid  Tunnel  Shaft  Located  between  Central Secretariat (CTST) & Khan Market (KM) Stations:
(A) General:

## Introduction

(i) Underground  Stations  on  Delhi  Metro  are  generally  interspersed  at  a  distance  of  0.6  to  1.8  Kms. Inter-station  distance  on  one  Section  between  'CTST'  &  'KM'  on  Line  '6',  however,  is  2.5  Kms. Increased Length of this Section is like to cause a possibility that more than one Train may enter in the Section at one time. To resolve the issue of Passenger Evacuation as a result of stalling of a Train for one reason or other in this Section, a Mid-shaft has, therefore, been provided in the middle of the Section to divide the Section in to two Ventilation Zones on each of UP & Down lines. The Mid Tunnel Shaft is provided at Cross Passage at Mast Nos. 01/048 - 01/050 on Down Line and 01/49 01/51 on UP Line. This Mid Tunnel Shaft is connected at Ground Level on Moti Lal Nehru Marg, which is at a walking distance from Udyog Bhawan Metro Station on Line -2 (Sunehri Masjid Side).

## Introduction

(ii) The  Tunnel  Ventilation  System  equipment  installed  at  Mid-shaft  can  be  operated,  controlled  and monitored from OCC at Metro Bhawan along with other TVS Equipment of Line '6'. As the Mid-shaft is  un  manned,  the  Station  Level  Control,  comprising  Work  Station  &  Ventilation  Control  Panel,  is located in Station Control room at CTST Station (Line '6').
(iii) Access Entry / Exit Doors to Mid-shaft are provided at Ground Level. While standing facing the Doors from outside, the Door on right hand side connects Staircase leading to Cross Passage. ## PART V
## 8.0 TRACTION CURRENT FAILURE

## 8.0 TRACTION CURRENT FAILURE

When the Traction Current Supplies are interrupted, the Train borne Batteries shall provide sufficient Power  to  operate  the  Emergency  Ventilation  for  approximately  45  Minutes.  The  condition  in  a crowded Train, however, is likely to become somewhat intolerable even before that upper limit of the time.  The  TC  must,  therefore,  actively  interact  with  TPC  to  ascertain  if  there  is  no  immediate possibility  for  the  Traction  Supply  to  be  restored.  If  that  be  the  case,  the  appropriate  Step  wise Procedure for Train to Track Detrainment, shall be initiated by him well in time.
## PART VI
## 9.0 (A) FIRE OR FUSING & THE TRAIN STALLED IN TUNNEL

## 9.0 (A) FIRE OR FUSING & THE TRAIN STALLED IN TUNNEL

If  a  Train  is  stalled  in  a  Tunnel  Section  between  Stations  and  there  is  Fire  or  Fusing,  resulting  in Smoke or Fumes, Passengers must be detrained without any delay.
The Traffic Controller, in consultation with TOs and the ASC (for the Tunnel System) shall decide the Direction of Evacuation of the Passengers and their Exit from the Train, either from Front End / Rear End, depending upon the following Considerations:
(i) Location of the Train in the Tunnel.
(ii) Location of Fire / Fusing in the Train.
(iii) Location of Nearest Station.
(iv) Ventilation Considerations.
Exit could be from one End or both the Ends, depending upon the prevailing Situation.
Exit could or could not be towards the Nearest Station.

## Introduction

In  Tunnel Sections with Rising Grades, the Tunnel acts as a 'Chimney' carrying Smoke, Heat and Fumes.  As  such,  unless  there  are  certain  'Definite'  &  'Exceptional  Reasons',  the  Evacuation  shall normally be planned towards the Falling Grade.

## Introduction

Route of Evacuation shall, in any case, be fully Ventilated and Exhausts worked towards the Opposite End.

## 9.1 Actions required from Chief Controller:

The  CC  must  immediately  summon  the  Delhi  Fire  Services  (DFS),  clearly  indicating  the  exact Location and the Station Entry / the Access Point and inform the Disaster management team (DMT) and other concerned Officials.

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

Preservation  of  Life  must  always  be  regarded  as  the  most  important  principle  of  fire fighting.

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

This SOP contains guidelines for handling fires,  smoke & fusing at a station between track sections or in train and describes stepwise action to be taken by staff concerned.

## 2.  SCOPE

This procedure is applicable in metro premises. This procedure shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020, Safety Circulars, Accident & Disaster Management Manual and other instructions in vogue.
For UTO Mode of Operation:Wherever, Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, is to be read as Train Operator (TO) / Roving Attendant (RA) / Emergency Train Operator (ETO).

## 3.  GUIDELINES FOR HANDLING FIRE AND FUSING

(ii) Immediately inform SM/SC/location in charge and TC/OCC,                                                                                            |

## 4.4  Maintain Supplies:

## 4.4  Maintain Supplies:

During  a  fire,  unless  the  safety  of  people  and  equipment  is  in  danger,  all  power  supplies, including the traction power supply must be maintained in consultation with TPC.

## 4.4  Maintain Supplies:

If  the  traction  power  supply system of any elementary section is affected due to fire, every effort  must  be  made  to  maintain  supplies  to other  elementary  sections  in  consultation  with TC. The traffic should be regulated accordingly.

## 8.  PANTOGRAPHS:

## 8.  PANTOGRAPHS:

If a fire affects electrical circuits, pantographs of the affected unit may be lowered, bearing in mind that the operation of air-conditioning equipment will be affected and only emergency load/ lighting shall be available in the affected unit.
## 9.  TRAIN MOVEMENT IN ADJACENT TUNNEL:

## 9.  TRAIN MOVEMENT IN ADJACENT TUNNEL:

TC may authorize trains to proceed through the tunnel adjacent to that occupied by the stalled train  however,  only  after  confirmation  has  been  received  that  the  affected  train  passengers have  been  safely  evacuated  from  the  Right-of-Way  and  that  tunnel  is  free  of  Smoke  and Fumes as certified by ECS Staff
The train  movement  in  unaffected  tunnel  must  be  in  Coded  Manual  mode  at  the  maximum speed of 40 km/hr till normalcy is restored.
## 10. RESUMING THE TRAIN SERVICES:

## 10. RESUMING THE TRAIN SERVICES:

The TC shall allow train movements through the station after confirming with the SC that the fire has been put out and the smoke level reduced to manageable limits inside the station.
The OCS (Officer in Charge at Site) in consultation with SC shall decide whether to re-open the station  completely  or  partially  in  accordance  with  the  condition  of  damage  after  the  fire  and inform OCC accordingly.
Final decision for reopening of station will be taken by OCC and conveyed to all concerned by suitable announcements.
## 11. MANPOWER BACK UP PLAN:

## 11. MANPOWER BACK UP PLAN:

To ease the impact of stress on staff during an incident, Manpower Back Up Plan shall be kept ready for each line so that additional staff as required can be deployed at short notice to the affected station.

## 12. OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR FIRE & SMOKE DETECTION INSIDE TRAIN (RS-10) IN UTO MODE ON LINE-7&8:

(i) In case of fire or smoke detection alarm is activated in a train, it will appear on the alarm list window of TC and RSC workstation. If the train is in mid-section, then the train shall continue to move to next station.

## 5.1 General Guidelines:

(i) ASC/OCC/MB-2, on becoming aware of the high speed wind through alarm raised by wind sensor  monitor  installed  at  his  work  desk,  shall  immediately  inform  (verbally)  to CHC/OCC/MB-2 for implementing train movement restriction on respective lines through Traffic  Controllers  as  specified  in  para-5.2  of  this  JPO.  After  communicating  verbally, ASC/OCC/MB-2 shall then also confirm in writing to CHC/OCC/MB-2. The above verbal communications made to CHC/OCC/MB-2 shall clearly mention the time and details of detection of event by wind sensor monitor.
(ii) CHC/OCC/MB-2  shall  immediately  inform  CHC/OCC/SHPK  and  CHC/OCC/MB-1;  to accordingly implement train movement restriction on respective lines.
(iii) CHC/OCC/MB-1, CHC/OCC/MB-2 & CHC/OCC/SHPK shall advise respective TCs and all other controllers in the OCC regarding high wind situation and to follow the PO for train movement in such situation.
(iv) CHC/OCC/MB-1, CHC/OCC/MB-2 and CHC/OCC/SHPK shall also advise Dy. HOD/Operations (Station Operation) concerned officers/officials of operations/Electrical/Track/Civil/S&T department of respective line accordingly about the high wind speed as monitored.
(v) All  TC  shall  implement/instruct  train  movement  restrictions  as stipulated  in this  PO  on concerned lines by suitable commands and/or by giving instructions as blanket message

## Introduction

to  all  Train  Operators  in group  mode (for  immediate UTO/ATO suspension and speed restriction enforcement) and keep on repeating it regularly till the speedy wind conditions improve and settle down to normal level.

## Introduction

(vi) On receipt of such instruction from TC, Train Operators shall acknowledge the message and comply accordingly by strictly adhering to speed restriction. TOs of the trains running in UTO/ATO mode shall change over to CM/ATP mode immediately to achieve manual control on speed of train.
(vii) Traffic Controller shall also advise Station Controllers about the wind condition, traffic plan etc. and ask them to take necessary action accordingly.
(viii) Station Controllers shall ensure announcement at their respective stations, inform Station Manager and take other appropriate actions as required  or  as  instructed  by TC/OCC. Station Manager/Station  Controller shall inspect platform level to check  for  any abnormality and must see that no self-moveable item/equipment is left at platform without securing it properly.
(ix) It  shall  be  the  responsibility  of  the  concerned  staff  that  after  completion  of  work/ maintenance, any equipment/material that may hinder passenger movement is removed or properly secured at some suitable place.
(x) However, if any material found unremoved by maintenance (E&M, Lift, Escalator etc.) department;  it  shall  be  removed  by  station  staff  after  consultation  with  concerned department and take other appropriate actions as required or as instructed by TC/OCC.
(xi) Train  Operators  shall  make  announcements  in  respective  trains  to  keep  passengers informed inside train.
(xii) Surprise mock drill shall be conducted on regular interval for preparedness in case of high wind speeds due to Thunderstorm/ Cyclone.

## 8.0  FAILURE MANAGEMENT OF WIND SENSOR:

In case of failure of wind sensors, following procedure shall be adopted:
8.1  In case of failure of one wind sensor, according to geographical location inputs may be taken from other serviceable wind sensors as per the table placed at Annexure 'B'.
8.2  In case of failure of two wind sensors at a time, input from remaining wind sensor may be considered.
8.3  If  all  sensors  fail  for  all  the  lines  and  thunderstorm  or  high  wind  condition  is  reported. Concerned CHC/OCC will seek information regarding the wind velocity from Meteorological Department. The information thus received shall then be considered for implementation of suitable train regulation strategy.
8.4  Wind sensor may be recalibrated after every 2 years by E&M wing. E&M staff will paste calibration date along with next due date of calibration on wind sensor.
8.5  Maintenance  schedule  of  wind  sensor  is  detailed  at Annexure-C .  E&M  department  shall maintain the records of maintenance of wind sensor.

## 9.0 ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINE: -

9.1 ASC/OCC/MB-2, on becoming aware of the high speed wind i.e. 60 kmph through alarm raised by wind sensor monitor installed at his work desk, shall immediately inform (verbally) to Traffic Controllers & CHC/OCC/MB-2 for implementing train movement restrictions on UTO enabled lines.
After communicating verbally, ASC/OCC/MB-2 shall then also confirm in writing with details to CHC/OCC/MB-2.
9.2 On getting information regarding high speed wind (60 kmph) from ASC/OCC/MB-2, TC/CHCOCC of Line-7 & 8 shall immediately apply suitable/relevant commands to bring the trains on hold on next platform.
9.3 TC/CHC-OCC shall  instruct  IC  for  announcements  inside  the  trains  to  keep  passengers informed.
9.4 In case RA/ETO is not onboard, TC shall instruct the nearest available RA/ETO to board the train as per procedure.
9.5 TC/CHC-OCC instruct RA/ETO to take the charge of the trains and ensure further movement in ATP mode as per Para-5 and 6 of this circular.
9.6 UTO Mode shall be resumed, when wind speed reduces below 55 kmph and same has been monitored and recorded for 05 minutes.

## 5.0 GENERAL:

5.1 Train shall be moved in degraded mode under the following circumstances after authorization from TC is obtained on exchange of private number as per Para '8' .
(i) In case of loss of proceed code.
(ii) For passing a signal at danger when driven in RM or ROS or Cut Out mode.

(iv) If ATP/Coded manual mode cannot be selected due to any reason.

## PROCEDURE FOR TRAIN MOVEMENT IN DEGRADED MODE IN LINE - 8

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure is applicable for the Train Movement in Degraded Modes of Train Operation in Line  8  and  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro  Railway  General  Rules,  2020  and  its Amendment, Safety Circulars & Other Instructions in vogue.
For UTO mode of train operation: Wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/Emergency Train Operator (ETO).

## 3.0 DEFINITIONS:

3.1 Degraded Mode: Degraded  Mode  of  Train  Operation,  hereafter  referred  as  Degraded  Mode includes train movement in ROS, RM & Cut-Out Mode. The train is moved by Train Operator on his line of sight exercising utmost vigilance so as to stop short of any obstruction ensuring that train speed does not exceed 25 kmph or less if applicable.
3.2 Route Set : A route is considered as set if its valid indication on the VIDEO WALL/CATS/LATS/VDU is displaying the track in white colour.
3.3 Point Set & Locked : A point is indicated as set & locked if and only if a valid indication for set & locked  is  displayed  on  the  VIDEO  WALL/CATS/LATS/VDU  along  with  'Lock  fail'  shall  be displayed  as  'Not  Detected'  in  description  &  control  area  for  the  point  and  the  point  number displayed on the CATS/LATS/VDU is not flashing in Red Colour.
3.4 Danger Signal : A Danger Signal means that a Fixed Signal is displaying:-
(i) Red aspect; or
(ii) Flickering of aspects; or
(iii) Multiple aspects; or
(iv) No aspect (Blank).

5.2 Movement in degraded mode shall be authorized from one point to other as per below given guidelines, provided the route is clear of any obstruction from the origin to the destination & all points enroute are set & locked and if there are any signal enroute, passing the same shall be explicitly included in the authorization clearly stating the aspect.
(i) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  from  one  station  platform  to  next  station platform.
(ii) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized to the train stopped in the mid-section/siding from the point of stopping to the next station platform.
(iii) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from a station platform to an intervening fixed signal before the next station platform, provided section is clear upto the intervening fixed signal, explicitly informing TO if next station is occupied, duly instructing TO to stop at foot of such fixed signal.
(iv) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized from a station platform to an intervening fixed signal or up to the next station platform, having a train in section, provided the TO of the preceding train in section has reported receipt of ATP/Proceed Code, without waiting for the train  to  clear  the  section,  explicitly  informing  TO  to  move  cautiously  observing  utmost caution so as to stop short of any obstruction.
(v) In  case  TC  gets  positive  indication  on  ATS  of  any  train,  running  in  degraded  mode,  has receiving ATP/Proceed Code, TC shall advise TO to stop his train and select ATP for further movement (In case of line-7 & 8 only).

(vi) Degraded Mode movement can be authorized to a revenue train by TC on permission of Chief Controller from one fixed signal to next fixed signal, covering more than one stations, only  after  ensuring  that  the  track  up  to  the  destination  signal  is  indicated  clear  on CATS/VIDEO  WALL,  explicitly  informing  Train  Operator  if  station  platform  next  to  the destination signal is occupied.
(vii) Degraded  Mode  movement  can  be  authorized  to  a  non-revenue  train  (a  train  without passengers)  by  TC  on  permission  of  Chief  Controller  from  one  fixed  signal  to  next  fixed signal, covering more than one station, provided train does not stop at intermediate stations &  ensuring  that  the  track  up  to  the  destination  signal  is  indicated  clear  on  CATS/VIDEO WALL, ensuring that the station platform immediately next to the destination signal is clear of trains.
(viii) During reversal/stabling in siding, authorization shall be given up to SRMB/stabling point.

## Note:-  TC  shall  not  authorize  any  train working  in  degraded mode to move  upto  a  virtual signal.

5.3 After  entering  into  a  station  platform  if  a  train  stops  before  the  NSP  and movement  up  to the NSP is to be done in degraded mode, train operator shall move in degraded mode up to the NSP  only  after  ensuring  that  the  track  on  the  line  of  sight  up  to  the  NSP  is  clear  of  any obstructions.  Train  Operator  shall  inform  OCC  about  the  same  and  if  further  movement  in degraded mode is required beyond the NSP, Train Operator, before any such movement, shall obtain authorization from TC as per Para '8'.
5.4 In case of intermediate terminal stations (stations other then terminal station where reversal of trains  takes  place  or  train  being  introduced  from/sent  to  depot),  before  authorizing  train movement  in  degraded  mode  from  adjacent  stations  on  either  side  towards  intermediate terminal  stations,  TC  in  addition  to Para  '8' shall  also  ensure  that,  there  is  no  train  under reversal  at  the  platform  at  intermediate  terminal  station  and/or  no  train  is  being  introduced from/sent to depot and the track up to the end of next platform is clear.

## Introduction

5.5 TC shall inform Chief Controller as and when train operation in degraded mode is authorized detailing train number, location and destination up to which it has been permitted. All cases of ROS, RM/Cutout authorization should be documented in a register for scrutiny by OCM/Chief Controller.
5.6 In  case  CATS  is  not  functioning  at  OCC,  TC  shall  advice  SC  of  the  concerned  interlocking station to take control on LATS and responsibility of granting authorization to the Train Operator shall  now  devolve  upon  the  SC  who  will  follow  the  detailed  procedure  for  Traffic  Controller described  in  this  circular.  SC  will  ensure  track  clearance  and  route/points  set  &  locked indications from the LATS &VDU.
6.0 As  per  rule-23  of  Metro  Railways  General  Rules,  2020,  in  case  train  is  not  running  under  the authority  of  cab  signals  and  train  operator  observes  that  a  fixed  signal  is  not  displaying  any aspect, he shall stop his train and seek instructions from the traffic controller by radio. TC shall follow the procedure as per para '9' as applicable.

(i) Whenever proceed code is not available to train, Train Operator shall inform TC/SC as per Para '8.2' and shall seek instructions for movement in degraded mode.
(ii) Train operator shall never pass a signal at danger when Train is driven in RM or ROS or CutOut mode without authorization from TC as per Para '8.2' .
(iii) On receiving authorization from TC under exchange of private number Train Operator shall acknowledge the same as per Para '8.2' .
(iv) While  moving  in  degraded  mode,  Train  Operator  is  responsible  for  the  safe  movement  of train. He shall take following precautions while working the train.
(a)  Train Operator shall never operate train in degraded mode without authorization from TC as per Para '8.2' only exception being the provision in Para '5.3' .
(b) While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode  from  one  station  platform  to  next  station platform, Train Operator shall be watchful of the signal enroute, if any. If aspect of such signal is more restrictive than the aspect for which authorization is provided by TC, Train Operator shall stop his train at the foot  of  such signal  and  shall  seek fresh  instruction from TC for movement in degraded mode.
(c) While working the train in degraded mode, Train Operator shall not allow his train under any  circumstances  to  pass  the  next  station/signal/location  for  which  authorization  is provided by TC, unless authorized by TC, afresh, as per Para '8.2' of this circular.

(d) While  working  the  train  in  degraded  mode  Train  Operator  shall  work  the  train  duly observing speed restriction of 25 kmph or the lower speed where ever prescribed as per TSR/PSR. Train Operator shall keep the Train Speed such that it can be brought to stop with in half the distance of visibility estimated by him and he should be able to stop his train short of any obstruction.
(e)  When authorized to pass a signal at  danger  by TC/SC  under  the  exchange  of  private number/written  authority,  Train  Operator  shall  move  cautiously,  look  out  for  points  (if available) that they are set for intended direction of movement, proceed cautiously over the  points  exercising  utmost  vigilance  and  be  prepared to  stop short  of  points  in  case they are lying in wrong direction or are not set properly. Train Operator must be alert to locate any train ahead of his/her train & be prepared to stop short of the train.

## Introduction

(v) After  resumption of ATP / Coded manual mode from degraded mode, Train Operator must inform OCC/TC about the same.
(vi) TO shall inform passengers through train PA system of likely delay/slow speed of train.

## 7.2 Traffic Controller:

(i) Authorization to pass signal at danger and/or to move in degraded mode shall be given by TC when having control as per the provisions given in this circular.
(ii) In case of failure of CATS, TC shall transfer control to the SC of the concerned interlocking zone  on  the  LATS,  on  whom  the  responsibility  of  providing  authorization  for  movement  in degraded mode shall now devolve.TC shall inform TOs about the same. After restoration of CATS in OCC, control shall be transferred back to TC duly informing TOs.
(iii) TC shall regulate the traffic in the network & shall arrange to inform passengers of the likely delay, as required by guiding Train Operators/Station Controllers for doing so.

## 7.3 Station Controller:

(i) In  case  CATS  is  not  functioning  at  OCC  and  operation  is  being  controlled  locally  by  SC through  LATS/VDU  at  station  level,  responsibility  of  granting  authorization  to  the  Train Operator  shall  devolve  upon  the  SC  who  will  follow  the  detailed  procedure  for  Traffic Controller described in this circular. SC shall ensure track clearance and route set, points set & locked indications from the LATS &VDU.
(ii) Whenever  consistency  of  information  about,  signal  no  &  its  aspect,  route  setting  &  its clearance  up  to  desired  location,  points  set  &  lock  indication  is  sought  by  TC,  SC  shall provide the same by comparing the indications available on LATS &VDU.
(iii) Incase  points  not  detected  set  and  locked,  when  instructed  by  TC,  SC  shall  physically examine the points, manually operate & secure (clamp & padlock) the points detected set & lock in the intended direction of movement and shall communicate the same to OCC under the exchange of private number.
(iv) If required, SC shall inform passengers through PA system about the likely delay.

## 8.0 GRANTING AUTHORIZATION:

8.1 CONFIRMATION BY TC: Whenever authorization for movement in degraded mode is sought by train operator, TC shall satisfy himself from CATS/VIDEO WALL about the following.
(i) TC shall compare the indication of CATS &VIDEO WALL and shall also confirm that the life indicators  of  CATS  are  working  properly  satisfying  himself  that  the  valid  indications  are available  on  CATS/VIDEO  WALL.  If  required,  TC  may  confirm  the  consistency  of  the information from the SC, who shall confirm the same by comparing the indications on LATS &VDU.
(ii) TC shall satisfy himself that there is no ambiguity about the information received from Train Operator and shall ensure that the information is consistent with the indications available on CATS/VIDEO WALL.
(iii) TC shall look for the availability of signal & points enroute to the next station and shall ensure that  the  route  is  set  up  to  the  destination  being  authorized  and  points  enroute,  if  any,  are detected set &locked on CATS/VIDEO WALL and no conflicting route is set. While providing authorization with Danger Signal & Points enroute, TC shall additionally confirm the status of such point as set & locked from the SC, who shall confirm the same by comparing on LATS & VDU.
(iv) TC shall ensure that the track ahead is clear up to the destination being authorized on CATS & VIDEO WALL. If Track section block is showing occupied, he will ask Train Operator to

reconfirm the status of track ahead on his line of sight. If Train Operators information is not sufficient, TC may also ask SC of next station to physically check the track occupancy from the station platforms. If required, TC, through radio communication, may try to establish the location of preceding train as per time table and shall ensure that track is clear up to the end of next platform.
8.2 COMMUNICATION  DURING  DEGRADED  MODE: Following  guidelines  for  communication  in degraded mode should be followed to ensure safety.
(i) Any instruction to the TO for authorizing him to move in degraded mode shall be given on Radio on exchange of private number between TO and TC. In case of communication failure, control  shall  be  transferred  to  the  SC  of  concerned  interlocking  zone  and  authorization  for movement in degraded mode shall be given to the TO by the concerned SC on exchange of private number or in writing if communication fails between them also.
(ii) Whenever a signal is Danger and proceed code is not available to train, Train Operator shall inform  TC  giving  his  Train  Number,  exact  location,  signal  number  &  aspect  (if  signal  is available), status of track on his line of sight, localization status of train &direction of travel and shall seek authorization from TC before moving the train in degraded mode.
(iii) TC, while giving authorization to Train Operator for movement in degraded mode shall clearly mention the train no, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), line (UP/DN)& destination upto which it is authorized, the degraded mode in which movement is authorized and shall offer his private number.

(iii) TC, while giving authorization to Train Operator for movement in degraded mode shall clearly mention the train no, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), line (UP/DN)& destination upto which it is authorized, the degraded mode in which movement is authorized and shall offer his private number.
(iv) Train  Operator  shall  acknowledge  the  message  by  repeating,  TC  private  no,  his  train  no, status of line of sight, signal number & aspect (if signal is available), line & destination upto which it is applicable and the degraded mode in which movement is authorized. He shall then provide his private number to TC and make the entry in the private number book.

## 10.0  CBTC Communication Failure Management

In  case  of  the  CBTC  Communication  Failure  where  the  Train/Trains  are  required  to  move  in Degraded Mode, Location of Train/Train's will not be available only lost train indication on its last location  with  Rake  ID  will  be  available  on  ATS  MMI/  VDU/Video  Wall.  In  this  case,  there  is possibility of more than one (CBTC or Non CBTC) Train present in the same axle counter (Track Section). The following steps shall be adopted:-
(i) TC shall positively identify leading Train by comparing view on ATS MMI/VDU.
(ii) After ensuring identification of leading Train, TC shall authorize leading Train as per extant procedure  described  in  this  procedure  order.  TC  shall  also  advice  Train  Operator  of succeeding Train/Train's present in the segment to wait for further instruction.
(iii) After the leading Train, so authorized to move in Degraded Mode, clears the authorized destination PF/Signal, TC shall authorize Train Operator of succeeding Train to move in Degraded Mode as per extant procedure.
(iv) If location of Train/Train's is not available through presence of Train ID or Rake ID on ATS MMI  or  VDU  (Video  Wall),  TC  shall  confirm  locations  along  with  train  ID  from  Train Operators  in  the  failed  Track  Segment.  Leading  Train  will  be  identified  using  this information, line of sight clearance and verification from time table.
(v) In case of control is at local, the responsibility of TC will delve upon the concerned Station Controller.

## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR NEGOTIATING NEUTRAL SECTION BY 4/ 6/ 8 CAR TRAIN

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order shall apply to the trains stopping for any reason in a Section, having Neutral Section. The Procedure shall be used to ensure that Pantographs with VCB/LCB closed does not negotiate the Neutral Section, after the train stops therein and shall be applicable for main Lines in the Normal and Reverse Direction of travel during Revenue/ Non-revenue Hours, unless otherwise guided by the EPIC or TC/OCC.

## 2.  SCOPE

This  procedure  is  applicable  to  all  line  of  Delhi  Metro  Network.  This  procedure  shall  be  read  in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 & its amendment, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
For UTO mode of Train Operation: wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/ Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
## 3.1. Types of Equipment provided at Neutral Sections:

## 3.1. Types of Equipment provided at Neutral Sections:

(i) Type  II: Neutral Section with Arthur  Flurry  or  SIEMENS  Make  Phase  Break Equipments:
This Neutral Section is equipped with Arthur Flurry or SIEMENS make phase break. Middle point  of  the  Neutral  Section  is  earthed  and  as  such,  these  Neutral  Sections  cannot  be bypassed. Only the supply can be extended by closing the bridging BM (Breaker Mains). The length of neutral section is 5.4/ 6.6/7.2/ 9.8 m.
(ii) Type - III: Neutral Section provided in ROCS (Furrer & Fray Design):
This  Neutral  Section  is  equipped  with  4  nos.  of  insulated  overlap  (IOL).  Middle  point  of  the Neutral Section is earthed and as such, these Neutral Sections cannot be bypassed. Only the supply can be extended by closing the bridging BM. The length of neutral section is 14 m.
Note: Line & Section-wise details of Neutral Sections has been placed at Annexure ' A' .
## 3.2. Marker Boards:

## 3.2. Marker Boards:

(i) In the Normal Direction of Travel, the Marker Boards (500 m, 250 m, VCB Open, NSCZ and VCB Close) are Black Printed with White Background.
(ii) In Reverse Direction, the Marker Boards (500 m, 250 m, VCB Open, NSCZ and VCB Close) are Black Printed with Yellow Background.
(iii)  For RS-2 Bombardier Trains, VCB shall be read as LCB.
(iv)  The 'VCB Open Board' is installed exactly at a Location 20.230 m before or ahead the Front Magnet (Applicable for Line-1 to 6).
(v) The  'VCB  Open  Board'  is  installed  at  a  Location  43.9  m  before  Neutral  Section  and  'VCB Close Board' shall be installed exactly at a Location 140 m after Neutral Section in Line 7 & 8.
(vi)  In AEL the 'VCB Open Board' is installed at a Location 83 m & 71 m before Neutral Section Dn & Up Line respectively and 'VCB Close Board' is installed exactly at a Location 140 m after Neutral Section for both lines.
## 4.  NSCZ (NEUTRAL SECTION CLEAR ZONE):

## 4.1. Line 1,2, 3 & 4

A Neutral Section Clear Zone (NSCZ) is defined as a Zone starting at '73' m from the end of the Neutral Section and extending for '2' m. It will ensure that when the Front Cab is in the NSCZ, the first two Pantographs are well under the Live OHE.

## 4.2. Line 5 & 6

A Neutral Section Clear Zone (NSCZ) is defined as a Zone starting at '21' m from the end of the Neutral Section and extending for '2' m. It will ensure that when the Front Cab is in the NSCZ, the first Pantograph is well under the Live OHE.
## 4.3. Line 7, 8 & AEL

## 4.3. Line 7, 8 & AEL

A Neutral Section Clear Zone (NSCZ) is defined as a Zone of '44' m beyond the end of Neutral Section in DOT of the train. It will ensure that when the Front Cab is in front of NSCZ board, the first Pantograph is under the Live OHE.
## 4.4. Appearance of NSCZ Board:

## 4.4. Appearance of NSCZ Board:

(i) Normal  Direction  of  Train  Movement:  -  Retro-reflective  Board  of  '2'  m  Length  with 'White  & Black  Chequered' Design  is  installed  along  the  Track  and  shall  be  deemed  as  NSCZ  for Normal Direction.
(ii) Wrong  (Reverse)  Direction  of  Train  Movement:  -  Retro-reflective  Board  of  '2'  m  length  with 'Yellow  &  Black  Chequered' Design  is  installed  along  the  Track  and  shall  be  deemed  as NSCZ for Wrong (Reverse) Direction.
Note: NSCZ Board shall be available only in Type-II, Type-III Neutral Section .

## 6.  PROCEDURE TO BE FOLLOWED :
## 6.1. Negotiation of the Train in Neutral Section:

## 6.1. Negotiation of the Train in Neutral Section:

(i) DMRC trains are equipped with devices which automatically open/close its  VCB(s)  in  neutral section.
(ii) TO shall maintain sufficient speed of the train in neutral section negotiation so that train does not stop in between the neutral section. In any case, TO shall not violate the target speed or any other speed restriction and shall stop of any obstruction.
(iii)  TO  shall  observe  the  opening  and  closing  of  VCB(s).  In  case,  VCB(s)  is  not  opened  or  not

## Introduction

closed automatically, TO will report the same to TC/OCC and take action as per direction of TC/OCC.
## 6.2. Procedure to be followed if Train Stops in a Section having neutral section

## 6.2. Procedure to be followed if Train Stops in a Section having neutral section

Whenever a train stops in section having neutral section,  TO shall inform TC/OCC about the same stating Train  No.,  location,  status  of  all  the  VCBs  and  Failure  in  the  train  or  reason  of Stopping.  TC/OCC  shall  advice  TO  to  act  as  per  the  below  mentioned  procedure  depending upon type of neutral section available there.
Procedure to be followed if Train Stops in a Section having Type-II or  Type-III neutral section:
## (i) Train stops after NSP but before VCB Open Board:

## (i) Train stops after NSP but before VCB Open Board:

(a) If VCBs are Closed, Proceed Normally.
(b) If VCBs are open, Close VCB & Proceed Normally.
## (ii) Train stops at or after the VCB Open Board but before NSCZ:

## (ii) Train stops at or after the VCB Open Board but before NSCZ:

(a) Move the 6 Car Train with Rear Pantograph up or 8 Car train with Rear two Pantographs up.
(b) Keep a look out for NSCZ board and stop the train in such a manner that the Front Cab is aligned  with  NSCZ  board.  If  due  to  any  reason  VCB  opens  and  the  Train  stops  before NSCZ, check the line voltage status, if available, Close VCB of pantographs selected as per (ii) (a) and move up to NSCZ board.
(c) At NSCZ board, deselect Rear Pantograph in 6 car train or rear two Pantographs in 8 car train and select the first two Front Pantographs in 6/8 Car train.
(d) Move the Train with both the Front Pantographs up to next Station NSP and Open Doors for Platform Duty as per extant Procedure. If due to any reason VCB opens and the Train stops before NSP, Close VCB and move up to NSP.
(e) At Station NSP, select all Pantographs and Proceed Normally.
## (iii)  Train stops at NSCZ board or after NSCZ board but before VCB Close Board:

## (iii)  Train stops at NSCZ board or after NSCZ board but before VCB Close Board:

(a) Move the Train selecting front two Pantographs up to next Station NSP and Open Doors for Platform Duty as per extant Procedure. If due to any reason VCB opens and the Train stops before NSP, Close VCB and move up to NSP.
(b) At Station NSP, select all Pantographs and Proceed Normally.
## (iv)  Train stops at or after VCB Close Board:

## (iv)  Train stops at or after VCB Close Board:

(a) Check whether all VCBs are closed.
(b) If the VCBs are closed, proceed normally.
(c) If one or more VCBs are open, close them.
(d) If VCBs are Closed, Proceed Normally.
(e) If VCB do not close, troubleshoot as per extant Procedure.
## B.  I  n Line 5 & 6:-

## (i) Train stops after NSP but before VCB Open Board:

(a) Check whether all VCBs are closed.
(b) If the VCBs are closed, proceed normally.

## Introduction

(c) If one or more VCBs are open, close them.

## Introduction

(d) If VCBs are Closed, Proceed Normally.
(e) If VCB do not close, troubleshoot as per extant Procedure.
## (ii) Train stops at or after the VCB Open Board but before NSCZ board:

## (ii) Train stops at or after the VCB Open Board but before NSCZ board:

(a) Deselect front pantograph for 4/6 car train and move the Train with Rear Pantograph up for 4 car train or Rear Two Pantographs up for 6 car train.
(b) Keep a look out for NSCZ board and stop the train in such a manner that the Front Cab is aligned  with  NSCZ  board.  If  due  to  any  reason  VCB  opens  and  the  Train  stops  before NSCZ board, check the line voltage status, if available, Close VCB of selected pantograph as per (ii) (a) above and move up to NSCZ board.
(c) At NSCZ board, deselect Rear Pantograph for 4 car train or Rear Two Pantographs for 6 car train and select the Front Pantograph for 4/6 car train.
(d) Move the Train with Front Pantograph upto next Station NSP and Open Doors for Platform Duty as per extant Procedure. If due to any reason VCB opens and the Train stops before NSP, Close VCB and move up to NSP.
(e) At Station NSP, select all Pantographs and Proceed Normally.
## (iii)  Train stops at NSCZ or after NSCZ but before VCB Close Board:

## (iii)  Train stops at NSCZ or after NSCZ but before VCB Close Board:

(a) Move the Train with only  Front  Pantograph  up  to  next  Station  NSP  and  Open  Doors  for Platform Duty as per extant Procedure. If due to any reason VCB opens and the Train stops before NSP, Close VCB and move up to NSP.
(b) At Station NSP, select all Pantographs and Proceed Normally.

## (iv)  Train stops at or after VCB Close Board:

(a) Check whether all VCBs are closed.
(b) If the VCBs are closed, proceed normally.
(c) If one or more VCBs are open, close them as per Procedure.
(d) If Closed, Proceed Normally.
(e) If VCBs do not close, troubleshoot as per extant Procedure.
## C.  I  n Line 7, 8 & AEL: -
## (i) Train stops after NSP but before VCB open board

## (i) Train stops after NSP but before VCB open board

(a) If VCBs are closed, proceed normally.
(b) If VCBs are open, close VCBs & proceed normally.
## (ii) Train stop at or after the VCB open board but before NSCZ board

## (ii) Train stop at or after the VCB open board but before NSCZ board

(a) Lower the front pantograph. Move the train with rear pantograph up.
(b) Keep a look out for NSCZ board and stop the train in such a manner that the Front Cab is aligned  with  NSCZ  board.  If  due  to  any  reason  VCB  opens  and  the  Train  stops  before NSCZ, check the line  voltage  status,  if  available,  close  the  VCB  and  move  up  to  NSCZ board.
(c) At NSCZ lower the rear pantograph and raise the front pantograph.
(d) Move the train with front pantograph up to next station NSP and open doors for platform duty as per extant procedure, if due to any reason VCB opens and train stops before the NSP, close VCB and move up to NSP.

## Introduction

(e) At Station NSP, raise all pantographs and close the VCB.
## (iii)  Train Stops at NSCZ or after NSCZ but before VCB close board.

## (iii)  Train Stops at NSCZ or after NSCZ but before VCB close board.

(a) Lower down the rear pantograph and move the train with front pantograph up to next station NSP and open doors for platform duty as per extant procedure, if due to any reason VCB opens and train stops before the NSP, close VCB and move up to NSP.
(b) At Station NSP, raise all pantographs and close the VCB.
## (iv)  Train Stop at or after VCB close Board

## (iv)  Train Stop at or after VCB close Board

(a) Check whether both VCBs are closed.
(b) If the VCBs are closed, proceed normally.
(c) If one VCB is open, close it.
(d) If closed, proceed normally.
(e) If VCB does not close, troubleshoot as per extant procedure.
Note: TO shall inform TC/OCC after following the above mentioned Procedure for Train Movement. In case of any other Problem, TO shall communicate with TC/OCC and ask for further Instructions.
Utmost Care shall be taken by system and all concerned that no Train enters a Neutral Section with VCB in Closed Condition.
## 8.   ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR UTO ENABLED LINES: -

(i) Signaling  system  shall  provide  conditions  enabling  a  train  to  maintain  sufficient  speed  in  the neutral section so that train doesn't stop in between the neutral section provided the following conditions are satisfied:
No TSR on the approach (84m before & 140m after) of neutral section should be applied below 30 KMPH. This should be condition both in system normal and system reverse.
Traction power section shall be in on condition before & after neutral section.
Non vital speed regulation from RS side with speed limit less than 25 KMPH shall not be in active state.
(ii) Whenever a train stops in section having neutral section,
TC/OCC  shall  inform  RSC,  SGC  and  TPC  regarding  stopping  of  train  in  section  having neutral section.
RSC, SGC and TPC shall verify the reason of stopping of train in section. On the basis of reason  of  stopping,  concerned  controller  in  OCC  shall  Troubleshoot  the  fault  /  advise  the troubleshooting for the fault to TC/OCC.
RSC shall verify the status of all the VCBs & troubleshoot/ advise to TC/OCC whether neutral section negotiation by RA/ETO is required or train can be moved with remote troubleshooting.
If  OCC  is  unable  to  restart  the  train  after  carrying  out  remote  troubleshooting,  TC  shall instruct nearest RA/ETO to board the train (if RA/ETO is not already onboard) as per extant procedure and to take charge of train.
TC/CHC shall instruct IC for announcements inside the trains to keep passengers informed.

TC/CHC shall instruct IC for announcements inside the trains to keep passengers informed.
RA/ETO shall  drive  the  train  in  ATP/ROS/RM  mode  and  negotiate  neutral  section  as  per instructions detailed above in Para 6.2 (C).
