## SAFETY CIRCULAR- 12 A (Rev.-02)
## STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR FIRE ON TRAIN IN UNDERGROUND SECTION OF ALL LINES

## 1.  INTRODUCTION:

This SOP contains guidelines for handling fires & fusing and describes stepwise action to be taken by staff concerned.

## 2.  SCOPE

This  procedure  is  applicable  to  Underground  section  of  all  lines  and  shall  be  read  in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020, Safety Circulars, Accident & Disaster Management Manual and other instructions in vogue.
For UTO Mode of Operation:Wherever, Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, is to be read as Train Operator (TO) / Roving Attendant (RA) / Emergency Train Operator (ETO).

## 3. General

The underground section of DMRC having stations at a distance of 0.6 to 1.8 Kms generally. has been provided with Tunnel Ventilation System (TVS) designed to meet the requirements of train running generally as per NFPA guidelines.
3.1. Design guidelines of NFPA (National Fire Protection Association) to be followed that:
(i) Provide a tenable environment along the path of egress from a fire incident in enclosed stations and enclosed train ways.
(ii)  Produce air flow rates sufficient to prevent back layering of smoke in the path of egress within enclosed train ways.
(iii) Be capable of reaching full operational mode within 180 seconds.
(iv) Accommodate  the  number  of  trains  that  could  be  between  the  ventilation  shafts  during  an emergency.'
## 4.  TUNNEL VENTILATION SYSTEM

## 4.  TUNNEL VENTILATION SYSTEM

The Tunnel Ventilation System shall be consider as a minimum, in the following events
(i) Fire in train way or station.
(ii)  Local Incident within the electrical utility that interrupts power to the emergency ventilation system.
(iii) Derailment.
To meet the above requirements, the system provided is as under
4.1. Each tunnel ventilation installation has a ventilation plant room at each end of the station box in which  there  are  two  fully  reversible  Tunnel  Ventilation  Fans  (TVFs)  and  Tunnel  Ventilation Dampers  (TVDs),  each  having  a  fan  isolation  damper  which  is  closed  when  the  fan  is  not  in operation. These are connected to both track ways and to the atmosphere through the ventilation shafts  at  the  end  of  the  station.  In  addition,  there  is  a  draught  relief  damper,  which  is  used  to allow the flow of air to bypass the fans during normal train operation when the fans are not in operation.
4.2. The Tunnel Booster Fans have also been installed inside the tunnel at the crossover and portal

## Introduction

locations to direct the flow in desired direction during congestion and emergent ventilation.

## Introduction

4.3. For station area, a separate ventilation system works through Trackway Exhaust Fans (TEF's), connected to Exhaust Ventilation Shafts generally adjoining to tunnel ventilation shafts at the end of the Station. The inlet of each track-ways at station is from Under Platform Exhaust (UPE) & Over Track Exhaust (OTE) and also from atmosphere through exhaust ventilation shaft, to enable separate  ventilation  of  each  station  trackway.  Tunnel  Ventilation  Dampers  (TVD)  are  used  to control and direct airflow from each track-way.
4.4. In DMRC, Tunnel Ventilation System has been designed to handle 20MW fire load of a car of the train, and the equipments are fire rated for 250 0  C for one hour Rolling stocks are designed for maximum allowed fire load in 20000 MJ - 28000 MJ.
## 5.  PRINCIPLES TO BE FOLLOWED FOR TVS DURING DETRAINMENT IN TUNNEL.

## 5.  PRINCIPLES TO BE FOLLOWED FOR TVS DURING DETRAINMENT IN TUNNEL.

The following are train operating conditions with reference to Tunnel Ventilation System covered:

### 5.  PRINCIPLES TO BE FOLLOWED FOR TVS DURING DETRAINMENT IN TUNNEL.

|   Sl. No. | Condition                     | Applicable                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Status of TVS                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|-----------|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|         1 | Normal Operation Condition    | When the trains are operating to time table throughout the system, at prescribed head-ways and dwell times.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | The TVFs are not operated in this condition. The ventilation during this condition is generated by the piston effect of the movement of trains and the trackway exhaust system.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|         2 | Congested Operating Condition | When trains are delay or any operational problems affecting time- table and causing trains to be held in tunnels, or at stations which may lead to rise in temperature in the tunnel beyond the set limits (Tunnel Stratified Temperature of 46 ℃ ) and if not corrected, would result in the 'under performance' of the train air conditioning system, creating discomfort to the passengers | During congested operation, the TVFs are operated to remove heat by circulating air in the tunnel in the direction of train movement. In underground section, on getting information from TO/any staff or through any other means regarding stoppage of any train in the tunnel for at least 2 minutes (presently, which is adjustable / resettable), the Traffic Controller shall in consultation with Auxiliary System Controller (ASC) decide which trains to be stopped at station. Auxiliary System Controller (ASC) will select the Master mode for 'congested mode' and relevant sub- group mode based (based on climate conditions and on Train location). |
|           | Emergency Operating Condition | When there is either fire on the train or in the tunnel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | In emergency condition the TVS is set to operate to control the movement of smoke and provide smoke free passage for passenger evacuation and access to the fire fighters. Dampers provided are also used to                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
## 6.  DETRAINMENT FROM TRAIN DURING FIRE AND OPERATION OF TUNNEL VENTILATION SYSTEM

## 6.  DETRAINMENT FROM TRAIN DURING FIRE AND OPERATION OF TUNNEL VENTILATION SYSTEM

Train Operator is to make all out efforts to take the incident train to the next Station. In case of fire in a train in underground tunnel section following principles are to be kept in mind:-

## 6.  DETRAINMENT FROM TRAIN DURING FIRE AND OPERATION OF TUNNEL VENTILATION SYSTEM

(i)  All cross-passage doors are normally closed.
(ii)  All trains are to be stopped / regulated on both the tracks of the affected section/station.
(iii) Adjacent stations are to be evacuated immediately.
(iv) Train Operator is to make all out efforts to take the incident train to the next Station.
(v)  In case the incident train is not able to move, the passengers are required to be detrained from the incident train, for which following is required:
## 6.1 In case of Fire inside the Salon/Car: -

## 6.1 In case of Fire inside the Salon/Car: -

(i) If  fire  is  inside  the  train,  stalled  in  the  section  and  fire  is  reported  by  the  passengers  using Emergency communication device or any other means, the TO will inform the OCC, determine the location of fire and try to extinguish the fire by using fire extinguishers. If the fire is extinguished, the TO of the train will update the OCC/TC and cautiously drive the train to the next station, where it would be inspected and evacuated (if required).
(ii) If  the  fire  continues /  uncontrollable,  the TO will immediately inform OCC/TC and evacuation of Train will be planned as per the procedure defined in Para-7 of this procedure.
6.2 In case of fire on equipment is in the under frame or roof top of the car (not inside the salon/car) : Following is to be ensured:
(a) OCC  to  instruct  TO  to  make  regular  announcements  to  avoid  panic  reactions  by  the passengers.
 Listen announcements patiently, follow instructions  and not to panic
 Move towards detrainment direction only
 Exit only as and when directed
 Beware of tripping hazards
(b) The location of the Fire on the Train and the number of the trains inside the same tunnel will decide direction of detrainment of passengers.

## Introduction

(c) Detainment will start only after the Ventilation Fans are 'Switched ON' for the direction opposite to the detrainment and if required, at least one Cross Passage is opened.

## Introduction

(d) Detrained passengers to be moved to the station, or to the adjacent tunnel - to a point of safety.
(e) The passengers will be able to egress safely.
(f) It is safe for the passengers to pass through the coach on fire as the under floor of the Coach is rated for 30 Minutes FRP.
(g) Prompt  Communication  is  available.  ASC/OCC  shall  ensure  that  Tunnel  lights  are  'Switched ON'. In case of fire, if communication breakdowns and it is not possible to operate TVS centrally then TVS need to be operated from Station Control Room through BMS / SCADA or locally at TVS MCC Room as per the hierarchy of commands at Para-6.4 of this Procedure.
(h) Power supply is available.
(i) Till an OCS (Officer In-charge at site) is nominated by OCC, TO will continue to perform duties of OCS, particularly in respect of safety of passengers to metro employees.
## 6.3 Responsibilities  of OCC:

## 6.3 Responsibilities  of OCC:

(i) OCC to instruct the TO to start evacuation and make suitable announcements in the train:-
(ii) Communication between OCC staff and TO to identify location of fire. OCC to arrange to clear the downstream platform.
(iii) OCC staff to  identify  affected  ventilation  zones  and  trains  involved  from  the  train  control  and signal system.
(iv) OCC staff will arrange to stop train movement on the adjacent tunnel also.
(v) OCC staff to inform the stations to put on the tunnel lights and intimate the Train Operator for passenger detrainment direction.
(vi) OCC to decide direction of passenger detrainment and identify appropriate TVS master mode.
(vii) OCC staff will activate the emergency mode and ensure confirmation through SCADA regarding success of mode (if unsuccessful, identify next possible mode).
(viii) Auxiliary System Controller to closely monitor status of various TVS plant in conformity with the selected mode.
(ix) After detrainment is completed and clearance from the Delhi/State Fire Services staff is taken, if necessary OCC staff may select any other appropriate mode of TVS Operation.
## 6.4  The Hierarchy of Control to be followed for TVS Operation

## 6.4  The Hierarchy of Control to be followed for TVS Operation

(i) Centrally from the OCC for entire section (inter-station) through SCADA workstation.
(ii)  Station control room for each station
(a)  Through local BMS / SCADA workstation in consultation with adjoining station.
(b)  Override priority through ventilation control panel (VCP)
(iii) Locally from ECS plant room (in phase-III only) through PLC touch screen.
(iv) Locally at each TVS MCC Room. By operation of the 'manual-off-auto' switch at MCC room.
## 6.5 Precautions to be taken during TVS functioning:

## 6.5 Precautions to be taken during TVS functioning:

(i) Once TVS is functioning,  in  NO  case,  the  passenger's  detrainment  will  be  planned  from

## Introduction

both ends of the Train.

## Introduction

(ii)  Once TVS is started, Direction of TVS OPERATION SHOULD NOT BE REVERSED, till the evacuation / rescue operation is completed.
(iii) TVS to be operated till:
(a) The evacuation is completed and
(b) The  TVS  Support  is  NO  more  required  by  Delhi/State  Fire  Service  Personnel  and Emergency Services.
(iv) The instruction regarding '  NOT TO REVERSE THE DIRECTION OF TVS OPERATION' stands 'TRUE' even if the TVS WAS OPERATING ON CONGESTED MODE prior to the occurrence of Emergency.
(v)  In the unlikely event of TVS not operating, the detrainment direction will remain the same as determined earlier.
(vi) OCC / Station Controller to remind  Delhi/State Fire Services Personnel not to aim the jet towards OHE till OHE is switched off and discharge rod provided.
## 6.6 Emergency Mode Operation of TVS with respect to Location of Fire on Train :

### 6.6 Emergency Mode Operation of TVS with respect to Location of Fire on Train :

| S.N   | Location                                                                       | Operation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Evacuation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|-------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| A     | Fire on train is at the track in Platform area (Station Trackway)              | TEF and TVF shall run as per mode table.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | In this case the passengers shall be evacuated from the salon doors towards the platform.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| B     | Fire on Train is partly on the Station Trackway and partly in adjacent tunnel. | In case the train has crossed the station platform but still remains on the station track- way and adjacent tunnel the TVF and TEF shall run as per the appropriate emergency mode after deciding the detrainment direction. Once passengers detrained emergency mode will be operated.                                                                                                                                                    | In case the train stops such that the some of the rear coaches are still on the station- trackway (platform) and a decision is taken to detrain the passengers from the salon doors to platform, the staff available at the station will open the salon doors and passengers will he detrained on the platform.                                                                                                                            |
| C     | Fire is on the train in Tunnel                                                 | (i) The TO will make all out efforts to take the train to the next station. (ii) In case the train stops inside the tunnel, detrainment will start after 'Switching ON' the tunnel ventilation system and tunnel lights and stopping train movements on the adjacent Line also. The sequence to be followed is as under: (a) The smoke is to be driven away from the train in one direction and detrainment will be planned from the other | (i) The TO will make all out efforts to take the train to the next station. (ii) In case the train stops inside the tunnel, detrainment will start after 'Switching ON' the tunnel ventilation system and tunnel lights and stopping train movements on the adjacent Line also. The sequence to be followed is as under: (a) The smoke is to be driven away from the train in one direction and detrainment will be planned from the other |
## 7. DIRECTION OF DETRAINMENT FROM TRAIN ON FIRE

## 7. DIRECTION OF DETRAINMENT FROM TRAIN ON FIRE

7.1 In case of a Fire on a Demobilized Train in The Tunnel , it is not advisable to bring any other train in the vicinity. The detrainment will take place from TRAIN-TO-TRACK or WALKWAY as per design and location of emergency exit door of train.

7.2 In the event of only ONE Train in the same ventilation zone .
The direction of detrainment from rear or front end will depend upon the location of the fire on the train. The objective is to minimize the length of the incident train that will be affected by smoke after the operation of the tunnel ventilation fans. TVS will direct the smoke away from the train e.g.
(a) If  the  fire  is  on  the  front  side  of  the  train,  the  tunnel  ventilation  fans  will  be  run  in  such  a manner that smoke is driven towards front end and de-trainment will be from the rear end.
(b) Conversely, if the fire is on the rear side of the train, the smoke will be directed towards the rear end of the train and the detrainment will be from the frontend.
(c) If the fire is on one of the middle coaches of the train (i.e. 2nd or 3rd coach in a 4 - car train composition, 3rd or 4th coach in a 6 -car train composition and 4th or 5th coach in a 8 - car train composition) smoke is to be driven in the direction, where less number of coaches   are likely to be affected. The direction of detrainment will be opposite to the direction in which the smoke is being driven.

(e.g. For ' 8-car train' , if the fire is on 3 rd   coach from the front , smoke is to be driven from front end of the train and passenger detrainment is to be done from the rear end. Similarly, if the  fire  is  on  5 th coach  the  smoke  is  to  be  driven  towards  rear  end  of  the  train  and  the detrainment will be from the front end.)
(d) This ventilation operation ensures that not more than half of the incident train will be affected by smoke once the tunnel ventilation system is operating.
7.3 In the event of two Trains in the same ventilation zone the following evacuation procedure is to be followed.
(a) If the f   ire is on the second (trailing) train, the TO of the first train will be informed by TC / OCC / SC, to continue his journey and reach the station and quickly vacate the platform to provide berth for the following incident train.
(b) In  case  second  (trailing)  train  is  disabled  and  unable  to  move  then  procedure  as described in Para-7.2 above shall be followed.
(c) If the fire is on the first (front) train, the non-incident train in the rear will be reversed
## to the station at speed as envisaged at Para-7.4 and 7.5.

## to the station at speed as envisaged at Para-7.4 and 7.5.

7.4 If the fire is in front coaches (up to first five coaches in case of '8-car train' and up to first four coaches in case of '6-car train) of the first train (Fig.1).

(i) TVS will be so operated that the smoke will be driven towards the front end of the train and  detrainment  will  be  arranged  from  the  rear  end,  asking  the  passengers  to  pass through the affected coach.
(ii) If the 2 nd train has already entered in the same tunnel section, it is the responsibility of the train operator of the 2 nd  train to ensure that at least there is one cross passages between the rear most coach of the first train and his train.
(a)  If the second train has already reached closer to the first train, the TO of the Second Train  will  select  SCS  and  then  reverse  the  train  (at  crawling  speed  of  maximum  10 Km/hr),  in  consultation  with  Traffic  Controller  and  ensure  that  at  least  one  cross passage (if available) between these two trains is available.
(b)  The  traction  supply  will  be  maintained  in  consultation  with  the  traction  controller.  In case traction supply is not available passengers of both the trains to be detrained from the rear and proceed as per evacuation planned.
(c)  The smoke will be driven from rear end to the front end of the first train.
(d) Passenger detrainment will be guided by TO from the rear end of the incident train and they will cross over to the adjacent tunnel and move in the direction of planned evacuation.
7.5 If the fire is in any of the rear coaches (6 th to 8 th coach in case of '8-car train' OR in 5 th / 6 th coach in case of '6-car train) of the first train (Fig-2)
(Figure-1)
## (Figure-2)

## (Figure-2)

(i) OCC shall advice TO of 2 nd  train to reverse the train to the station in rear without any loss of time in consultation with Traffic Controller. TO will select SCS mode and move the train in reverse.

## (Figure-2)

(ii) If 3rd train has already occupied the platform at station in the rear, it will also be reversed first to the station in rear of it to accommodate the second train (being reversed).
(iii) The traction supply will be maintained in consultation with the traction controller.
(iv)   In  case traction supply is not available, the 2nd train passengers will be detrained from the rear and asked to proceed in the direction of planned evacuation. TVS to be regulated accordingly. ASC/OCC  shall  ensure  that  TVS  is operated in desired direction in consultation with CHC/OCC, keeping in view the nature of fire & extent and direction of evacuation of each train.
(v) Once the second train has been reversed to the platform of the station in rear, the smoke of first train will be driven towards the rear end of the first train (incident Train).
(vi)  Passenger detrainment will be arranged from the front end of the incident train and they will move on the same track or cross over to adjacent tunnel through cross passage and move towards the station in the direction of the planned evacuation.
## 8. For UTO Mode of Train Operation

## 8. For UTO Mode of Train Operation

8.1 Wherever it is mentioned that OCC shall instruct Train Operator to troubleshoot, it is to be read as 'TC shall troubleshoot through remote commands or instruct TO/RA/ETO, as required.'
8.2 Wherever it is  mentioned that TO shall make announcements, it is to read as IC shall make necessary announcements in train/s.
8.3 In case of fire and smoke detection inside train (RS-10) in UTO mode, extant procedure as per SC-12 shall be followed.

text:
## 1. Introduction

Delhi  Metro  is  using  many  types  of  non-ATP  maintenance  vehicles  including  self-propelled vehicles. This JPO lays down the procedure for movement of these vehicles with / without loco on the  main  line  including  their  upkeep,  manning,  stabling,  securing  &  their  actual  operation/ movement. This JPO also includes the rescue operation of/by these vehicles.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p1_3

text:
## 1. Introduction

This procedure order deals with the movement of non-ATP maintenance vehicles including selfpropelled vehicles and should be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules 2020 and its amendment, Safety Rules, Station Working Orders & Depot Working Orders and Special Instructions in force.
Non-ATP vehicles defined in this circular are Diesel / Battery powered locomotive, Mercedes Benz/ phooltas 'Rail cum Road' Emergency vehicle, LORAM Rail Grinding machine, Flat wagon, CTMC, OMV, CMV, Motor trolley, etc.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf

text: ## 2. Stabling

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p4_5

text:
In general, any non-ATP vehicle shall be stabled and secured in concerned depot at nominated place and the stabling place shall be protected by displaying a red light/red flags on accessible ends for vehicles stabled on rail track.
However, to increase effective maintenance time during block, non-ATP vehicle can be stabled in siding of main line. Following points to be followed for stabling of non-ATP vehicle on main line:
Request for night stabling of non-ATP vehicle will be included in the requisition for Weekly General Order submitted by respective controller to Chief Controller.
Night stabling of non-ATP vehicle should be planned at siding nearest to EP section granted to that vehicle.
After stabling of non-ATP vehicle at siding, EPIC will ensure that all mechanical/parking brakes are fully applied. He will secure the vehicle by putting scotch blocks at both sides of wheels at all four end wheels and chain must be tied around scotch blocks on wheels and must be tied with fixed object at track side. A red colored retro reflective tape not less than (10 cm X 10 cm) - 2 nos. shall be pasted at both side of vehicle and Red banner flags having 3-4-inch-wide reflective tape stitched diagonally making X mark in center and along the borders should be placed from stabled vehicle at both sides or at entry side in one-way sidings.
EPIC  is  responsible  for  securing  the  vehicle.  EPIC  will  exchange  private  number  with concerned  controller  in  OCC.  AT  OCC,  concerned  controller  will  inform  TC  in  writing  that vehicle has been properly secured.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p4_7

text:
EPIC  is  responsible  for  securing  the  vehicle.  EPIC  will  exchange  private  number  with concerned  controller  in  OCC.  AT  OCC,  concerned  controller  will  inform  TC  in  writing  that vehicle has been properly secured.
Traffic Controller (TC) or (Station Controller, if control is at local level) will block all possible routes towards siding where vehicle has been stabled and apply maintenance block in the siding.
Only after ensuring above steps train movement will be permitted in the mainline.
Concerned SC and TC will maintain the log of vehicle stabling in designated siding.

## 3. Usage

3.1 The Diesel / Battery powered locomotive shall be used to carry the work train (consisting of Flat wagon, CTMC, OMV and Rail Grinding power car with two grind carts etc.) or Locomotive alone for the planned maintenance and in emergency for rescue of other non-ATP vehicles and trains as suggested by RSC. The Mercedes Benz / phooltas 'Rail cum Road' Emergency vehicle is used for Re-railing & rescue needs within the depot and in the mainline.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p4_10

## Introduction

3.2 The LORAM Rail Grinding machine vehicle is used for grinding of rail head within the depot and in the main line & for preventive maintenance during non-revenue hours.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p1_0

## Introduction

3.3 The  4-wheeler  OHE  maintenance  vehicle,  the  catenary  track  motor  car  shall  be  used  for attending the OHE breakdown during the traffic hours & for preventive maintenance during the non-traffic hours. Catenary Maintenance Vehicle shall be added to the list of work train.
3.4 The flat wagon shall be used for transportation of heavy material during breakdowns during the traffic hours & for preventive maintenance during the non-traffic hours.
3.5 The motor trolley shall be primarily used for inspections and for carrying minor light weight items in case of emergency.
Note: - List of Non-ATP vehicles have been placed at Annexure 'A'.

text: ## 5. Engineer's Possession in Charge and Possession Procedure -

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p6_2

text:
5.1 All non-ATP vehicles shall work in Engineer's Possession only.
5.2 JE/RS shall be in charge of diesel / battery powered locomotives i.e.; Mercedes Benz 'Rail cum Road' Emergency vehicles and Flat wagon. The OHE supervisor shall be in charge of the  OHE  maintenance  vehicle/  Catenary  Track  Motor  Car/CMV  and  Flat  Wagon.  Motor Trolley/ Dip Lorry shall be under the charge of P. Way Supervisor. JE/P. Way shall be in charge of Rail Grinding Machine. Material Trolley shall be under the charge of P. Way/ Works Supervisor.
5.3 The vehicle shall be in possession of Engineer's Possession in Charge. She/He shall have TETRA Radio set in working condition. She/He shall submit the requisition for traffic block and permit to work as per Safety Circular 02 pertaining to Procedure order for granting & cancellation of power blocks and permit to work. For Vehicle Movement, EPIC shall give the requisition to OCC/CHC for Traffic and Power Blocks respectively. For PTW, she/he shall give the requisition to concerned SC with required details.
5.4 Concerned Supervisor in charge should be conversant with OHE, Track, Point & Crossing, Signaling  system  and  Communication  system.  She/He  shall  be  responsible  for  vehicle's operation at work site including safe movement and safety of staff and equipment in the area under the Engineers Possession.
5.5 In case of grant of power block, the EPIC of vehicle shall be responsible for confirming to the SC/DC on completion of the work that OHE is safe for Traction power to be switched on, all men & material have been removed & track is safe for trains to run.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf

text: ## 6. Working:

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p6_5

text:
## 6. Working:

6.1 Maintenance Vehicles shall run in accordance with the Instructions contained in MRGR-2020 Rule-33 & Rule- 84(2)' for 'Running of Self-Propelled Vehicles not fitted with ATP'.
6.2 In  case  of  planned  /  regular  scheduled  maintenance,  the  movement  of  vehicle  shall  be planned in advance. In case of any breakdown, the movement is to be decided based on the location where breakdown occurs.
6.3 During all non-ATP vehicles movement in depot or mainline, the driver must ensure that all the  shutters  and  doors  of  vehicle  are  shut  /  closed  and  there  is  no  protruded  part  from emergency vehicle which can infringe the kinematics envelope or minimum safe distance from OHE.
6.4 During  the  movement  of  non-ATP  vehicles  any  commands  from  CATS/LATS/CCIP/VDU (Whichever is applicable) involving signals/routes/points (including setting, blocking, unblocking etc.) shall be given after confirming location of non-ATP vehicles from EPIC.
6.5 Before entering into the main line, the supervisor shall obtain an authority to proceed for the movement  of  the  vehicle  (as  applicable)  from  the  Traffic  Controller/Station  Controller  of concerned interlocking station mentioning the number and date of valid fitness certificate on the exchange of Private Numbers or in writing, if the Tetra radio set Communication is not possible.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p6_6

text:
## Introduction

Such an Authority shall be given only if the Section up to the next interlocking station is clear of trains and other vehicles and has been blocked by the 'Engineer's Possession or Section up to the next interlocking is granted to the Same EPIC seeking authority to proceed.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p1_0

text:
6.6 Violet  signal  aspect  shall  be  considered  as  RED  for  all  non-ATP  vehicles.  Authority  to Proceed shall be obtained from OCC (TC)/SC by the in charge/EPIC/Vehicle operator as per extant procedure for passing any signal at danger i.e. displaying red / violet / blank aspect.
6.7 If  the Movement of Vehicle is taken on the Main Line to attend the breakdown of OHE or some failure  during  traffic  Hours,  the  Traffic  Controller  shall  grant  necessary  Engineer's Possession & Traffic Block and the Traction Power Controller shall grant the Emergency Power Block as per the requirements duly following the SOP for Granting & Cancellation of Traffic Block & Power Block.
6.8 The Driver of above Vehicles shall not move the vehicle over points & crossings until he has satisfied himself that these points are set in the intended direction of movement.
6.9 Self-Normalizing points should be blocked by OCC/ DCC before movement of Vehicle.
6.10 Following  precautions  shall  be  ensured  by  operator  of  all  types  of  non-ATP  vehicles  for movement through self-normalizing points and trap points:
After inspecting the status of point enroute set and locked condition the non-ATP vehicle should be moved through it at normal speed. In case of following specific situation special precautions/actions shall be taken:
When to and fro motion is required through the point for working on OHE.
When non-ATP vehicle has to be stopped in the point zone area.
When non-ATP vehicle is to be moved at very slow speed through this point.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p7_2

text:
When to and fro motion is required through the point for working on OHE.
When non-ATP vehicle has to be stopped in the point zone area.
When non-ATP vehicle is to be moved at very slow speed through this point.
In above conditions, before moving through the point, non-ATP vehicle operator shall get the point blocked from OCC/DCC/SC and get the confirmation on tetra set under exchange of private number.
If due to any reason/defect moving non-ATP vehicle gets stalled, non-ATP vehicle operator shall get the point blocked by OCC/DCC/SC before making any further movement through the point.
In  case  of  departure from point  zone, for which blocking of point was done (i.e.; once purpose  of  blocking  of  points  gets  solved),  non-ATP  vehicle  operator  shall  inform TC/DCC/SC about completion of work and request to unblock the point on tetra under exchange of private number.
6.11 Special Instructions for the Movement & Stabling of Bogie Flat for Rail (BFR) Coupled with Catenary Track Motor Car (CTMC) in Metro Corridor & Khyber Pass Depot (KPD)-
BFRs (2 no. four wheeler flat top wagons, trailer car with reel stand model TC01 & trailer car  model  T02,  non-self-propelled  vehicles)  shall  be  stabled  and  secured  near  ETU Building, in east shunting line between emergency lines 1 & 2.
For the Movement of BFRs coupled with Catenary Maintenance Vehicle, Instructions for movement of CTMC are to be followed.

Movement  of  BFRs  coupled  with  CTMC  to  main  lines  shall  only  be  permitted  under Engineer's Possession extended up to next interlocked station with CTMC leading. The movement  is  subject  to  the  condition  of  OHE  shutdown.  Further  movement  to  east shunting  line  shall  not  be  permitted  unless  OHE  supervisor  gives  clearance  of  east shunting line and status of BFRs and CTMC in writing in case of routine movement and by exchanging private number in case of emergency.

## Introduction

To stable the BFR in east shunting line, route S01S_S14S shall be set by LATS/CCIP from shunting neck to stabling line.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p1_0

text:
## Introduction

BFRs pushed by CTMC shall be sent to the stabling line. However, the coupled unit shall not  clear  the  signal  S14S  for  controlling  the  opposite  movement.  While  pushing  the vehicle, the speed shall not exceed 10kmph & shall be hand-signaled.
After stabling the BFRs, CTMC shall be uncoupled & its Movement from stabling line to shunting neck shall be controlled by hand signals.
BFRs to be secured by the application of Parking Brakes and wooden wedges shall be placed at all the four exterior wheels. BFRs shall also be chained and padlocked with buffer stop. Keys shall be kept in custody of OHE Department.
For the movement of BFRs from east shunting line, route S01S_S14S shall be set for the CTMC. CTMC shall be moved to shunting line & coupled with BFRs. The coupled length of BFRs with CTMC may not clear S14S, hence the pull-out movement of this coupled unit from stabling line to shunting neck shall be controlled by hand signals. It is to be ensured that for this movement points P33S, P32S, P29S, P19S, P16S & P02S must be secured by clamp & padlock and this movement to be done with exchange of private number between CTMC driver and DCC.

text: ## 6.12 Movement of CMV/CTMC coupled with BFR/FW

text:
## 6.12 Movement of CMV/CTMC coupled with BFR/FW

(i) Movement of Bogie Flat for Rail (BFR) / Flat Wagon (FW) coupled with Catenary Track Motor Car (CTMC) / Catenary Maintenance Vehicle (CMV) on Main Line shall only be permitted under Engineer's Possession extended up to next interlocked station with CTMC/CMV leading.
(ii) Normally,  the  movement  is  subject  to  the  condition  of  OHE  shutdown  but  may  be allowed under live OHE condition (OHE Live /Shutdown condition as specified in the traffic and power request submitted by the concerned department) when BFR is used for Cable Transportation subject to following precautions: -
(a) Cable should be carried in loop condition (making 8 type loop) and secured on BFR, but if Cable Drum is necessary for carrying cables then it shall be secured properly on BFR and adequate clearance shall be maintained from live OHE.
(b) Availability of Look out person shall be ensure in CMV rear Cab during movement.
(c) Tool box talk with contractor staffs shall be conducted before execution of work.
(d) CMV speed limit in couple consist (CMV/CTMC+ BFR/FW) shall be ensured with proper braking arrangement as per prescribed limit.
(e) CMV operator shall be careful about signal aspect, points set in desired direction and speed restriction at gradient during movement.
(f) No person shall be allowed on BFR/FW when OHE is in charged condition.
(g) EPIC will certify above precautions in the form of check sheet before departure of BFR from site to depot or vice versa.

## 7. Rescue:

7.1 In  emergency  non-ATP  vehicles  will  be  used  for  rescuing  another  non-ATP  vehicle  or defective train. Train can also be used for rescuing non-ATP vehicle. The loco/Vehicles that can be used for rescue operation are placed at ' Annexure B' . Priority for rescue operation shall be given to metro train.

7.2 The  decision  of  selection  of  rescuing  vehicle  will  be  taken  in  coordination  of  concerned controllers in OCC keeping in view of OHE charge/discharge requirement, concerned staff availability, track layout/gradient, etc.

text:
7.3 In  case  the  non-ATP  vehicle  becomes  non-operative  on  the  main  line,  the  concerned supervisor accompanying non-ATP vehicle shall inform concerned controller in OCC, who in turn shall advise the Traffic Controller, Rolling Stock Controller & PPIO to arrange the rescue locomotive / train for the rescue of disabled vehicle.
7.4 The DMRC official of concerned department in leading vehicle shall be made the EPIC.
7.5 To request for the rescue of vehicle, the concerned Supervisor shall inform following details to the concerned controller in OCC:
The Station/Block Section where the disabled vehicle is stranding.
Kilometerage/ KM or OHE mast no. where the disabled vehicle is standing.
Line in which movement required.
7.6 For rescue of disabled vehicle, the EPIC, who is in charge of disabled vehicle shall observe the following precautions:
Permit to work shall be cancelled.
All shadow block shall be cancelled, if required.
Power block shall be cancelled, if required.
Concerned controller shall withdraw patrolling from section en-route of rescue loco.
All blocks given by Traffic Controller shall also be cancelled in the respective section& all patrolling parties including P. Way staff to be called back. If rescue is being planned by train, all shadow/power blocks to be cancelled immediately.
While coupling, the vehicle to be coupled shall be secured to avoid roll down by providing scotch block on extreme end of outer wheels if, no other brake is available in the vehicle.
The Operator of the rescue locomotive shall be advised of the circumstances & location and shall be issued necessary authority for entering into the obstructed section at the reduced speed of 15kmph by Traffic Controller.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p9_2

text:
The Operator of the rescue locomotive shall be advised of the circumstances & location and shall be issued necessary authority for entering into the obstructed section at the reduced speed of 15kmph by Traffic Controller.
Rescue Loco should stop 10 m short of the disabled non-ATP vehicle/train and gently move to it for coupling.
Again, rescue loco/train must be dead stopped at 3-5 m before the disabled Non-ATP Vehicle and then only it shall be moved forward for coupling with the inching operation.
Before  Coupling,  Check  both  coupler  are  in  line  (ensure  proper  vertical  &  horizontal alignment of couplers, required for smooth coupling).
Train Operator and the supervisor available in the rescue unit shall make sure that the speed of the train during coupling shall not exceed 03 KMPH.
After coupling, after removing all four Scotch Blocks, Vehicle driver shall Perform a 'Pull Test/Coupling Test' by giving a very little bit of jerk before releasing the parking brakes of Disabled Non-ATP Vehicle. After successful Pull Test/ Coupling test, parking brakes shall be released by non-ATP vehicle driver. He shall inform to the operator of rescue loco through  CAB-to-CAB  communication  or  through  wireless  Radio  set  (Tetra)  &  by  the exchange of hand signal or tri Colour torch.
In coupled condition, whether in forward or in reverse direction, tractive effort shall be of the rescue vehicle only. This shall be ensured both by rescue vehicle operator & another non-ATP vehicle/train operator.

text:
## 8. Maintenance of Vehicles:

8.1 The Diesel/Battery Powered Locomotives, Emergency Vehicle, Flat Wagon shall be regularly given preventive periodic maintenance and required overhauls by the rolling stock supervisor. The rolling stock portion of OHE maintenance vehicle shall be regularly checked/ inspected/ maintained by the rolling stock wing or an authorized body under his supervision and shall be declared fit to run after every such check/ inspection/maintenance.
8.2 The  diesel-powered  rail  grinding  machine  shall  be  regularly  given  preventive  periodic maintenance  under  the  supervision  of  DMRC  trained  staff.  It  shall  always  have  a  valid certificate of fitness for working on main line.
8.3 Though the movement vehicle shall have a valid certificate of fitness, the driver of the vehicle shall also examine the healthiness of the batteries, lights, diesel, lube oil, brake pressure, braking  system  &  other  safety  items,  lighting  &  communication  equipment's,  hydraulic  & pneumatic equipment's, carry out necessary safety & operational checks as required before moving and after completion of the work. The battery (if applicable) shall be kept on charging in depot.

text:
9.1 The staff including the driver available in the emergency vehicle shall observe all safety rules including the instructions for working inside the tunnel. All such staff shall be familiar with traction,  E&M,  ECS,  ETS,  Tunnel  Ventilation  system  &  fire-fighting  system  and  other associated equipments & systems.
9.2 Staff shall not be allowed to climb on the roof of the vehicle, without making the OHE dead and earthed.
9.3 While working, care shall be taken that any metallic part shall not come in the close vicinity of OHE i.e. within 2 meters from the OHE.
9.4 The non-ATP vehicle operator shall be trained in operation & driving and shall be conversant with safety rules including the general rules, special working instructions and working of trains on  the  main  line  for  which  the  competency  certificate  shall  be  issued  by  the  respective department. He should have the proper route learning.
9.5 As far as Rail Grinding Machine is concerned, if it is operated and maintained by outsourced person, RGM shall be piloted by EPIC who shall be trained in the working of trains on the main line for which the competency certificate shall be issued by the respective department and should have proper route learning. The responsibility of RGM movement shall be with EPIC.

text: ## 9.7 Precaution pertaining to Bogie Flat for Rail (BFR) / Flat Wagon (FW):

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p12_1

text:
The movement of BFR/FW is permitted in Power Block Condition but may be allowed under live OHE condition as per aforementioned para 6.12.
Adequate precautions & safety measures shall be taken while carrying out the movement of flat wagon in loaded or unloaded condition.
The loading or un-loading of the flat wagon shall be done under the Power Block condition i.e.; when 25KV AC OHE shall be in the de-energized condition.
Any working of crane & any activity over the flat wagon shall be carried out under the power block condition and in presence of OHE supervisor.
No metallic  part  of  the  Flat  wagon  shall  come  within  the  range  of  Standard  Electrical clearance (320mm) from the 25KV AC live OHE.
When the Loaded Flat Wagon, hauled by Diesel Locomotive is moved, it shall be the responsibility of the EPIC to ensure SOD (Standard Operating Dimension) is not infringed.
Loose Shunting of Flat Wagon in loaded or in unloaded condition is not permitted.
When the Maintenance Work by OHE Maintenance Vehicle, Flat Wagon is to be carried out in the stretches where OHE has got restricted clearance i.e. less than 2m from each other,  the  necessary  precautions  against the  Electrocution  of the Worker,  like  shutting down the OHE of adjacent Line, shall be taken before taking up the Maintenance Work in hand. TPC shall particularly check this before granting the Power Blocks.

Before entering in tunnel area/section, the rail grinding machine In-charge shall inform OCC and ASC staff for putting TVF in operation as per location/section. Same will be applicable to other vehicles too exhausting diesel fumes.

text: ## 9.11 Precautions  and  Procedure  in  case  of  uncoupling/  damage  in  coupling  during movement of combined consists of Non-ATP Rail Vehicle on Mainline or in depot yard.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p12_5

text:
## 9.11 Precautions  and  Procedure  in  case  of  uncoupling/  damage  in  coupling  during movement of combined consists of Non-ATP Rail Vehicle on Mainline or in depot yard.

Shunter/Operator of Non-ATP vehicle shall always inspect the physical condition of both side couplers before coupling to avoid mechanical failure.
Shunter/Operator shall ensure proper coupling by pulling back and physical inspection of couplers after coupling to avoid coupling failure during movement of the vehicle/ consist.
Non-ATP Vehicle must carry minimum 02 pairs of scotch block in vehicle storage before starting any movement
In depot, before starting of movement of train consists with Non-ATP vehicle, maximum rated pressure by self-power or by external pneumatic supply is to be ensured.
Covers of BIC Panel in Non-powered train shall be kept in open condition before starting of any movement with Non-ATP Vehicle.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p12_6

text:
## Introduction

In case of uncoupling, shunter/ operator of Non-ATP vehicle or train/ unit whoever first noticed  incident  of  uncoupling,  immediately  inform  to  other  shunter/  operator  about uncoupling.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p1_0

text:
Both shunters/ operators immediately shall apply emergency brake of Non-ATP vehicle & shall make normal BIC of train consists of both vehicles to avoid any roll which may take place due to gradient on track.
If train consist is in stable condition after uncoupling then Shunter/ operator, of Non-ATP vehicle, shall immediately provide the scotch blocks at both sides of end axles of nonpowered consist.
After that Shunter of Non-ATP vehicle shall inform to PPIO and DCC in depot and to OCC on main line regarding incident with location and condition of both vehicles.
For incident on mainline, CHC/TC/OCC shall inform to RSC to dispatch maintenance staff to the location of incident near uncoupled consist in station/ section and take decision whether consist to be sent in depot or to siding and arrange rescue relief on mainline. For incident in depot, PPIO shall immediately inform & instruct the inspection staff regarding incident to reach at the location of uncoupling or present location of consist in depot.
For  incident  on  main  line,  CHC/TC/OCC  shall  inform  to  HOD  &  concerned  Dy.  HOD operations  regarding  incident  details.  For  incident  in  Depot,  PPIO  shall  also  inform  to concerned RS officers i.e.; HOD & concerned Dy. HOD regarding the incident and convey the instructions of officers to staff available on incident site.
OCC in mainline and DCC in depot shall ensure that no other train movement shall be done in area/ adjoining line where Incident took place.
After ensuring that non powered consist is stabled with help of scotch blocks then inspect coupler condition of both vehicles to find out the possible causes of uncoupling.

metadata.source: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 20. SC-20 (Rev-08) Movement of Non-ATP rail vehicle_p13_2

text:
After ensuring that non powered consist is stabled with help of scotch blocks then inspect coupler condition of both vehicles to find out the possible causes of uncoupling.
If no abnormalities found then execute re-coupling of non-powered consist with non-ATP vehicle immediately to take control of non-powered vehicle by non-ATP vehicle.
In case of any damage or abnormality in coupler of any vehicle or coupling is not possible due to any mechanical damage or failure in Coupler of any vehicle execute coupling from other end of non-powered vehicle with other Non-ATP vehicle or other self-powered Train to shunt non powered vehicle at desired/safe location.

text: ## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 43B (REV-01)

## Applicable to Line-7 only.

Subject :- Safety Circular - 43B (Rev-01) regarding 'Procedure order for movement of train between depot & mainline and induction/ stabling of outstation stabled train in UTO mode at line-7'.
Find enclosed Safety Circular - 43B (Rev-01) regarding 'Procedure order for movement of train between depot & mainline and induction/ stabling of outstation stabled train in UTO mode at line-7'.
Provisions for UTO Mode of operation in this circular shall be applicable only after CMRS sanction for UTO Mode of operation.
All  concerned are  to  ensure that  staff  working under  them  have  read and  understood the procedure and assurance regarding the same is taken.
This is issued with the approval of the competent authority.
(Rajesh Kumar Raghav) Sr. DGM/Ops/C&P
Copy to: All EDs/HODs (O&M) and DG (DMRC Academy), All Dy. HODs (O&M), Mgr/AM (Train Operation, Station, OCC), All Stations, All Crew Controls and All DCC and DMRC Academy.
## SAFETY CIRCULAR-43 'B' (Rev-01)
## Procedure order for movement of train between depot & mainline and induction/ stabling of outstation stabled train in UTO mode at line-7.

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This procedure shall be applicable for UTO induction/stabling of train from Station/Depot/Outstation  to  mainline  and  vice  versa  in  UTO  mode  with/without  Train Operator/Roving Attendant. This  procedure  defines  roles  and responsibilities  of  staff  of  all concerned department and actions to be taken by them during train movement.

## 2. SCOPE

This procedure order is applicable to Line-7.
This procedure order shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and its amendment and other relevant Safety Circulars, Station Working Order, Depot Working Order, Special Instructions in vogue.
## 3. STABLING  TRAIN  AFTER  REVENUE  SERVICE  AND  PUTTING  THE  TRAIN  IN  SLEEP MODE:

TC/DCC shall plan UTO fit trains to be stabled at MKPD/VND/Mainline in consultation with RSC/PPIO.
After  completion  of  last  trip,  the  train  destined  for  MKPD/VND  will  stop  at  MKPR/IPE platform while the trains needed to be stabled on mainline Siding/Platform will stop at their respective last service platform. TC shall apply Platform hold on the Platform.
TO/RA/SC shall give confirmation to TC/OCC that all passengers have de-boarded from the train.
If Train is in modes other than UTO, After Train Door and PSD Operation by RA in ATP mode or Automatically in ATO mode, RA shall ensure that Mode Selector (MS) is in AUTO position of both the cabs, and UTO mode is selected by pressing  UTO soft button and remove the mascon key and release EB. RA shall verify that UTO mode 'UTO' symbol appearing on the DMI and shall inform TC accordingly. The following symbol appears on DMI.
On successful execution of above steps, TC shall ensure the train indication box turn green (As per Annexure-2 ) on ATS MMI in line overview.
RA shall de-board the train after ensuring that no passenger is onboard and inform to TC.
TC after getting  confirmation  that  all  passengers  and  RA  (if  on  board)  himself  has  deboarded from train shall remove the Platform Hold to authorize train movement.
Train shall move towards Depot/Siding for train stabling as per timetable or TC/DCC shall set the route manually towards stabling location subject to area of authority of depot/Siding.

Train shall move towards Depot/Siding for train stabling as per timetable or TC/DCC shall set the route manually towards stabling location subject to area of authority of depot/Siding.
After train is stabled & properly docked at its location, Sleep Mode On command will be executed automatically as per timetable. In case train not in time table or Sleep Mode On command not executed automatically, TC/DCC shall give manual remote Sleep Mode On command to set the train to sleep.
TC/DCC shall confirm from SGC that No EB is applied before giving Sleep Mode On command.
In case EB is applied then TC/DCC shall give Remote Emg Brake Reset command from

## Introduction

ATS for that train.

## Introduction

In case EB cannot be released by above steps then TC shall inform to RSC and DCC shall inform this to PPIO and signaling system controller shall inform to signaling (O&M) staff in depot for its rectification.
On successful execution of Sleep Mode On command TC/DCC shall ensure the train (Rake No.) indication turns purple (as per Annexure 2 ) on ATS MMI in line overview.
Note: In case due to emergency, if RA/Shunter has to stable the train at MKPD/VND SBL or mainline in any mode other than UTO, RA/SHUNTER shall ensure train is properly docked at NSP as per the docking symbol on DMI. The following symbol appears on DMI.
## 4. Maintenance of train in Sleep Mode / any other work on SBL

## 4. Maintenance of train in Sleep Mode / any other work on SBL

Maintenance of any train in Sleep Mode/any other work on SBL should follow procedure detailed in Annexure-1.
After completion of maintenance activities, PPIO shall endorse fitness of the train as per Para 8.
## 5. Wake-up process of the train

PPIO  shall  ensure  that  Operational  ID  and  fitness  of  all  depot  stabled  trains  (with corresponding rake ID) scheduled for induction is provided to DCC and RSC. RSC shall further provide the same to ACC/CHC-OCC.
DCC shall inform TC, Train set number for dispatch to Main Line well in advance (at least 75 min prior to departure).
If required, DCC shall instruct the points-man to operate/remove the Staff Protection Key (SPKS) in order to allow the RA/maintenance staff to enter the train for preparation/fault analysis.  Details  of  SPKS  in  depot  SBL  is  placed  at Annexure-4 , Annexure-5 and Annexure-6 .
In depot, DCC shall setup the priority however for outstation stabled train, TC shall setup the priority.  In depot, after setting priority ATS shall assign Service ID automatically as per timetable  to  Train  set  numbers  for  that  service  day  60  minutes  before  the  scheduled mainline departure time. For mainline trains, TC shall assign service ID to trains. Note: Service ID assigned to train in stabling track will be visible to TC/DCC.
Train will  automatically  initiate  execution  of the Wakeup process 45 minutes before the scheduled mainline departure time. Cab light, head light and TCMS will turn on as soon as wakeup process initiates. If train wake up process does not initiate automatically 30 minutes before schedule time, DC/TC shall give manual wake up command in consultation with SGC.
Train Indications available on ATS MMI for UTO mode are described in Annexure-2 .

Train Indications available on ATS MMI for UTO mode are described in Annexure-2 .
After  execution of Wakeup process, one of the following two ('Finished and Passed' & 'Finished  and Failed') departure status would be available in events log on ATS terminal and UST result 'train ready without fault/ train ready with fault/ train not ready' would be available on RSC terminal. All the concerned controllers (TC/DCC, RSC and SGC) shall monitor wake up process on their terminals for possible results and shall take prompt action for  any  unusual  occurrence.  Concerned  controllers  shall  take  necessary  action  for rectification of fault.
Combined result of UST and VATC Departure test is shown in Train properties and EB feel test result will be shown in event logs on ATS. SGC shall communicate the result of EB feel test to TC/DCC as soon as result available.
## A. Departure Test Status: 'Finished and Passed' with UST result train ready without fault

## A. Departure Test Status: 'Finished and Passed' with UST result train ready without fault

Route from respective Stabling location shall be triggered automatically 5 min before the scheduled departure time in case EB feel test result comes finished and passed and train shall depart automatically.

## A. Departure Test Status: 'Finished and Passed' with UST result train ready without fault

Route from respective Stabling location shall not be triggered automatically 5 min before the scheduled departure time in case EB feel test result comes finished and failed, Para 5.C.V shall be followed.
Train stabled at SBLs will get the Operational destination ID at Transfer Track and further movement will be in timetable mode towards MKPR/IPE platform. For mainline stabled trains, Operational ID shall be assigned before schedule departure.
## B. Departure Test Status: 'Finished and Failed' with UST result train ready without fault

## B. Departure Test Status: 'Finished and Failed' with UST result train ready without fault

Route will not be fired automatically & Train will not move.
Hot Stand by train shall be inducted in its place (Refer Annexure-3).
Same train may be inducted in ATP/ATO mode after confirmation of Rolling Stock Controller (RSC) and Signalling System Controller (SGC) if the train is being inducted from Siding/Platform.
Signaling (O&M) shall take the train for maintenance as per appropriate procedure.
## C. Departure Test Status: 'Finished and Failed' with UST result train ready with fault

Route will not be fired automatically & Train will not move.
RSC/PPIO and Signaling System Controller shall analyse the reason of failure
PPIO shall consult RSC about the fault and possibility of inducting train with fault.
PPIO/RSC and Signaling (O&M) staff/ Signaling System Controller shall analyze the fault and decide if train can be introduced in revenue service with the fault. PPIO/RSC shall inform this to DCC/TC accordingly.
In  case  of  fault  analysis/induction  in  mode  other  than  UTO,  if  train  needs  to  be accessed by maintenance staff/Train Operator, then Annexure-4 shall be followed.
Note: If  the  time  taken  for  fault  rectification  is  long  then  another  train  set  shall  be assigned in that Service ID. And later on, that train set may be used in another Service ID as per requirement.
If the train can be introduced with the fault in UTO :
EB feel test command has to be executed manually by the TC/DC and if EB feel test result comes as 'EB feel test Finished and Failed' on ATS then TC/DC shall consult with RSC & SGC and after consultation if RSC & SGC suggests to induct the train with this failure ('EB feel test finished and failed'), TC/DC shall set the desired route. DC shall set the route towards respective mainline entry signal under exchange of Private No with TC. TC/DC shall reset EB and train will depart automatically after giving 'Start Train' command from ATS.

EB feel test command has to be executed manually by the TC/DCC and if EB feel test result comes as 'EB feel test Finished and Passed' on ATS then TC/DCC shall set the route towards respective mainline entry signal. For trains to be inducted from depot,  DCC  shall  set  the  route  towards  respective  mainline  entry  signal  under exchange of Private No with TC. Train will depart automatically.
If the train cannot be introduced in UTO for revenue service:
DCC shall assign Service ID for the Hot Standby UTO train in depot.

## Introduction

After assignment of the train set in that Service ID, Route has to be set manually till mainline entry signal and train will depart automatically.

## Introduction

Same train may be inducted in ATP/ATO mode after confirmation of Rolling Stock Controller  (RSC)  and  Signalling  System  Controller  (SGC)  if  the  train  is  being inducted from Siding/Platform
## D. Departure Test Status: 'Finished and Failed' with UST result Train not ready .

## D. Departure Test Status: 'Finished and Failed' with UST result Train not ready .

DCC  shall  assign  Service  ID  for  the  Hot  Standby  UTO  train  in  depot.  After assignment of the  train  set  in  that  Service  ID,  Route  has  to  be  set  manually  till mainline entry signal and train will depart automatically (Refer Annexure 3).
Same train may be inducted in ATP/ATO mode after confirmation of Rolling Stock Controller  (RSC)  and  Signalling  System  Controller  (SGC)  if  the  train  is  being inducted from Siding/Platform
## 6. Sleep Mode Off Command failure/Any other failure.

If Train does not automatically start execution of the Wakeup process 30 minutes before the scheduled mainline departure time and/or manual sleep mode off command fails, then train indication will be checked as per Annexure-2 and Hot Standby Train shall be inducted as Annexure-03.
TC/DCC shall inform about the fault to RSC/PPIO and Signaling System Controller shall inform about the fault to signaling (O&M) staff.
PPIO shall consult with RSC and signaling (O&M) staff shall consult with Signaling System Controller about the fault and possibility of its rectification.
PPIO/RSC, signaling (O&M) staff/Signaling controller shall analyze the fault and decide whether the train can be introduced to MKPR/IPE Platform / platform connected to siding in UTO/ Non-UTO mode and shall convey to DCC/ACC accordingly.
If  the  train  is  to  be  inducted  in  UTO  mode,  then  procedure  as  per para 5. C (V) to  be followed.
If induction is in Non-UTO mode, then TC/DCC shall instruct RA to board the train and take charge. In order to board the RA on train, DCC and RA shall follow Annexure-4 of this procedure. Afterwards existing procedure shall be followed. Train ID and time of induction to be decided by TC/OCC.
On mainline, as per procedure in vogue, TC shall instruct RA to AUX-ON and then AUXOFF the train from the rear end cab side. After normal AUX-ON and AUX-OFF from rear end side, RA shall give AUX-ON command from leading end cab. ON successful AUX-ON, train may be inducted in ATP/ATO mode otherwise Hot Standby train shall be inducted as per Annexure-3.
## 7. In case, UTO train abruptly stops in between movement from MKPR/IPE Platform to SBL or vice versa:

## 7. In case, UTO train abruptly stops in between movement from MKPR/IPE Platform to SBL or vice versa:

TC/DCC (as per jurisdiction) shall instruct nearest available RA to board the train. Before authorizing RA to access the train, TC/DCC (as per jurisdiction) shall ensure suitable block commands are enforced on occupied and adjacent track section.
RA further move the train as per procedure in vogue.
In  this  case,  TC/DCC  shall  ensure  that  train  movement  is  carried  out  from  other available/unaffected route of MKPR/IPE to SBL/other area of MKPD/VND Depot and vice versa.
## 8. PROCEDURE ORDER ON THE FITNESS OF TRAINS FOR UTO: -

## 8. PROCEDURE ORDER ON THE FITNESS OF TRAINS FOR UTO: -

Depot signalling staff shall submit the UTO fitness of Trains to the PPIO for 168 hour/daily basis in the format attached as Annexure- 7.1.

## Introduction

Depot Telecom staff shall submit the UTO fitness of Trains to the PPIO for 168 hour/daily basis in the format attached as Annexure-7.2.

## Introduction

The  PPIO  shall  endorse  the  UTO  fitness  on  The  Train  Fitness  certificate  in  the  format attached as Annexure-7.3 to the Depot Controller and RSC/MB-2, at least 75 minutes prior to Departure of the Pilot Train.
On receipt of UTO fitness of trains from PPIO, RSC shall submit compiled Train Fitness certificate ie including fitness details of trains that are stabled on main line to the TC/OCC.
The Depot Controller/TC-OCC shall confirm the validity of the UTO Fitness of the Trains from the signed fitness certificate submitted by PPIO to DCC and RSC/MB-2 to ACC/CHC-OCC.
The Depot Controller shall hand over the Keys as applicable and Tetra Set to the nominated Train Operator/Roving Attendant (in case of UTO Operation with RA/ETO on board).
In case Train is planned in UTO Mode of operation with RA/ETO on main line, RA/ETO shall board  the  train  in  IPE/MKPR  before  revenue  operation  and  the  train  shall  continue  its trip/journey in UTO mode on Main line.
## 9. INDUCTION OF TRAIN FROM SIDING: -

## 9. INDUCTION OF TRAIN FROM SIDING: -

RSC shall confirm the UTO fitness of the stabled train to TC well in advance as mentioned in para 8.
RA shall board outstation stabled train as per SC-27C well in advance before.
Train wake up process as per Para 5 and Para 6 shall be monitored by TC, RSC and SGC.
ATS shall assign Service ID automatically as per timetable to Train set numbers for that service day 60 minutes before the scheduled mainline departure time.
Induction of trains from siding(s) (where UST functionality is available) on main line to the first station shall be in UTO mode.
Note: Wherever UST facility is not available, Train induction from siding to mainline shall in ATP/available mode. UST shall be done at platform.
## 10. Procedure for movement of train from Mainline to IBL/ IHCS/ WBL/PWL:

## 10. Procedure for movement of train from Mainline to IBL/ IHCS/ WBL/PWL:

After completion of last trip, the train destined for depot will stop at MKPR/IPE platform. RA/SHUNTER shall follow the steps 3.iii, 3.iv and 3.vi and TC shall follow step 3.ii, 3.iv, 3.v and 3.vii of this procedure.
TC shall ask the DCC to set the route from the depot entry signal till the outside signal of that  respective location of Inspection Bay Line (IBL)/ Workshop Bay line (WBL)/Internal Heavy Cleaning Shed (IHCS)/Pit Wheel Lathe (PWL).
If timetable is set till depot then Route from MKPR/IPE platform will be triggered in timetable else TC shall manually set the route for UTO from MKPR/IPE platform to depot entry signal.
For  train  to  be  stabled  inside  IBL/IHCS  and  outside  WBL/PWL,  DCC  shall  send  the RA/SHUNTER to that location in advance; in case RA/SHUNTER is not on board.
After train stops outside IBL/IHCS, RA/SHUNTER shall board the train and shall move as per the procedure in vogue.
For trains to be stabled outside WBL/PWL RA/SHUNTER shall board the train and stable the train manually as per procedure in vogue.
## 11. Procedure for movement of train from IBL (inside)/ IHCS (inside)/ WBL (Outside)/ PWL (Outside) to Mainline:

## 11. Procedure for movement of train from IBL (inside)/ IHCS (inside)/ WBL (Outside)/ PWL (Outside) to Mainline:

11.1 PPIO shall ensure fitness test for UTO have been carried out for trains.
11.2
(i) For  trains  inside  IBL  of  MKPD  and  VND,  IHCS  inside  of  VND,  DCC  shall  instruct

## Introduction

RA/SHUNTER to board the train and move the mode selector to FWD/ROS mode (as per availability)  and  move  the  train  till  ATC  begins  as  per  the  procedure  in  vogue.  After stabling of train outside WBL/PWL/IBL and outside IHCS of VND, RA/SHUNTER shall shift  Mode Selector (MS) to AUTO position of both the cabs, and UTO mode shall be selected by pressing UTO soft button and remove the Mascon key.

## Introduction

Note :  In  MKPD,  UST  facility  is  not  available  outside  WBL-1,  WBL-2  &  WBL-5.  For induction of trains from these locations RA/SHUNTER shall move the train to UST enabled location as per instructions of DCC.
(ii) RA shall verify that UTO mode 'UTO' symbol appearing on the DMI and shall inform DCC accordingly. The following symbol appears on DMI.
(iii) For trains stabled outside WBL/PWL/IBL and inside IHCS of MKPD and outside IHCS of VND, DCC shall assign the priority to trains 75 min before schedule main line departure.
11.3 DCC shall give manual remote Sleep Mode On command to set the train to sleep.
11.4 Further scheduled departure will be as per Para 5, 6 and 7.

## Introduction

Annexure: - 1
## Part-A:- Procedure to be followed by EPIC for maintenance/cleaning of Train/Track/Other installations /other infrastructures at SBL.

Any maintenance activity on Train/Track/Other installations/other infrastructures at SBL must be carried out with the permission of DCC.
For maintenance/cleaning work on train, permission shall be given under exchange of Private number between PPIO and DCC. For other works PTW shall be issued by DCC.
Before permitting any work as defined in Sl. No 1 above, DCC shall apply 'Signal Block/Maintenance block on that stabling location from ATS MMI.
DCC shall instruct the Points Man to operate/remove the SPK, and allow the maintenance person to enter the zone as mentioned in PTW.
5)
For any work on the train, if the UTO mode has to be removed, RSC/PPIO/DCC shall be advised accordingly.
Once the train is stabled in SBL, Safety Cutout switch (SCS) should not be operated by any staff. If need arises then after SCS is normalized train shall be moved from its location to Shunting Neck and back to its stabling location.
After completion of work, EPIC shall ensure the train is in UTO mode and No EB is applied in train and if required shall ensure that Mode Selector (MS) is in AUTO position of both the cabs, and UTO mode is selected. EPIC shall verify that UTO mode 'UTO' symbol appearing on the DMI and shall inform PPIO accordingly.
If required, PPIO shall inform DCC to issue remote sleep on command as per steps defined in Para 3.(x) .
DCC shall also confirm the train is in Sleep mode as defined in Para 3.(ix) .

If required, PPIO shall inform DCC to issue remote sleep on command as per steps defined in Para 3.(x) .
DCC shall also confirm the train is in Sleep mode as defined in Para 3.(ix) .
After completion of maintenance/cleaning work on train or maintenance  activity on Train/Track/Other installations/infrastructures  and  clearing  the  site,  EPIC  shall  inform  DCC about the completion of work.
After completion of train related work and clearing the site, EPIC who has taken the Job Card from PPIO, shall close the Job Card and declare that Site has been cleared to PPIO.
After completion of train related work and clearing the site, PPIO shall inform DCC that work has been completed and site has been cleared of men & material under exchange of Private number.
For other works, concerned EPIC shall cancel the PTW at DCC.
Only after cancellation of all PTWs/permissions (if given), DCC  shall Unblock all signals/remove maintenance block and instruct the authorized Points Man to normalize/reinsert the SPK.
