## Annexure:- 2
## Procedure to prepare the hot standby Train in UTO mode

## Procedure to prepare the hot standby Train in UTO mode

PPIO  in  consultation  with  DCC  shall  nominate  preferably  last  two  scheduled  trains  as  hot standby. Same shall be communicated to TC well in advance after preparing and stabling them for UTO movement.

## Procedure to prepare the hot standby Train in UTO mode

TC/DCC shall give the remote Sleep Mode Off command from the ATS MMI.
After execution of wakeup process, TC/DCC shall confirm Departure test status 'Finished and Passed'.
TC/DCC shall inform RSC/PPIO about the same.
TC/DCC shall give Dozing mode set command. The same shall be reset by TC/DCC before inducting that train to main line.
RSC shall verify that train is in Dozing state (i.e., in dozing mode HVAC, saloon light, etc. will be turned off in order to save energy) from RSC controller workstation and confirm the same to TC.
In case of departure test failure of train to be inducted in UTO for revenue service, TC/DC shall assign service ID to Hot Standby train.
If standby train is not inducted then RSC/PPIO and TC/DCC shall consult one another and set the train to sleep mode.
Annexure: - 3

## 1. INTRODUCTION

Main purpose of SPKS (staff protection key switch) in depot is to ensure safety of staff during movement of Trains on IBL /WBL/SBLs. SPKS are installed at entry/exit point of each IBL/WBL and SBL. Each & every IBL/WBL has dedicated SPKS, however on SBLs one SPKS may be mapped with one SBL or group of SBLs.

## 1. INTRODUCTION

Details of SPKS are mentioned in the attached Annexure 5 and Annexure 6 .
## 2. SPKS Operating Procedure:
## 2.1 For Maintenance work: -
## a. SPKS Activation/ ON procedure :

## a. SPKS Activation/ ON procedure :

Maintenance Staff, who needs to access track section shall approach DCC for track access request.
On receiving of such access request, DCC shall consult PPIO and permit the track access, as per procedure in vogue.
DCC shall also provide concerned SPKS Box Key(s) to the EPIC to operate concerned SPKS.
The EPIC shall get the SPKS box key(s) issued from DCC for the required track and approach to the SPKS Location.
After reaching at site EPIC shall seek permission from DCC for operation of SPKS clearly mentioning SPKS No. in group mode.
DCC shall confirm concerned area assigned with SPKS to be operated and permit the operation of SPKS and opening of specified Track access door under exchange of private number on group mode.
The EPIC shall unlock the SPKS box located near the door of Specified track.
The EPIC shall rotate the SPKS key already available inside SPKS box from OFF Position to ON position (rotate the key to position 'O' which is marked on the key switch Actuator)  and  wait  for  LED  to  glow  Red  (indicating  SPKS  activation).  Indication  of SPKS activation shall also be visible at DCC ATS MMI.
The EPIC shall take out the SPKS key from the SPKS box, secure it, lock the SPKS box and keep the box key in his custody and unlock Track access Door with the keys attached with SPKS key.
The EPIC should keep the SPKS Box key, SPKS Key, Track Access door key in his custody till the requirement of track Access is over.
## b. SPKS Deactivation/ OFF Procedure:

## b. SPKS Deactivation/ OFF Procedure:

After  completion  of  maintenance  work,  the  EPIC  shall  inform  the  DCC  about completion of work clearance of the track section clearly mentioning all men and material is removed from area of Engineer's Possession, under exchange of private number.
After getting confirmation about clearance of track section, DCC shall instruct EPIC to lock the track access door, unlock SPKS box and put the SPKS key back into the SPKS and twist it to OFF position (twist the key to "1" position which is marked on the key switch actuator).
LED at SPKS box will go blank (back to normal condition) and SPKS status become normal at DCC ATS MMI.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 27 A (Rev. - 06)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR STABLING OF TRAINS AT OUTSTATIONS/DEPOT DURING NONREVENUE (NIGHT) HOURS

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order details the responsibilities of the concerned Metro Staff and the Methodology to be followed for Stabling of Trains at Outstations/Depots in such a manner so that Trains remain Clean, Secure and Fit for Revenue Services overnight.

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order is applicable to all the Staff related to Stabling of Trains at Outstations/Depots during Non-revenue Hours (Night).

3.1 All the Trains, which are offered for Revenue Services shall be issued train and ATP/ATO/UTO Fitness for 72 Hrs and 168 Hrs for L-7&8 shall be stabled at Outstations/on stabling lines inside Depots.
3.2 Electrical Department shall provide Lightings in the Sidings/SBLs. OCC/DCC shall also advise the concerned Department to switch 'ON' the Lights for the Safe Movement of Train Operator during Dark Hours/in Tunnel.
3.3 After  Completion  of  Revenue  Service,  the  Train  Operator  shall  stable  the  Train  as  per  extant Procedure at the designated Siding/Platform/SBL as per time table.
3.4 The Train Operator shall then go to the SCR/DCC, as per extant Procedure.
3.5 Sign-on/Sign-off Register and Breath Analyzer Equipment for Train Operators shall be kept with the on duty SC/DC of the designated Station/DCC.
3.6 The  Train  Operator  shall  submit  the  Log  Book,  Cab  Door  Key,  Square  Key,  PSL  Key  (where applicable), Tetra Set, and Mascon Key to the SC/DC of that Station/DCC and sign-off, as per Procedure.
3.7 The Possession of Hand Portable Tetra Set of Stabled Trains shall be with Station Controller/Depot Controller and he/she shall ensure Working Condition/Charging of Tetra Set. If Tetra Set of Train is faulty, it shall be replaced by SC/DC as per existing practice.

3.7 The Possession of Hand Portable Tetra Set of Stabled Trains shall be with Station Controller/Depot Controller and he/she shall ensure Working Condition/Charging of Tetra Set. If Tetra Set of Train is faulty, it shall be replaced by SC/DC as per existing practice.
3.8 On Duty SC/PPIO shall open the Train Door for entry of Cleaning Staff and will ensure that the Train is cleaned only from inside, in the night. No Roof Cleaning shall be done. After cleaning of the Train, SC/PPIO will lock the Train and inform the same to OCC/DCC.
3.9 A Security Guard shall be deployed at the Siding/Stabling area to ensure the Safety of the Stabled Train in Siding/ Stabling area by the Security Department. Chief Controller/OCC shall inform the same to the Security Controller at OCC.
3.10 The Mascon Key shall be kept in the Custody of concerned SC/DCC/PPIO and Movement of the same shall be recorded in the Key Register.

## Introduction

3.11 The Train Operator booked by Crew Control to take Charge of the Out-stationed/Depot stabled Train shall Sign-on at the SCR/DCC, as per the extant Procedure and read the Notice Board for Train Operator. TO will collect Mascon Key, /Cab Door Key, PSL Key (where applicable), Tetra Set, Square Key and Train Log Book from the SC /DC and shall go to the Stabled Train as per Procedure in vogue. The Train Operator shall check the Fitness of the Train in the previous Page of the Log Book and if Fitness is valid till date shall endorse the same on the next Page as per SC35. If the Fitness is not valid, TO shall not take Charge of the Train, inform the TC/OCC/DC and wait for further Instructions in the SCR/DCC.

## Introduction

3.12 TO shall conduct the Pre-departure Checks, as per the Procedure in vogue. TO shall inform the OCC/DCC/SCR, if Train is ready for departure. OCC/SC/DCC will then set the desired Route for Revenue Service of the Train.
3.13 Any  deficiency or failure noticed during the Pre-departure  Checks  shall be  reported to OCC/DCC/PPIO immediately  and  noted  down  in  the  Train  Log  Book.  TO  shall  ensure  Verbal Authorization  from  OCC/DCC  on  Train  Radio,  before  the  departure  of  the  Train  from  Stabled Location/SBL.
3.14 All trains being stabled on Outstation/SBLs and not due for 72 hrs or 168hrs (on Line-7&8) check, will always be in locked condition other than the time period required for internal cleaning/minor corrective maintenance.
3.15 Civil  Engineering  Department  shall  ensure  that  the Track  Area/Siding/Stabling  Area  is  Safe for Walking.
3.16 If the Train is designated for Piloting, as per Timetable, that shall be done as per extant Procedure.
## 3.17  FOR STABLING OF TRAINS AT OUTSTATIONS

(i) PPIO, in consultation with DC shall plan the Operational ID No. to the Trains to be stabled at Outstations according to the Train Timetable.
(ii) OCC shall assign the Operational ID Nos. to Out-station stabled Trains in such a way that the Trains return to the Depot before the expiry of Fitness.
(iii) The Locations for Stabling Train (s) at Outstations shall be approved by a Committee comprising of HODs of Operation, Civil, RS, E&M, Traction, S&T and Security. In case Location for Stabling of  Train  changes,  OCC  shall  ensure  that  both  the  Sidings/Platforms  are  not  occupied simultaneously. Space should be available for Reversal/Movement of Vehicles.
(iv) In case of any deviation from the Timetable regarding Stabling of the Train at Outstation, OCC shall inform the same to Crew Control in advance and to the Train Operator under the Exchange of Private Numbers.
(v) Station Manager of the concerned station shall maintain the training details of the Supervisor of Cleaning Staff. S/He shall ensure that no Supervisor of Cleaning Staff to be deployed for cleaning of  the  train  without  valid  competency  certificate.  S/He  shall  coordinate  with  the  concerned Manager  or  AM/RS  for  the  competency  certificate  of  the  Supervisor  of  Cleaning  Staff.  The Supervisor of Cleaning Staff must be trained & certified for 3 Months by the respective Manager or AM/RS for ensuring Safety during the Cleaning of Train. No Water Jet & Telescopic Rod shall be used during Cleaning. Only Dry Mopping would be done inside the Trains.

(vi) The SM/SC of the Station, where Train is stabled during night shall be advised the Departure Time  of  the  Train  and  Sign-on/Arrival  Time  of  Train  Operator  by  OCC  and  Crew  Control respectively,  who  will  accordingly  facilitate  the  Opening  of  Station  Entry  Gate  for  the  Train Operator.

## Introduction

(vii) The SC/SM shall be responsible to up-date the Notice Board for the Train Operator and CDI of the concerned Crew Control shall be the Nodal Agency to get the Notice Board updated.

## Introduction

Note: Locations for outstation stabling of Trains are attached as 'Annexure B'.
## 3.18  FOR TRAIN STABLING IN DEPOTS

## 3.18  FOR TRAIN STABLING IN DEPOTS

(i) Train should be cleaned inside and from outside on daily basis as per schedule.
(ii) No Daily Check will be carried out (other than daily train cleaning) on the trains stabled on depot SBLs.
(iii) The need of any minor corrective maintenance on the train will  be  evaluated  based  on TOs' remarks in the defect book/faults recorded in the TIMS/TCMS. In case any corrective maintenance needs to be carried out, it will be carried out strictly as per Job Card & SIC (Safety independent check sheet) procedures. Additionally the testing of the corrective maintenance related work will be the responsibility of PPIO.
## 3.19  ADDITIONAL STEPS FOR TRAIN STABLING IN UTO ENABLED LINES

(i) All the trains which are offered for revenue services and shall be stabled at Outstations/on stabling lines inside depot, shall be issued train and UTO fitness for 168 Hrs .
(ii) At last revenue platform, TO/RA/ETO shall ensure that all passengers have de-boarded the train. Thereafter, TO/RA/ETO shall de-board the train and inform TC/OCC. After that TO/RA/ETO shall go to SCR to Sign OFF as per extant procedure.
(iii) After completion of revenue services as per timetable, TC/OCC and DCC will set the route of train for  designated  siding/platform/stabling  lines  inside  depot  (as  applicable)  where  train  is  to  be stabled in non-revenue hours.
(iv) After stabling the train in siding/platform/depot, TC/OCC or DCC (as applicable) shall give remote sleep command to the train and shall confirm the sleep status of train from ATS workstation.
(v) If TO/RA/ETO is stabling the train in siding/depot then TO/RA/ETO should confirm from TC/OCC or  DCC  (as  applicable)  regarding  train  mode  and  position  of  the  mode  selector  of  both cab.TO/RA/ETO  will  leave  the  train  in  AUX  OFF  /  SLEEP  condition  as  per  instruction  from OCC/DCC.

(vi) Whenever train has to be cleaned from inside, on-duty SC/PPIO shall take permission of TC/OCC or  DCC (as applicable) before permitting  housekeeping staff.TC/OCC or DCC (as applicable) shall block all possible routes and apply maintenance block and stop train from available ATS commands, before permitting concerned SC/PPIO and housekeeping staff to access the track for boarding the train.  In  depots,  Staff  Protection  key  is  available  and  extant  procedure  shall  be followed.
(vii) SC/PPIO shall switch on/off the saloon light of the train for cleaning of the train by operating ILS (Interior light switch) button in the ECM (End cubical module) cubicle in each DM car. Location photograph and details are attached as Annexure 'A'.
(viii) After cleaning of train, on duty SC/PPIO and TC/OCC or DCC (as applicable) to ensure train is in UTO mode. On-duty SC/PPIO to consult TC/OCC or DCC (as applicable) before moving mode Selector of the train for any reason. After cleaning of the train has been done, TC/OCC or DCC (as applicable) shall confirm blocking of all possible routes and apply maintenance block and stop train from available ATS commands before permitting the housekeeping staff and SC/PPIO to access the track to return back to station/depot. In depots, Staff Protection key is available and extant procedure shall be followed.

## Introduction

(ix) On-duty SC/PPIO shall confirm to TC/OCC or DCC (as applicable) that all housekeeping staff deployed for train cleaning has returned back to station platform/depot and also that all Men, Materials, Equipment's, Tools & Plants have been removed from the work place (Train & Track).

## Introduction

(x) TO/RA/ETO shall Sign ON at SCR/DCC as per extant procedure. TO/RA/ETO shall take charge of  train  at  first  revenue  platform  as  per  schedule  timetable  and  inform  TC/OCC  or  DCC  (as applicable). Train hold shall be applied by TC/OCC at platform where RA has to take charge of the train. Only after getting confirmation that, TO/RA/ETO has boarded the train TC/OCC shall remove the platform hold or release the train.

## B.  Revised Para-4.2:

## B.  Revised Para-4.2:

At  present,  there  are  four  TETRA  networks  operational  in  DMRC.  Each  one  serves specific or group of Lines. Phase-II radio network covers Line-2, Line-3, Line-4 & Line-5. Phase-III radio network covers line-6 & Line-8. Phase-IV radio network covers Line-1, Line-7 and Line-9 and last one (AEL radio network) is designated for Airport Express Line.
The Rescue and Relief talk group used in Phase-II & Phase-III radio network is named R&R. In order to have a seamless communication between both networks R&R talk group during emergency, the relevant Rescue and Relief talk group is patched for both radio networks of Phase-II & Phase-III i.e. communication in R&R is common for Lines -2, 3, 4, 5, 6 & 8
The Rescue and Relief talk group used in Phase-IV radio network is also named as R&R, but this group is not patched with other radio networks i.e. Phase-II & Phase-III. Hence

## Introduction

communication between R&R group of Phase-IV and R&R of other radio networks is not possible. For Airport Line no R&R talk group is available.

## Introduction

In  Phase-II,  Phase-III  and  Phase-IV  radio  network,  Concerned Chief Controller /OCC shall decide either Concern Operation talk group or R&R talk group shall be used by OCC,  Train  Operation,  Station  and  Emergency  response  staff  during  Passenger Evacuation,  Rescue  of  defective  train  or  any  unusual/emergent  occurrence.  Chief Controller /OCC shall arrange to advise all concerned to select decided talk group on Radio/Train Radio/Tetra handset for further communication.
In  Phase-II, Phase-III and Phase-IV radio network, during Emergency Detrainment of Passengers from Mid Tunnel Shaft, the Train operator and station controller involved in detrainment  will  communicate  with  their  traffic  controllers  in  Concern  Operation  talk group/ R&R talk groups. For Airport Line, during Emergency Detrainment of Passengers from Mid Tunnel Shaft, the Train operator and station controller will communicate with their traffic controllers in Operation talk groups.
In  case  of  no  Service  or  Hanging  of  Train  Radio,  Train  Operators  shall  reset  the appropriate MCB as per the respective OTM of concerned RS for immediate restoration. In  case  the  Problem  persists,  Train  Operator  shall  convey  it  to  respective  TC  for information of Telecom controller through any SCR/PSB or any other means.

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION

1.1 This procedure shall apply to all communicating on mainline and depot Talk Groups on radio channel including the Communication required to be made to meet the Emergent Situations.

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION

1.2 This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules, 2022, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
1.3 For UTO Mode of Train Operation: wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/ Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO).

## 2.0  SCOPE

This procedure is applicable to all Lines. The purpose of this procedure order is to provide specific & separate talk group for each line or section and depot to ensure smooth train operation as well as station management. This also ensures that message is passed concisely & clearly and that hearing as well as understanding is established between the intending parties.

## 3.0  GENERAL

3.1 The Concerned staff shall use the Radio system for only professional conversation to avoid Radio congestion.
3.2 The concerned staff shall use only the dedicated talk group for communication as mentioned in a table below for communication with the train.
3.3 The census of all Train Radios, Zetron and Portable sets shall be carried out on quarterly basis by the concerned department and status report shall be sent to Telecom department.

## 4.2  General Instructions Regarding Train Radio Talk Groups:

## 4.2  General Instructions Regarding Train Radio Talk Groups:

(i) At present there are three TETRA networks. One network (phase-II radio network) pertains to Line-2,  Line-3,  Line-4  and  Line-5  working,  and  second  network  (phase-III  radio  network) pertains  to  Line-1,  Line-6,  Line-7,  Line-8  and  Line-9  working  and  third  network  pertain  to Airport line radio network.

(ii)  The Rescue and Relief talk group used in Line-1 to Line-9 is named R&R. In order to have a seamless  communication  between  both  networks  R&R  talk  group  during  emergency,  the relevant Rescue and Relief talk group is patched for both radio networks of Ph-II and Ph-III i.e. communication in R&R is common for Lines, from Line-1 to Line-9.
NOTE: For Airport Line no R&R talk group is available.
(iii) In Phase-II and Phase-III radio network, Concerned Chief Controller /OCC shall decide either Concern Operation talk group or R&R talk group shall be used by OCC, Train Operation, Station  and  Emergency response staff during  Passenger Evacuation,  Rescue  of  defective train or any unusual/emergent occurrence. Chief Controller /OCC shall arrange to advise all concerned  to  select  decided  talk  group  on  Radio/Train  Radio/Tetra  handset  for  further communication.
(iv) In Phase-II and Phase-III radio network, during Emergency Detrainment of Passengers from Mid  Tunnel  Shaft,  the  Train  operator  and  station  controller  involved  in  detrainment  will communicate with their traffic controllers in Concern Operation talk group/ R&R talk groups. For Airport Line, during Emergency Detrainment of Passengers from Mid Tunnel Shaft, the Train operator and station controller will communicate with their traffic controllers in Operation talk groups.

(v)  In case of no Service or Hanging of Train Radio, Train Operators shall reset the appropriate MCB as per the respective  OTM  of  concerned RS for  immediate  restoration.  In  case  the Problem persists, Train Operator shall convey it to respective TC for information of Telecom controller through any SCR/PSB or any other means.

## 5.1 Initiation of Conversation

## 8.0  USE OF EMERGENCY BUTTON

## 8.0  USE OF EMERGENCY BUTTON

8.1 The emergency button is a feature attached with all radio equipments and used to activate the emergency mode in any particular talk group. In emergency situations, there is an urgent need to initiate conversation by the user but the user may not be able to transmit due to the following two reasons.
(i) Another user with same or higher priority may already transmitting in the Talk Group.
(ii)  All the channels are already in use at the affiliated site.
In such situation, the user has an option of using emergency call /mode.  As soon as the user switches to emergency mode by pressing emergency button, the same/higher priority call will be preempted and user will get the permission to transmit. If all the channels are busy, one of the calls will be preempted and freed channel will be allocated to the user.

## Introduction

8.2 During the emergency mode, following scenario occurs.

(i) When the user switches to emergency mode (known as initiated user), if the user does not press the PTT button, the emergency mike of user's equipment is automatically activated and transmitting the surrounding voice for the predefined time of 300 seconds without pressing the PTT button and Talk Group (TG) remains engaged for the communication of the initiated user. (If PTT button is pressed by initiated user, the emergency mike is immediately turned off and TG is released to be used by other user with priority assigned to the initiated user).
(ii)  After  300  seconds  (5  minutes),  the  emergency  mike  is  turned  off  and  TG  is  free  for communication to other user. Now other user of that TG can communicate with each other by pressing PTT button on their equipments.
(iii) During the course of communication in TG by other user, if this initiated user again press the PTT, all other communication will get suspended in that TG and transmission priority is again restored to the initiated user. Now initiated user can communicate with all other users of that TG with high emergency transmission priority.
(iv) This process continues till the initiated user ends the emergency mode on his/her equipment.
(v)  Emergency mode on all lines may be turned off:
From RCW (Radio Control Workstation) at OCC; or
By switching 'OFF & ON' of particular RCH (Radio Control Head) or Portable Radio Handset; or
By pressing right soft key on RCH or portable Radio Handset, end call first then again long press the same key to exit from emergency mode.

By switching 'OFF & ON' of particular RCH (Radio Control Head) or Portable Radio Handset; or
By pressing right soft key on RCH or portable Radio Handset, end call first then again long press the same key to exit from emergency mode.
(vi) Some TETRA sets have been provided at designated locations (as mentioned in table under para 7.4) for use during emergency. These TETRA sets also have a NSG talk group meant for use in emergency, so as not to disturb communication in all other operation talk groups while passing any message of emergent nature.
## 9.0  COMMUNICATION FAILURE

If TO perceives that communication is not taking place with Train Radio, hand portable radio set should be used. In case communication could not be established between TO and TC even then, TO  shall  select  DMO*  mode  preferably  on  hand  portable  radio  and  shall  communicate  with nearest Station Controller to pass on the message to OCC. If TC observes that a train is standing at a location for more than a minute and communication could not be established with the TO, then he/she shall inform SC of nearest stations of stalled train to select the DMO* mode preferably on  hand  portable  for  communication  with  the  TO.  After  completion  of  conversation  both  the parties will resume to trunk mode on their hand portable.
In the case of extreme emergency and in rarest of rare circumstances,
If  communication cannot be established between SC & TO even on DMO Mode then, TO shall try to communicate with OCC by Mobile Phone of any passenger.
If  communication  cannot  be  established  between  SC  and  OCC  then  SC  shall  try  to communicate with OCC by Shift Mobile Phone.
TO/SC can also use intercom phones available at PSB/Emergency Panel to communicate with OCC.
In  underground  section,  TO  shall  communicate  with  TC  using  Emergency  Telephone  placed along the Tunnel/ Platform Ends. These Emergency telephones is configured as a Hotline, which means when Handset is picked, it will place a call  to respective  Traffic Controller, and  if  TC doesn't answer that call; the call will automatically be transferred to the TPC.
*DMO mode shall be applicable for open sections and not for Underground Section.

*DMO mode shall be applicable for open sections and not for Underground Section.
Note: Whenever Private Number is exchanged by any other means as defined above in case of communication failure, both the parties shall mention the means by which the private number has been exchanged in their private number books.

## 10.0  SAFETY COMMUNICATION

All  communication  between  Operations  Control  Centre  and  Train  Roving  Attendant,  Station Controller, Depot Controller, maintenance staff of electrical, rolling stock, signal and telecommunication and track structures department and other pertaining to movement of trains shall be recorded with time stamping, and preserved for incident analysis and training. All types of  communication  in  all  talk  group/all  modes  on  all  train  radio/portable  hand  radio  shall  be automatically recorded and saved except communication in Direct Mode of Operation (DMO). ## 11.0  FOR UTO MODE OF OPERATION ON LINE- 7 & 8

Train Radio is available in both cab of RS-10 trains. Both Train radio are redundant to each other in case of failure.
## 11.1  Following May be the Train Radio Failure Scenarios

## 11.1  Following May be the Train Radio Failure Scenarios

(a)  Current  status  of  train  radio  (active/inactive)  is  available  on  Train monitoring  and  Tracking panel  on  RCW  (Radio  Control  Workstation).  If  any  train  radio  fails,  then 'Active  Radio off/Inactive Radio off' status will be displayed under train status on Train Monitoring and tracking panel and respective controllers of OCC. An audio-visual alarm will be generated and displayed on the respective TC/CHC/IC Radio Control Workstation under Alarm panel .
(b)  In case of failure of both Train Radio, affiliated Talk group status of that train will show blank under Train Monitoring and tracking panel.
## 11.2  Procedure to be followed in case of Train Radio failure in UTO mode

(a)  In case of failure of one train radio no action is required, train may be continued in UTO mode. During failure of any one train radio,  anyone functionality will be  available  at  a time  either Passenger emergency communication or live/pre-recorded announcement by TC/CHC or Live announcement by RA /ETO in train.
(b)  In  case  of  failure  of  both  train  radio,  Passenger  emergency  communication,  and  live/prerecorded announcement by TC/CHC and live announcement by RA/TO/ETO in train shall not be possible and on Passenger emergency communication call activation, CCTV view of that particular camera (associated to the PAD button) will not pop-up at CCTV Workstation at OCC. Train shall be run in UTO mode up to the next station. TC/OCC shall arrange RA/TO/ETO to change  train  mode  to  ATO/ATP  non-UTO  mode  so  that  emergency  calls  initiated  by  the passenger shall be available to RA/TO/ETO through Rolling Stock System. RA/TO/ETO shall communicate the TC/OCC through the Hand portable Radio.
(c)  TO/RA/ETO shall work the train till train radio failure is rectified as per OCC instruction.
(d)  If remote troubleshooting could not rectify the train radio fault, then telecom staff shall be sent to train.
(e)  If both train radio failure could not be rectified then OCC shall take decision to run the train in non UTO mode or withdraw the train in consultation with Telecom Controller as per feasibility, proximity to terminal station, depot, siding etc.

## JOINT PROCEDURE ORDER FOR OPERATION DURING EARTHQUAKE

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order deals with the event of earthquake and specifies the precautions and care to be taken by all the concerned Staff.

## 2.0  SCOPE

This procedure is applicable to all lines of DMRC. This procedure shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and its amendments, Safety Circulars and special Instructions in vogue.
For UTO Mode of Train Operation: Wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/Emergency Train Operator (ETO).
## 3.0  REPORTING / DETECTION OF OCCURRENCE OF EARTHQUAKE:

## 3.0  REPORTING / DETECTION OF OCCURRENCE OF EARTHQUAKE:

The reporting /detection of earthquake to Operation Control Centre (OCC) at Metro Bhawan can be through any of the following means: -
3.1 DMRC has installed an earthquake warning system (EQWS) through CSIO-CSIR to detect the  earthquake  in  NCR  region. The  EQWS  system  has  Central  Control  Unit  (CCU) installed in OCC/MB with Auxiliary System Controller (ASC)/Line-6 /MB-I. The above CCU will generate only visual or both visual & audio alarm depending upon severity of Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA) value detected as per limit/range specified in table below: -

### 3.0  REPORTING / DETECTION OF OCCURRENCE OF EARTHQUAKE:

|   S. No. | PGA Value   | Earthquake severity   | Alarms              | Action required                                          |
|----------|-------------|-----------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
|        1 | 0.0-0.039   | Low                   | Only Visual         | No action required                                       |
|        2 | 0.039-0.18  | Moderate              | Both Visual & Audio | As mentioned in subsequent Para of this procedure order. |
|        3 | Above 0.18  | Strong                | Both Visual & Audio | As mentioned in subsequent Para of this procedure order. |

## 3.0  REPORTING / DETECTION OF OCCURRENCE OF EARTHQUAKE:

Note; 1) Five sensors for EQWS has been installed at following locations: -
(i) Metro Bhawan (MB) Basement-II
(ii) Mundka RSS (MUDK) -Line-5
(iii)  Sushant Lok RSS (STLK) -Line-2
(iv)  Botanical Garden RSS (BCGN) -Line-3
(v) Faridabad Sec-46 RSS -Line-6
Maintenance and calibration schedule of Earthquake Warning System (EQWS) is detailed at Annexure-A.
3.2 On generation of alarm, only visual or both visual & audio by EQWS indicating the detection of occurrence of earthquake, ASC/Line-6/ MB-I shall immediately ascertain the intensity (low, moderate or high) of earthquake from PGA value detected by EQWS and then communicate the PGA value and the corresponding intensity verbally to CHC/MB-I for taking further actions as per the procedure order.
3.3 After having communicated verbally, ASC/ Line-6/ MB-I shall then also confirm in writing to CHC/MB-I the above verbal communications made to CHC/ MB-I clearly mentioning the time details of detection of event by EQWS. First verbal communication made with CHC/ MB-I and the written communication now is sent to CHC/MB-I.

## Introduction

3.4 Any staff/official of DMRC who comes to know about earthquake in Delhi & NCR region, shall immediately  inform  about  the  same  to  OCC.  If  there  is  any  ambiguity  between  reading displayed by EQWS (due to malfunctioning or damage) and from other reporting source of earthquake  or  self-observation  of  any  staff,  CHC/OCC/MB/I  shall  try  to  contact  DDMA (District Disaster Management Authority) or NDRF (National Disaster Response Force) or GSI (Geological Survey of India) or NCS (National Centre for Seismology) or Metrological department to know the severity of earthquake. According to received input, OCC shall take further steps.

## Introduction

3.5 Surprise mock drill shall be conducted on regular interval for preparedness for measures to be taken in case of earthquake
## 4.0  ACTIONS TO BE TAKEN ON DETECTION / REPORTING OF EARTHQUAKE :-

4.1  Earthquake Severity Low: Earthquake severity being detected as low (PGA values being in the range of 0.00 to 0.039) through EQWS system and Earthquake not being reported by any other means (except EQWS) mentioned in Para 3.0, then no action is required to be undertaken by CHC/MB-I.
4.2  Earthquake Severity Moderate: Earthquake severity  being  detected  as  moderate (PGA values being in the range of 0.039 to 0.18) through EQWS system and/or moderate intensity Earthquake being reported by any other means as mentioned in Para 3.0.
(i)  CHC/MB-I, on becoming aware about the occurrence of earthquake under the above mentioned conditions, shall inform the same to CHC/MB-II & CHC/MB-III and concerned officer/official of Electrical, Civil & Track. Each CHC/TC shall also inform to all concerned DCC of their respective lines.
(ii) Each CHC shall advise respective TCs to instruct all trains in respective section to stop immediately.
(iii) During the earthquake, TC shall instruct for announcements at stations and inside the trains.
(iv) After earthquake has subsided, trains at station platforms shall be evacuated.
(v) Trains stopped between stations (tunnel/elevated/at grade section) may proceed to the next platform observing utmost vigilance and caution at maximum speed of 10 KMPH in RM mode and evacuate passengers on the next platform.

In that section, Train movement shall take place only after fitness certificate is received from concern department as mention in para 4.4(x).
(vii)  Normal operation shall be resumed as per the following procedure: -

On being advised by CHC/OCC, respective controllers at OCC shall apprise concerned staff/officers about the procedure being adopted to resume services and arrange staff from different wing to board in cab of first piloting train as per feasibility. ASC/OCC shall instruct to all UG stations to switch on the tunnel lights before movement of first train.
TC/OCC shall ensure that two consecutive empty trains are worked in each section at cautious speed not exceeding 25 kmph in RM mode for the first train and 40 kmph in

SGC shall also alert all concerned to take necessary action with respect to safety and health of signalling system and submit fitness certificate for the same.
He/she shall also inform field  staff and  officers to  be  in  readiness  to  deal  with  any

## Introduction

emergent situation and mobilize resources for rescue and relief work, if necessary.

## Introduction

On receipt of fitness certificate from the concerned regarding S&T equipment, SGC will communicate same to CHC/OCC in writing.
He/she shall coordinate and cooperate with chief controller in crisis management.
## (viii) Duties of Civil Controller

## (viii) Duties of Civil Controller

(a)  Civil Controller shall also inform the supervisor in-charge of P. Way &  Works and all concerned officers to be readiness to deal with any emergent situation and mobilize resources for rescue and relief work if necessary.
(b)  Civil Controller shall instruct supervisor in-charge of P. Way &  Works  to board in cab of first piloting train (if feasible).
(c)  Communicate the receipt of fitness certificate from all concerned P. Way &  Works system to CHC/OCC in writing.
## (ix) Duties of other Controllers at OCC: -

## (ix) Duties of other Controllers at OCC: -

All other controllers e.g. RSC, TMC (Telecom Controller), SI/CISF shall also alert all concerned to take necessary action with respect to safety and health of respective system and submit fitness certificate for the same.
They  shall  also  inform  field  staff  and  officers  to  be  in  readiness  to  deal  with  any emergent situation and mobilize resources for rescue and relief work, if necessary.
They shall coordinate and cooperate with Chief Controller in crisis management.
Rolling Stock Controller shall observe all trains stuck in section due to non- availability of traction power or any other abnormality. RSC will advise CHC to change over the different functions of trains as saloon lights, A.C. etc. in appropriate mode to minimize inconvenience of passengers and to avoid total power drain of trains, as traction power is already cut-off.
Note: The  concerned  department  may  prepare  their  own  methodology  of  carrying inspection & issuance of fitness certificate.
## (x) Resumption of Normal Services: -

## (x) Resumption of Normal Services: -

After the earthquake has been subsided, entire network shall be evacuated. For this purpose, trains stopped in between stations (tunnel/viaduct section) shall be brought to platform. All controllers in OCC shall instruct their on-duty staff to assist SC/SM in rescue and relief work.
Detailed examination of track and structure including OHE/ROCS and other track side equipment's shall be carried out under the co-ordination of TPC.
SGC shall coordinate the examination of S&T equipment's.
After examination of track and structure including OHE/ROCS, S&T equipment's and other track side equipment's, supervisor or above of the concerned department shall submit fitness certificate for respective section / line including sidings that the section / line & sidings is safe for train operation to respective controller of OCC under exchange of private numbers.
After receipt of fitness certificate, TPC & SGC shall communicate the same in writing to TC/CHC/OCC, only after this, normal services shall be resumed in the section which has been declared 'FIT' as per following para (f).
The sections which have been declared 'FIT' for train movement, the train services will be started with speed restriction mentioned in fitness certificate (Wherever applicable)

## Introduction

under  exchange  of  private  number  between  TC  and  TO.  If  no  speed  restriction  is mentioned, or speed mention higher than 25 kmph, even normal services will resume only after piloting by the first empty train with max 25 kmph & second empty train with max 40 kmph in both directions in permitted sections.

## Introduction

Fitness certificate of Depot including transfer track may be submitted to either DCC or concern Controller in OCC. TC/OCC and DCC will exchange the fitness of area under exchange of private number.
All  controllers  in  OCC  shall  obtain  serviceability  status  of  all  other  secondary infrastructure and equipment of DMRC such as AFC, lift, escalators, ASS, RSS, SER, TER, firefighting equipment etc.
## 5.0  FOR UTO MODE OF TRAIN OPERATION ON LINE - 7 & 8

## 5.0  FOR UTO MODE OF TRAIN OPERATION ON LINE - 7 & 8

5.1 Whenever earthquake is observed through EQWS or through any other means, TC/OCC shall immediately stop all trains running in UTO mode according to earthquake severity by relevant commands.
5.2 TC/CHC-OCC shall instruct IC for  announcements  inside  the  trains  to  keep  passengers informed. ACC/OCC shall do relevant announcements at station.
5.3 In case, RA/ETO is already available inside the train, TC/CHC-OCC shall instruct RA/ETO to take charge of train as per extant procedure. In case RA/ETO is not on-board, after earth quake subsides, TC/CHC-OCC shall instruct nearest available RA/ETO to board the train as per procedure.
5.4 TC/CHC-OCC instructs RA/ETO to take the charge and ensure further movement as per extant procedure.
5.5 UTO mode shall be suspended till 'resumption of normal services'.

## 3.4 SMS Interface:

SMS system interface with BHS provides following information in advance to BHS Control system:
Rake ID/No of arriving train.
ii) Platform on which train is arriving.
iii) Direction of arriving train.
iv) Whether arriving train is revenue or a non-revenue train.
Information mentioned in Para 3. 4 (i) above is provided in advance of train arriving at platform, so that BHS is able to orient movements of containers in  direction    of    arriving    trains.  This  enables  smooth  change  of container movements without causing any delay in train operation.

text:
Under  normal  mode  of  operation, BHS  operation will  be carried out automatically as per SMS information received. However, if SMS interface is not functional, following procedures shall be followed:
BHS supervisor at NDRU, SJSU (when operational) and APOT will obtain a time table with Rake id/No from the SC/TC for the entire day.
Station controller will communicate from time to time any changes to above time table  and any changes in normal operations as provided in 3.5 (i) to the BHS  Operator  over  Tetra  communication  or  telephone  under  exchange  of private numbers.
BHS  supervisor  will  instruct  the  BHS  operator  the  exact  sequence  of Operations  in  line  with  the  information  received  from  SC/TC  to  enable loading/unloading operation at his platform.
In  case of any abnormality, if  BHS supervisor feels that the BHS operation will result in delay of departure of train, he shall advise the station controller, who in consultation with TC shall take a decision to let the train depart from the platform without carrying out container loading/unloading operations.
If  SMS _BHS interface is not functional, information of Rake ID/No shall be manually  selected  by  BHS  operator  based  on  information  received  from Station  Controller  after  pressing  SMS  override  button  on  BHS  HMI.  BHS Operator,  before  opening  of  the  BCD  form  PEL,  shall  verify  the  manually entered  Rake  ID/No  with  actual  Rake  ID/  no  after  arriving  of  train  and opening of PED..

| 17 | Tetra communication | Normally Tetra communication is not required for BHS operation. However scenarios where Tetra communication is required during emergency BHS operation is as under : i) Cut Out Mode with or without door loop bypassed: Unless containers are required to be unloaded at Airport station, BHS operation is prohibited in LSRM and HSRM modes. Under these situations , BHS door control on the Asst. Driver Desk should be placed in manual mode so that operation of BCD is inhibited from the PEL panel and is controlled by the TO. In such a scenario the BCD shall be closed by the TO only after confirming of completion BHS operation from BHS operator/supervisor on TETRA under exchange of PN and informing OCC. ii) SMS _BHS interface is not functional. BHS Operation under such conditions shall be as per provisions defined in Para 3.4 & 3.5. iii) Undershoot / Overshoot of train at BHS stations. In event of undershoot / overshoot of train, the BHS HMI indicates that train has undershot / overshot resulting in non opening of the BCD. In such a scenario the BHS operator has to inform the TO on TETRA requesting him to realign the train to correct stopping window in order to enable BHS operation. TO shall realign the train after informing the OCC as per procedure in vogue. The BHS operation is possible only after the train is realigned to the correct stopping window of +/- 500 mm. ## 4. Fundamental Precautions and protection/System Interlock among BHS, PSD and Rolling Stock.

T hese loading bridges can obstruct train movement in the lowered position.
Movement of Train with loading bridge lowered condition can result  in  catastrophic  damage  to  the  train,  BHS,  PEDs  and other platform equipment and can also cause severe injuries to operating staff.

text: ## 4.1. Following precautions should be taken to ensure that trains on platforms are safe  :

metadata.source: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL_p10_4

text:
## 4.1. Following precautions should be taken to ensure that trains on platforms are safe  :

The PEDs should remain closed unless a passenger train is berthed at the correct platform to receive or deliver containers.
ii) Unless  in  operation;  the  Loading  Bridge  should  be  in  upright  (raised) condition  and  the  indications  of  its  raised  condition  should  appear  on  the BHS HMI.
iii) Under  no  circumstances  the  train  should  be  allowed  to  move  unless  the following conditions are met:
-Loading Bridges are in their UPRIGHT (raised) positions and
-BCDs AND PEDs are fully CLOSED.
4.2.  Additional  Safety  precautions  as  defined  below  in  Para  4.3  are  required  to  be  taken under following conditions:
The Door Loop is by-passed on the train.

text: ## 4.3.  Protection/ System interlock among BHS, PSD and Rolling Stock.

metadata.source: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL_p11_2

text:
The door loop on the train will remain open as long as BCDs are open - preventing traction on the train. However, the train operator should  ensure  that  the  Traction Brake Controller is in coasting position and holding brakes are applied as long as BHS operation is in progress.
BHS operator presses 'BCD Door open' on PEL Panel. The BCD's on the DMLC car will open completely.  The same is confirmed by two laser  sensors installed in train as  a confirmation for carrying out any further action and acknowledge in the BHS HMI as   a secondary safety interlock.
BHS Operation  is  fully  safe  during  AM  and  CM  mode  of  train  operation  because when  both  PED  and  BCD  are  open  train  will  not  get  target  speed  to  start  its movement.
However  to  ensure  that  the  train  does  not  get  the  target  speed  on  account  of incomplete BHS operation, the TO shall initiate the door closing , on receipt of door closing authorization  ,  only  after  confirmation  of  closing  of  BCD  from    the    TCMS screen.
In RM mode also, BHS Operation is safe, as train will not get target speed if BCD is open. However as PSD / PEDs are not being monitored in RM mode, the TO shall ensure closure of all PSD / EED / PED before starting the train even if he obtains the target speed.
The PED safety loop circuit is bypassed only if PED closed indication is not available to TO in AM/CM mode, by authorized BHS operation staff after physically confirming closing of PED.

metadata.source: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL_p11_4

text:
The PED safety loop circuit is bypassed only if PED closed indication is not available to TO in AM/CM mode, by authorized BHS operation staff after physically confirming closing of PED.
Cut Out Mode with or without door loop bypassed: BHS operation is prohibited in LSRM and HSRM modes, unless containers need to be  unloaded at Airport station. In this situation, the BHS door control on the Asst. Driver Desk should be placed in manual mode so that BCD is controlled by the TO, and is inhibited from the PEL panel. In such a scenario the BCD shall be closed by TO only after confirming completion of BHS operation from the BHS Operator/supervisor.
4.4. When conditions as defined in Para 4.2 - (i), (ii) and (iv) is exist, trains are driven in degraded mode. In such a scenario, normally BHS operation should not be permitted on the train.
However in case of emergency, BHS operation can be permitted as per details provided in Section 6 and 7.
4.5. The procedure to deal with situations described in Section 4.2 is defined in Sections 6 and 7 .

Should be fully aware of arrival timing, berthing platform and direction (UP/DN) of the train through SMS information / alternate source such as train time table as advised by Station Controller / Traffic Controller.

text:
He shall ascertain whether train arriving at his platform(s) is a revenue service train that is scheduled to carry containers.
Should be aware of signals received about train arrival through WLAN, PEL  indications.
He  shall  properly  coordinate  alignment  and  lowering  of  loading  bridge  and  the functions of the laser sensing unit for alignment of the bridge with the train doors.
He shall ensure that the time allotted for BHS operation is adhered to. In case there are faults on the system that could lead to delays in container transfer sequence; he shall make attempts to cancel the container transfer; withdraw the bridges and close the BCDs and PEDs and release the train as soon as possible.
He shall report all such incidences to the BHS Supervisor who in turn shall intimate Traffic Controller and Station Controller immediately.
In  normal  operation  procedure,  he  should  operate  the  PEL  panel  on  getting confirmation      that  the  train  has  arrived  on  UP  or  DN  platform  for  opening  of  the PED, BCD and lowering of the loading bridge.
BHS Auto operation is the normal mode of operation; however, present configuration    requires  confirming  lowering  OR  raising  of  loading  bridges  through HMI by  the  BHS  Operator as described in Section 3.6 , Step No  9  and Section 3.6 and Step No  12 as  above.
In  case of degraded modes of operation as described in Section 6 and 7 he shall seek assistance from the BHS Supervisor. In case the BHS supervisor cannot be contacted he shall intimate the Station Controller/TO/TC directly by Tetra / Phone.

## 5.2. BHS Supervisor

Should  be  aware  of  the  entire  BHS  system  in  the  AMEL  and  its  operational procedures.
Should strive for trouble free transfer of bags and containers throughout the BHS by efficient coordination between BHS supervisors of other stations.
Should  be  fully  aware  of  movement,  timing,  location/direction  (UP/DN)  of  the  train through SMS information or alternate sources such as train time table as advised by Station Controller / Traffic Controller.
Should be vigilant about the train movements and all activities on the Platform, BHS area  and should make all efforts for smooth flow of containers to and from trains / hoists and the conveyor system on both platform and concourse levels.
Should be aware of the train-BHS alignment systems; its  operation and interlocks provided    in  the  system.  He  should  also  be  aware  of  the  basic  hazards  of  BHS operation.
He shall maintain all fault records during his shift with the help of SCADA Operator. He shall also maintain the attendance records of BHS O&M personnel working during his shift.
He should always have quick access to O&M and troubleshooting manuals of BHS.
He  shall  immediately  inform  over  telephone  the  Traffic  Controller  and  Station Controller about faults in the BHS system on his platform or on the train, if any.
In  case  of  degraded  modes  of  operation  as  described  in  Section  6  and  7  BHS supervisor shall be present at the platform to supervise safe loading / unloading of containers at his station.
During non functioning BHS_SMS interface :

text: ## 5.4. Train Operator

metadata.chunk_id: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL_p13_4

text:
The train operator shall be vigilant of BHS operation on NDRU, SJSU and APOT stations.
He  shall  monitor  the  status  of  Baggage  Car  Doors  (BCD)  and  Platform  Edge Doors (PED) during the dwell time at these stations.
He shall ensure that the BCDs are shown as closed before attempting to close train doors.
He shall  not move the train  unless all Train Doors, BCDs, Platform Screen Doors (PSD) and Platform Edge Doors (PED) are confirmed as closed on his HMI.
He shall attempt to move the train only in AM or CM modes with the following conditions being fulfilled:
Train Doors including BCDs are c onfirmed as closed.
Platform Screen Doors including PEDs are c onfirmed as closed.
Door Loop is not bypassed
Traction Loop is not bypassed
If  the train is in RM/degraded mode, Train Operator should always ensure that the PSD / EED closed indication and PED Closed Indication are available on the PSL panel on BHS platform (Island platform on BHS Stations - see Figure 1). In case indication of PED is not available on PSL panel, the TO to ensure closure of PEDs and BCDs from BHS operator, under exchange of private number, who shall confirm the same based on indications available on PEL.
If  the  train  is  required  to  be  moved  in  one  or  more  of  above  situations  (degraded modes), the process defined in Section 6 in this circular shall be followed.
In  case  of  degraded  modes  operation  after  a  train  has  already  been  loaded  with containers, the processes defined in Section 7 shall apply.

## 5.6. Station Controller

The station controller shall be vigilant about BHS operations on his/her stations.
As soon as he is made aware of problems on the platform equipment including BHS and PEDs OR a problem on the BHS or door circuitry on the trains; he shall intimate the OCC.
He shall also ensure that BHS operators are present on the platform BHS area and that a BHS supervisor is present at his station.
In case of failure of SMS or non-availability of SMS signal to BHS, SC shall advise the  BHS  Supervisor/Operator  of  any  changes  in  normal  operation  as  provided  in Para  3.2  and  provide the following information to the BHS supervisor:
The platform on which the train is arriving.
Rake ID/No of the arriving train.
The direction of the arrival of the train.
Whether the train is a revenue train or a non-revenue train.

6.1. In all degraded modes of operation (RM & Cut Out Mode with or without door loop bypassed ) of train, the Train Operator , before moving the train , should  ensure that the  BHS loading bridge operation has been completed , the loading bridge has been lifted and BCD , PED are closed.
6.2. If  the  train  is  in  degraded  mode,  Train  Operator  should  ensure  that  the  PSD  /  EED closed and PED Closed Indications are available on the PSL panel on BHS platform and BCD closed indication is available on the TCMS panel . In case , indication of PED &  BCD closed    is  not  available  on  PSL  &  TCMS  panels  respectively  ,  the  TO  shall ensure  closure  of  PEDs  and  BCDs  from  BHS  operator  under  exchange  of  private number, who shall confirm the  same based actual status and indications available on PEL.
6.3. If  the  BHS  operator  is  not  able  to  open  BCD  through  the  PEL  panel,  TO  can  be requested       by  BHS  Operator,  under  exchange  of  Private  No,  to  open  the  BCD  by placing the BHS Door control on the Asstt. Driver Desk in manual mode. However, in such circumstances the TO shall open/ close BCD only on advice of BHS operator and with knowledge of OCC.

6.5. BHS Operation is prohibited if the Door Loop and Traction Loop are bypassed. In all these situations, the BHS Door control on the Asstt. Driver Desk should be placed in

6.6. Before moving the train after completion of BHS operation under conditions defined in para  6.1-6.5  above,  TO  shall  obtain  confirmation  for  closing  of  all  Train  Doors, PSDs, EEDs, PEDs & BCDs from a combination of indications available on PSL panel,  PEL  Panels,  TCMS  screen,  and  confirmation from  SC &  BHS Operational staff under exchange of Private No. and as per details defined in Para 7 below.

text: ## 7. Unloading of Containers at APOT in abnormal situations

metadata.source: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL_p15_2

text:
7.1. If containers that  have been loaded on the train from NDRU and SJSU stations have to be  unloaded  at  APOT  station  in  case  of  degraded  mode  operations  as  described  in Para 6 above, following process shall apply :
The SCADA operator shall identify the train in which the containers are loaded and shall intimate the BHS supervisor and BHS Operator.
The BHS supervisor shall be present at the platform level BHS area and take charge of the situation. He shall ascertain number of loaded containers that are arriving on the affected train from the SCADA operator.
The BHS supervisor shall ensure that the train has stopped in the correct position and then instruct the BHS operator to open the PED from PEL.
BHS supervisor shall advise the Train Operator to open the BCD's doors using the manual open buttons on the assistant driver desk in the train cab.
The train operator shall apply parking brakes on the train and open the BCD on the island platform side.
After PED and BCD are opened, BHS supervisor/Operator shall verify that the train is    in  the  correct  stopping  window  and  instruct  BHS  operator  to  lower  the  loading bridges.  The  containers  shall  then  unload  in  automatic  mode  from  the  train.  The loading bridges shall then be raised by BHS operator.

metadata.source: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 42. SC 42 (Rev-01)  PO for Loading Bridge & BHS operation in AEL_p15_4

text:
The  BHS  Operator/supervisor  shall  then  instruct  the  Train  Operator  to  close  the BCDs on the train. Once the Train Operator confirms that he/she has seen the BCDs as  closed  on  the  TCMS  screen,  the  BHS  supervisor  shall  then  instruct  the  BHS operator to close the PEDs.
Once the PEDs are closed, the train operator can release the parking brakes, inform OCC and proceed towards DSTO and wait for further instructions.

## 8. Anomalies in Containers Arrivals

8.1. The BHS operation at various stations is designed to handle full or empty containers at a given platform in a particular direction of train movement as described in Section 3.1.
8.2. The anomalies can arise if the above sequence is violated possibly resulting in empty containers arriving at platforms designed to receive full containers and  vice-versa.
8.3. The BHS will not accept such anomalies. Under such situations the BHS operator will not attempt to load or unload containers manually.

 Make sure BCDs & PEDs are closed before moving
 Ensure that the PSD / PED closed indication is available on the PSL on BHS platform

## Sub:-Operating System for execution of Critical Commands for DMRC-Airport Line.

Find  enclosed  Safety  Circular-29'D'  (Rev.-02)  regarding  Operating  System  for  execution  of Critical Commands for DMRC-Airport Line.
All  concerned  are  to  ensure  that  staff  working  under  them  have  read  and  understood  the procedure and assurance regarding the same is taken.
This issues with the approval of the competent authority.
Copy to: -
All EDs/HODs (O&M) and Dean/DMRA, All Dy. HODs (O&M), Mgr/AM (Train Operation, Station, OCC),
All Stations, All Crew Controls and All DCC and DMRA.
## SAFETY CIRCULAR-29'D' (Rev.-02)

## SAFETY CIRCULAR-29'D' (Rev.-02)

(Raman Goyal) AGM/Ops/C&P
## SAFETY CIRCULAR-29-D (Rev.-02)
## Operating System for Execution of Critical Commands for DMRC-Airport Line

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This  Procedure  applies  to  OCC  and  all  Stations  of  Airport  Line  for  Safe  Execution  of  Safety Critical Commands. This Procedure shall ensure that additional measures for execution of Critical Commands by the Chief Controller / Traffic Controller / Station Controller are followed properly and correctly for Safe Passage of Trains and Safety of Staff.

## 2. SCOPE

This procedure is applicable on Airport line. This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways  General  Rules,  2020  and  Metro  Railways  General  (Amendment)  Rules,  2022, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
The Procedure also reminds the Operator - TC / SC about his / her responsibility for additional Safety  Measures  which  are  required  to  be  undertaken  at  the  time  of  Execution  of  these Commands.

## 3. GENERAL

Critical  commands  are  necessary  to  release  or  circumvent  certain  Safety  Features  built  in  the System with the  complete Knowledge & Consent of  the  Operator,  to  deal  with  certain  specific Operational Situations or some Signaling System Anomalies. The Operator, therefore, is allowed to  issue  Critical  Commands  with  additional  Measures  for  Safeguarding  and  Control  of  critical Operations.
A Critical Command is programmed in such a way that its Issue shall have to be confirmed within a  pre-determined  time  interval  on  the  Central  /  Local  ATS,  before  it  shall  be  executed  by  the Interlocking and / or ATP.
Before a Critical Command is executed the CC/TC / SC/DCC must:
(i) Check if the  Critical  Command  is  absolutely  necessary  or  if  it  can  be  avoided  by utilizing another Alternative.
(ii) Ensure that using this Command does not in any way leads to Hazardous Situation.
(iii)  Obtain Permission from the Chief Controller, in case the critical command is used by TC, and from TC, in case it is used by SC. CC/TC as the case may be, shall have to agree that, the conditions (i) & (ii) above are satisfied.
(iv)  If TC / SC has any doubt about the Safety of using the envisaged Critical Command, in combination with the necessary Measures, he / she must stop and check for other Solutions or consult the Chief Controller & FMC.
(v) Use of Critical Commands is recorded and numbered in the Log Lists of the ATS System and shall have to be checked periodically by the Chief Controller.
## 4. WARNING INDICATIONS

## 4. WARNING INDICATIONS

Where  a  risk  of  injury  or  damage  cannot  be  totally  ruled  out  in  execution  of  the  command described,  attention  is  drawn  to  the  relevant  dangers  by  means  of  specially  highlighted  safety information.  The  safety  notices  used  are  classified  according  to  the  gravity  of  the  danger  and have the following significance:

## WARNING

## 5. OPERATING FUNCTIONS FOR CRITICAL COMMANDS
## 5.1 Critical Operation

## 5.1 Critical Operation

Some  critical  operations  by-passing  security  provided  by  interlocking  are  performed  through Critical  Commands.  Certain  special  procedure  should  be  performed  by  CC/TC  &  SC  before executing critical commands.

## NOTE

For use of critical command, the controller has to own the access right 'IntlCrit'.
The following sequence should be followed for executing Critical Commands:

The command buttons for signal operations and the [Break] button become visible and operable. |

The button [Execute] will be operable.                                                                                                 |

## REQUIREMENT

Before a track section may be unlocked against route setting, the TC/SC must:
Ensure that the reason to lock the track section is no longer necessary.
Ensure  that  no  maintenance  or  operation  reasons  exist  to  prevent  the unlocking of the track.
Ensure that no train proceeds unintentionally into the track section.
Set the access signal to stop, if required.
Obtain the permission of the Chief Controller.
Verify that the next train receives the correct route setting.
Set the required route manually if required.
Inform the relevant train operator accordingly if required.

## (iii) Track Release, Auxiliary
## ADDITIONAL SAFETY REQUIREMENT

## ADDITIONAL SAFETY REQUIREMENT

The command RelAux is applied to selected track circuits in order to set them to a basic position of 'not claimed' (yellow indication). This can be done when more track  circuits  than  necessary  have  been  claimed  for  a  train  route.  It  may  be necessary  to release  some  of  the unoccupied  track circuits for another movement. Before a track section is released auxiliary, the TC/SC must:
Ensure that the auxiliary release operation will not effect other operations.
Ensure that the track is not part of another route or overlap.
If the track to be released belongs to a route such as an overlap, ensure with the Train Operator that a train or track vehicle in the track section concerned has come to a full stop.
Obtain the permission from the Chief Controller.
Example: State before operation: A track circuit T131D is not released from a route.
Figure 6 State before track release, auxiliary
The  operation  sequence  is:  Select  the  Track  &  execute  the  [RelAux]  as  per  the  procedure mentioned in 5.1.
State  afterwards:  After  the  successful  execution  of  the  critical  command RelAux the  track section T131D is released from the route fragment.

## (iv) Track Logically Clear

## ADDITIONAL SAFETY REQUIREMENT

With this command, a logical occupation of a track can be cancelled. Before a track is set logically free, the TC/SC must:

## ADDITIONAL SAFETY REQUIREMENT

Attempt to release the track using the RelAux command.
If  above step fails,  check possible causes for an  assumed incorrect track occupation.
Obtain the permission from the Chief Controller.
Set the track logically to 'free'.
If  above  step  fails,  order  the  next  Train  Operator  to  move    train  in  ROS mode  under procedure in vogue and report to the Traffic controller after TO has passed the track section concerned.

## WARNING

The TC/SC must be sure that the track detection is working properly.
Example: State before operation: A track section T113A is logically occupied but physically free.

The operation sequence is: Select the Track & execute the  [LogClear] as per the  procedure mentioned in 5.1.
State  afterwards:  After  the  successful  execution  of  the  critical  command LogClear the  track T113A is logically free.

## (v) Temporary Speed Restriction / Limit (TSR) setting in Track section

## (v) Temporary Speed Restriction / Limit (TSR) setting in Track section

In case of maintenance work at track side or because of any other reason, the Traffic Controller can limit the speed of the trains as required. The ATP controls the train according to the setting of temporary speed limit on the tracks.

## ADDITIONAL SAFETY REQUIREMENT

Any  qualified  person  may  request  a  speed  restriction  to  be  applied.  Before speed limits are set, the Traffic Controller must:
Confirm  and  log  the  reason  for  the  speed  restriction  in  the  Traffic Controller's logbook.
Ensure that written authority to impose a TSR has been received from a authorized person or permission granted by the Chief Controller.

## Introduction

Check that the new speed-limit is not exceeding any other existing speed restriction.

## Introduction

Stop any approaching trains to avoid unintentional emergency stopping.
After inputting the speed restriction, request the Train Operator of the next train to proceed cautiously in CM mode through the new speed restriction zone  and  to  monitor  the  train  run  carefully  for  any  speed  variations  to avoid any effects of conflicting speed limits.
Example:    Start  before  operation:  Normally  there  is  no  temporary  speed  limit  on  the  track T140A.
Figure 10  State before Speed Limit
The operation sequence is: Select the Track & execute the command (e.g. [SpLi,20] for setting restrictive speed to 20 kmph) as per the procedure mentioned in 5.1.
State afterwards: After execution of the command SpLi xx (xx can be for example 5, 10, 15, 20, …, 115) the automatic train regulation doesn't allow the train to pass the track T140A faster than xx km/h.
Figure 11   State after Speed Limit
## (vi) Release Temporary Speed Limit in track section

## (vi) Release Temporary Speed Limit in track section

The SpLi off function has to be executed together with pressing the 'ATP KF switch' located in concerned  SER  Crank  Handle  cabinet  for  completely  releasing  the  existing  imposed  speed restriction  to  designed  permanent  speed  restriction  in  that  track  circuit  or  relaxing  it  to  any higher value of restrictive speed limit.

## ADDITIONAL SAFETY REQUIREMENT

Speed  limits  imposed  by  Maintenance  department  may  only  be  released  with  the written authority of the authorized personnel of Rank not less than junior Engineers as per  the  procedure  for  Imposition/alteration  &  cancellation  of  TSR.  Speed  limits imposed by Operations for safety (e.g. temporary limit to protect incident management activities)  may  be  released  with  permission  of  the  Chief  Controller.  Before  a  speed limit can be released, the TC/SC must:
Check that the cause has been resolved and that written authority to release it has been received from the authorized personnel or permission granted by the Chief Controller as stated above.
Check  that  the  new  speed-limit  is  not  exceeding  any  other  existing  speed restriction.

## Introduction

## (x) Point Switching, Auxiliary

This operation permits to throw a point even if it is indicated as occupied. If the point is claimed by a route or for flank protection, if it is locked against throwing or if it is indicated as trailed, the command SwiAux is rejected.

## NOTE

Use this command to throw points if the corresponding tracks vacancy detection is disturbed.
SwiAux is a critical command, please refer to 5.1.
## SAFETY REQUIREMENT

## SAFETY REQUIREMENT

This function is used to switch points, which are indicated as occupied. Before it is allowed to switch a point by using the function Sw iAux the TC/SC must:
Check possible signalling causes for an assumed incorrect point occupation.
Ensure  that  point  is  not  under  maintenance  and  no  other  maintenance reason exists against switching of the point.
Receive a report from a Station Controller that the point is physically free from vehicles. If there is any doubt contained in the report from site, do not take  further  action  until  it  is  clarified  and  the  vehicle  or  obstruction  is confirmed clear of the turnout area.

## Introduction

Ensure that  the  point  is  not  needed  for  another  route,  flank  protection  or overlap.

## Introduction

Ensure  that  a  train  or  vehicle  running  in  a  route  or  overlap  to  which  the point belongs has come to full stop.
Obtain permission from the Chief Controller.

## (xi) Point Switching, Trailed

If a point loses its point detection without a throwing command, a trailing indication for this point is detected.
If  a  point  is  indicated  as  trailed,  both  automatic  (by  route  setting)  as  well  as  manual  point throwing  commands  are  rejected.  The command  'switch  trailed point' is necessary  to synchronize the real point position with the interlocking logic.

## ADDITIONAL SAFETY REQUIREMENT

This function is used for throwing points that are showing a trailed indication. This indication means that the actual position of the point at site is different to a normal locked position or the point is not completely set in any of the positions.
Points  in  the  depot  are  designed  so  that  they  can  be  trailed  without damaging the point elements.
Since  the  mainline  will  operate  mostly  in  ATO/ATP  mode  with  a  greater degree of route protection, the points on the line were designed so that they cannot be trailed (without causing damage to them).
In  event  of  trailing  of  any  point  a  proper  inspection  of  the  point  must  be

## Cancellation of Train Stop, UP and DOWN Direction

If some stopping points are set, it is possible to cancel them manually with this command. This command is not available for all tracks.

## WARNING

The Train Controller must be sure that the track detection is working properly.

## ADDITIONAL SAFETY REQUIREMENT

Before a Train stop is Cancelled, the Traffic Controller must:
Note the reason requiring execution of the Cancel Train Stop command.
Obtain permission of Chief Controller.
Ensure that train has completely stopped and is in stationary position
Inform the Train operator that the Stopping Point has been cancelled and
Ensure that after passage of the train, the OSP (Operational Stopping Point) has restored to its original position i.e. indication of OSP becomes Yellow.

## 6. ARC (Automatic Route Calling)

## 6. ARC (Automatic Route Calling)

On  Airport  Line,  there  are  two  independent  ATS  systems,  namely,  Primary  ATS  System  and Backup  ATS  system.  At  a  time,  only  one  ATS  system  controls  and  operates  CBI.  In  case  of failure/View  loss  of  Primary  ATS,  Backup  ATS  system  (OCC  or  Main  Line)  shall  be  used. Preferably Backup ATS at OCC shall be used. In case Backup ATS at mainline is used, Station Controller  shall  perform  all  duties  mentioned  hereafter  for  Traffic  Controller.  In  the  event  of communication break with ATS, a feature of ARC (Automatic Route Calling) is provided on AEL to avoid disruption in train operation. This CBI feature shall provide route setting and other CBI function automatically during the absence of ATS control and view. This feature gets activated, automatically  when  there  is  breakage  of  communication  with  ATS  system.  The  CBI  and  ATP continue to operate normally and ARC provides route automatically to all the trains.
## 6.1 Prerequisites of ARC

In  case  of  ATS  view  loss  on  Traffic  Controller's  Primary  ATS  Workstation,  Backup  ATS workstation located in OCC shall be used.
In  case,  view  on  both  ATS  workstation  i.e.  Primary  ATS  workstation  and  Backup  ATS workstation is not available, trains shall get target under ARC as per previous route setting which implies activation of ARC.
In case train is running in mid of the section, the points of crossover at Dhaula Kuan, Airport and Dwarka Sector-21 shall not move and remain set and locked in normal position as were prior  to  ATS  view  loss  in  OCC,  Clamp  and  Pad  locking  shall  not  be  required.  ARC  shall provide  same  route  setting,  signal  aspect  and  point  position  as  per  previous  condition  i.e. before failure of ATS and Train shall continue to get target speed even after ATS failure.
At  terminal  stations,  Points  shall  remain  in  the  position  they  were  set  prior  to  failure  of communication between ATS and CBI. Manual Terminal Operation (MTO) shall be required to be carried out for Train reversal. Trains shall move in RM mode after reversal until Trains get target speed in ATP.
In  case train is  standing at platform, route is set and signal aspect is proceed before ATS failure,  the  ARC  shall  provide  same  setting  after  ATS  failure,  then  train  shall  get  target speed.

In  case train is  standing at platform, route is set and signal aspect is proceed before ATS failure,  the  ARC  shall  provide  same  setting  after  ATS  failure,  then  train  shall  get  target speed.
In case train is standing at platform, but route is not set and signal aspect is danger before ATS failure, the ARC shall provide same setting even after ATS failure, then train shall not get target speed.
## 6.2  Operation of ARC

## 6.2  Operation of ARC

The following steps should be followed for operation of train under ARC:
In  case  of  ATS  view loss on Traffic Controller's Primary ATS Workstation, TC/OCC shall inform Signalling Controller and check the ATS view on Backup ATS workstation located in OCC. ARC shall get activated automatically.
If view on Backup ATS workstation is available, TC/OCC shall inform Chief Controller and take control on Backup ATS. TC shall load time table online and provide Train ID manually to the trains in section. Trains will run automatically by backup ATS and ARC shall not be required. TC shall switch off ARC from Backup ATS.

## Introduction

If  view  on  backup  ATS workstation  is  also  not available, TC/OCC  shall  inform  Signalling Controller  and  announce on  group mode to all the Train  Operators & Station Controllers about non-availability of ATS view at both OCC and Stations.

## Introduction

TC/OCC shall instruct all Train Operators of trains running on mainline, to check availability of Cab signal and target speed.
In  case,  target  speed  available  is  reported  by  concerned  Train  Operators, TC/OCC shall instruct all concerned TO to continue operating train by observing Cab Signal & Line side signal.
On every arrival & departure at stations, TO shall report following to TC/OCC:
status of PSD and train doors,
availability of proceed code (Cab Signal), and
Signal aspect with signal number.
Train  operators  shall  take  permission  before  departing  train  from  second  last  terminal station, further movement shall be as per extant procedure.
TC/OCC shall arrange MTO at both terminal stations (NDRU and IICC) for train reversal as per extant procedure. After reversal, trains shall move in RM mode until Trains get target speed in ATP.
TC/OCC  shall  instruct  all  train  operators  to  operate  train  in  Coded  Manual  mode  (ATP Mode) during  ARC mode between  Shivaji Stadium PF  to  Dwarka  Sector-21  PF  on  both lines.
When ATS view and control becomes available at either OCC or Station, TC shall switch off ARC and restore ARS. TC shall inform all Train Operators & Station Controllers regarding resumption of normal operation under ARS (Automatic Route Setting).

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This procedure shall be applicable for  induction/ stabling of train from Depot (JLA Stabling Yard and Kalindi Kunj Depot)  to JLA  3 rd /UP/DN  Platform  and  vice versa in  UTO  mode  without  Train Operator/Roving Attendant.

## 1. INTRODUCTION

However, provision to board Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA), if required, has also been made. This procedure defines roles and responsibilities of staff of all concerned department and actions to be taken by them to ensure safe movement of train in UTO mode: -
1.1. Between  Jasola  Vihar  Stabling  Line  (JLA  SBL)  to  Jasola  Vihar  Shaheen  Bagh  Station  (JLA) 3 rd Platform and vice versa. (without TO/RA) (Signaling Layout placed at Annexure-05).
1.2. Between Kalindi Kunj Depot (KIKD) to UP/DN/3 rd  Platform of Jasola Vihar Shaheen Bagh station (JLA) and vice versa. (without TO/RA) (Signaling Layout placed at Annexure-05).

## 2. SCOPE

This procedure order shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and other relevant Safety Circulars, Station Working Order, Depot Working Order, Special Instructions in vogue.

On successful execution of above steps, TC shall ensure the train indication box turns blue (as per Annexure-2) on ATS MMI in line overview.

## A. Static Test failure

If  static  test  result  is  other  than all  correct (Static  test  result  code  0x0001)  then DCC/TC shall give manual static test command.
If static test result is still other than all correct , then S&T (O&M)/Signalling System Controller shall analyse the fault and decide whether the train can be introduced in UTO mode or Non UTO mode and shall convey to DCC/TC accordingly.

## B. Dynamic Test failure

If  dynamic test result is other then all correct (Dynamic test result code 0x0001) then EB shall be applied in Train, which cannot be released remotely.
DCC shall instruct TO/RA to board the train and take charge as per Annexure 4.
