## 7. Unscheduled wakeup of UTO Train on mainline or depot:

UTO train may wakeup without any remote/ automated command, if either of these conditions is altered (manually or due to system failure) during sleep status:
Change in position of Mode Selector from AUTO to other position.
Change in position of master controller (TBC) from B Max to any other position.
Operation of SCS switch.
Loss of Stop detection.
Loss of coupling with P0(s) Balise.
Any one VOBC in fault state.
Loss  of  CBTC  communication  between  Wayside  Zone  controller  (SC)  and  On-Board Signalling system (VOBC).

## Procedure to prepare the hot standby Train in UTO mode

PPIO in consultation with DCC shall nominate preferably last two scheduled trains as hot standby which may be used in case of failure of UTO Tests including Static/Dynamic Test. Same shall be communicated to DCC well in advance after preparing and stabling them for UTO movement.

## Procedure to prepare the hot standby Train in UTO mode

DCC shall give the remote wakeup command from the ATS MMI.
After execution of wakeup process, DCC shall confirm that train is Ready without fault.
DCC shall inform PPIO about the same.
DCC shall ask the TC to give Dozing mode set command, The same shall be executed by TC.
RSC shall verify that train is in Dozing state (i.e., in dozing mode HVAC, saloon light, etc. shall be turned off in order to save energy) from RSC controller GUI and confirm the same to TC.
TC shall reset Dozing mode set command before inducting that train to main line.
If standby train is not inducted then PPIO and DCC shall consult one another and set the train to sleep mode or may use as per requirement.

## 1) Depot: -

Main purpose of SPK (Staff protection Key) in depot is to ensure safety of staff during movement of trains between interlocked area (yards) and non-interlocked area (IBL, WBL, IHCS & PWL). IBL/WBL/IHCS/PWL being a manned area, thus a manual supervision is required during train movement. SPK is installed at entry/exit point of each IBL/WBL/IHCS/PWL and is interlocked with corresponding signal/route for respective movements.

SPK keys remain inserted by default in SPK box and removed only during operation.
Procedure : As per requirement of train movement, the Depot Controller shall authorize a particular SPK and SPK can be removed only after authorization from DCC.
Case-1: For movement of train from inside of IBL/WBL/IHCS/PWL towards outside of IBL/WBL/IHCS/PWL
Depot controller shall give SPK authorization through ATS terminal.
At SPK, the RED LED shall glow. On ATS terminal SPK soft button shall turn blue and SPK number shall turn green.
Depot controller shall inform the Points-man to go and operate that particular SPK under exchange of private number.
Points-man shall physically check the track for any obstruction and after ensuring clearance of the track in all respects shall remove the SPK. Removal of SPK shall change the STOP aspect of signal to PROCEED aspect. ON ATS terminal, the SPK number shall turn red.
Depot Controller shall set the route corresponding to that IBL/WBL for train movement from inside of IBL/WBL/IHCS/PWL towards Yard (to the next signal).
The maintenance staff/shunter/TO/RA (as applicable) shall move/shunt the train upto speed of 5 kmph while coming out of IBL/WBL/IHCS/PWL.
The points-man shall supervise the train movement and once the train has completely moved out of IBL/WBL/IHCS/PWL area and reached the next signal, TO/RA/Shunter shall ensure UTO mode as per Para 3.4 for further Movement in UTO Mode.

The points-man shall supervise the train movement and once the train has completely moved out of IBL/WBL/IHCS/PWL area and reached the next signal, TO/RA/Shunter shall ensure UTO mode as per Para 3.4 for further Movement in UTO Mode.
If TO/RA/Shunter has to deboard, DCC shall instruct TO/RA/Shunter to get deboarded by operating EED (Emergency Egress Device). Thereafter, TO/RA/Shunter shall close the door and give confirmation of the same to DCC.
After clearing the UTO Zone TO/RA/Shunter shall confirm to DCC in group mode.
The points-man shall also confirm clearance of UTO Zone and insert the SPK through private number exchange with DCC.
After normalization of SPK (insertion of SPK), the DCC shall proceed with further route setting as per requirement.

2.1 This procedure order shall be applicable to Airport Express Line. This Document should be read in  conjunction  with  the  Metro  Railways  General  Rules-2020  and  Metro  Railways  General (Amendment) Rules-2022Station Working Orders in vogue and other Special Instructions issued, from time to time for Working of Trains on Airport Express Line.
2.2 This procedure is applicable considering TSR imposed in NDRU-DSTO (both UP & DN) section for implementation of maximum speed restriction as approved by CMRS or below subjected to other speed restrictions on turnouts, platforms etc.
## 3. PROCEDURE:

3.1 All the request for imposition/alteration/cancellation of TSR on main line should be made to Chief Controller/OCC  and  the  CHC/OCC  shall  instruct  Traffic  Controller for the Imposition / Alteration/Cancellation  of  Temporary  Speed  Restrictions  &  Issue  of  Caution  Orders  to  Train Operators, as required on the Main Line Sections.
3.2 Chief  Controller  shall  be  overall  responsible  for  imposition/alteration  (increase/decrease)  and cancellation of TSR on main line. Chief Controller / Depot Controller shall keep a record of all the accepted TSR Requests.
3.3 In case of any of the TSR Commands, not directly being under Control of TC, the Compliance of the same shall be ensured by TC by the Station Controllers on the Exchange of Private Numbers.
3.4 All Requests for the Imposition / Alteration/Cancellation of Temporary Speed Restrictions & Issue of Caution Orders to the Train Operators (Annexure - 'A') , as required within the Depot, shall be submitted to the Depot Controller, who is responsible for Coordination of all such Requests. Depot Controller shall also inform the TSR details to the PPIO, under Exchange of Private Numbers, to enable him to advise the Shunting Supervisors accordingly.
3.5 All Requests of the TSRs imposition/alteration/cancelation shall be submitted by the Authorized Personnel of Rank, not less than Junior Engineers as per prescribed format in Annexure - 'B'. The Requests for the TSRs for a Planned Work shall normally be submitted to TC by authorized personal not less than Junior Engineer or equivalent before 1700 Hrs. of the previous day.

3.6 On receipt of Request for Imposition / Alteration & Cancellation of Temporary Speed Restriction (TSR) on a Section / in the Depot, the Traffic Controller / Depot Controller shall verify the TC No. corresponding to the OHE Mast No./chainage No. from the Conversion Table from Annexure 'C' of  this Circular and shall take further action for Imposition / Alteration / Cancellation of the Temporary Speed Restriction.
3.7 The Requests, arising out of Emergency or Failure, shall be taken up promptly, duly advising the Official, who has made the Request.

## Introduction

3.8 TSRs can be implemented through central ATS System for main line and DATS for Depots (for test track only) in terms of affected Track circuits zone (first and last track circuit) and, therefore,  the  Traffic  Controller  /  Depot  Controller  shall  prepare  the  Caution  Orders,  as required, by converting the Chainage/OHE Mast number in terms of the affected Track Circuit Zone.

3.9 In depot for speed restrictions on other track/lines in depot (equipped with DC track circuits), request shall be given in required proforma to Depot Controller for further necessary action. All TSRs in Depot, shall be advised to Train Operator/Shunter in writing on Caution Order form.
3.10 For increasing or removal of the TSR, TC shall intimate Signaling System Controller in written, who shall coordinate with the Signaling maintenance staff  available at the Stations for the same. On intimation, the Signaling  staff  at the station shall enter the SER  (after obtaining S ER ke y as  per  procedure) and shall pressed/turned the LA (Latch acknowledge) button (this key should be turned within 20 second of command of cancelation given) in crank handle cabinet (as per signaling instruction/manual) for further cancellation of the TSR by the TC. The same shall be immediately informed by Signaling staff to Signaling Controller. Signaling Controller shall first inform  to  Traffic  Controller  verbally  to  execute/complete  the  TSR  cancellation  process.  After completion of TSR cancellation process, Signaling Controller shall inform to TC in writing as well.
3.11 On completion of imposition / alteration / cancellation of TSRs, status of all TSRs shall be verified by TC / DC (for only test track) by viewing the numeric value against all concerned Track Circuits on ATS MMI. In case of any alteration in TSR, complete list of TSRs shall be reconciled by the TC.

3.12 In case a TSR is imposed or cancelled in revenue hours, Traffic Controller  shall give details of such caution order to the train operator of the first train approaching caution zone on radio exchanging Private number to proceed in Coded Manual mode through the TSR zone and to monitor train run carefully. TO shall verify the target speed displayed on HMI during the movement on the affected area and confirm the same to Traffic controller. TO must check and advice TC for any speed variations to avoid any effect of conflicting speed limits and TC will log/record the same.
All other train operators should be provided with caution order in writing by Station Controller  of adjacent station or Crew Controller / DC. This procedure shall be followed until the implementation of TSR in ATS system is assured ( Annexure-A ).
3.13 At the time of modifications of TSRs the Traffic controller shall advise the same to concerned SC/DC/CC (Station Controller/Depot Controller/ Crew Controller), who shall maintain records of all imposed TSRs. Chief controller shall periodically crosscheck the records of TSRs maintained by SC, CC and DCC respectively.
3.14 Depot Controller/Crew Controller/Station  controller shall  advise  all  TSRs  in force  to  the Train Operator of the pilot train and also all other train operators before start of revenue services. The train operator of the pilot train shall verify, during the run, the start and end locations of all TSRs in force on the mainline from the target speed display on driver's panel and satisfy himself that TSRs are correctly implemented over the entire train length in the TSR zone and give a confirmation to the Station Controller / Crew Controller/Depot controller of the terminating station who will relay the same to the Traffic Controller.

3.15 Primary  CATS  and  Backup  CATS  server  is  available  at  Dwarka  Depot  and  Shivaji  Stadium respectively which is common for Main Line and Depot. Provision of local control of station on LATS MMI or control through VDU locally, is NOT available at AEL. Primary CATS workstation is available  at  OCC  Metro  Bhawan, SCRs' of New Delhi, Shivaji Stadium, Dhaula Kuan , Delhi Aerocity,  Airport,  Dwarka  Sector  21  and  I.I.C.C.-DWARKA  SECTOR-25  station   and  Dwarka DCC. Backup CATS workstation available at OCC Metro Bhawan, SCR,s of Shivaji Stadium, New Delhi ,Airport and Dwarka DCC.

## Introduction

3.16 TSRs  can  be  Imposed  /  Altered  (only  Decrease)  by  the  Traffic  Controller  from  CATS  MMI, available in OCC for Line. Station Controller is not authorized to impose/alter/cancel any TSR on main  line.  Signaling  Controller  shall  co-ordinate  with  TC/OCC  and  Signaling  staff  during alteration/cancelation of TSR.

## Introduction

3.22 The Traffic  Controller  shall  advise  the  Depot  Controller  &  Station  Controllers  of  the  Terminal Stations of all TSRs to be in force during next day on the entire Mainline on daily basis and shall maintain  a  Record  of  the  same.  Traffic  Controller  shall  also  advise  the  TSRs  to  the  Crew Controller and the Crew Controller and depot controller shall write in the notice boards and sign on register as well however for those TSRs not imposed through the system due to any reason shall  be  advised  to  Train  operators  of  each  passing  train  in  the  form  of  caution  order  at  the preceding station of affected section.
3.23 Traffic Controller shall ensure that before the Start of Revenue Services all the TSRs requested on the Section have been 'Set' on the Sector and shall advise, under the Exchange of Private numbers, the first Train Operator passing the affected Section. Traffic Controller will confirm from the said TO with regard to the imposition of TSR. Train Operator in turn shall intimate the Target Speed displayed on DMI over the affected area to the Traffic Controller. TC shall log / record the same.
3.24 In the event of complete Power Failure to the Track side ATC System trains run in degraded mode of train operation with speed not exceeding 25kmph hence all TSRs below 25 kmph shall be dealt as per Para-3.25 of this circular. After restoration, Chief controller shall verify that all the TSRs which are prevailing have been applied in the system.

3.25 Since Trains can run in non-ATP Mode at Speeds lower than 25 Kmph, the System as such cannot enforce the TSRs of Values less than 25 Kmph in non-ATP Mode of Working. TSRs of Values less than 25 Kmph shall, therefore, be advised to the Train Operator in writing in the form

## 3. SYSTEM OF WORKING

## 3. SYSTEM OF WORKING

Under the ATS, in Manual Mode, when the 'Level of Control' is 'Local ATS' ,  each MSS Station can control their Interlocking or OCC Controllers can control their 'Area of Control' from  their  ATS  Workstations. When  the  'Level  of  Control'  is 'CENTRAL ATS' ,  all  other Secondary  Stations  can  only  monitor  the  Main  Line  (their  respective  Interlocking  Area) Movements. All Controllers (Local Station, Depot, Secondary Station & Central) are able to consult  all  the  'Views'  simultaneously  but  only  one  Controller  (Local  Station,  Depot,  or Central), at a time, is allowed to send Controls towards one Interlocking.
When LATS / CATS are restarted or initialized, the 'Level of Control' is always Local and further Change of Level is only possible with mutual Consent of both LATS and CATS Users except when a Local ATS User wants the Transfer of Control to meet with certain Emergent

## Introduction

situation,  in  which  case  such  a  Transfer  is  done  in  the  Emergency  Mode  even  without Consent.

## Introduction

Normally  the  Control  of  all  Interlockings  should  be  with  OCC  Controllers,  with  'Level  of Control' being 'CENTRAL ATS' .
## 4. LINE OPERATING MODE MANAGEMENT

## 4. LINE OPERATING MODE MANAGEMENT

This Function manages the Line Operating Mode, according to Control Level of the Line, Area of Control Regions assigned to the Operator and the Location of the Operator to carry out the Control (Central Control Level or Local Control Level).
Different Line Operating Modes are - Manual, Constant Headway & Scheduled.
Scheduled Mode is available in Central ATS. The other ones viz. the Manual & Constant Headway are available in Central and Local ATS both ( Figure 1 ).
Line Operating Modes
Figure-1
Line Operating Modes can be Monitored and Controlled by an Operator located in a LATS or CATS.
Line Operating Mode is not available in the Depot.
## 4.1.  Manual Mode:

## 4.1.  Manual Mode:

The Operation will be entirely manual. At the Initialization of a Control Level (Central or Local), the Line Operating Mode shall be 'Manual'. In the event of loss of Central Control Level, all ATS Sectors of a given Corridor shall have the change of the Control Level from Central to Local, and of the Line Operating Mode from one amongst the three Modes to Manual Mode.
## 4.2.  Constant Headway Mode:

## 4.2.  Constant Headway Mode:

In this Mode, the Trains will be regulated based on the predefined 'Headway'.
When the Line Operating Mode is switched from 'Constant Headway' to 'Manual', Routes and Cycles are not cancelled automatically. The Operator is in charge of the Cancellation of

## Introduction

Controls.
## 4.3.  Scheduled Mode:

## 4.3.  Scheduled Mode:

In  this  Mode,  the  Regulation  will  be  applied  to  the  Trains  running  in  the  Normal  Traffic Direction in accordance with the current Timetable. Trains running in the Reverse Traffic Direction are not regulated. In a little variant of this Mode, the Calendar Mode, an added Feature of Loading of Timetable automatically, predefined for each weekday in advance could also be made available.

## 7. LATS / CATS MANAGEMENT:

## 7. LATS / CATS MANAGEMENT:

The 'Control Level' Operations are used to transfer the 'Control' between an entire Local ATS  Sector  and  the  Central  ATS  and  vice-versa,  in  order  to  manage  Train  regulation Operations and Line Operating Mode.
With CATS, the Normal Mode of Operation, the Line Operating Modes available are Manual Mode, Constant Headway Mode and Scheduled Mode. LATS, however, allows the Constant Headway or Manual Modes as its Line Operating Modes.

## 9. TRANSFER OF CONTROL FROM CATS TO LATS:

## 9. TRANSFER OF CONTROL FROM CATS TO LATS:

Normally  the  Control  of the  Interlockings  remains  with  OCC  (Central  ATS  Traffic Controllers). But in certain situations, like performing of Shunting or Occurrence of some other  incident  requiring  Physical  Supervision  at  the  Local  Interlocking,  the  Transfer  of Control to the Local ATS may be required. Such Transfer of Control can be done in two ways - Normal Mode of Transfer and Emergency Mode of Transfer.
While  in  Local  ATS  both  the  Transfer  Modes  are  possible,  in  Central  ATS,  Emergency Transfer of Control Mode is not available.

## 10.1 CATS/LATS MMI Display Problem:

## 10.2 Safety Indicators :

Safety Indicators shall allow the ATS Operator to be sure that the MMI Client & Server are running in 'Coherence'. Before taking any Decision linked to Safety Control regarding a Sector, the ATS Operator shall, therefore, check the Status of following Safety Indicators:
(i) Date & Time Display: It should be the Current Date & Time. The Display is updated based  on  the  Time  Reference  received  from  ATS  Server.  Format  of  Date  shall  be 'dd/mm/yyyy' and Format of Time shall be 'hh:mm:ss'.
(ii) Monitor Indicator: Three Colour Controls (Red, Green & Blue) allow checking of the Fundamental Colours Availability. These Fundamental Colours are used to elaborate all other Colours. The Colours are updated cyclically by Rotation of the three Colours. The  successive  Display  indicates  that  the  Screen  is  refreshed.  If  Colours  are  not changing cyclically, this would indicate to the User that the Monitor or the Graphic Card is not functioning normally.
(iii) MMI-Server Link Indicator: This Animated Control Indicator allows checking the Link between the MMI Client and the Application Server. If the Link is Down, there shall be no Animation in this Window.
(iv) Interlocking and Server Data Acquisition Freezing Indicator: This Indicator shall indicate  the  Status  of  IXL  (Interlocking)  &  Server  Data  Acquisition.  It  is  refreshed cyclically and the Dynamic Animation indicates the Correct Communication between HMI Client & ASCV through Servers. 'Flashing Green' means that the Link is 'OK'. 'Steady Green' indicates Communication Problem and 'Red' shall mean that the Link is 'Not OK'.

(v) Not  Updated  Value  Indicator: When  an  Equipment  Value  is  'Not  Updated',  the Graphical Object shall be displayed in Black Colour. The ATS Operator, therefore, must check that the Colour of the Graphical Object, being viewed, is 'Not Black', as it would be a 'Not-Updated' State.
If  any one of above five Indicators show 'Mal-functioning / Stopped or Not-Updated', the Workstation should be treated as 'Failed' and the Control of Interlocking shall be switched over to CCIP, if the 'Level of Control' is at LATS or if the 'Level of Control' is at CATS, the Control of Interlocking shall be switched over to LATS. Monitoring can still be continued on MPD.
The 'Level of Control' switches to LATS Server, when the CATS Server is switched off.

## b.  ATS Alarm of SRRC Command :

The ATS raises an 'Alarm' in case the requested SRRC has not been correctly performed (as expected) by the CBI or ATC. The ATS Operator must, therefore, Check for 'Alarms' in the Alarm Bar, after executing a SRRC Command.
## c. Confirmation of the SRRC Command Set:

## c. Confirmation of the SRRC Command Set:

After Setting a SRRC Command (Examples: Signal / Points / Route - Blocking / Un-blocking, Setting  /  Release  of  Maintenance  Blocks  and  Setting  /  Release  of  TSRs  etc.),  the  ATS Operator  shall  attempt  to  execute  a  Conflicting  Command  and  see  that  the  intended Operation does not get executed by the Interlocking because of the Execution of the earlier SRRC Command.
For Example, Set a Route on a Blocked Route, Set an Incompatible Route encompassing a Route  Blocked  for  Maintenance  or  Operate  a  Blocked  Point  etc.  All  such  Conflicting Commands shall be rejected by the Interlocking. This shall prove that the SRRC Command in question has been correctly handled by the Interlocking. Rejection of the Command shall appear at the Top of the Screen in the Alarm Bar. If the Correct Protection is not achieved by the related 'Safety Related Remote Control', the action must not be 'Authorized'.

## 11. TEMPORARY SPEED RESTRICTION (TSR) MANAGEMENT:

The Temporary Speed Restriction  is  a  value  set  in  to  the  ATC  Sub-system  to  limit  the Running Speed when a special condition ours on the track, for example, Maintenance etc. These values can be set either by the ATS, or directly by the ATC Maintenance Terminal. TSR Values can be set in both Directions, the possible starting point and length is relative to list of track Portions and the track circuits, defined internally in to the ATC Sub-system.
A Track Segment including one or more Track circuits can be in Speed restriction during a given time period.
TSR is a High Integrity Level Control (HILC). The control is sent to the ATC Sub-system and if accepted, a Confirmation pop up Message is displayed. Second Operator Entry is required to confirm the Initial control and should be sent before '5' minutes, to be fully accepted by the ATC Sub-system.

## 13. TRAIN HOLD MANAGEMENT:

'Train Hold' is 'Advisory' in case of Trains running in ATP Mode and it is a 'Restriction' in case of Trains running in ATO Mode. 'Train Hold' Icon appears on the DMI after the Dwell Time Expiry.
The following 'Train Hold' States are available:
(i) Global Train Hold : The State is for the entire Line. It is a single Command issued for all Platforms at a time. It shall hold all Trains at their next platform Arrival.
(ii) Platform  Train  Hold: A  Manual  Control,  applied  at  any  time  by  the  Operator.  To release Trains of a given Platform, the Operator has to request 'Platform Release'.
It  may  be  noted  that  'Train  Hold  Management'  is  also  operated  'Automatically'  and simultaneously through the Tunnel ventilation management (TVM) Function. However, the Manual Operator Action train Hold 'Set / Release' has always 'Priority' on the Automatic one. This would mean that if the Operator has set a 'Manual Train Hold', and the TVM Function is identifying an 'Automatic Train Hold Release' Event, the Train is still 'Held' at the Platform until the Operator releases the 'Manual Train Hold', and vice-versa.

## Annexure 'A' (SC- 29A)
## OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR EXECUTION OF CRITICAL COMMANDS FOR LINE NO- 2

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This Procedure applies to OCC and all Stations of Line No- 2 for Safe Execution of Safety Critical Commands. This Procedure shall ensure that additional measures for execution of Critical Commands by the Chief Controller / Traffic Controller / Station Controller are followed properly and correctly for Safe Passage of Trains and Safety of Staff.

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and its amendments, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue for working of Trains on Line No- 2.
This  Procedure  also  reminds  the  Operator  -  TC  /  SC  about  his  /  her  responsibility  for additional Safety Measures which are required to be undertaken at the time of Execution of these Commands.

## 2. SCOPE

This Procedure is applicable for Line-2. Safety Critical Commands on Line No- 2 are identified as ' High Integrity Commands '.
Critical  /  High  Integrity  Commands are necessary to release or circumvent certain Safety Features built in the System with the complete Knowledge & Consent of the Operator, to deal with  certain  specific  Operational  Situations  or  some  Signalling  System  Anomalies.  The Operator,  therefore,  is  allowed  to  issue  Critical  Commands  with  additional  Measures  for Safeguarding and Control of critical Operations.
A Critical Command is programmed in such a way that its Issue shall have to be confirmed within a pre-determined time interval on the Central / Local ATS or CCIP, before it shall be executed by the Interlocking and / or ATP.
Before a Critical Command is executed the TC / SC must:
(i) Check if  the  Critical  Command  is  absolutely  necessary  or  if  it  can  be  avoided  by utilising another Alternative.
(ii) Ensure that using this Command does not in any way leads to Hazardous Situation.
(iii) Obtain  Permission  from  the  Chief  Controller,  who  shall  have  to  agree  that,  the conditions (i) & (ii) above are satisfied.
(iv) If TC / SC has any doubt about the Safety of using the envisaged Critical Command, in  combination with the necessary Measures, he / she must stop and check other Solutions or consult the Chief Controller & SGC.
(v) Use of Critical  Commands is recorded and numbered in the Log Lists of the ATS System and shall have to be checked periodically by the Chief Controller.
## 3. STEPS FOR EXECUTION OF HIGH INTEGRITY CONTROL COMMANDS:

## 3. STEPS FOR EXECUTION OF HIGH INTEGRITY CONTROL COMMANDS:

Execution of each High Integrity Control Command is done in '3' Steps:

## 3. STEPS FOR EXECUTION OF HIGH INTEGRITY CONTROL COMMANDS:

## 4.7. Automatic Train Regulation (ATR)

## 4.7. Automatic Train Regulation (ATR)

This dialogue is designed for the operation of automatic train regulation. The main tasks of the ATR are:
Determining dwell time.
Determining travelling time for a track section between two stations.
Releasing station stopping points.
Modifying the operation modes.
## Automatic Train Regulation

## Automatic Train Regulation

Automatic Train Regulation is responsible for calculation of Dwell time at a station when train id steps  to  a  station  PF  Berth  The  value  of  dwell  time  counter  depends  upon  the  dwell  time calculated  plus  12  sec  for  reaching  time  of  train  to  stopping  point  _On  expiry  of  dwell  time counter, operation stopping point (OSP)/8 car up and 8 car DN is released automatically. On releasing of these OSP's train will get target speed at PF to depart. After departure of train all OSP's will set to stop again.

It  is  possible  that  due  to  some  abnormal  behavior OSP may  not  release  after  expiry  of  dwell time  counter.  In  such  cases  Traffic  Controllers  can  release  OSP  through  ILD  Dialogue  using different OSR buttons for both directions and 8 Cars.
When  minimum  dwell  time  is  applied  to  a  train  at  a  PF  and  train  approaches  very  slowly towards stopping point, it can cause OSP to release on expiry of such dwell time even before the train reaches the stopping point. This will cause the train to skip the station as train will not find  stopping  point  at  PF.  If  observed  traffic  Controllers  should  warn  the  approaching  train operator  to  take  precaution  and  try  to  get  the  train  to  the  stopping  point  within  the  stipulated time.  Train  operator  should  also  remain  cautious  at  station  entry  and  if  he  feels  that  train  is going to skip station, he shall stop the train manually by applying EB.
Due  to  manual  stepping  of  train  id  or  wrong  stepping  of  train  id  due  to  some  track  circuit flickering,  dwell  time  counter  can  start  and  OSP  will  release  on  expiry  of  above  dwell  time counter,  if  observed  traffic  controller  should  warn  the  approaching  train  operator  to  take precaution to stop the train on PF manually.

In  case  of  ATS  server  crash  or  link  failure  to  interlocking.  OSP  of  that  area  are  managed  by SICAS.
OSP remains set if train Hold is applied on a platform for a train or all trains.
OSP is released for an approaching train if Skip train or Skip station is applied on a platform for a train or all trains.
Station Skip Stop:
When station skip stop is applied the trains bypass both the platforms without stopping there.
Train Skip Stop:
When a train is going to depot, without taking any passenger (for a specific platform), this state is applied for the next stations following the actual train position.

## V. OTBS Dialogue Description

This dialogue offers the possibility to allow only one train between two underground stations (or to withdraw this limitation).
That means, if OTBS is active: After the dwell time for a train in the respective station has run out, the ATR checks whether the track circuits from the current station to the next are clear. If they are clear,  the  ATR  releases  the  stopping  points  that  are  currently  set  and  thus  allows  the  train  to continue.  If  they  are  not  clear,  the  stopping  points  will  not  be  released.  In  this  case,  the  ATR repeats the check cyclically and releases the stopping points as soon as the result of the check is positive.

## 4.11.  FALKO Offline

Within  this  offline  system,  the  timetable  construction  component  is  used  to  build  up  complete daily timetables
in  a  graphical manner within a very short time - under consideration of the relevant operational aspects.  Using  highly  automated  generation  functions,  it  optimizes  vehicle  schedules  and generates an operative timetable with the precision of route segments.
Applying  an  event-based  simulator  the  resulting  behavior  of  the  railway  system  due  to  the constructed  timetable  can  be  imitated  realistically.  The  operability  of  regular  or  alternative timetables  with  respect  to  all  important  technical  and  operational  constraints  (e.g.  dynamic behavior of trains, switches and signals) can be verified.
The  detailed  investigation  of  the  generated  Time  table  is  performed  by  different  analysis functions.
After  verification  the  time  table  can  be  exported  to  the  FALKO  online  and  hence  available  for loading.
## 4.12.  FALKO Online

## 4.12.  FALKO Online

Once a timetable has been created and exported to the running system, FALKO online can be used, to modify a train schedule if  required.
Changes will only apply for the current time table, and have no effect to the stored schedule. If the  Temporary  modifications  are  not  needed  anymore,  the  imported  timetable  can  be  loaded again.

## O PERATING PROCEDURE FOR EXECUTION OF C RITICAL COMMANDS FOR LINE NOS. '3' & '4'

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

This Procedure shall ensure that additional measures for execution of Critical Commands by the Chief Controller  /  Traffic  Controller  /  Station  Controller/  DCC  are  followed  properly  and  correctly  for  Safe Passage of Trains and Safety of Staff.
The Procedure also reminds the Operator - TC / SC about his / her responsibility for additional Safety Measures which are required to be undertaken at the time of Execution of these Commands.

## 2.  Scope

This Procedure applies to OCC, DCC and all Stations of Line Nos. '3' & '4' for Safe Execution of Safety Critical Commands
This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.

## 3.  GENERAL

Critical / High Integrity Commands are necessary to release or circumvent certain Safety Features built in  the  System  with  the  complete Knowledge & Consent of the Operator, to deal with certain  specific Operational  Situations  or  some  Signaling  System  Anomalies.  The  Operator,  therefore,  is  allowed  to issue Critical Commands with additional Measures for Safeguarding and Control of critical Operations.
A Critical Command is programmed in such a way that its Issue shall have to be confirmed within a predetermined time interval on the Central / Local VDU, before it shall be executed by the Interlocking.
Before a Critical Command is executed the CC / TC / SC / DCC must:
3.1. Check if the Critical Command is absolutely necessary or if it can be avoided by utilising another Alternative.
3.2. Ensure that using this Command does not in any way leads to Hazardous Situation.
3.3. Obtain Permission from the Chief Controller, in case the Critical Command is used by TC, and from TC, in case it is used by SC. CC / TC, as the case may be, shall have to agree that the conditions 3.1 & 3.2 above are satisfied.
3.4. If TC / SC has any doubt about the Safety of using the envisaged Critical Command, in combination with the necessary Measures, he / she must stop and check other Solutions or consult the Chief Controller & FMC.
3.5. Use of Critical Commands is recorded and numbered in the Log Lists of the ATS System and shall have to be checked periodically by the Chief Controller.
## 4.  CRITICAL COMMANDS FOR SIGNALS :
## 4.1. Unlock Signal from Lock & Stop (SU):

## 4.1. Unlock Signal from Lock & Stop (SU):

Signals can be locked against Operation by means of 'SL' Command. Locking a Signal with a 'Clear'

## Introduction

Aspect automatically results in setting the Signal to 'Stop'. 'SU' Command is used to unlock a Locked Signal.

## Introduction

Before a Signal is Unlocked, the TC / SC must:
(i) Check that the reason for Locking the Signal is no longer necessary.
(ii) Check that the Signal is not required for another Route, which is not intended to be Set.
(iii)  Ensure that there are no Operational or Maintenance reasons existing to keep it Locked.
(iv)  Inform the Chief Controller / Traffic Controller.
## 5.  CRITICAL COMMANDS FOR TRACK SECTIONS:
## 5.1. Unlock Track for Route Setting (TSU):

## 5.1. Unlock Track for Route Setting (TSU):

Command 'TSL' locks a Track Section against an unintended Route Setting. With the execution of 'TSL' Command, the Operator ensures that any Route covering this Track Section cannot be 'Set'. Command 'TSU' is used to unlock a Track Section for Route Setting.
Before a Track Section is Unlocked for Route Setting, the TC / SC must:
(i) Ensure that the reason to Lock the Track Section is no longer valid.
(ii) Ensure  that  no  Operational  or  Maintenance  reasons  exist  to  prevent  the  Unlocking  of  the Track.
(iii) Ensure that no Train Proceeds un-intentionally in to the Track Section.
(iv) Obtain the Permission of Traffic Controller.
(v) Set the required Route Manually (if required).
(vi) Inform the relevant Train Operator accordingly (if required).
## 5.2. Track Release from Route (TSRR):

## 5.2. Track Release from Route (TSRR):

If  due  to  a  disturbance of the  Vacancy Detection System,  a  part of a Route comprising one or more elements has not been released by the Train Operated Route Release (TORR), the Track Sections still claimed by the Route can be released individually from the Route one after the other by this Command.
Before a Track Section is released, the TC / SC must:
(i) Ensure that the Track Section Release Operation shall not impair other Operations.
(ii) Ensure that the Track Section is not part of another Route or Overlap.
(iii) If  the Track Section to be released belongs to a Route such as an Overlap, ensure (with the train Operator / Driver) that a Train or Track Vehicle in the Track Section concerned has come to a Full Stop.
(iv) Obtain the Permission from the Traffic Controller.
## 5.3. Set Track Logically Free (TSCL):

## 5.3. Set Track Logically Free (TSCL):

After a Failure of Track Circuit Power Supply, all affected Sections are indicated as Logically Occupied.
The Command TSCL is designed to cancel a Logical Occupation of a Track. In order to 'Set' Track Logically Free, the TC / SC must:

## Introduction

(i) Attempt to release the Track using TSCL Command.

## Introduction

(ii) If  Step '(i)' fails,  check the  possible causes for an assumed incorrect Track Occupation from FMC.
(iii) Inform Chief Controller / Traffic Controller.
(iv) Retry to Set the Track Logically Free by TSCL Command.
(v) If  Step '(iv)' fails, instruct  the Train Operator to move his / her train in ROS Mode under the Procedure in vogue.
## 5.4. Release Speed Limit (RSDR):

## 5.4. Release Speed Limit (RSDR):

The Command RSDR is designed to release the Speed Limits imposed by Maintenance or Operations for Safety Reasons.
Before a 'Set' Speed Limit is released, the TC / SC must:
(i) Ensure that the cause for imposition of the Speed Limit has been resolved and that the written authority to release it has been received from the Maintenance Manager or the permission has been granted by the Traffic Controller.
(ii) Check that the new Speed Limit, now being 'Set' is not exceeding any other existing Speed Restriction on the Track section.
(iii) Inform the respective Maintenance Engineer and the Chief Controller / Traffic Controller.
## 6.  CRITICAL COMMANDS FOR POINTS:
## 6.1. Unlock Point for Throwing (PUT):

## 6.1. Unlock Point for Throwing (PUT):

Command 'PLT' locks a Point against an unintended Throwing Command. With the execution of 'PLT' Command, the  Operator  ensures  that  the  Points  cannot  be  thrown  in  any  case  either  by  Automatic Throw Operations by Route or by Flank Protection Requests or by Manual Requests.
The 'PUT' Command removes the Manually Set Lock on the Points. Route or Flank Protection Lockings are not affected by the 'PUT' Command.
Before a Point is Unlocked for Throwing, the TC / SC must:
(i) Ensure that the reason to Lock the Point is no longer valid.
(ii) Ensure that no Staff is endangered by this Operation, whenever applicable.
(iii) Obtain the Permission from Chief Controller / Traffic Controller.
(iv) Set the Access Signal to Stop, if required.
(v) Ensure that the Operation does not impair other Operations.
(vi) Ensure that the position of the Point at Site is correctly shown on the MMI.
## 6.2. Point Release from Route (PRR):

## 6.2. Point Release from Route (PRR):

If  due  to  a  disturbance of the  Vacancy Detection System,  a  part of a Route comprising one or more elements has not been released by the Train Operated Route Release (TORR), the Points still claimed by the Route can be released individually from the Route one after the other by this Command.
Before a Point is released by PRR Command, the TC / SC must:
(i) Confirm from TO / Driver that the Point is Clear from a Train / Vehicle. In case the Point is occupied or if there is  any  doubt  regarding  the  Clearance  of  the Point from Site,  no further action shall be taken until this is clarified and the Vehicle or Obstruction is confirmed 'Clear' by Physical Verification through SC / TO.

## Introduction

(ii) Ensure that the Point is not needed for another Route, Flank Protection or Overlap.

## Introduction

(iii) Confirm from TO / Driver that a Train or Vehicle running in a Route or Overlap to which the Point belongs, has stopped.
(iv) Obtain Permission from the Chief Controller / Traffic Controller.
## 6.3. Set Point Logically Free (PCL):

## 6.3. Set Point Logically Free (PCL):

After a Failure of Track Circuit Power Supply, all affected Sections are indicated as Logically Occupied.
The Command PCL is designed to cancel a Logical Occupation of a Point. In order to 'Set' the Point Logically Free, the TC / SC must:
(i) Attempt to release the Point using PCL Command.
(ii) If  Step  '(i)'  fails,  check  the  possible  causes for an assumed incorrect Point Occupation from FMC.
(iii) Ensure that no Maintenance Reasons exist against the Setting of the Point Logically Free.
(iv) Ensure that the Point is not needed for another Route, Flank Protection or Overlap.
(v) Ensure that the Train or Vehicle running in a Route or Overlap to which the Point belongs, has stopped.
(vi) Inform Chief Controller / Traffic Controller.
(vii) Retry to Set the Point Logically Free by PCL Command.
(viii) If Step '(vii)' fails, Instruct the Train Operator of next Train to move his / her train in ROS Mode under the Procedure in vogue.
## 6.4. Enforce Throw Point (ETP):

## 6.4. Enforce Throw Point (ETP):

The Command ETP is used to throw Points that are indicated as Occupied, although they should be Free.
Before it is allowed to throw a Point using the Command ETP, the TC / SC must confirm from the Driver / TO, if a Vehicle / Train is involved, that the Vehicle / Train has come to a 'Stop' and is standing 'Clear' of the Point in question and if there is no Vehicle / Train then the SC shall visit the Site and confirm the Clearance of the Point.
If  the  Point  has  been  claimed  by  a  Route  or  for  Flank  Protection  or  if  the  Point  is  blocked  against moving or if indicated as 'Trailed', the Command ETP is rejected.
## 6.5. Throw Trailed Point (TTP):

## 6.5. Throw Trailed Point (TTP):

If  a  Point  loses  its  Point  Detection  without  Throwing  Command,  a  Trailing  Indication  for  this  Point  is raised and Trailing of this Point by an Un-Controlled Vehicle Movement is assumed.
If a Point is indicated as 'Trailed', both Automatic (by Route Setting) as well as Manual Points Throwing Commands are rejected.
TTP Command is to be used in following Situations to synchronize the Element Control Unit with the Central Interlocking Logic of the Interlocking System:
(i) On Main Line:
(a) After every use of Crank Handle.
(b) If  a Text Message 'Command rejected by the Interlocking 'IXL' appears in the Dialog Box, after giving the TP Command without Trail through Indication on the Point.

## Introduction

(ii) In the Depot:

(a) After every use of Crank Handle.
(b) If  a Text Message 'Command rejected by the Interlocking 'IXL' appears in the Dialog Box, after giving the TP Command without Trail Through Indication on the Point.
(c) If  a  Trail  Through  Indication  (Flashing  Indication  of  Point  in  'N'  and  'R'  both  directions) appears on the VDU.
Before  a  Trailed  Point  in  the  Depot  can  be  switched  to  a  Normal  Locked  Position  with  the  TTP Command, the DCC must:
(a) If a Train is involved, ensure it is stopped immediately. Do not allow it to proceed until it is checked  and  confirmation  is  given  that  it  shall  complete  any  remaining  portion  of  the Traversing Movement safely.
(b) Issue a Track Possession to a qualified Person to check and report on the Status of the Trailed Set of Points.
When a Point in the Depot is not damaged, but is in the wrong Position, the DCC can use the TPP Command. In this case, the DCC must:
(a) Check the position of the Point reported from Site with the Indicated Position on the MMI, after the Point has come to an End Position.
(b) Confirm that any Train involved is 'Clear' of the Moving Elements of the Point.
(c) Change the Point to other position and check if the point is working correctly.
(d) Lock the Point Manually, if required to make it Safe.
(e) Log the Locked Point in the Log Book and inform the Personnel concerned.

(d) Lock the Point Manually, if required to make it Safe.
(e) Log the Locked Point in the Log Book and inform the Personnel concerned.
Since the Line shall operate mostly in ATP Mode with a higher Degree of Route Protection, the Points on the  Line  cannot  be  trailed  without  causing Damage to them.  If the  Point  is  on  the  Line,  a  proper Inspection of the Point must be done by the Track Maintenance before it may be operated again. It may be clamped in to a Position with a Point Lock until repaired or released for normal Operations by the Maintenance Department.
## 6.6. Unlock Point for Route Setting (PSU):

## 6.6. Unlock Point for Route Setting (PSU):

Command 'PSL' locks Points against Route Setting. Command 'PSU' is designed to remove that Lock from the Point.
Before a Point is Unlocked for Route Setting, the TC / SC must:
(i) Ensure that the reason to Lock the Point is no longer valid and send a Person to the Site to confirm that the set of Points are Free.
(ii) Ensure that the point is not needed for another route or Overlap.
(iii) Ensure that no Operational or maintenance reasons exist against Unlocking the Point.
(iv) Obtain Permission from the Traffic Controller.
## 6.7.  Release Speed Limit (RSDR):

## 6.7.  Release Speed Limit (RSDR):

The Command RSDR is designed to release the Speed Limits imposed by Maintenance or Operations for Safety Reasons.
Before a 'Set' Speed Limit is released, the TC / SC must:

## Introduction

(i) Ensure that the cause for imposition of the Speed Limit has been resolved and that the written authority to release it has been received from the Maintenance Manager or the permission has been granted by the Traffic Controller.

## Introduction

(ii) Check that the new Speed Limit, now being 'Set' is not exceeding any other existing Speed Restriction on the Point.
(iii) Inform the respective Maintenance Engineer and the Chief Controller / Traffic Controller.
Command 'RSDR' shall have to be inputted by the Station Controller, within 10 Sec. of twisting of the Key by JE/Sig. in the Rememo Box provided in the SER.
## 7.  CRITICAL COMMANDS FOR INTERLOCKING:
## 7.1.  Release Command after Starting (RCAS):

## 7.1.  Release Command after Starting (RCAS):

When an Interlocking Computer  has  been 'Reset',  the  TC  /  SC  must  release  the  Interlocking  by  an Operational Command and before executing this 'Release' Command, the TC / SC must:
(i) Receive Information from FMC that the Interlocking is 'Reset'.
(ii) Inform Chief Controller / Traffic Controller.
After Releasing the Interlocking, the TC / SC must:
(i) Ensure all previous Locks (Routes, Signals, & Points etc.) are restored.
(ii) Check which Signals can be Unlocked.
(iii) Check where the Automatic Route Calling can be Turned 'ON'.
(iv) Check where Speed limit or Locks have to be Set.
## 7.2.  Setting all Track sections in an Interlocking Area Logically Free (SATF):

## 7.2.  Setting all Track sections in an Interlocking Area Logically Free (SATF):

After  System  Restart,  all  track  circuits  of  the  interlocking  are  considered  as  Logically  Occupied.  The Command  'Setting  all  Track  sections  Logically  Free'  is  used  to  set  all  Track  circuits  of  a  complete Interlocking Area Logically Free.
Before this Command is executed, the TC / SC must:
(i) Check the possible Signaling Causes for this Incident.
(ii) Ensure that no Train or Vehicle is affected.
(iii) Ensure that no Operational or Maintenance reasons exist against executing the Command.
(iv) Obtain Permission from Traffic Controller.
## 7.3.  Enforce Take Control (ETC):

## 7.3.  Enforce Take Control (ETC):

With this Command, the Station Controller can take over the Control of an Interlocking Area by Force. However,  before  executing  this  Command,  the  SC  should  preferably  talk  to  the  Controller  that  is currently responsible for Operations over this Area.
This  Command,  in  any  case,  does  not  affect  or  bypass  any  Interlocking  of  the  Safety  Logic  of  the Interlocking.

## 4.0 PROCEDURE  FOR  MOVEMENT  OF  TRAIN  IN  UTOMODE-:

Following conditions shall be fulfill before induction of train from Depot/siding in UTO mode
Mode  selector  in  AUTO  position in  both  CABs.
UTO  needs  to  be  selected  from DMI by  pressing UTO  button  and  then  ACK  button  on DMI. '
After  UTO  selection, verify  symbol  'U'  is  displayed on DMI at  current  mode  position.
EB  to be  released  from DMI  (if  required).
If the train is properly berthed, then train will automatically depart after  finish of DWELL  Time. If  the train is not properly  berthed, then the train needs  to be moved  in ATP  mode  or  Rev. mode  (As  the case may  be)  for  some  distance  for  proper  berthing and then stop  and  select  UTO  mode, reset EB remotely  or  from DMI (if  required) and then  take  'Departure'  command  from  TC/SC  (CATS/LATS/VDUV)  to  depart.
.
When any train is inducted in UTO mode, TC has to ensure from OCC  that SCS switch  status  is  NORMAL  of  both  the  CABs. a)
The platform side doors will be enabled, when  the train has stopped within stopping window. Saloon doors and PSD will be opened automatically. The train and PSD doors  will be closed  automatically  at  the  end  of  dwell  time.

## Sub:-    Safety  Circular-10  (Rev-06)  regarding  'Joint  Procedure  Order  to  Cut-Off  the  OHE Supply by Operating the ETS/BLS Plunger at Under-Ground Section'.

Find enclosed Safety Circular-10 (Rev-06) regarding 'Joint Procedure Order to Cut-Off the OHE Supply by Operating the ETS/BLS Plunger at Under-Ground Section'.
All concerned are to ensure that staff working under them have read and understood the procedure and assurance regarding the same is taken.
This is issued with the approval of the competent authority.
## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 10 (REV-06)

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 10 (REV-06)

(Rajesh Kumar Raghav) Sr. DGM/Ops/Cord.
Copy to: -
All EDs/HODs (O&M) and DG (DMRC Academy), All Dy. HODs (O&M), Mgr/AM (Concerned Line, Station and OCC), All Stations, All Crew Controls, All DCC and DMRC Academy.
## SAFETY CIRCULAR-10 (REV-06)
## JOINT PROCEDURE ORDER TO CUT -OFF THE OHE SUPPLY BY OPERATING THE ETS/BLS PLUNGER AT UNDER-GROUND SECTION

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This  procedure covers the responsibilities of metro employees and the methodology to be followed by them in regard to operation of Emergency Trip System (ETS/BLS), installed in under-ground  stations  of  DMRC,  to  switch-off  the  OHE  in  the  event  of  arising  out  of  an emergent situation.

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure order shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and its amendment, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
## 3.0 GENERAL INSTRUCTION

## 3.0 GENERAL INSTRUCTION

(i) The overhead line equipment means:
(a) Contact Wire
(b) Messenger Wire
(c) Registration arm
(d) Insulator
(e) Any other wire wires or support brackets
(f) Arcing or fusing on the overhead line equipment either continuous or intermittent.
Any staff who observes damage to damage to the overhead line equipment must note the  location  and,  if  possible,  the  identification  of  the  nearest  overhead  line  support structure (mast) and the Chainage. In case minimum safety radius of 2 meters is likely to  be  infringed,  must  inform  TPC,  by  most  expeditious  means  to  switch  off  Traction Power Supply.
(ii) The means to be used for such emergency communication may include:
(a) TETRA hand set via the Traffic Controller or Station Controller or Maintenance Controller or direct
(b) Telephone via the SCR or direct
(c) Train Radio
(d) Mobile telephone
(e) Emergency telephone provided at BLS
(f) Help point phone
(iii) The request must specify:
(a) The track concerned (Up, Down, Depot line etc.)
(b) The station or inter-station section.
(c) The nearest overhead line support (mast) identification number or signal number (if visible) and Chainage.
(d) The reason for the request.
## 4.0 PART-A (APPLICABLE FOR UNDERGROUND SECTION OF LINE - 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 & 9)
## 4.1 Location of Emergency Trip Systems (ETS/BLS):

## 4.1 Location of Emergency Trip Systems (ETS/BLS):

Emergency Trip Systems (ETS/BLS) are provided at following locations:
(i) 02 ETS/BLS Boxes (One for UP Line and another for DN Line) are installed at each SCR except Integrated SCR of two lines at Interchange stations where 04 ETS/BLS Boxes are installed (02 for each line).

## Introduction

(ii) In the Tunnel near cross-passages (Nearest OHE mast location UP/DN is given in the Annexure-A for ease of identification.)

## Introduction

(iii) Total 04 ETS/BLS boxes are installed at platform area {except in underground section of L-6 (KG-JNPH), L-7, L-8, L-9}, 01 ETS/BLS at both ends of each platform i.e. 02 on UP Line and 02 on DN Line.
Note:ETS/BLS is not available, only Emergency telephone/ Hot line is available on platforms in  underground  section  of  L-6  (KG-JNPH),  L-7,  L-8  &  L-9.  Total  04  Emergency telephone/ Hot line are installed at platform area, 01 Emergency telephone/ Hot line at both ends of each platform i.e. Two on UP Line and two on DN Line.
The  other  details  of  ETS/BLS  viz.  Auto/Manual  reset  feature,  the  communication  facility available near different ETS/BLS locations are given in the following table:

## Introduction

If TC does not respond to call made from Emergency telephone, call gets diverted to TPC of respective line.
The  Emergency  Telephone  Numbers  near  ETS/BLS  and  their  nearest  OHE  mast locations are attached as Annexure-B .
## Instructions Affixed on ETS/BLS:

## Instructions Affixed on ETS/BLS:

In Case of Emergency Break Glass with Hammer

## Instructions Affixed on ETS/BLS:

Press Red Push Button Switch until Red LED Glows.
Inform OCC with Emergency Telephone.
Reset  Key  Is  Available  with  Station  Controller.  ETS/BLS  shall  be  Reset  by  Station Controller after completion of  w ork.
## 4.2 Procedure for Operation of ETS/BLS:

## 4.2 Procedure for Operation of ETS/BLS:

(i) In case of any Emergency situation, where it becomes necessary to switch off the OHE, the Glass cover of the Plunger (ETS/BLS) shall be broken with the hammer provided therein  and  the  Plunger  shall  be  pressed  until  Red  LED  starts  glowing.  However, confirmation is required from OCC to ensure dead status of OHE section.
(ii) For UG section of Line-2, 3 & 6 (CTST - JGPA) :-
Pressing of ETS/BLS plunger shall automatically switch off the 25 KV traction supply of the respective elementary section. When ETS/BLS is operated, an audio-visual alarm shall be generated in the TPC workstation which will indicate the location of ETS/BLS from where it is operated. Also the respective ETS/BLS icon in the ETS/BLS synoptic at TPC Work-station shall flicker in red color. TPC shall not take any action to recharge the OHE, until clearance is given by TC.
## For UG section of Line-6 (KG-JNPH), 7, 8 & 9 :-

## For UG section of Line-6 (KG-JNPH), 7, 8 & 9 :-

Pressing of ETS/BLS plunger shall automatically switch off the 25 KV traction supply of the NS-NS or NS-Dead end of both UP and DN Line.) When ETS/BLS is operated, an audio-visual  alarm  shall  be  generated  in  the  TPC  workstation  which  will  indicate  the location of ETS/BLS from where it is operated. Also the respective ETS/BLS icon in the ETS/BLS synoptic at TPC Work-station shall flicker in red color. Command block icon shall  also  appear  on  the  respective  CBs/BMs  associated  with  tripping  logic  of  this ETS/BLS.
(iii) TPC shall immediately inform to the traffic controller  of the concerned line about the ETS/BLS operation  with  location  details  of  ETS/BLS  and  OHE  status  (Live/Dead)  of section affected, under the exchange of private numbers.
(iv) The person, who had pressed the ETS/BLS Plunger shall contact the Traffic controller through  telephone  or  Hot  Line  connection  provided  near  the  ETS/BLS  box  and communicate  the  reasons  for  which  ETS/BLS  Plunger  was  pressed  by  him,  duly indicating  his  Name  and  Designation.  If  no  one  reports  to  OCC,  Para  4.3  shall  be followed.
## (v) For UG section of Line-2, 3 & 6 (CTST - JGPA) :-

## (v) For UG section of Line-2, 3 & 6 (CTST - JGPA) :-

On getting the information of ETS/BLS operation & OHE section affected, TC shall ask TO  of  train  (approaching  affected  OHE  section  of  operated  ETS/BLS)  to  stop  at preceding platform to avoid entry of approaching train from live OHE section to dead OHE section.

## For UG section of Line-6 (KG-JNPH), 7, 8 & 9 :-

On getting the information of ETS/BLS operation & OHE section affected, TC shall ask TO  of  train  (approaching  affected  OHE  section  of  operated  ETS/BLS)  to  stop  at preceding platform to avoid entry of approaching train from live OHE section to dead OHE section. Thereafter, on advice of TC, TPC shall charge all elementary sections

## Introduction

except OHE of affected elementary section (where ETS has been operated).

(vi) If any train happens to be at overlap of affected elementary section, TO shall find some of the pantographs in live section and other in dead section. TO shall inform the same to TC. TC shall ask TO to down the pantograph in the dead OHE section and move towards Live OHE section by using pantograph of Live OHE as per directions of TC. In case of any other abnormality such as paralleling of overlap by pantograph (detected by charging of affected elementary section), TO shall come out of the train and check the physical condition of pantograph and inform TC accordingly for further directions
(vii) TC shall confirm the OHE dead status from TPC and then confirm it to to the person who had pressed the ETS/BLS Plunger, if he/she can be contacted directly or through the nearest station staff, about the switched-off status of the traction supply of that section. Traffic  Controller  shall  also  inform  the  incident  to  SC  of  that/nearest  station  with  the instructions to keep a watch on the situation, render whatever help could immediately be extended by him and keep the Traffic Controller informed about the development of the situation.
(viii)  Even after the ETS/BLS is operated and OHE dead status has been confirmed, no one shall try to climb on the roof of the train or infringe the '2' meters danger zone from the OHE. Any work within ' 2 ' meters of OHE shall be carried out under provision of Shadow Power block as per SC-02.

(ix) IF ETS/BLS is not available at Platform then in case of any Emergency situation, where it is necessary to switch off the OHE, the person available at platform, shall contact the TC through emergency telephone, duly indicating his Name (and Designation) and report abnormality and reason for which OHE de-energization is required. TC shall ask TPC to de-energize OHE from NS-NS or NS-dead end (as per location of ETS). Simultaneously, TC shall also ask TO to stop the train to prevent entering in affected area. After getting confirmation of OHE dead from TPC, TC shall confirm OHE dead status to respective person and Para-4.2 (v) to Para-4.2(viii) shall be followed.
## 4.3 If ETS/BLS is operated and no one reports about it then following action should be taken as per location of the ETS/BLS:

## 4.3 If ETS/BLS is operated and no one reports about it then following action should be taken as per location of the ETS/BLS:

(i) At Platform (if ETS/BLS is available)
(a) TC shall ask SC to check the vicinity for any abnormality near identified ETS/BLS and report the status to TC/OCC.
(b) If any abnormality is reported by SC, Para-4.2 (v) to 4.2 (viii) shall be followed.
(c) If no abnormality is found and ETS/BLS is in operated condition (Glass Broken), SC  shall  seek  permission  from  TC  for  resetting  the  ETS/BLS.  On  getting permission, SC shall  reset  the  ETS/BLS and then  inform TC/OCC accordingly, under the exchange of private number.
(d) If ETS/BLS glass is found in intact condition, SC shall report the same to TC/OCC, who in turn shall ask the TPC to disable the ETS/BLS and inform the concerned SCADA  Staff  to attend the ETS/BLS. After disabling the ETS/BLS, OHE may be charged through forced operation by TPC.
## (ii) In tunnel:

## (ii) In tunnel:

If train operation is normal and ETS of tunnel is operated without any communication to OCC, TC shall ask TPC to disable the ETS/BLS and charge OHE of affected section. OCC/TC shall instruct the TOs of train approaching the location of operated ETS in both directions  to  restrict  the  train  speed  to  25  Kmph,  keep  a  sharp  look  out  and  move cautiously to report anything unusual in the vicinity. If nothing unusual is reported, the

## Introduction

concerned SCADA staff shall be instructed to attend the ETS/BLS. If any abnormality is reported by TO, Para-4.2(v) to 4.2(viii) shall be followed.
## (iii) SCR

## (iii) SCR

TC shall ask SC to report cause of operation and ETS/BLS status to OCC/TC.
If nothing unusual is reported, TC shall ask TPC to charge OHE of affected section. If any abnormality requiring switching off of OHE supply is reported by SCR, step 4.2(v) to 4.2(viii) shall be followed.
## 4.4 Procedure for resetting the ETS/BLS:

## 4.4 Procedure for resetting the ETS/BLS:

The  ETS/BLS  once  pressed  shall  remain  in  pressed  (operated)  condition  and  has  to  be released  with  a  key  to  resume  normal  working.  ETS/BLS  reset  keys  are  secured  with  the Station Controller in emergency key hive. After completion of work on OHE, Station Controller shall reset the ETS/BLS after taking permission from TC by inserting the key in to plunger and moving it clockwise. Once the ETS/BLS is reset, Red LED shall turn off. The Station Controller shall thereafter inform the Traffic Controller about the resetting of ETS/BLS.
Station Controller, while moving to the ETS/BLS location to reset the ETS/BLS, shall carry the loudhailer with him to announce, for the benefit of staff working in the vicinity, that the ETS/BLS is now being reset by him.
After resetting of the ETS/BLS, the Standard Procedure of Cancellation of Power Block, Traffic block and Permit to work etc. shall be followed. The ETS/BLS box shall be restored in its original status by SCADA staff for use in future.
## 4.5 ETS/BLS Disable Function:

## 4.5 ETS/BLS Disable Function:

ETS/BLS Disable function has been provided with the TPC to take care of the malfunction / spurious tripping of ETS/BLS. This function however shall be used with great care by the TPC only in assured cases of malfunctioning of ETS/BLS, resulting in frequent tripping and when the ETS/BLS could not be reset due to the failure of ETS/BLS reset mechanism.
TPC shall disable the ETS/BLS only after taking clearance from TC, under the exchange of private number. After disabling the ETS/BLS, OHE may be charged through forced operation by TPC.
SCADA Staff shall be immediately deputed by the TPC to examine the ETS/BLS mechanism and  set  right  the  failure  after  taking  PTW.  However,  ETS/BLS  installed  in  tunnel  shall  be examined  during  non-revenue  hours.  After  rectification  of  problem,  TPC  shall  enable  the ETS/BLS in question to make it ready to cater for any further eventuality.
## 5.0 PART-B (APPLICABLE FOR AIRPORT EXPRESS LINE)
## 5.1 Locations of Emergency Trip System (ETS/BLS)

## 5.1 Locations of Emergency Trip System (ETS/BLS)

Emergency trip systems (ETS) are provided at following locations:
(i) 02 ETS/BLS (One for UP Line and another for DN Line) are installed at each SCR.
(ii) 01 ETS/BLS at each platform end of both UP and DN lines. Total 04 ETS/BLS boxes are installed at platform area of SJSU, DKV, DACY, DSTO each while 08 ETS/BLS boxes are installed at platform area of NDRU and APOT each and there are no ETS/BLS boxes installed at platform area of IICC.
(iii) 04 ETS/BLS are installed at Tunnel Ventilation Building near Dhaula Kuan, 02 ETS/BLS are installed at Park Street RSS and '02' ETS/BLS at Airport RSS are installed.
(iv) In the Tunnel near cross-passage (UP/DN), nearest OHE mast location is given in the

## Introduction

Annexure'A' for ease of identification.

## Introduction

(v) Emergency  Telephone  along  with  ETS/BLS  are  provided  only  at  cross  passage  of underground section in New Delhi to IICC section and along with ETS/BLS of platform level at IICC station only (List added with Annexure-B ). Emergency Telephone are not provided  with  ETS/BLS  of  elevated  section.  The  other  details  of  ETS/BLS  viz. Auto/Manual reset feature, the communication facility available near different ETS/BLS locations are given in the following table:

### Introduction

| Section    | No. of ETS/BLS   | Reset Feature of the ETS/BLS   | Communication Arrangement             | Communication Arrangement                                             | Communication Arrangement                                                                                        |
|------------|------------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Section    | No. of ETS/BLS   | Reset Feature of the ETS/BLS   | SCR                                   | Tunnel                                                                | Platform                                                                                                         |
| NDRU- DSTO | 184              | Auto Reset                     | Standard Telephone is provided in SCR | Hot line (Emergency telephone) with audio indication is provided near | Standard telephone provided in PSB and Help point has been provided at each platform.                            |
| DSTO- IICC | 184              | Manual Reset                   | Standard Telephone is provided in SCR | BLS to call TPC. Audio ringing provided TPC/TC call back phone.       | Standard telephone provided in PSB and Emergency Telephone has been provided to BLS at the end of each platform. |

## Introduction

Instructions affixed on telephone (TUNNEL):'IN CASE OF ANY EMERGENCY, PICK THE RECEIVER OF EMERGENCY TELEPHONE TO INFORM TRACTION POWER CONTROLER'.
Instructions affixed on Manual Call Point (Platform): 'IN CASE OF EMERGENCY, PUSH BUTTON TO INFORM SCR'
(vi) Further, in station control rooms, the Blue Light Stations shall be integrated with IBP panel. In case of activation of plunger at IBP panel, the connected BLS shall be activated and related actions as per de-energization scheme shall be activated.
(vii) Functioning of Blue Light Station to switch off traction power is kept disabled & 'NOT IN USE CAUTION" is displayed on each BLS, the emergency phone/help point phone is to be used for informing the Traction Power Controller/Traffic Controller for emergency switching off power in case of any serious abnormality or unsafe situation to possibly prevent the approaching train.
## 5.2 Operation of ETS/BLS:

## 5.2 Operation of ETS/BLS:

(i) When ETS/BLS available at platform/tunnel/cross passage is operated, an audio-visual alarm  will  be  generated  in  the  TPC  workstation  which  will  indicate  the  location  of ETS/BLS from where it is operated. Also the respective ETS/BLS icon in the ETS/BLS synoptic at TPC Work-station shall flickers in red color.
(ii) TPC shall immediately inform the ETS/BLS operation with location details of ETS/BLS and OHE section affected to the traffic controller, under the exchange of private numbers.
(iii) Pressing of the ETS/BLS Plunger will automatically switch off the 25KV Traction Supply to the relevant OHE section and the adjacent section in the direction of travel of train will be de-energized automatically through SCADA. When ETS is operated, an Audiovisual

## Introduction

alarm will be generated in the TPC, which will indicate the location of ETS from where it is operated. Also the respective ETS in the ETS synoptic at the TPC workstation flicker in Red color. TPC shall inform the ETS operation with location details to traffic controllers under exchange of private numbers. TPC shall not recharge the OHE until clearance is given by TC.

(iv) The person, who had pressed the ETS/BLS Plunger if happens to be the DMRC staff, shall contact the TC/TPC through the telephone near the ETS box (as described in the table) and convey the reason for which ETS plunger has been pressed duly indicating his name and designation. This phone connects to TC or TPC (in case of Airport Express Line) immediately when receiver is lifted from cradle.
(v) TPC shall check the OHE Dead status from the TPC workstation and shall confirm the same to TC under exchange of private number. TC shall contact the person who has pressed the ETS directly, if he/she can be contacted directly or through Station Staff, about  the  switched-off  Status  of  the  Traction  Supply  of  that  section.  Station  of  that nearest station shall also be informed by TC who shall keep Traffic Controller informed about the situation.
(vi) If person operating the ETS informs OCC, Para-5.3(i) to 5.3(viii) shall be followed. If no one  reports  about  it,  then  following  action  should  be  taken  as  per  location  of  the ETS/BLS.
(a) At Platform
TC shall ask SC of respective station to check the platform area for any abnormality and  report  the  status  to  OCC/TC.  If  abnormality  is  reported  by  SCR,  requiring switching off of OHE supply Para-5.3(i) to 5.3(viii) shall be followed.
(b) In tunnel :

(b) In tunnel :
OCC/TC will instruct the TOs of train approaching the location in both directions to restrict the train speed to 25 Kmph, keep a sharp look out and move cautiously to report anything unusual in the vicinity. If nothing unusual is reported, the concerned SCADA  staff  shall  be  instructed  to  attend  the  ETS/BLS.  If  any  abnormality  is reported by TO, Para-5.3(i) to 5.3(viii) shall be  followed.
## 5.3 Procedure for Switching off OHE supply by communication with OCC and / or Operation of ETS/BLS

## 5.3 Procedure for Switching off OHE supply by communication with OCC and / or Operation of ETS/BLS

(i) Communication with OCC (In case of emergency at platform)
(a) In case of any Emergency situation, where it becomes necessary to switch off the OHE, the person available at platform, shall contact the SCR through manual call point, duly indicating his Name & Designation and report abnormality and reason for which OHE de-energization is required. SC shall inform the same to TC.
(b) TC shall ask TPC to de-energize OHE from NS-NS or NS-dead end of both UP/DN line (as per location of ETS). After getting confirmation of OHE dead from TPC, TC shall confirm OHE dead status to respective person.
(ii) Communication with OCC (In case of emergency in tunnel)
(a) In case of any Emergency situation, where it becomes necessary to switch off the OHE, the person available  at tunnel, shall  contact the  TPC through emergency telephone, duly indicating his Name (and Designation) and report abnormality and reason for which OHE de-energization is required. TPC shall inform the same to TC.
(b) Under advice of TC, TPC shall de-energize OHE from NS-NS or NS-dead end of

## Introduction

both UP/DN line (as per location of ETS). After getting confirmation of OHE dead from TPC, TC shall confirm OHE dead status to respective person.

(iii) TC shall ask TO of train (which may approach affected OHE elementary section after charging  of  rest  of  the  section)  to  remain  at  preceding  platform  to  avoid  entry  of approaching train from live OHE to dead OHE section. TC shall also ask TO of train behind  NS  (which  may  approach  OHE  elementary  sections  except  the  affected elementary section, until clearance is given by TC.
If any train happens to be at overlap of affected elementary section, TC shall ask TO to down the pantograph of dead OHE and move towards healthy OHE section by using pantograph of live OHE as per directions of TC.
(iv) In case of any other abnormality such as paralleling of overlap by pantograph (detected by charging of affected elementary section), TO will come out of the train and check the physical condition of pantograph and inform TC accordingly for further  directions.
(v) TC shall also instruct SCR of that/nearest station with the instructions to keep a watch on the situation, render whatever help could immediately be extended by him and keep the traffic controller inform about the development of the situation.
(vi) Even after the ETS/BLS is operated and OHE dead status has been confirmed, no one shall try to climb on the roof of the train or infringe the '02' meters danger zone from the OHE. Any work within '02' meters of OHE shall be carried out after earthing the OHE by using discharge rods by competent staff.

(vii) In case power block is required to work within '02' meters of OHE, TPC shall ask OHE Supervisor on duty to rush OHE Maintenance Team at site. Power block shall be granted to  OHE  supervisor.  OHE  Supervisor  may  also  grant  shadow  power  block  to  station controller authorized to provide discharge rod as per safety circular SC-02. Any work on the OHE, however, shall be carried out only after ensuring earthing of the OHE.
(viii)  After competition of work, the Standard Procedure of Cancellation of Power Block, Traffic block and Permit to work etc. shall be followed. The ETS/BLS box shall be restored in its original status by SCADA staff for use in future.
## 5.4 Procedure for Resetting the ETS (Blue Light Station):

## 5.4 Procedure for Resetting the ETS (Blue Light Station):

(i) Blue light Station once pressed is automatically reset but OHE of concerned section is charged by TPC after following procedure in vogue.
(ii) There may be some instance of ETS/BLS operation unnecessarily by some miscreant. If  nobody  reports  OCC  about  the  operation  of ETS, TC  shall  ask  SC of  that/nearest station to check the concerned ETS/BLS and any abnormality in the section.SC shall check the respective ETS and the concerned section. If no abnormality is observed, SC shall inform the same to TC.TC shall then give clearance to TPC to charge the OHE under exchange of private numbers.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR-29 C (Rev.-03)
## CATS OPERATION PROCEDURE OF ATS OVER LINE - 5 & 6

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This  procedure  order  covers  the  working  of  CATS  operation  and  also  describes  the procedures  to  transfer  the  control  among  CATS  users  (OCC  Traffic  Controllers)  to  LATS users (SCR Station Controllers) or vice versa to have the operation & overview of the train movement and the Signaling gears status in the LINE 05 & 06.

## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 and Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules, 2022, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue for  working  of  Trains  between  Kashmere  Gate  -  Raja Nahar  Singh  (LINE  -06)  and Brig. Hoshiar Singh - Inderlok (LINE-05).

## 3.0 System of Working

Under ATS in  manual  mode,  when  level  of  control  is 'Local' Each  IXL  Station  (Inderlok, Paschim Vihar West, Nangloi, Mundka, Tikri Kalan, Brig. Hoshiar Singh, Central Secretariat,

## Introduction

Lajpat  Nagar,  Nehru  Place,  Sarita  Vihar  and  Badarpur  can  control  their  Interlocking  or Authority  Area  assigned  to  them  from  their  ATS  workstation.  When  level  of  control  is 'CENTRAL' ,  all  other  secondary  station  can  only  monitor  the  main  line  (their  respective interlocking area). All controllers are able to consult all the views simultaneously. But only one controller  (local  station,  depot,  central)  at  a  time  is  allowed  to  send  control  towards  one Interlocking.

## Introduction

The  CENTRAL  ATS  will  assign  train  identification  numbers  &  provide  all  necessary  train information to the operator.
When CATS is restarted or initialized level of control is at Local. When LATS & CATS both are restarted level of control is at 'VDU'. Further change of level is only possible with mutual consent of both LATS and CATS users. Normally the control of all Interlocking should be with OCC Controllers with level of control being 'CENTRAL'.
