## Annexure 'A' (SC-29C)
## OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR EXECUTION OF CRITICAL COMMANDS FOR LINE NOs. '5 & 6'

## 1.0 SCOPE:

This Procedure applies to OCC and all Stations of Line Nos. '5' & '6' for Safe Execution of Safety  Critical  Commands.  This  Procedure  shall  ensure  that  additional  measures  for execution  of  critical  Commands  by  the  Chief  Controller  /  Traffic  Controller  /  Station Controller  are  followed  properly  and  correctly  for  Safe  Passage  of  Trains  and  Safety  of Staff.

## 1.0 SCOPE:

This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
The  Procedure  also  reminds  the  Operator  -  TC  /  SC  about  his  /  her  responsibility  for additional Safety Measures which are required to be undertaken at the time of Execution of these Commands.
## 2.0 GENERAL:

## 2.0 GENERAL:

Critical Commands are necessary to release or circumvent certain Safety Features built in the System with the complete Knowledge & Consent of the Operator, to deal with certain specific  Operational  Situations  or  some  Signalling  System  Anomalies.  The  Operator, therefore, is allowed to issue Critical Commands with additional Measures for Safeguarding and Control of critical Operations.
A Critical Command is programmed in such a way that its Issue shall have to be confirmed within a pre-determined time interval on the Central / Local ATS or VDU, before it shall be executed by the Interlocking and / or ATP.
Before a Critical Command is executed the TC / SC must:
(i) Check if  the  Critical  Command  is  absolutely  necessary  or  if  it  can  be  avoided  by utilising another Alternative.
(ii) Ensure that using this Command does not in any way leads to Hazardous Situation.
(iii) Obtain  Permission  from  the  Chief  Controller,  who  shall  have  to  agree  that,  the conditions (i) & (ii) above are satisfied.
(iv) If TC / SC has any doubt about the Safety of using the envisaged Critical Command, in  combination  with  the  necessary  Measures,  he  /  she must  stop  and  check  other Solutions or consult the Chief Controller & FMC.

## Introduction

(v) Use of Critical Commands is recorded and numbered in the Log Lists of the ATS System and shall have to be checked periodically by the Chief Controller.
## 3.0 CONTROLLING PROCESS WITH CRITICAL COMMANDS:

## 3.0 CONTROLLING PROCESS WITH CRITICAL COMMANDS:

While  Normal  Commands  can  be  executed  right  away,  the  Critical  Commands  require Command  Confirmation.  The  Operators  can  see  the  Critical  Command  Confirmation Request Indication in the Dialog Box.
## 4.0 CRITICAL COMMANDS:

## 4.0 CRITICAL COMMANDS:

(A) For Signals:
## Un-block Signal (UNBLOCK_SI):

## Un-block Signal (UNBLOCK_SI):

(i) Right Click on 'CBI_SI' Button and Left Click on 'UNBLOCK_SI' from the popup Commands.
(ii) Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'.
(iii) Since it is a Critical Command, a Confirmation is required. Right Click again and  Left  Click  on  'CONFIRM_UNBLOCK_SI'  Command  to  confirm  the Execution of the Command.
(iv) Before Un-blocking the Signals, TC / SC must:
(a) Check  that the reason  for 'Blocking' the Signals is no  longer necessary.
(b) Ensure that there are no Operations or Maintenance reasons existing to keep the Signals 'Blocked.
(c) Obtain the Permission of Chief Controller.
## (B) For Points:
## Emergency Switch On / Emergency Switch Off (EMER_PT_ON / EMER_PT_OFF):

## Emergency Switch On / Emergency Switch Off (EMER_PT_ON / EMER_PT_OFF):

'Emergency Switch On' Command provides the facility to the Operator to Normal or Reverse a point, while its Track circuit is occupied.
(i) Right Click at the Point and Left Click on 'EMER_PT_ON' Command from the pop-up Commands.
(ii) Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'.
(iii) Since it is a Critical Command, a Confirmation is required. Right Click on the Point Symbol again and Left Click on 'CONFIRM_EMER_PT_ON' Command

## Introduction

to  confirm  the  Execution  of  the  Command.  Then Execute  the Command  at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'

## Introduction

(iv) Indication 'Emergency Switch On' is indicated at the point as a 'Green Dot'.
(v) TC / SC can now switch the Point to Normal or Reverse Position.
(vi) Before  giving  Command  for  'Emergency  Switch  On',  the  TC  /  SC must:
(a) Check  possible  Signalling  Causes  for  an  assumed  incorrect  Point Occupation with FMC.
(b) Ensure that there are no Operations or Maintenance reasons existing against setting the Point freely to the  requisite Position - Normal or Reverse.
(c) Confirm from the Driver / TO, if a Vehicle / Train has come to stop and is  standing clear of the Point in question and if there is no Vehicle / Train, then the SC should visit the Site and confirm the Clearance of Point.
(d) Obtain the Permission of Chief Controller.
## Manual Point On / Manual Point Off (MAN_PT_ON / MAN_PT_OFF):

## Manual Point On / Manual Point Off (MAN_PT_ON / MAN_PT_OFF):

The  Operator  can  give  Authority  to  manual  control  point  by  giving  MAN_PT_ON Command and MAN_PT_OFF to inhibit Authorise Manual Point Operation. Out of the two, MAN_PT_OFF is a Critical Command.
(i) To  inhibit  Authorised  Manual  Point  Operation,  Right  Click  at  the  Point  and Left Click on 'MAN_PT_OFF' Command from the pop-up Commands.
(ii) Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'.
(iii) Since  'MAN_PT_OFF'  is  a  Critical  Command,  a  Confirmation  is  required, indicated by display 'M' in Red at the desired Point. Right Click on the Point Symbol  again  and  Left  Click  on  'CONFIRM_MAN_PT_OFF'  Command  to confirm the Execution of the Command. Then Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'. The Point manual control is now inhibited.
(iv) Before giving Command for 'Manual Point Off', the TC / SC must:
(a) Check  possible  Signalling  Causes  for  an  assumed  incorrect  Point Occupation.
(b) Ensure that there are no Operations or Maintenance reasons existing against Setting the Point logically to be Free.
(c) Obtain the Permission of Chief Controller.
## Self Normalisation On / Self Normalisation Off (NORM_PT_ON / NORM_PT_OFF):

## Self Normalisation On / Self Normalisation Off (NORM_PT_ON / NORM_PT_OFF):

The Point Self Normalisation will allow the Point to automatically switch back to its Normal  Position,  after  the  Route  is  released.  The  Operator  can  set  the  Self Normalisation  by  giving  'NORM_PT_ON'  Command  and  'NORM_PT_OFF'  to remove  Point  Self  Normalisation.  Out  of  the  two,  NORM_PT_OFF  is  a  Critical Command.

## Self Normalisation On / Self Normalisation Off (NORM_PT_ON / NORM_PT_OFF):

(i) To remove Point Self Normalisation, select 'NORM_PT_OFF' Command from the pop-up Commands.
(ii) Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'.
(iii) Since 'NORM_PT_OFF' is a Critical Command, a Confirmation is required, indicated by display 'N' in Red at the desired Point. Right Click on the Point Symbol again and Left Click on 'CONFIRM_NORM_PT_OFF' Command to confirm the Execution of the Command. Then Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'. The Status of Self Normalisation is changed to 'Inhibit' and the red Frame disappears.
(iv) Before giving Command for 'Manual Point Off', the TC / SC must:
(a) Ensure  that  the  Point is  not  needed  for  another  Route,  Flank Protection or Overlap.
(b) Ensure  that  a  Train  or  Vehicle  running  in  the  Route  or  Overlap,  to which the Point belongs, has stopped.
(c) Obtain the Permission of Chief Controller.
## (C) For Routes:
## Route Blocking / Un-Blocking (BLOCK_RTE / UNBLOCK_RTE):

## Route Blocking / Un-Blocking (BLOCK_RTE / UNBLOCK_RTE):

Operator  can  prevent  a  Route  Setting  by  executing  BLOCK_RTE  Command.  The Blocked can  be  Un-blocked  by  the  Command  'UNBLOCK_RTE'. Un-blocking of  a Route is a Critical Command.
To Un-block a Route, TC / SC shall:
(i) Select the Start Point (Start Object) of the Route by  Left Clicking. A White Rectangle is drawn around the Start Point.
(ii) Select the End Point (End Object) of the Route by Right clicking. The White Rectangle appears around the End Point.

## Introduction

(iii) A Route Menu appears immediately when the End Point is selected. Select the 'UNBLOCK_RTE' Command. Then

## Introduction

Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'.
(iv) The 'Un-block' Command  is a Critical  Command, which requires a Confirmation, indicated by display 'R' in Red at the Start & End Signal.
(v) Select the 'CONFIRM_UNBLOCK_RTE' Command and Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'. Route Bar then disappears and the Route is Un-blocked.
(vi) Before Un-blocking the Route, the TC / SC must:
(a) Check that the reason for 'Blocking' the Route is no longer necessary.
(b) Ensure that there are no Operations or Maintenance reasons existing to keep the Route 'Blocked.
(c) Obtain the Permission of Chief Controller.
(d) Set 'Un-blocking Route'.
## (D) For Track Circuits:

## (D) For Track Circuits:

The Operator can block a Track for Maintenance by giving 'BLOCK_TC' Command. The  Maintenance  Block  can  be  removed  by  the  Command  'UNBLOCK_TC'.  Unblocking of a Track circuit is a Critical Command.
To Un-block a Track circuit, TC / SC shall:
Right Click  at  the  Track  Symbol  and left Click at  'UNBLOCK_TC'  and then Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'.
The 'Un-block'  Command  is a Critical Command,  which requires a Confirmation, indicated by display 'T' in Red below the Track Symbol.
Right  Click  at  the  same  point  and  Left  Click  at  'CONFIRM_UNBLOCK_TC' Command and Execute the Command at the Command Bar or Press 'Enter'. The Maintenance Block is now removed.
Before Un-blocking the Track, the TC / SC must:
(a) Check that the reasons for 'Blocking' the Track no longer exist.
(b) Ensure that there are no Operations or Maintenance reasons existing to keep the Track 'Blocked.
(c) Obtain the Permission of Chief Controller.

## 1.  INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order covers certain Salient Features of the Working of CATS over Line Nos. '1' and  also  describes  the  Procedure  to  transfer  the  Control  from  LATS  Users  (SCR  Station Controllers) to CATS Users (OCC Traffic Controllers) and vice versa. Wherever CATS & LATS are  mentioned,  it  is  to  be  read  in  terms  of  indigenous-Automatic  Train  Supervision  (i-ATS) system.

## 2.  SCOPE

2.1  This procedure order is applicable to Line 1 only, when working on i-ATS system.
2.2  This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 & its amendment, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue for working of Trains on Line No-1.
2.3  Wherever HILC/HIC/SRRC/Critical Command/ Safety Critical Commands are mentioned, it is to be read as SRRC.
2.4  ATS operator/operator at central, local and depot may be read as Traffic Controller (TC), Station Controller (SC) and Depot Controller (DC) respectively.

## 3.  SYSTEM OF WORKING

Under the ATS, in Cutoff Mode, when the 'Level of Control' is 'LOCAL ATS' , each MSS Station can control their Interlocking or OCC Controllers can control their 'Area of Control' from their ATS Workstations. When the 'Level of Control' is 'CENTRAL ATS' , all other Secondary Stations can only monitor the Main Line (their respective Interlocking Area) Movements. All Controllers (Local Station, Depot, Secondary Station& Central) are able to consult all the 'Views' simultaneously but only  one  Controller  (Local  Station,  Depot,  or  Central),  at  a  time,  is  allowed  to  send  Control towards one Interlocking. When LATS / CATS are restarted or initialized, the 'Level of Control' is released and further 'Level of control' is possible by any LATS/CATS user as per their authority.
Normally the Control of all Interlockings should be with OCC Controllers, with 'Level of Control' at 'CENTRAL ATS' .

## 4.  LINE OPERATING MODE MANAGEMENT

This Function manages the Line Operating Mode, according to Control Level of the Line, Area of Control  Regions  assigned  to  the  Operator  and  the  Location  of  the  Operator  to  carry  out  the Control (Central Control Level or Local Control Level).
Different  Line  Operating  Modes  are  -  Cutoff  mode  (previously  known  as  Manual  mode), Headway Mode (previously known as Constant Headway mode) & Timetable mode (previously known as Scheduled mode).
Timetable  mode  is  available  in  Central  ATS.  The  other  ones  viz.  the  Cutoff  &  Headway  are available in Central and Local ATS both ( Figure-1 ).
Figure-1   Line Operating Modes
Line Operating Modes can be Monitored and Controlled by an Operator on LATS or CATS. Line Operating Mode is not available for control in the Depot. Only monitoring of Line operating mode is visible.
## 4.1 Cutoff Mode (Manual Mode):

## 4.1 Cutoff Mode (Manual Mode):

The operation shall be entirely manual. At the Initialization of a Control Level (Central or Local), the Line Operating Mode shall be 'Cutoff'. In the event of loss of Central Control Level, all ATS

## Introduction

Sectors of a given Corridor shall have the change of the Control Level from Central to Released State, and of the Line Operating Mode from one amongst the three Modes to Cutoff Mode.
## 4.2 Headway Mode (Constant Headway Mode):

## 4.2 Headway Mode (Constant Headway Mode):

In this Mode, the Trains are regulated based on the predefined 'Headway'.
Before switching Line Operating Mode from 'Headway' to 'Cutoff', Fleet and Cycles should be released by clicking on 'Reset Cycle' button in headway parameter setting window.
## 4.3 Timetable Mode (Scheduled Mode):

## 4.3 Timetable Mode (Scheduled Mode):

In this Mode, the Regulation will be applied to the Trains running in the Normal Traffic Direction in accordance with the current Timetable. Trains running in the Reverse Traffic Direction are not regulated. The system will provide following features:
(a) Automatic numbering of the Trains based on assigned rake-ID.
(b) Automatic route setting

The 'Control Level' Operations are used to transfer the 'Control' between an entire Local ATS Sector and the Central ATS and vice-versa, in order to manage Train Regulation Operations and Line Operating Mode.

## 9.  SAFETY RELATED INSTRUCTIONS:
## CATS/LATS MMI Display Problem:

## CATS/LATS MMI Display Problem:

In case of CATS/LATS MMI display problem, Traffic Controller / Station Controller shall confirm all  the  Information  displayed  by  CATS/LATS  MMI,  with  those  displayed  by  the  Large  Video Screen (LVS) / CCIP/VDU for Monitoring.
In  case  of  'Incoherence'  of  ATS  Information  displayed  between  CATS  MMI  and  LVS,  Traffic Controller  shall  verify  the  Equipment  Status  on  LATS  MMI  or  CCIP/VDU  through  Station Controller, before giving the Authorization to make a specific Train Movement.
In case of unavailability of Large Video Screen at OCC, if the Traffic Controller has to take a Decision for giving an Authorization to Train Operator to overpass a Red Signal or a Defective Signal, he shall get the confirmation from the Station Controller that all the Information displayed

## Introduction

by the CATS MMI is consistent with that displayed by LATS MMI or CCIP/VDU. If there is no LATS MMI or CCIP/VDU in Operation, no decision related to Safety Control can be taken and the  situation  shall  be  handled  as  per  Physical  Verification  at  site  and  according  to  extant Emergency Handling Instructions in vogue.
## 9.1 Safety Indicators:

## 9.1 Safety Indicators:

Safety  Indicators  shall  allow  the  ATS  Operator  to  be  sure  that  the  MMI  Client  &  Server  are running in 'Coherence'. Before taking any Decision linked to Safety Control regarding a sector, the ATS Operator shall, therefore, check the status of following Safety Indicators:

## 9.3  Verification of Safety Related Remote Control (SRRC) Commands Returned by ATC/CBI:

The  Station  Controller  /  Traffic  Controller  shall,  without  fail,  check  on  ATS  MMI,  the  SRRC (Safety Related Remote Control) Messages (Examples: Signal / Points / Route - Blocking / Unblocking, Setting / Release of Maintenance Blocks etc.) returned by the CBI or ATC Sub-system, within the Preparation (time 15 Sec.) and Acknowledge the Message of each HILC Operation. ## 9.4  ATS Alarm of SRRC Command:

## 9.4  ATS Alarm of SRRC Command:

The ATS raises an 'Alarm' in case the requested SRRC has not been correctly performed (as expected) by the CBI or ATC. The ATS Operator must, therefore, check for 'Alarms' in the Alarm area on line overview or alarm browsing window. after executing a SRRC Command.
## 9.5  Confirmation of the SRRC Command Set:

## 9.5  Confirmation of the SRRC Command Set:

After  Setting  a  SRRC Command (Examples: Signal / Points / Route - Blocking / Un-blocking, Setting/ Release of Maintenance Blocks and Setting / Release of TSRs etc.), the ATS Operator shall attempt to execute a Conflicting Command and see that the intended Operation does not get executed by the Interlocking because of the Execution of the earlier SRRC Command.
For  Example,  set  a  Route  on  a  Blocked  Route,  Set  an  Incompatible  Route  encompassing  a Route Blocked for Maintenance or Operate a Blocked Point etc. All such Conflicting Commands

shall be rejected by the Interlocking. This shall prove that the SRRC Command in question has been correctly handled by the Interlocking. Rejection of the Command shall appear at the lower right side of the Screen in the Event/Alarm Bar. If the Correct Protection is not achieved by the related 'Safety Related Remote Control', the action must not be 'Authorized'.

## 10. TEMPORARY SPEED RESTRICTION (TSR) MANAGEMENT

## 10. TEMPORARY SPEED RESTRICTION (TSR) MANAGEMENT

The Temporary Speed Restriction is a value set in to the ATC Sub-system to limit the Running Speed when a special condition ours on the track, for example, Maintenance etc. These values can be set either by the ATS, or directly by the ATC Maintenance Terminal. TSR Values can be set in both Directions, the possible starting point and length is relative to list of track Portions and the track circuits, defined internally in to the ATC Sub-system.
A Track Segment including one or more Track circuits can be in Speed restriction during a given time period.
TSR is a High Integrity Level Control (HILC). The control is sent to the ATC Sub-system and if accepted, a Confirmation pop up Message is displayed. Second Operator Entry is required to confirm the Initial control and should be sent before '5' minutes, to be fully accepted by the ATC Sub-system.
(i) Following Controls are possible for TSR Management, at Local ATS:
Monitoring of TSR
Setting (Increase or Decrease) of TSR,
Delete or Cancel all Active TSRs of an ATC Sector.
(ii)  Following controls are possible for TSR Management, at Central ATS:
Monitoring of TSR
Setting (Decrease) of TSR,

## OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR EXECUTION OF CRITICAL COMMANDS FROM i-ATS SYSTEM FOR LINE NOS. '1'

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This Procedure applies to OCC and all Stations of Line Nos. '1' for Safe Execution of Safety Critical  Commands.  This  Procedure  shall  ensure  that  additional  measures  for  execution  of Critical Commands by the Chief Controller / Traffic Controller / Station Controller are followed properly and correctly for Safe Passage of Trains and Safety of Staff.
This  procedure  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  the  Metro  Railways  General  Rules,  2020, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue for working of Trains on Line Nos. '1'.
This Procedure also reminds the Operator - TC / SC about his / her responsibility for additional Safety  Measures  which  are  required  to  be  undertaken  at  the  time  of  Execution  of  these Commands.

## 2. SCOPE

This Procedure is applicable for Line-1. Safety Critical Commands on line Nos. '1' are identified as ' High Integrity Commands '.
Critical  /  High  Integrity  Commands  are  necessary  to  release  or  circumvent  certain  Safety Features built in the System with the complete Knowledge & Consent of the Operator, to deal with  certain  specific  Operational  Situations  or  some  Signaling  System  Anomalies.  The Operator,  therefore,  is  allowed  to  issue  Critical  Commands  with  additional  Measures  for Safeguarding and Control of critical Operations.
A Critical  Command is programmed in such a way that its Issue shall have to be confirmed within a pre-determined time interval on the Central / Local ATS or CCIP/VDU, before it shall be executed by the Interlocking and / or ATP.
Before a Critical Command is executed the TC / SC must:
(i) Check if the Critical Command is absolutely necessary or if it can be avoided by utilizing another Alternative.
(ii) Ensure that using this Command does not in any way leads to Hazardous Situation.
(iii)  Obtain Permission from the Chief Controller, who shall have to agree that, the conditions (i) & (ii) above are satisfied.
(iv)  If TC / SC has any doubt about the Safety of using the envisaged Critical Command, in combination with the necessary Measures, he / she must stop and check other Solutions or consult the Chief Controller & SGC.
(v) Use of Critical Commands is recorded and numbered in the Log Lists of the ATS System and shall have to be checked periodically by the Chief Controller.

## 3. STEPS FOR EXECUTION OF HIGH INTEGRITY CONTROL COMMANDS:

LATS

## 3. STEPS FOR EXECUTION OF HIGH INTEGRITY CONTROL COMMANDS:

ASCV
Execution of each High Integrity Control Command is done in '3' Steps:
(i) The Operator clicks on the First Button.
(ii) Second possible Step appears on the Window. The Operator clicks on the Second Step Button to send a 'Preparation Request' to the Interlocking (ASCV).
(iii)  When  the  Control  is  prepared,  a  Confirmation  Window  appears.  The  Operator  has  a choice  to  abort  the  Command.  Content  of  the  Message  provides  a  reference  to  the equipment being controlled.
If the Operator confirms the Control within 15 Sec., the Command is executed.
In  case,  the  Operator  clicks  on  the  'Cancel'  Button,  the  Control  is  cancelled  without  any change in the Status and the Dialog Box is closed.
If the Operator does not finish the Control Sequence within 15 Sec., then too the Command is cancelled / Timed out.
During the progress of a Control, the concerned Button is disabled.
The Message regarding Operator Operations are displayed in the Event Area.
## 4.1  Block / Un-block all the Signals in Interlocking:

## 4.1  Block / Un-block all the Signals in Interlocking:

(i) Click on 'GSB' button on concerned Interlocking region.
(ii) A Dialog Box to confirm the Control is opened, click on 'OK'.
(iii)  A final confirmation dialog is opened, Click on 'OK to perform the Control.
(iv)  Before Un-blocking all the Signals, TC / SC must:
(a) Check that the reason for 'Blocking' all the Signals is no longer necessary.
(b)  Ensure that there are no Operations or Maintenance reasons existing to keep all the Signals 'Blocked'.
(c) Obtain the Permission of Chief Controller.
(d) Set 'Un-blocking all Signals by again clicking on 'GSB' button and giving confirmation for the same.

## 4.2  Route Blocking:

(i) To perform a 'Route Blocking Control', the TC / SC must successfully click on Entrance Signal of concerned route and then click on 'Route Blocking' Button. (ii) Select the Route blocking control indication displayed on the end of the route and click 'Ok' on the dialog for confirmation

## 4.2  Route Blocking:

(ii) A final confirmation dialog is opened, Click on 'OK' to perform the Control.
(iii) If  the  'Route  Blocking  Control'  is  successful,  and  the  concerned  Route  is  updated  to 'Route Blocked State'.
(iv) When a 'Route Blocking Button' is selected, only valid 'Route Blocking Options' will be displayed near destination signal.

## 4.3  Route Un-Blocking:

(i) To perform a 'Route un-blocking control' click on the Entrance signal of concerned route to unblock and then click on 'Route Blocking control' button again
(ii) Select the route un-blocking control indication displayed on the end of the route and click 'Ok' on the dialog for confirmation
(iii)  A final confirmation dialog is opened, click on 'OK' to perform the Control.
(iv)  Before Un-blocking the Route, the TC / SC must:
(a) Check that the reason for 'Blocking' the Route is no longer necessary.
(b) Ensure  that  there  are  no  Operations  or  Maintenance  reasons  existing  to  keep  the Route Blocked.
(c) Obtain the Permission of Chief Controller.

## 4.4  Block / Un-block the Point:

(i) Click on Point text and then on 'Point Block/unblock' Button in the Dialog Box.
(ii) A Dialog Box to confirm the Control is opened, click on 'OK' to proceed.
(iii)  A final confirmation dialog is opened, click on 'OK' to perform the Control.
(iv)  Before a Point may be Un-blocked, the TC / SC must:
(a) Ensure that the reason to 'Block' the Point is no longer valid.
(b) Ensure  that  there  are  no  Operations  or  Maintenance  reasons  existing  to  keep  the Point 'Blocked'.
(c) Obtain the Permission of the Chief Controller.
(d) Set 'Un-blocking Point' by again clicking on point text and then on 'Point Block/unblock' button and giving confirmation for the same.

## 4.5  Trap Points Control:

The Trap Points are Self-normalized. They are represented by point text in box. The Automatic restoration to the Normal Position will be subject to a 20 Sec. delay period after releasing of the Route and the conditions locking the Point.
## A.  There are two additional Controls for the Trap Points:
## (i) To Set Point Self Normalization Inhibition:

## (i) To Set Point Self Normalization Inhibition:

(a) Click on 'Point object' text in the Line overview and click on 'Point Self normalization inhibition Button.
(b) A Dialog Box to confirm the Control is opened, click on 'OK' to proceed.
(c) A final confirmation dialog is opened, click on 'OK' to perform the Control
## (ii)  Release Point Self Normalization Inhibition:

## (ii)  Release Point Self Normalization Inhibition:

(a) Click  on  'Point  object'  text  in  the  Line  overview  already  set  and  click  on  'Point  Self normalization inhibition Button'.

## (ii)  Release Point Self Normalization Inhibition:

(b) A Dialog Box to confirm the Control is opened, click on 'OK' to proceed.
(c) A final confirmation dialog is opened, click on 'OK' to perform the Control
## B.  Before any of the above Operations, the TC / SC must:

## B.  Before any of the above Operations, the TC / SC must:

(i) Ensure that the Point is not needed for another Route, Flank Protection or Overlap.
(ii) Ensure  that  a  Train  or  Vehicle  running  in  the  Route  or  Overlap,  to  which  the  Point belongs has stopped.
(iii)  Obtain the Permission of the Chief Controller.
## 4.6  Maintenance Block Setting Control:
## A.  To 'Set' or 'Release' a Maintenance Block:

## A.  To 'Set' or 'Release' a Maintenance Block:

(i) Click on the Track first and then 'Maintenance Block' Button. The 'Maintenance Block' Dialog Box will appear.
(ii) Click on 'OK' Button in the Dialog Box.
(iii)  A final confirmation dialog is opened, click on 'OK' to perform the Control action.
(iv)  If  the  Maintenance  Block  Control'  is  successful,  the  selected  Track  Circuit  Area  is displayed  by  'Red  vertical  lines'  above  and  below  the  track  circuit.  All  the  Routes involving this Track circuit shall get blocked.
## B.  Before operating the above Command, the TC / SC must:

## B.  Before operating the above Command, the TC / SC must:

(i) Ensure that the reasons for Setting or Releasing of the 'Maintenance Block' are valid.
(ii) Obtain the Permission of the Chief Controller.

text:
## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This Procedure Order covers the Methodology of Imposing / Alteration and Cancellation  of  Temporary  Speed  Restrictions  on  Line  Nos.  '5'  &  '6'  equipped  with Signalling & Train Control System of BOMBARDIER.

metadata.source: 23.3 SC-23C (Rev-02) Temporary Speed Restrictions in L- 5&6.pdf
metadata.chunk_id: 23.3 SC-23C (Rev-02) Temporary Speed Restrictions in L- 5&6_p1_3

text:
## 2.0 SCOPE

This procedure shall be read in conjunction with the Metro Railways General Rules-2020, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue for Working of Trains on Line Nos. '5' & '6'.

metadata.source: 23.3 SC-23C (Rev-02) Temporary Speed Restrictions in L- 5&6.pdf

text:
3.1 All the request for imposition/alteration/cancellation of TSR on main line should be made to chief controller/OCC and  the CC/OCC  shall  instruct Traffic Controller for the Imposition / Alteration/Cancellation  of  Temporary  Speed  Restrictions  &  Issue  of  Caution  Orders  to Train operators, as required on the Main Line Sections.
3.2 In  cases  of  any  of  the  TSR  Commands,  not  directly  being  under  Control  of  TC,  the Compliance of the same shall be ensured by TC, through the Station Controllers under the Exchange of Private Numbers.
3.3 All Requests for the Imposition/Alteration/Cancellation of Temporary Speed Restrictions & Issue of Caution Orders to the Train Operators, as required within the Depot, shall be submitted  to  the  Depot  Controller,  who  is  responsible  for  Coordination  of  all  such Requests.  Depot  Controller  shall  also  inform  the  TSR  details  to  the  PPIO,  under Exchange  of  Private  Numbers,  to  enable  him  to  advise  the  Shunting  Supervisors accordingly.
3.4 All  Requests of the TSRs shall be submitted by the Authorized Personnel of Rank, not less than Junior Engineers as per prescribed format in Annexure-'C' .

metadata.chunk_id: 23.3 SC-23C (Rev-02) Temporary Speed Restrictions in L- 5&6_p2_8

text:
3.4 All  Requests of the TSRs shall be submitted by the Authorized Personnel of Rank, not less than Junior Engineers as per prescribed format in Annexure-'C' .
3.5 On receipt of Request for Imposition / Alteration & Cancellation of Temporary Speed Restriction  (TSR)  on  a  Section  /  in  the  Depot,  the  Traffic  Controller  /  Depot Controller  shall  verify  the  TC  No.  corresponding  to  the  OHE  Mast  No.  from  the Conversion  Table  at Annexure -  'A' to  this  Circular  and  shall  take  further  action  for Imposition / Alteration / Cancellation of the Temporary Speed Restriction.
The  Requests,  arising  out  of  Emergency  or  Failure,  shall  be  taken  up  promptly,  duly advising the Official, who has made the Request.
The  Requests  for  the  TSRs  for  a  Planned  Work  shall  normally  be  submitted  before 1700 Hrs. of the previous day.
Traffic Controller / Depot  Controller shall  keep  a  record  of  accepted  TSR Requests.

3.8 The  Traffic  Controller  shall  advise  the  Depot  Controller  &  Station  Controllers  of  the Terminal Stations of all TSRs to be in force during next day on the entire Mainline on daily basis and shall maintain a Record of the same. Traffic Controller shall also advise the  TSRs  to  the  Crew  Controller  and  the  Crew  Controller  and  depot  controller  shall write  in  the  notice  boards  and  sign  on  register  as  well,  however  for  those  TSRs  not imposed through the system, due to any reason shall be advised to Train operators of each  passing  train  in  the  form  of  caution  order  at  the  preceding  station  of  affected section.
3.9 Traffic Controller shall ensure that before the Start of Revenue Services all the TSRs requested  on the Section have been 'Set' on the Sector and shall advise, under the Exchange  of  Private  numbers,  the  first  Train  Operator  passing  the  affected  Section. Traffic Controller will confirm from the said TO with regard to the imposition of TSR. Train  Operator  in  turn  shall  intimate  the  Target  Speed  displayed  on  DMI  over  the affected area to the Traffic Controller. TC shall log / record the same.
3.10 On Completion, the imposed TSR is visible on MMI (Local & Central), written under each TC in Numeric Form.

text:
3.10 On Completion, the imposed TSR is visible on MMI (Local & Central), written under each TC in Numeric Form.
3.11 In the event of complete Power Failure to the Track side ATC System trains run in degraded  mode  of  train  operation  with  speed  not  exceeding  25kmph  hence  all TSRs  below  25  kmph  shall  be  dealt  as  per Para  3.12 of  this  circular.  After restoration,  Chief  controller  shall  verify  that  all  TSRs  which  are  prevailing,  have been applied in the system.
3.12 Since  Trains  can  run  in  non-ATP  Mode  at  Speeds  lower  than  25  Kmph,  the System as such can not  enforce  the  TSRs of  Values less  than  25  Kmph  in  nonATP  Mode  of  Working.  TSRs  of  Values  less  than  25  Kmph  shall,  therefore,  be advised  to  the  Train  Operator  in  writing  in  the  form  of  caution  order  by  the preceding stations controller of the station.  Such  an Advise shall  be  in addition to the TSR imposed by the System.
3.13 All TSRs in the Depot shall be advised in writing to the Train Operators.

3.15 The  Drivers  of  Maintenance  Rail  Vehicles  shall  respect  and  follow  the  Caution Orders advised to them, while moving on Main Line / Depot line.
3.16 Format of the Caution Order for advising the TSRs to the Train Operators is enclosed at Annexure - 'B' to this Circular.
3.17 During  high  speed  testing  of  train,  trains  run  in  non-ATP  mode  (SCS  cut  out/ATP  by pass).  During  such  testing,  temporary  speed  restrictions  above  25  kmph  should  also  be advised to the train operators of testing trains at the preceding stations in the form of caution order.
3.18 The application of TSR's from an EBI screen workstation will have an immediate effect upon the  speed  restriction  on  the  track  circuit,  at  which  TSR  is  applied.  This  will  affect  any approaching ATP equipped train. TSR's should not be applied until it is confirmed that there are nọ trains approaching the TSR affected TC, and if there is any approaching train then it is to be made stationary.

## CORRIGENDUM - 02 TO SAFETY CIRCULAR - 02 (Rev-04)
## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR GRANTING & CANCELLATION OF POWER BLOCKS AND PERMIT TO WORK DURING NON-REVENUE HOURS

## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR GRANTING & CANCELLATION OF POWER BLOCKS AND PERMIT TO WORK DURING NON-REVENUE HOURS

This Corrigendum - 02 to Safety Circular-02 (Rev-04) shall be read in conjunction with SC-02 (Rev04) and its Corrigendum - 01 regarding 'Procedure Order for Granting & Cancellation of Power Blocks and Permit to Work During Non-Revenue Hours.'

## PROCEDURE ORDER FOR GRANTING & CANCELLATION OF POWER BLOCKS AND PERMIT TO WORK DURING NON-REVENUE HOURS

This Corrigendum is prepared to incorporate 'granting of PTW to Project wing with concurrence of respective O&M department'.
Following Para is revised: -
## A.  Revised Para - 5.0: -
## 5.0 PREPARATION OF WEEKLY GENERAL ORDER:

Granting of EP/IB/Power Block/Shadow Power Block shall be in the form of a 'Weekly General Order' to be issued by OCM on every Friday, for the ensuing Week commencing from Saturday Night till Friday Night.
Requirements for OHE Power Block, Shadow Power Block & Permit to Work during NonRevenue Hours shall be submitted by the all concerned controllers, until 1500 Hrs. of every Thursday to the Chief Controller (CHC) / OCC. However, Requirements for OHE Power Block, Shadow Power Block & Permit  to  Work  during  Non-revenue  Hours  shall  be  endorsed  by concerned O&M wing before submitting to the Chief Controller (CHC) / OCC.
All Submissions shall be scrutinized by CHC and CTPC. OCM/CHC & Mgr/AM (Traction)/CTPC of the concerned Line shall check the Requisitions for the following:
5.1 The Department seeking Track Access & Possession.
5.2 Location (Section), Date, Time of Commencement & Expected Duration.
5.3 Nature of Work to be carried out along with requirement of power block/shadow power block.
5.4 Details of equipment to be used (relevant from Track Access & other Departments working point of view).
5.5 Points of Entry & Exit of Men & Materials, Equipments and Tools & Plants.
5.6 Engineers Possession In-charge (EPIC) along with Nos. of accompanying Gang Members.
5.7 Description & movement of Self-propelled / Non-self-propelled (Non- motorized)/ Vehicle or Rolling Stock requires.
5.8 Movement of Maintenance Vehicles (Tower Wagon / CTMC / OMV / CMV / Ladder Trolleys / other Maintenance Vehicles) on the section.

5.7 Description & movement of Self-propelled / Non-self-propelled (Non- motorized)/ Vehicle or Rolling Stock requires.
5.8 Movement of Maintenance Vehicles (Tower Wagon / CTMC / OMV / CMV / Ladder Trolleys / other Maintenance Vehicles) on the section.
5.9 Feasibility & Process of De-energisation of the OHE of the Section.
5.10 Feasibility of this Power Block with other Power & Traffic Block Demands.
5.11 Compatibility  of  this  Power  Block  with  'No  Power  Block  Section'  in  case  of  required  Train Movement.
5.12 Longitudinal, Transverse or Cross Protections, as per SWO.
5.13 Means to protect the area under Engineers possession/ Integrated Block.
During Non-Revenue Hours Power Block can be allowed in following manner:
(i) Neutral Section (NS) - Neutral Section (NS).
(ii) Neutral Section (NS) - Dead End

## Introduction

NOTE: Being a separate line-04, Power block of Line-04 section from Laxmi Nagar to Vaishali shall be permitted by opening Breaker Mains at Yamuna Bank SSP.

## Introduction

Based on the above, OCM shall issue a "weekly general order" comprising EP/IB/OHE Power Block/Shadow power Block/PTW Programs and convey the same to all concerned controllers through CHC/OCC.
No Variation from the Weekly General Order, issued by OCM, shall ordinarily be allowed. Only in cases of extreme emergency, the Unscheduled Requests may be considered by the OCM. Concerned controller sending emergency block request to CHC/OCC will mention the exact reason  of  such  emergency  request  for  the  consideration  of  OCM.  Based  on  OCM consideration, the block paper will be revised.
## B.  New Para Added - 6.8: -

## B.  New Para Added - 6.8: -

To ensure safe working, EPIC shall place red banner flag/ Red batten light at the track at a distance  of  at  least  200  meter  on  both  sides  of  the  actual  working  area  within  the allotted/sanctioned EP Area.
## C.  New Para Added - 6.9: -

## C.  New Para Added - 6.9: -

Whenever Traffic Controller grants the EP/IB in a particular section where staff is permitted to work then simultaneously maintenance block/ signal block should be applied through ATS to protect the allotted block section.
## D.  Revised Para - 9.1: -

## D.  Revised Para - 9.1: -

After switching off the OHE, TPC shall check the status of OHE on his Monitor. The Voltage at PT shall be indicated as 0.2 to 0.5 KV. After the provision of Discharge Rods on the OHE, it shall be shown as 0.0 KV on the Monitor. TPC, in this way, can re-confirm the assertion of Traction Staff in regard to the provision of Discharge Rods on the OHE.
The Elementary Section / Line is shown in 'Green' Colour on TPC's Monitor, when the OHE is in charged condition with 25 KV. After switching off the OHE, it becomes 'Red'.
## E.  Revised Para - 11.2: -

## E.  Revised Para - 11.2: -

Station  Controller  shall  confirm  from  'Weekly  General  Order'  as  well  as  OCC,  under  the exchange of private numbers, about the planned EP. If OCC/TC approves the said EP, the Station Controller shall issue the 'Permit-to-Work (PTW)' to the EPIC / Sub-EPIC. PTW format is  placed  at  Annexure  -  A.  In  the  PTW,  the  nature  of  work,  location  and  name  of  Gang Members shall be clearly mentioned.
In  case  of  PTW  issue  to  Project  wing,  Concerned  OCC  controller  shall  prior  inform  to CHC/OCC regarding permitting PTW to EPIC/Sub-EPIC of project department through email by 23:00 hours for the following night.
Issue of PTW for one line in tunnel/elevated section indicates that EPIC and his staff shall not use  cross  passage  doors/any  other  access  point  and  shall  not  go  to  other  line  unless  so authorized by TC under exchange of private number. iii.
## F. Revised Para - 12.5: -

## Introduction

Station  Controller  shall  confirm  from  'Weekly  General  Order'  as  well  as  OCC,  under  the exchange of private numbers, about the planned IB. If OCC/TC approves the said IB, the Station Controller shall issue the 'Permit-to-Work (PTW)' to the EPIC / Sub-EPIC. PTW format is  placed  at  Annexure  -  A.  In  the  PTW,  the  nature  of  work,  location  and  name  of  Gang Members shall be clearly mentioned.

## Introduction

## SAFETY CIRCULAR - 02 (Rev.-04)

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION:

This  Procedure Order covers the Methodology for obtaining Permission for Engineer's Possession & Integrated  Blocks  including  Power  Blocks  and    Shadow  Power  Blocks  during  Non-Revenue  Hours, required for Inspection, Repair, Testing, Maintenance and Construction of Signaling, Communication, Track & Structure, Over-Head Equipment, Line Side Structures and Tunnel Equipment in a manner that shall ascertain complete Safety of all concerned, while ensuring that the Metro Rail Assets and Safety Equipments  are  not  adversely  affected  during  Working.  The  Procedure  Order  also  lists  out  the Responsibilities of Metro Staff and that of Contractor's Authorized Representatives during their Testing, Maintenance & Repairs, and Construction Activities.

## 2.0 SCOPE:

This  procedure  is  applicable  for  all  lines.  This  procedure  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro Railways General Rules-2020 and Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules-2022, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue.
For UTO mode of Train Operation : Wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/Roving Attendant (RA)/Emergency Train Operator (ETO).

## 3.0 GENERAL:

OHE Power Block and Shadow Power Block shall be required in case the Working zone is within a radius of '2' m from OHE.
## 4.0 DEFINITIONS:
## 4.1 Engineer's Possession (EP):

## 4.1 Engineer's Possession (EP):

Engineer's  Possession  is  an  Authority  given  to  an  Agency  or  Department  within  an  Organization  to have access to the portion of the Track or Tracks or a Line Segment for a specified period of time for the purpose of Inspection, Repair, Maintenance, Construction, Re-habilitation and Testing of Equipments etc.
EP shall normally be granted during Non-Revenue Hours.
## 4.2 Engineer's Possession In-charge (EPIC):

## 4.2 Engineer's Possession In-charge (EPIC):

The Person-in-Charge of Engineer's Possession shall be termed as 'EPIC'.
(i) For E&M and Civil departments:-
Only  DMRC staff,  not  below  the  Rank  of  Maintainer  with  minimum  03  years  of  service  having  valid Competency, shall be EPIC.
(ii)  For all other departments except E&M and Civil departments:-
Only DMRC staff, not below the Rank of Sr. Maintainer having valid Competency shall be EPIC.
EPIC shall be properly trained and certified in the Duties and Responsibility of the Role. Responsibility to ensure Competency of the EPIC shall be of the concerned Department nominating EPIC.
## 4.3 Sub Engineer's Possession In-charge (Sub-EPIC):

## 4.3 Sub Engineer's Possession In-charge (Sub-EPIC):

If more than one Maintenance Agencies are required to work within the limits of the same Engineer's Possession, the EPIC can permit other DMRC Official to work as Sub-EPIC, if so notified in advance in

## Introduction

the  Weekly  General  Order.  Only  DMRC  Staff  having  Competency,  designation  and  experience  as mentioned in para 4.2 shall be the Sub-EPIC.

## Introduction

EPIC of a section may also be the Sub-EPIC of the other section. However, an Area under Engineers Possession shall be the sole Responsibility of EPIC. Sub-EPIC shall be responsible for the Issues of Safe Working pertaining to the Nature of Work being undertaken by the Maintenance Agency working under Sub-engineer's Possession.
Responsibility  to  ensure  Competency  of  the  Sub-EPIC  shall  be  of  the  concerned  department nominating Sub-EPIC.
Sub-EPIC cannot authorize further Sub-EPIC.
## 4.4 Integrated Block (IB):

## 4.4 Integrated Block (IB):

Integrated Blocks are such Blocks, where the Maintenance Staff of different Disciplines, viz. Signalling, Telecommunication, Civil, Traction,  and Track  etc.  can  work  simultaneously  in  a  portion  of  Track  or Tracks or on a Line Segment for a specified period of time for the purposes of Inspection, Repairs, Maintenance & Testing and Construction Activities, without affecting the Integrity of Track and other Commissioned and Working Assets.
Integrated Blocks shall be granted during Non-revenue Hours with / without Power Block.
## 4.5 Traction Staff:

## 4.5 Traction Staff:

Not below the rank of Sr. Maintainer (OHE or PSI), who has been issued Competency by appropriate Authority to avail Power Block & give Shadow Power Blocks to others.
## 4.6 Power Block:

## 4.6 Power Block:

Power Block means Switching off Power Supply in a particular Section. On demand of Traction Staff, the  TPC  at  OCC  in  consultation  with  TC  make  a  Line  /OHE  Section  de-energized  electrically  and confirm the same to the Traction Staff, who has placed such a demand.
The  Messages  exchanged  between  Traction  Staff  and  TPC  shall  be  recorded  in  the  Power  Block Message Book / Register.
The Line /OHE Section, which is under the Power Block shall remain under the Control of only one Traction Staff who has taken the Power Block from TPC. The same Traction staff is only authorized to cancel the Power Block, as per laid down Procedures. Cancellation Messages shall also be recorded in the Power Block Message Book / Register.
## 4.7 Shadow Power Block:

## 4.7 Shadow Power Block:

Shadow Power Block is further extension of the Power Block, granted by the Traction Staff to other Authorized Person seeking permit to work  in the part area covered by the 'Power Block',  under the provisions of Discharge Rods as per extant Procedures. The Authorized Person could be the Station Controller, PSI Supervisor or the supervisor of the other departments.
While  granting  and  cancelling  the  Shadow  Power  Block,  all  the  formalities  of  Power  Block  shall  be complied with.
Shadow power block shall be required when the working zone is within 2 m of OHE.
In  no  case,  a  Shadow  OHE  Power  Block  can  be  granted  to  the  Contractor,  directly  by  the  Traction Wing.

## 6.0 GENERAL PRECAUTIONS:

6.1 No Maintenance Staff shall enter on to the Track of any Running Line without the Permission of the Traffic Controller.
6.2 Metro Employees and Authorized Contractor's Representatives, when on Right of Way

(i) Shall  be  responsible  for  their  own  Safety  and  observe  all  Safety  Rules  and  Regulations  during  the course of Work.

(i) Shall not hang upon or lean on the sides of moving vehicles.

## 7.1 Granting Power Block:

On the basis of 'Weekly General Order', the TPC shall grant the Power Block to the authorized Traction Staff,  as  per  Procedure  in  vogue.  In  any  case,  the  Power  Block  shall  be  granted  by  TPC  only  after obtaining Confirmation from the Traffic Controller, duly obtaining his Signature in the Register meant for the purpose.  Traction Power Controller shall thereafter confirm the same, under Acknowledgement, to TC.
## 7.2 Power Block Coordination between Traction Power Controller & Traffic Controller:

## 7.2 Power Block Coordination between Traction Power Controller & Traffic Controller:

The Traction Power Controller shall maintain a Register & shall obtain the Signature from the Traffic Controller, as Acknowledgement:
(i) Before granting the Power Block.
(ii) After granting the Power Block.
(iii) Before cancelling the Power Block.
(iv) After cancelling the Power Block.
Any alteration in the Power Block or any contemplated Train Movement, prior to the grant of Power Block,  shall  be  advised  by  Traffic  Controller  to  the  Traction  Power  Controller,  by  duly  signing  in  the Traction Power Controller Register.
Only  after  obtaining  Confirmation  from  the  Traffic  Controller,  duly  obtaining  his  Signature  in  the Register,  the  Traction  Power  Controller  shall  grant  Power  Block  &  confirm  the  same,  under Acknowledgement, to TC/OCC.

## Introduction

If, because of any reason, the Traction Power Controller is not in a position to grant 'Power Block', he shall  cancel  the  'Power  Block'  and  accordingly  intimate  to  the  Traffic  Controller,  duly  taking  his Signature for Acknowledgement.
## 7.3 Cancellation of Power Block:

## 7.3 Cancellation of Power Block:

Power  Block  is  to  be  cancelled  by  Traction  Staff  after  ensuring  that  all  Shadow  Power  Blocks, authorized by him are cancelled.
Traction  Staff  shall  inform  the  Traction  Power  Controller  by  a  Message  duly  exchanging  Private Numbers that all Shadow Power Blocks have been cancelled, all Men, Materials, Equipments, Tools & Plants and temporary Earths have been removed & all the working parties have been informed that OHE is now going to be energized, OHE is fit for the Restoration of the Power Supply & fit for the Electric Traffic.
After obtaining the Message for Cancellation of Power Block from the Traction Staff to whom the Power Block was granted by Traction Power Controller, the Traction Power Controller shall inform the Traffic Controller that the concerned Power Block has now been cancelled & OHE is going to be energized as per  Procedure,  duly  obtaining  the  Signature  of  the  Traffic  Controller  as  Acknowledgement  in  the Register meant for the purpose.
Before giving acknowledgement to TPC, the TC shall ensure that all PTW's, issued for work under the provision of Power block / Shadow Power Block have been cancelled.
After the enerzisation of the OHE, the Traction Power Controller shall confirm the same immediately to the Traffic Controller in writing and take his Acknowledgment in the Register.

## 9.0 STATUS OF THE 'OHE' IN SHADOW POWER BLOCK:

## 9.0 STATUS OF THE 'OHE' IN SHADOW POWER BLOCK:

Status of Electrically De-energized OHE shall be ensured in the following manner:
## 9.1 By TPC:

## 9.1 By TPC:

After switching off the OHE, TPC shall check the status of OHE on his Monitor. The Voltage at PT shall be indicated as 0.2 to 0.5 KV. After the provision of Discharge Rods on the OHE, it shall be shown as 0.0 KV on the Monitor. TPC, in this way, can re-confirm the assertion of Traction Staff in regard to the provision of Discharge Rods on the OHE.
The  Elementary  Section  /  Line  is  shown  in  'Green'  Colour  on  TPC's  Monitor,  when  the  OHE  is  in charged condition with 25 KV. After switching off the OHE, it becomes 'Red' for DMRC (Line 1 to 9). For  Airport  Line the  Elementary Section/Line is shown in 'Red' colour on TPC's monitor, when the OHE is in charged condition with 25kv. After switching off the OHE, becomes 'White'.
.
## 9.2 By Traction Staff:

## 9.2 By Traction Staff:

On confirmation of the status of electrically de-energized OHE from the TPC, the Traction Staff shall put the Discharge Rods on the OHE and confirm the same to TPC.
## 9.3 By Station Controller & PSI Supervisor taking Shadow Power Block:

## 9.3 By Station Controller & PSI Supervisor taking Shadow Power Block:

On  confirmation  of  status  of  electrically  de-energized  OHE  from  the  Traction  Staff  (who  has  taken power block), Station Controller & PSI Supervisor shall provide Discharge Rods on the OHE and inform accordingly to the Traction Staff, who in turn shall confirm the same to TPC.

## 9.4 By Other Supervisors taking Shadow Power Block:

(i) E&M,  S&T  and  Civil  Works  of  general  nature  i.e.  Maintenance  /  Repair  Works  on  AC  Units, Lighting System, Fans (other than on the Platforms within a radius of 2 m from the OHE or Track), Electrical Distribution System, Fire Fighting Equipment, Clocks, PAS, and Drainage & Sewage etc. can be carried out in Revenue hours. As far as possible, the Supervisor supervising the Work shall ensure that the Public Amenities are not affected and the Barricading / Diversion done shall cause minimum  inconvenience  to  the  Public.  No  PTW  shall  be  required  to  carry  out  such  Works  at

## Introduction

Stations.

(ii) In  case  of  the  In-house  Maintenance  at  the  Platforms  within  a  radius  of  2  m  from  OHE,  the Authorized O&M Supervisor / Sr. Maintainer shall take the PTW from the Station Controllers of the individual Stations. Concerned Station Controllers shall issue the PTW after ensuring that Shadow Power Block is available for such Works.
(iii)  All staff working at the site shall be responsible for their own safety and observe all Safety Rules and Regulations during the Course of Work.
(iv)  After Completion of work, DMRC/Project Staff shall cancel the PTW in the requisite Performa with the SC, who in turn will inform OCC, under the exchange of Private Numbers.
(v) For the purpose of Maintenance, Repairs, Inspection or Testing of Lifts and Escalators, A/C Units, Lighting System & Fans (other than on Platforms within a radius of 2 m from the OHE or Track), Electric Distribution System, Fire Fighting Equipment, a list of Authorized Contractors Personnel to carry out above Works will be made available to the concerned controller in OCC by the concerned Mgr./AM/E&M.

(vi)  OCC/TPC  shall  inform  the  concerned  SC  before  the  Authorized  Contractor's  Staff  reaches  the Station  to  carry  out  the  Work  specified  in  the  PTW.  SC  will  note  down  the  details  including  the Location,  Duration,  Time  of  Start  and  the  Name  of  the  Authorized  Supervisor,  and  Number  of Workers etc. in the Station Controller's Diary. In the Underground Section, the Contractor's Staff shall be accompanied by the DMRC Staff who will be responsible for Verification of their Identity and the Work to be done by them. In case of any doubt about the Identity of the Contractor's Staff, the same shall be got verified from OCC / TPC. When the concerned Working Party reports to SC, SC will verify their Identity and other details given by OCC / TPC / Supervisor, inform OCC / TC and then only allow the Contractor's Staff to carry out the Work. After Completion of the Work, SC will again inform OCC/TC about the same.

(vii) However, in case the Contractor's Staff is required to visit one Station for once or twice only for a very  specific  /  non-repetitive  nature  of Work,  they  need  not  be  issued  I.  Card  by  the  DMRC,  to avoid  the  misuse  later.  Such  Contractor's  Staff  shall  be  accompanied  by  the  DMRC  Staff.  The Contractor's  Staff  shall  only  be  allowed  to  enter  the  Station  by  the  Station  Controller  after  the Identification  of  their  Identity  by  the  said  DMRC  Staff  accompanying  them,  either  during  Nonrevenue / Revenue Hours, as the case may be.
(viii)  For  regular Maintenance in the Equipment Rooms, the concerned Departmental In-charges shall be responsible & no PTW shall be required for the same. Regular Maintenance can be done in Revenue Hours only, if it does not affect the Train Operations / Public Amenities.
(ix)  In addition to the above, following Safety Precautions shall always be observed, when the Work is required to be carried out at the Platform Level:
(a)  The Work will be carried out maximum up to Hand Railing Level on the Platform Periphery.
(b)  No Ladder or Tool more than 45 cm. long (other than Pick-up Rod & Point Machine Rod) shall be used. At all times, a minimum clearance of 2 m shall be ensured from the Live OHE.
(c) All Workmen will remain clear of the Yellow Line on the Platform, towards the Platform Edge.

(c) All Workmen will remain clear of the Yellow Line on the Platform, towards the Platform Edge.
(d)  Concerned Supervisors& all Workmen shall be responsible for their own Safety in case of any eventuality.
(x) Contractor's Party shall always be accompanied by the DMRC Staff during the period of imposition of Red Alert and heightened Security Situations.

## A. Procedure for award of Competency to SC for applying discharge Rods

## A. Procedure for award of Competency to SC for applying discharge Rods

Station Controllers, during their Initial Training shall be trained to put and remove Discharge Rod on OHE.  Competency  Certificate,  after  their  successful  Training  shall  be  issued  by  AM/Manager (Traction) & AM/Manager (Operations) jointly.
Concern  AM/Manager/Ops  shall  plan  for  refresher  training  of  concerned  employee(s)  to  put  and remove  Discharge  Rod  on  OHE  by  the  end  of  validity  period  of  their  existing  competency;  in coordination with concerned AM/Manager/Traction (O&M).
Competency shall be valid for one year from the date of issue.
Format of Competency shall be as per Annexure K1.
## B. Maintenance of discharge rods

## B. Maintenance of discharge rods

Discharge Rods shall be handed over to respective Station Controllers, who shall be responsible for their safe Custody .Physical Condition of Discharge Rods shall be monthly checked by OHE Wing.
Documentation of the proper upkeep of Discharge Rods shall be kept by OHE Wing, duly countersigned by respective Station Controllers.
Station Controllers   shall report for any defect noticed in Discharge Rods to TPC / OHE Wing of respective Lines.
Record of Maintenance of Discharge Rods shall be periodically audited by Safety Wing.
Following Check List shall be observed for Maintenance of Discharge Rods:
(i) Check the continuity of Cable connection between the top Clamp and Earthing Clamps.
(ii) Replace the Cable, if more than 20% Strands are broken.
(iii) Check the end connections of the Clamps for firmness. Rectify the connection, if so required.
(iv) Examine the Spring Tension of top Clamp & adjust the same as per requirement.
(v) Tighten all Nuts & Bolts of Earthing Clamp.
(vi) Check the Insulation of Cable.
SSE / SE / ASE / JE PSI or OHE of respective Lines shall examine the Discharge Rods as per the Check List, given in  Para '5'  above  and maintain the  Records  in  a  Register  in Token  of  above Checks.

## SAFETY CIRCULAR-29 E (Rev.02)
## CATS OPERATION PROCEDURE OF ATS OVER LINE-7 and Line-9

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This procedure order covers the working of CATS operation and also describes the procedures to transfer  the  control  among  CATS  users  (OCC Traffic Controllers)  to  LATS  users  (SCR  Station Controllers)  or  vice  versa  to  have  the  operation  &  overview  of  the  train  movement  and  the Signaling gears status in the LINE - 07 and Line -09.

## 2. SCOPE

This  procedure  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  the  Metro  Railways  General Rules,  2020  and Metro  Railways  General  (Amendment)  Rules,  2022,  Safety  Circulars  and  other  instructions  in vogue for working of Trains between Majlis Park-Shiv Vihar (LINE -07) and (LINE- 09).
For UTO mode of Train Operation (Line-7): wherever Train Operator (TO) is mentioned, it is to be read as Train Operator (TO)/ Roving Attendant (RA)/ Emergency Train Operator (ETO). The document should be read in conjunction with provisions of EBI Screen UIC Operator Manual and special instructions for working of Trains between Majlis Park-Shiv Vihar (LINE -07).

## 3. System of Working

Under  ATS  in  manual  mode,  in  case  of  Line-7,  when  level  of  control  is 'LATS' Majlis  park, (Shakurpur/  Mayapuri/  Durgabai  Deshmukh  South  Campus),  (Lajpatnagar/  Sarai  Kale  Khan Nizamuddin), (IP Extension/ Mayur Vihar Pkt-1), (Maujpur/ Krishna Nagar/ East Azad Nagar/ Shiv Vihar),  Mukundpur Depot  and  Vinod  Nagar Depot  can  control their interlocking  or  authority  area assigned to them from their ATS workstation. In case of Line-9, when level of control is "LATS" Dwarka/ Najafgarh/ Dhansa Bus Stand station (Controlling region 1 Interlocking i.e. from Dwarka to Dhansa Bus Stand) and Najafgarh depot (Controlling  Region  2 interlocking i.e.  Najafgarh  depot) can control their Interlocking or Authority Area assigned to them from their ATS workstation.

## 3. System of Working

When  level  of  control  is 'LATS' ,  all  other  secondary  station  can  only  monitor  the  main  line (respective Interlocking Area). All controllers are able to consult all the views simultaneously. But only one controller (local station, depot, central) at a time is allowed to send control towards one Interlocking.
The CENTRAL ATS will assign train identification numbers automatically & provide all necessary train information to the operator.
When CATS having control is restarted or initialized, control will be released and can be taken from 'Local' workstation or 'VDU' . When LATS having control is restarted control will be released and can  be  taken  from 'VDU'. Further  change  of  level  is  only  possible  with  mutual  consent  of  both LATS and CATS users. Normally the control of all Interlocking should be with OCC Controllers with level of control being 'CATS'.

## Introduction

Manual route release and Emergency route release guidelines regarding cancellation of a pre-determined route is as following: - (Note-Route shall be cancelled only under provisions of MRGR,2020 rule 19 sub rule 3)
## a)  Manual Route Release:

## a)  Manual Route Release:

Train has not entered on route and approach lock indication is not active:
In case train has not entered on route and approach lock indication is not active, the route shall be released immediately.
Train has entered on route or approach lock indication is active:
In case train has entered on route or approach lock indication is active, the manual route release request will be rejected by the signaling system.
## b)  Emergency Route Release:

## b)  Emergency Route Release:

Emergency route Release  is  used  to  release  locked  routes.  When  the  command  has been  executed  and  completed,  the  section  in  the  former  route  is  available  for  setting other routes.
## 1. Train has not entered on route and approach lock indication is not active:

## 1. Train has not entered on route and approach lock indication is not active:

In case train has not entered on route and approach lock indication is not active, the route shall be released immediately.
## 2. Train has entered on route or approach lock indication is active:

## 2. Train has entered on route or approach lock indication is active:

In  case  train  has  entered  on  route  or  approach  lock  indication  is  active,  the  route  will  be released as per following criterion:
(i) For  communicating  CBTC  trains  in  approach  locking  zone  or  in  route: In  case communicating CBTC train is present in the route or in approach locking area, route will be released immediately, when CBTC train in approach locking zone or in route are confirmed to be in standstill position or ERR timer (90 sec) has been expired; whichever is earlier.
(ii) For  non-communicating CBTC  trains  in  approach  locking  zone  or in  route: In  case non-communicating CBTC train is present in the route or in approach locking area, route will be  released  only  when  ERR  timer  (90  sec)  expires.  Early  route  release  as  mentioned against (I) shall not be available for routes that span a region boundary. If ERR is issued for a  route  that  spans  region  boundary,  Full  ERR  timer  will  be  run  for  releasing  of  route irrespective  of  communicating  CBTC  or  non-communicating  train  present  in  route  or  in approach locking area.
## Note -

## Note -

TC/SC shall ensure that trains are held at standstill in conjunction to the use of Emergency Route Release command.
In all cases new route shall be communicated to train operator under exchange of private number.

## 9. General Instruction

## 9. General Instruction

9.1. Critical  Commands: Critical Commands are necessary to release or circumvent certain safety features built in the system with the complete Knowledge & Consent of the Operator, to deal with certain specific  operational  situations  or  some  signaling  system  Anomalies.  The  operator, therefore,  is  allowed  to  issue  Critical  Commands  with  additional  Measures for  safeguarding  and control of critical operations.
A Critical Command is programmed in such a way that its Issue shall have to be confirmed within a pre-determined time interval on the Central / Local ATS or VDU, before it shall be executed by the Interlocking and / or ATC.
Before a Critical Command is executed the TC / SC must:
(i) Check if the Critical  Command is absolutely necessary or if it can  be avoided  by  utilizing another alternative.
(ii) Ensure that using this Command does not in any way leads to Hazardous Situation.
(iii) Obtain Permission from the Chief Controller, who shall have to agree that, the conditions (i) & (ii) above are satisfied.
(iv) If  TC/SC  has  any  doubt  about  the  Safety  of  using  the  envisaged  Critical  Command,  in combination with the necessary Measures, he / she must stop and check other Solutions or consult the Chief Controller & FMC.
9.2. (a) In case of RATP (Region ATP) cold start, before re-applying TSRs, CBI stop command & other wayside protection (by OCC commands); TC shall ensure that all trains in the region of respective RATP, are protected.

## Introduction

(b) Train operation can only be resumed after all trains in affected region are located by RATP.

## Introduction

9.3. In certain cases, for example when active interlocking unit is operational, and the standby unit has been switched  off,  any  command issued  with input  from  a  non-volatile  data  might  be  lost  when active  is  also  switched  off  and  then  the  standby  has  been  powered  ON  or  vice-versa  in  an interlocking cabinet. Operator must re-initiate all the safety critical commands while switch over has been performed in a way described in this scenario. FMC will confirm the same to TC/CC.
9.4. To apply system hold and system stop commands, only region wide commands shall be used by TC/SC.
9.5. For routes across any interlocking boundary, the TC/SC shall not set a route within 08 seconds after the same route is manually cancelled.

## 10.4. Train Details

## 10.4. Train Details

The tab [Train Details]-Window is a tabbed window with following pages:

## 10.4. Train Details

 Train Properties
In train properties the following information available are as follows
Train set number is the vehicle ID or rake ID.
CBTC train id is the vehicle ID.
ATS Train No is the train ID displayed on the track layout (destination ID + service ID).
There are various operating modes: No Mode, Cut-Out, ROS, RM, Forward, Reverse, ATP, ATO, UTO and ATB.
The general tab also tells the delay status of the train. There are four delay classes: early, ontime, late and very late.
Other information e.g. skip, next stop, destination and door statuses are also included in the general tab.
 Motion

## Introduction

The speed and information related train running e.g. acceleration rate, deceleration rate, cruise speed, coast level etc. are displayed in the motion tab.

## Introduction

Speed gives the current speed of the train in km/h.
Acceleration gives the current acceleration of the train in km/h^2.
Physical front and rear give the segments on which the physical train is present.
Virtual  front  and  rear  give  the  segments  on  which  the  virtual  occupancy  of  the  train  lies. Coasting gives the current coasting value as per the performance regime:
The System shall provide at least 5 different performance regimes including 1) A maximum train performance  regime  2)  Full  coasting  regime  3)  Energy  Saving  Regime  4)  5%  coasting performance regime 5) 8% coasting performance regime.
##  VATC

##  VATC

In the VATC tab, the active VATC and active train cab status are shown at the top and followed by the train initialization status e.g. initialization track.
The train sleeping, jogging status, backward permitted status and configured for reverse are shown at the bottom with either yes or no.
##  Alarms

## Introduction

Train alarms are displayed in the Alarms tab e.g. PEA (passenger emergency alarm), departure test result and other alarms.

## 10.6. VATC Alarms: -

### 10.6. VATC Alarms: -

|   Alarm No. | Alarm Name                                       | Description                                                                                                                                                    |

|           1 | Emergency Brake Trainline De-energized VATC      | Set whenever the VATC de-energizes the emergency brake train line(s).                                                                                          |
|           2 | Emergency Brake Train line De-energized non-VATC | Set whenever the VATC detects a de-energized emergency brake trainline(s) that it did not command.                                                             |
|           3 | Unscheduled Door Opening                         | The train All Doors Closed indication is de-energized when conditions for safe door opening are not present.                                                   |
|           4 | Loss Of Vital Zero Speed                         | Set whenever the train is at rest and one or more of the conditions for vital zero speed has been violated. When this occurs the emergency brakes are applied. |
|           5 | Improper Travel Direction or Cab Setting         | The emergency brakes are applied because the travel direction cannot be determined or the active cab does not align with the traffic direction.                |

## 10.7. Tunnel Ventilation Mode

## 10.7. Tunnel Ventilation Mode

The tunnel ventilation mode is represented by a rectangle button. It is placed between stations in the underground section. Tunnel Ventilation limit can be set to 1 or 2 or no limit.

## 10.8. Traction power status

## 10.8. Traction power status

ATS system receives the power supply status from the Power Traction System. The status received will be displayed to the ATS Operators as ON/OFF/Not Updated.

## 10.8. Traction power status

Traction power status is displayed as-
Green circle - Powered ON Section
Red circle - Powered OFF Section
Black circle -Power Status not updated
## 10.9. Reduced Brake Rate

## 10.9. Reduced Brake Rate

The operator can change the brake rate regarding the condition of the track areas. When the track area is wet, the operator activates the reduced brake rate function and deactivates it when the area is dry.
The operator can operate the reduced brake rate function on the system wide (entire system) or the areas between stations.

### Introduction

|   S. No | Event Log Text (Example)            | Remark                                                                                    |
|---------|-------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|       1 | Reduced brake rate area not updated | The reduced brake rate area is not updated because RATO is failed or not connected to ATS |
|       2 | Reduced brake rate area deactivated | The reduced brake rate area is inactive for dry condition.                                |
|       3 | Reduced brake rate area activated   | The reduced brake rate area is active for wet condition.                                  |

## Introduction

The system wide reduced brake rate button is placed in a separate box with the other system wide buttons.
## 10.10.  RA Area

## 10.10.  RA Area

The routing automation status of a specific area is represented by a rectangle button. This function provides the feature of automatic route setting & will be available in OCC, BCC & Local View.
The RA button for each region is placed in the interlocking box of each region where the interlocking computer status is presented.

### Introduction

|        2 | RA Disable                 | (Background: Red, Text: Black text 'Off')        | The routing automation is disabled; the ATS operator has to set routes in the area manually.           |
|        3 | RA Enable                  | (Background: Light green, Text: Black text 'On') | The routing automation is enabled. Routes in the area are set automatically regarding the timetable.   |
## 10.11.  Self-Normalization On/Self-Normalization Off

## 10.11.  Self-Normalization On/Self-Normalization Off

The point self-normalization will allow point to switch back to its normal position automatically after a route is released.

## 10.11.  Self-Normalization On/Self-Normalization Off

The default state for point self-normalization is inhibited, the operator can activate point selfnormalization by giving command NORM_PT_ON.

## Introduction

Figure144:SetNORM_PT_ON

## Introduction

The operator has to confirm by executing the command CONFIRM_NORM_PT. To confirm, right-click on point and left-click on CONFIRM_NORM_PT command.
Figure149:Pointnormalizationactiveisindicated
To  remove  point  self-normalization,  select  command  NORM_PT_OFF  and  click  Execute  button  at command bar. The operator must confirm to remove the self-normalization by executing CONFIRM_NORM_PT_OFF command.
## 10.12.  Emergency Stop Plunger

## 10.12.  Emergency Stop Plunger

Emergency Stop Plungers will be provided at each platform and station rooms in order to provide the capability  for  passengers  or  staff  to  react  to  dangerous  situations.  The  emergency  stop  plunger  is represented on ATS by a rectangle button with text 'ESP'.

3.1 All  the  request  for  imposition/alteration/cancellation  of  TSR  on  main  line  should  be  made  to chief  controller/OCC  and  the  CC/OCC  shall  instruct  Traffic  Controller  for  the  Imposition  / Alteration/Cancellation  of  Temporary  Speed  Restrictions  &  Issue  of  Caution  Orders  to  Train operators, as required on the Main Line Sections.
3.2 In cases of any of the TSR Commands, not directly being under Control of TC, the Compliance of  the  same  shall  be  ensured  by  TC  by  the  Station  Controllers  on  the  Exchange  of  Private Numbers.
3.3 All  Requests  for  the  Imposition  /  Alteration/Cancellation  of  Temporary  Speed  Restrictions  & Issue of Caution Orders to the Train Operators, as required within the Depot, shall be submitted to  the  Depot  Controller,  who  is  responsible  for  Coordination  of  all  such  Requests.  Depot Controller shall also inform the TSR details to the PPIO, under Exchange of Private Numbers, to enable him to advise the Shunting Supervisors accordingly.
3.4 All Requests of the TSRs shall be submitted by the Authorized Personnel of Rank, not less than Junior Engineers as per prescribed format in Annexure -' C ' .

3.5
(a) On  receipt  of  Request  for  Imposition  /  Alteration  &  Cancellation  of  Temporary  Speed Restriction (TSR) on a Section / in the Depot, the Traffic Controller / Depot Controller shall verify  the  TC  No.  corresponding  to  the  OHE  Mast  No.  from  the  Conversion  Table  at Annexure  -  'A' to  this  Circular  and  shall  take  further  action  for  Imposition  /  Alteration  / Cancellation of the Temporary Speed Restriction.
(b) The Requests for the TSRs for a Planned Work shall normally be submitted before 1700 Hrs. of the previous day.
(c) The  TSR  Requests,  arising  out  of  Emergency  or  Failure  during  revenue  hours,  shall  be taken  up  promptly,  TC  shall  ensure  implementation  of  such  TSR,  from  the  first  train operator, who is passing the affected section under exchange of private numbers, the train operator  in  turn  shall  intimate  the  target  speed  displayed  on  DMI  over  the  affected section.TC shall log/record the same.
(d) Traffic Controller / Depot Controller shall keep a record of accepted TSR Requests.

3.8 The Traffic  Controller  shall  advise  the  Depot  Controller  &  Station  Controllers  of  the  Terminal Stations of all TSRs to be in force during next day on the entire Mainline on daily basis and shall maintain  a  Record  of  the  same.  Traffic  Controller  shall  also  advise  the  TSRs  to  the  Crew Controller and the Crew Controller and depot controller shall write in the notice boards and sign on register as well however for those TSRs not imposed through the system due to any reason shall  be  advised  to  Train  operators  of  each  passing  train  in  the  form  of  caution  order  at  the preceding station of affected section.
3.9 Traffic Controller shall ensure that before the Start of Revenue Services all the TSRs requested on the Section have been 'Set' on the Sector and shall advise, under the Exchange of Private numbers, the first  Train  Operator  passing  the  affected  Section.  Traffic  Controller  will  confirm from the said TO with regard to the imposition of TSR. Train Operator in turn shall intimate the Target Speed displayed on DMI over the affected area to the Traffic Controller. TC shall log / record the same.
3.10 On Completion, the Status of all the TSRs shall be verified by the ' TSR Status' Request on the ATC Maintenance Terminal or by viewing the ' TSR List ' appearing in TSR Overview Dialog Box of LATS/CATS MMI for the particular ATC Zone. Complete List of TSRs shall be reconciled with the Traffic Controller in case of any alteration in TSRs.
